News.title: Leaked phone call with Patrick Clancy’s dad during Lindsay’s murder trial leads to charges for true crime influencer
News.content:
Next

A TRUE crime influencer obsessed with the Lindsay Clancy murder case has been charged with felony wiretapping after police linked her to a secret recording of Patrick Clancy’s father.

Shawna Gramkow, 46, allegedly posted audio of Christopher Clancy after he received a mystery phone call while Lindsay’s blockbuster murder trial was underway in Massachusetts.



Gramkow runs the Instagram account “saltylunatics,” which has amassed more than 50,000 followers through extensive coverage of the case.

Christopher told investigators he was driving in Scituate around August 6 when a call came in from a number he did not recognize.



He said he accidentally accepted the call while trying to decline it, leaving the line open without realizing what had happened, according to a Scituate Police report obtained by CBS Boston.

Police said the unknown caller then recorded Christopher without his knowledge or permission.



Christopher told officers that some of his comments concerned his oldest son, Brian.

He said he did not realize he had been recorded until the audio later appeared online.

The recording was posted on Gramkow’s Instagram account on August 30 before being circulated elsewhere on social media.

Christopher recognized his own voice and contacted Scituate police to file a report.



Gramkow also discussed the call in the Instagram video, which investigators later reviewed.

The publicly reported police material does not identify Gramkow as the person who placed the call or secretly recorded Christopher.

Instead, the report says she discussed audio that had been obtained by someone else and later posted on her Instagram account.



According to the police report, Gramkow said Lindsay’s attorney Kevin Reddington had read Patrick’s phone number aloud during the trial.

She then allegedly said “one of y’all decided to give him a call,” indicating that someone following her coverage had contacted the number.

Fox News similarly reported that the Instagram video showed an unknown individual calling the number Gramkow claimed belonged to Patrick.

“Patrick’s dad was still on the line,” Gramkow allegedly said in the video, according to the report.

She allegedly added that Christopher was mumbling and appeared not to realize the phone remained connected.



Police say Christopher’s comments were recorded without his knowledge or permission.

PEOPLE, citing the police report, states that Gramkow did not personally make the recording but is accused of publishing it.

Massachusetts wiretapping law covers more than the person who personally makes a secret recording and can also apply to someone accused of knowingly using or disclosing illegally intercepted audio.

The felony charge carries a maximum sentence of five years in state prison.

Investigators later subpoenaed Meta for records linked to the Instagram post and confirmed Gramkow was the person speaking in the August 30 video, according to PEOPLE.



Scituate police ultimately filed a criminal complaint against Gramkow in Hingham District Court on October 20.

She is scheduled to be arraigned on November 20 on a felony unlawful-wiretapping charge.

Gramkow has denied wrongdoing, publicly calling the allegations “false” and “easy to prove.”

Gramkow’s account has also posted extensively about conspiracy theories accusing Patrick of involvement in the deaths of his three children.

Some online commentators went further and falsely accused Patrick himself of killing Cora, five, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan.



Patrick has never been charged in connection with their deaths, prosecutors have never accused him of involvement, and there is no public indication law enforcement treated him as a murder suspect.

Evidence presented in court placed Patrick away from the Duxbury home, with Judge William Sullivan citing GPS data and surveillance footage showing Lindsay was the only person there at the relevant time.

Prosecutors said Lindsay sent Patrick out for takeout food and medication on January 24, 2023, before taking the children into the basement and strangling them with exercise resistance bands.

Cora and Dawson died that night, while Callan died in hospital three days later.

Patrick testified that he returned home to find the children with bands around their necks and moved between them performing CPR until first responders arrived.



Prosecutors said Lindsay then cut her wrists and jumped from a second-story window, suffering injuries that left her paralyzed from the waist down.

Her defense maintained that she was not criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis, with the five-week trial featuring competing psychiatric testimony and extensive evidence about her treatment and medications.

The U.S. Sun previously examined some of the key evidence presented during the trial.

The trial ended in a mistrial on September 4 after the jury split 11-1, with 11 jurors favoring a finding that Lindsay was not criminally responsible.

Her lawyers are now asking Judge Sullivan to dismiss the charges on double-jeopardy grounds, while prosecutors want the case to remain alive.



Lindsay is due back in Plymouth Superior Court on November 2 for arguments over the dismissal bid.

Patrick has also filed a wrongful-death lawsuit against mental health professionals involved in Lindsay’s care, while she has separately filed a medical malpractice suit.

His attorney Howard Cooper told a judge he believes Lindsay could eventually testify in the wrongful death case that she warned providers about homicidal thoughts.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Lindsay’s attorney Kevin Reddington disputed that account, saying she never told providers she harbored homicidal ideation toward her children and had never indicated she intended to testify in Patrick’s lawsuit.

“Mr. Clancy’s counsel does not speak for Lindsay Clancy,” Reddington said in response to the testimony claim.

News.title: ‘Islamic state jihadist’, 28, who arrived in Britain on a small boat claimed asylum then raped woman insider her home
News.content:
SICK ATTACK ‘Islamic state jihadist’, 28, who arrived in Britain on a small boat claimed asylum then raped woman insider her home







Next

AN alleged Islamic State jihadist who “took part in ISIS operations” raped a woman inside her home after arriving here on a small boat, The Sun can reveal.

Ayman Mohammed Al-Shammari, 28, was trying to escape being tried for terror offences in Austria when he crossed the Channel.



The Kuwaiti national allegedly fought for the terror group in Iraq in 2016.

He is also said to have “taken part in ISIS training camps” and held a role “promoting” their ideology.



Yet the alleged terrorist was able to claim asylum in Britain after arriving illegally and later moved into a pal’s flat in Taunton, Somerset.

Four months after arriving he entered a woman’s home in the historic market town in the early hours of November 15 last year.



In a prolonged attack, he raped her inside her bedroom.

The victim, who met Al-Shammari two weeks before on her birthday in a nightclub, tried to escape by “scratching” him.

Al-Shammari then brazenly used her shower before using Google Translate on his phone to tell her: “This is how I am in sex, do you like this or not?”

Jurors at Bristol Crown Court today found him guilty of one count of rape.



Separately, Al-Shammari faces extradition to Austria where he is wanted over a string of alleged terror offences.

His alleged ISIS background emerged at a previous extradition court hearing but jurors at the rape trial were not told about it.

According to prosecutors at a Westminster court, Al-Shammari was part of ISIS between January and October 2016.

During that time, ISIS militants had launched a massive offensive against the minority ethnic group the Yazidis in northwest Iraq forcing 400,000 to flee their homes.

Thousands of Yazidi men, women and children were executed with their bodies dumped into mass graves.



More than 6,800 Yazidi women and children were captured or trafficked with young girls subjected to systemic sexual slavery and torture.

Prosecutor Emma Eatwell said at a Westminster court last week: “This defendant is alleged to have participated in ISIS and did so by promoting the ideology of the group and participating in training courses.”

She added: “He also took part in terror operations affiliated with that group.”

A Home Office spokesperson told The Sun: “Our thoughts are with the victim of Al-Shammari’s crime. He has been rightly convicted, and justice has been delivered by the courts.

“Foreign nationals who commit sexual offences will be excluded from refugee protections, and we will do everything in our power to get them out of the country.”



In court, when probed about the rape, Al-Shammari shockingly insisted the victim “wanted sex.”

David Dainty, defending, claimed the woman had been a “willing participant”.

Jurors heard Al-Shammari “persuaded” the woman to allow him to enter her home with a bottle of spiced rum.

The victim managed to reach for her phone to capture harrowing recordings of the attack on her phone.

Afte raping her, Al-Shammari brazenly took a shower inside the woman’s home before leaving to go back to his flat.



The woman later told police she had been raped and provided them with the disturbing recordings.

Simon Burns, prosecuting, said: “She was a happy girl, was she not, who had met Al-Shammari. They had struck up a rapport but she drew the line.

“We can hear that girl protesting in pain.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“In her panic, pain and protest she was able somehow to activate her phone.”

Al-Shammari will be sentenced in November.

News.title: Tragedy as hedgehog ‘screams itself to death’ after yobs spray-paint it blue ‘to make prickly animal look like Sonic’
News.content:
CRUEL STUNT Tragedy as hedgehog ‘screams itself to death’ after yobs spray-paint it blue ‘to make prickly animal look like Sonic’







Next

A HEDGEHOG has tragically died “screaming” in pain after vile yobs spray painted it blue to make it look like “Sonic”.

The adult male was found by a farmer in one of his fields just behind Wakefield Police Station, West Yorkshire, after it appeared he had been painted to look like the cartoon character.



The paint was sprayed so close to a large area of the animal’s back that the chemicals burned off “several” layers of skin and also caused its spines to “melt away”.

The poor animal was rushed to nearby Castleford Hedgehog Rescue, West Yorks., arriving around 4 pm on Tuesday, October 27.



But the innocent hedgehog tragically died the next morning of his injuries.

Beth Campsill, 29, who runs the charity and tried to save the hedgehog, said it was the worst case of spray paint-based cruelty she has seen in her 16 years.



The animal lover said: “When the hedgehog was brought to us he was screaming in pain.

“I gave the poor thing the maximum pain relief I could, but he didn’t stop, he effectively screamed himself to death.

“I don’t know how anyone could be so cruel to an animal. It is disgusting.

“I haven’t seen anything as bad or as sad as this in a long time.”



Beth said that the hedgehog died due to an infection caused by the chemical burns as well as potentially being poisoned by the toxins in the paint.

The charity worker posted about the tiny nocturnal creature on her Facebook page, with several people commenting it could be an antiseptic spray to treat livestock.

But Beth believes it was a form of spray paint due to its “thick texture” and how it burned the skin, something she says an antiseptic spray wouldn’t do.



She also had to scrape it off its remaining spines which hadn’t already fallen out.

The spiny mammal was also suffering from “flystrike”.

This is when flies lay eggs on an animal’s wounds and soft tissue, and the hatched maggots feed on and burrow into the animal’s flesh, according to the RSPCA.

Flystrike is also potentially fatal and Beth said the animal most likely would have endured a “slow and ultimately and extremely painful death” in the wild.

She said: “I’m glad he was brought in as it meant at least we could ease his suffering and make him feel comfortable.”



Hedgehogs are sadly in decline in Britain and are now listed as “vulnerable” on Britain’s red list of mammals.

According to the latest State of Britain’s hedgehogs report, numbers of hedgehogs have fallen by up to 30 per cent in urban areas and 50 per cent in rural areas since the turn of the century.

Beth says she will report the incident to the police, but is unsure if the person responsible will be “held responsible” due to the location where it was found.

It comes after a hedgehog was left on the brink of death after yobs painted her in the colours of a Premier League football club.

The adult female was discovered by a woman in her back garden in Yeadon in West Yorkshire, covered in yellow and blue paint – the colour of the Leeds United football club.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The paint had left the spiny mammal unable to curl up into a ball and struggling to breathe due to the fumes.

Staff at an animal rescue centre – who scrubbed the oil-based paint from each spine and gave the hedgehog pain relief – branded the act “disgusting”.

News.title: Moment fire rips through hotel near Everest base camp as terrified Brit says ‘no one can rescue us’
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a raging inferno rips through a hotel near Everest base camp leaving terrified Brits begging for rescue.

Shocking footage has emerged showing towering flames and thick plumes of smoke filling the air at the snow covered mountain resort in Nepal.



A wall smoke can be seen erupting from the wood-clad hotel amidst a pounding flurry of snow.

In a clip posted to social media, British travel blogger Callan Bowl warned of the emergency, frantically saying “the hotel is on fire.”



He said: “It’s spreading…There’s no rescue here, nobody is allowed to move out of this area because of the snowfall, because of avalanches, so nobody can come put the fire out.”

Desperate people can be seen tossing belongings onto the snow-covered ground from windows as the fire grows.



Another video shows smoke filling the inside of a hotel as petrified guests scramble to escape, the Mail reports.

The horror blaze erupted at Hotel Good Luck in Dingboche around 11am on Friday.



Emergency crews rushed to bring the fire under control, with early reports suggesting the blaze may have been caused by a gas cylinder explosion.

Police Deputy Superintendent Nabin Raja Budhathoki said: “Preliminary information suggests the fire may have been caused by a cooking gas cylinder explosion.

“We will know more after further investigation.”



Hotel owner Kul Bahadur Tamang confrimed all guests and staff were safely evacuated from the 17-room establishment after the fire broke out in the kitchen.

Speaking from the scene of the inferno, trekking guide Arjun Gurung told the Everest Chronicle: “We could not do anything but watch it burn down.

“There were many gas cylinders in the kitchen, making it virtually impossible to put out the fire.”



He said as the building was cladded in wood the fire spread quickly.

Dingboche lies on the trekking route to Everest Base Camp.

The area is currently experiencing intense snowfall, leaving base-camp-bound climbers stranded and making Dingboche particularly busy.

Arjun continued: “We could neither go higher nor descend.

“We are stuck here for a couple of days, waiting for the weather to clear.”



Hotel Good Luck was a fixture for climbers and guides alike, so to watch it go up in flames was particularly painful for Arjun.

He said: “We have many good memories of the hotel. It was painful to watch.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Efforts are now underway to extinguish the fire, and further details of the damage are being assessed.

There have been no reported casualties.

News.title: Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ while taking pictures of moon as ‘smelly’ attacker ‘hit her on head and pulled her to floor’
News.content:
'ATTACK' PROBE Woman ‘sexually assaulted’ while taking pictures of moon as ‘smelly’ attacker ‘hit her on head and pulled her to floor’







Next

A WOMAN was allegedly sexually assaulted while taking pictures of the moon – as cops launch a manhunt for a suspect with “strong body odour”.

The shocking incident unfolded at South Common in Lincoln at around 6.30pm on Tuesday evening.

Lincolnshire Police said a woman in her 30s was walking at the top of the common and had been taking pictures of the full moon and city skyline.

The force believe she was struck on the back of the head and pulled to the floor.





She was able to flee the scene and call police after sustaining what are described as minor injuries during the attack.

The alleged suspect is described as around 5 ft 8 ins to 6ft and wearing a dark hoody and jeans.

They also had bad breath and a strong body odour smell, cops said.

A police spokesperson said: “It is estimated the location of the assault was around the halfway point and just below the footpath that runs from Cross O’Cliff Hill through to Canwick Road.

“Our investigation is ongoing and we would like to hear from anyone who was walking on South Common between 6pm and 8pm on Tuesday evening and who may have seen or heard anything they feel maybe related.

“While we have not had any similar reports in the area we understand this reported incident maybe unsettling for people who use South Common.”

Anyone with information is urged to contact Lincolnshire Police quoting incident 445 of October 27.

News.title: Christa Pike death row Dr exposed: Sunday school teacher paid $3k/execution ‘compares himself to Jesus’ in 1st interview
News.content:
Next

CHRISTA Pike’s execution doctor — a Sunday school teacher and evangelical Christian — has defended his role helping put inmates to death and compared the criticism he has faced to the treatment of Jesus.

In his first interview since the murderer’s botched execution in Tennessee, Dr. Mark Fowler has insisted he is not “evil,” “uncaring” or “incompetent” — and vowed he will not walk away from the job.



The 69-year-old grandfather has taken part in around seven lethal injections over the past decade and receives $3,000 for each execution, according to a deposition he gave last year.

Speaking to New York Magazine’s Intelligencer, Fowler said of Pike, “I lament that I am having to deal with Christa Pike, who bludgeoned another woman to death. She is what she is.”



He still hopes Tennessee will try to execute her again, saying carrying out her sentence would provide “a sense of justice” for the mother of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom Pike tortured and murdered in 1995.

On September 30, Pike, 50, survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her after two doses of pentobarbital apparently went into tissue in her arms rather than properly entering her bloodstream, leaving her alive and hospitalized.

Christa Pike MY TORTURE Christa Pike reveals botched execution agony as she relives death chamber hell



Fowler’s job that night was to enter the death chamber after the drugs had been administered and pronounce Pike dead, but instead he found himself helping save her life when the execution failed.

He has fiercely rejected how he says he has been portrayed since his secret role became public, insisting, “I’m not an evil, vicious person. I’m not unscrupulous. I’m not uncaring, and I’m not incompetent.”

Fowler said death-penalty opponents hoped that if they could “humiliate me I would step back from it,” adding that “there ain’t anybody else in Tennessee going to 

Describing the criticism against him as “calumny,” he made the striking comparison, “People said bad things about Jesus, didn’t they?”



His role puts him at odds with the American Medical Association, which opposes doctors taking part in executions, including inserting IVs and declaring death, because it conflicts with the medical duty to “do no harm.”

Fowler sees no contradiction, and Intelligencer described his career as one built around doing the “dirty work” others avoid.

Before becoming a doctor, Fowler worked as a public defender, then retrained in medicine and went on to work in nursing homes, jails, hospice wards and as a medical examiner.



About a decade ago, a surgeon who oversaw Tennessee executions retired and Fowler agreed to take his place.

“How can you morally say, ‘I’m for the death penalty so long as somebody else does the work?'” Fowler said. “I do things that nobody wants to do.”

He has also said he wants to be remembered as a “Renaissance man” and “someone who has an advanced appreciation of life.”

Fowler also believes his work does not clash with his evangelical Christian beliefs, despite teaching Sunday school and beginning his mornings with devotional readings from the Book of Common Prayer.

“‘Thou shalt not kill’ does not have any application to the legitimate actions of the government in terms of executing murderers,” Fowler said.



He added that the commandment does not apply to self-defense or war, saying, “When the state says, ‘We think there are some things so heinous that we should effectuate the ultimate punishment,’ I think that’s legitimate.”

But Fowler acknowledges flaws in capital punishment, saying, “Is it unfairly administered? Probably. Is it always deserved? Not necessarily. My job is not to say ‘yay’ or ‘nay.'”

Those flaws have been apparent in executions in which Fowler himself has been involved.

Aside from Christa, he was identified as the physician in Byron Black’s execution, where officials refused to deactivate the inmate’s implanted defibrillator and Black groaned that it was “hurting so bad” as the lethal drugs took effect.

And in May, Fowler was involved in Tony Carruthers’ failed execution, which was abandoned after staff could not establish the required IV access.



He has nevertheless criticized how Pike’s execution was handled, saying, “She complained of pain in her arm. They should have stopped and reassessed, and they didn’t.”

Fowler wants the people who place the IV lines to remain and monitor them as the drugs are administered, and favors an older three-drug cocktail involving potassium chloride over pentobarbital.

The attempt began to unravel after staff struggled to establish IV access, with Pike’s lawyers later alleging repeated needle attempts before the drugs were administered.

Fowler said he knew something was wrong when 45 minutes passed without word from the warden and he entered the chamber to find Pike still strapped to the gurney and gasping for air.

He recalled the warden telling him, “She’s not dead,” before another half-hour passed and he feared Pike could survive with catastrophic brain damage.



“She’s going to be in a permanent vegetative state with a quarter-million dollars in medical expenses,” Fowler recalled thinking.

Instead of pronouncing her dead, he diagnosed Pike as comatose, ordered oxygen and summoned an ambulance to Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

He later said the IV had been “delivering medicine to the subcutaneous tissue” of Pike’s arms rather than into her bloodstream, with Pike eventually waking six days later.

Pike returned to prison on October 10 and on Friday broke her silence for the first time, saying, “There hasn’t been a moment since that night when I haven’t been in pain,” and blaming what happened on “incompetence.”

Her lawyers are also preparing to expand her existing legal challenge after previously securing an order to preserve evidence from the failed execution for possible future claims.



New court papers filed this week and obtained by The U.S. Sun show Pike has until January 28, 2027, at 11.59 pm to file her first amended complaint, after the judge cited her medical condition and move to the infirmary at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fowler and the state could also face malpractice or negligence claims over what happened, according to Intelligencer, but the doctor says he is “not worried” and that his “conscience is clear.”

And despite the failed execution, legal threat and public backlash, Fowler says he will not be driven out, declaring, “I cannot be pushed off a course that I find correct. I refuse to compromise.”

News.title: Madeleine McCann suspect Christian Brueckner’s round-the-clock surveillance scrapped as paedo deemed ‘not high risk’
News.content:
Next

MADELEINE McCann suspect Christian Brueckner 24/7 surveillance has been scrapped after the rapist was deemed “not high risk”.

The paedophile – suspected of snatching and murdering the toddler – has been followed non-stop by German officers since his release from prison last September.



Now the watch – intended for public safety and to guard the rapist from vigilantes – is set to be scrapped according to a court ruling on Friday.

Brueckner will remain tracked by an electronic ankle monitor.



A new independent expert report found there was “only an increased abstract danger” by letting the paedophile be free of 24-hour surveillance.

Brueckner’s attorney Philipp Marquort said: “Two judicial instances have now reached the same conclusion: the legal requirements for round-the-clock surveillance are not met.

“Based on the new expert report, the Higher Regional Court has explicitly revised its earlier assessment. That deserves respect.”

The court heard on Friday that: “Anyone who has served their full sentence must be given the chance to rebuild a life in freedom.

“For 13 months, that was impossible, with police officers following every single step. Now, my client can begin that process.

Marquort, the lawyer for the convicted sex offender, said that “necessary legal grounds” no longer existed for the “form of surveillance” his client was subject to.



The rapist previously admitted that he had been within 150 yards of Madeleine McCann‘s holiday apartment on the night she vanished.

In a bombshell interview, Brueckner told the Mail on Sunday: “I was on the beach, not far from Maddie’s hotel, selling drugs.

“I’d been in Spain and smuggled the weed into Portugal.”



Brueckner denies any involvement in Maddie’s disappearance and has said he “f***ing hates” the toddler for wrecking his life.

In footage allegedly filmed secretly and posted online the rapist smirks as he gets into a car to evade the cops appointed to follow him 24 hours a day.

Brueckner is filmed saying: “She’s f***ing my life. The whole time. I can’t go out of the street. People think I killed Maddie. She’s f***ng my life.”

Speaking of the police tailing him he boasted: “They don’t know where I am. Because I left the house, jumped in your car, and we go.

“Otherwise they would follow me when I walk around or with a bicycle.”



The 24-hour surveillance has now been called off after a court ruled he was not deemed “high risk” enough for the round-the-clock monitoring.

Brueckner was named as a key suspect in the toddler’s disappearance back in June 2020 and Portuguese police formally accused him in 2022.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police had uncovered a vile stash of sex abuse images on a USB file – and linked him to the disappearances of a number of other young children.

But in 2024 the convicted child abuser was cleared of all charges relating to the Madeleine McCann case.

News.title: Biker dies after crashing motorcycle on coastal road & plunging into sea – as cops probe tragedy
News.content:
TRAGIC FALL Biker dies after crashing motorcycle on coastal road & plunging into sea – as cops probe tragedy







Next

A MOTORCYCLIST has died after crashing on a coastal road before plunging into the sea below.

The horror crash occurred on the headland’s scenic Marine Drive in North Wales, at around 10.30pm on Thursday night.

The incident prompted a major rescue operation to be launched in Great Orme with multiple emergency services scrambling to the scene.



But despite the best efforts of the emergency services, the man was tragically pronounced deceased, said cops.



His next of kin have been informed and the coroner has been notified, police added.

A police spokesperson said: “An investigation is underway following a fatal road traffic collision in Llandudno last night (Thursday, 29th October).

“We received a report at 10:31pm of a collision involving a black motorcycle on Marine Drive, approximately one mile from the Toll House towards the direction of the Great Orme summit.

“As a result of the collision, the male motorcyclist, entered the sea below the Great Orme. A multi-agency response involving ourselves, HM Coastguard and the RNLI was launched.

“The casualty was recovered from the water and airlifted by Coastguard helicopter to Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor.”

Sergeant Alun Jones is now appealing for witnesses to come forward.

He said: “Sadly, this is now being investigated as a fatal road traffic collision, and our thoughts are with the man’s family and friends at this very difficult time.



“We are urging anybody who may have witnessed the collision, or anybody who was travelling or walking along Marine Drive on the evening of Thursday, October 29, to contact us.

“We are particularly keen to hear from anyone who was travelling from the Toll House towards the Great Orme summit between 10:00pm and 10:30pm and who may have dashcam footage.

“Any information, no matter how insignificant it may seem, could assist with our investigation.”

Anyone with information is encouraged to get in touch via webchat on the force’s website, or by ringing 101, quoting reference number 26000888717.

News.title: Farmer's 'blazing row' with dad before strangling him and leaving body in shallow grave
News.content:
Farmer's 'blazing row' with dad before strangling him and leaving body in shallow grave

Charles Wright, 52, strangled Brian Wright, 82, and left his body in a shallow grave at Hall Farm near Newark in Nottinghamshire

View 3 Images Brian Wright was 82 when he was killed by his son (Image: Nottinghamshire Police / SWNS)

A man killed his father and buried him on the family farm before taking his own life following a "blazing row" over money, an inquest heard.

‌



‌



Charles Wight, 52, saw a "flash of red" when he felt his father, Brian, 82, was "cutting him out" of the family's business. He choked him to death to death placed his body in a shallow grave at Hall Farm near Newark in Nottinghamshire.

‌



Two days later, Charles took his own life. Nottingham Coroner's Court heard today that, in a voice message left by Charles for police, he said his father was "thinking of replacing him" and "giving the lion's share of the farm to another family member".

‌



In the note, which was sent on November 22, Charles said: "I just had a flash of red and after 25 years and everything I have given him, he was just cutting me out like that. I just saw red, dragged him out of the car and throttled him."

View 3 Images Police near the scene where Brian Wright was buried in Nottinghamshire (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

The inquest was told Brian had called Charles "useless" and "not capable of farming" and said it was a "mistake to let him farm that land" during the heated argument. Detective Chief Inspector Ruby Burrow, of Nottinghamshire Police, told the court of the voice message: "Charles stated that he had killed his father and intended to kill himself.

‌



"He described that his father Brian had criticised him and there had been a disagreement about finances. He stated he had buried his father Brian on the family farm."

Brian was reported missing to police shortly before midnight on November 20 as he had failed to take his wife to a hospital appointment. The next day, Charles, his brother James Wright and a colleague who worked on the family farm as a mechanic spoke to police officers.

‌



DCI Burrow told the inquest that Charles, who was interviewed the day before he took his own life, "was able to assist by describing difficult family dynamics and difficulties in relationships over the years, including issues around finances and also working arrangements on the farm". She continued: "We had a number of interactions with Charles.

"Charles provided similar contextual information about relationships within the family. He described an argument he had had with his father. He described his father had been critical towards him and he, himself, had taken some time to calm down."

‌



View 3 Images Police near the farm following the two deaths (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

Charles Wright told police his father had "left in the opposite direction after the small argument", the court heard. Later on November 21, Brian's vehicle was reported as appearing "out of place" where it had been left overnight, and his body was discovered buried on the farm four days later.

‌



His cause of death was found to be pressure applied to the neck, the inquest heard. Ms Burrow said there had been a report on November 22 of "a collision between a vehicle and two gentlemen", where the vehicle was driven at them "apparently deliberately".

She stated that Charles had driven his vehicle at his brother James, who was running alongside a friend, "causing injury". Charles Wright took his own life later that same day, with his body discovered in an outbuilding area on Hall Farm.

Article continues below

Senior coroner for Nottinghamshire Mairin Casey ruled that Brian Wright had been unlawfully killed, while his son's death was concluded to be suicide. Addressing the family members present in person and those joining via video-link, she said: "The horror of this, I'm clear in my mind, will have affected all of those who have survived in a very deep and painful way."

Samaritans can be contacted for free, day or night, 365 days a year, on 116 123, or visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch.

News.title: Armenian parliament erupts into brawl over 'Ministry of Sex' as fists fly and chair hurled
News.content:
Armenian parliament erupts into brawl over 'Ministry of Sex' as fists fly and chair hurled

Footage from Yerevan shows dozens of people brawling after a trade of insults over a proposal aimed at resolving what opposition MPs said was a problem with women turning to activism

Armenian MPs in Parliament Punch Up

A meeting over a proposed 'Ministry of Sex' during an Armenian Parliamentary session descended into the third all-out brawl on the premises in a matter of days - with fists flying and an MP hurling a chair.

‌



‌



Armenian lawmakers appeared at the National Assembly in its capital, Yerevan, on Thursday for a debate over the unusual proposals. Lawmakers with the pro-Russian Strong Armenia party had put forward the idea after bizarrely claiming that a lack of sexual satisfaction was leading middle-aged women into political activism.

‌



The ruling party, Civil Contract, immediately objected to the idea - which was meant to leave “no unsatisfied women” - and demanded a public apology, after which the chamber descended into a fight.

‌



Fists fly as huge brawl breaks out in Albanian parliament over student protests READ MORE :

View 4 Images The fight began after a verbal disagreement between Taron Chakhoyan and opposition leaders

The violence erupted after Civil Contract MP Taron Chakhoyan accused opposition members of being "steeped in corruption" and demanded an apology for proposing the ministry.

Chakhoyan said: "People steeped in corruption are talking about corruption, fake accounts, and targeting family members. Mr [Narek] Karapetyan, it is not my fault that your entire extended family is involved in politics, including your uncle, your father, and your cousin, who even tried to open a ministry in our country.

‌



"It is not my fault that he wanted to open a ministry that would satisfy all women. You have still not apologised to women for that."

View 4 Images Narek Karapetyan was also involved in the trade off

‌



A shouting match followed, with Strong Armenia member Narek Karapetyan allegedly calling Chakhoyan a "mess from head to toe". The rush towards the central podium, where Chakhoyan was speaking, broke out afterwards, with members seen punching and kicking each other.

Video taken of the fight shows assembly members rushing towards the chamber's centre and brawling with one another, with fists flying.

‌



At one point, Vahagn Aleksanya, the chamber's deputy speaker and a member of Civil Contract, picks up a red chair and chucks it at the group's periphery, but they keep fighting. Chakhoyan was seen at another point pouring a glass of water on a rival.

View 4 Images The brawl enveloped all of the Parliamentary chamber

‌



According to the Daily Telegraph, other MPs joined in the chaos by throwing bottles and breaking tables before the brawl was broken up.

Armenia's prime minister Nikol Pashinyan, said in a statement after the fight that, while he condemned the violence, he supported "the measures" taken by his faction. He said Strong Armenia, a younger party which formed earlier this year, being present in Parliament "does not mean that one should become insolent".

‌



He said: “I condemn violence, but I support the measures taken by the Civil Contract faction today, because [Strong Armenia] being in the opposition does not mean that one should become insolent."

View 4 Images The brawl at one point saw a chair thrown into the crowd

‌



“Whether with a chair or something else, it is proportionate and right.” Chakhoyan later apologised to the public for the behaviour of his opponents, saying it was "hooligan" before adding: "It won’t work to provoke a fight and escape from the National Assembly session hall without getting beaten."

The Ministry of Sex row comes following two previous brawls, both of which followed Civil Contract and Strong Armenia members trading insults.

Article continues below

And it was capped off with a tongue-in-cheek comment from the prime minister, who joked on Facebook after the incident about the opposition's physical - or lack thereof - strength. He joked that, despite being called "Strong Armenia" the party's MPs were not "physically strong".

News.title: Russell Myers: King Charles in danger of being remembered as monarch who didn't apologise
News.content:
As the King stood in reflection in Georgetown, on the very ground where enslaved Africans were executed after the Demerara uprising of 1823, it was impossible not to be encapsulated by the moment.

Even before Charles' arrival in The Bahamas earlier this week and Guyana today, this tour has been dominated by the issue of slavery and reparations.

I have no doubt that Charles' personal feeling over slavery is deeply felt and perhaps, given the freedom to do so rather than being restricted by the government, he would feel moved to issue an apology for Britain and the monarchy's historic role in slavery.

King Charles reflects at spot where slaves were publicly executed after uprising READ MORE :

King Charles' popularity sinks to lowest level of reign amid Harry and Meghan return READ MORE :

View 3 Images King Charles in Guyana today (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Indeed, within hours of landing in Nassau on Tuesday, he told a youth rally: "It is only right that we acknowledge the great suffering of the past in these islands and beyond". Yet, however heartfelt his words, they have not quietened the clamour that has followed him across the Caribbean.

At a Junkanoo parade in Nassau, one sign in the crowd read simply: "Pay us what you owe us." In Guyana, President Irfaan Ali has welcomed the King's past expressions of regret but made clear an apology must be the next step. And today came perhaps the most striking intervention of the tour so far.

Speaking to Sky News, Bahamian Prime Minister Philip Davis said he was open to losing the King as head of state, just days after giving him the warmest of welcomes.

View 3 Images Protestors hold up posters during the King's visit to Guyana (Image: Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

‌



The future of the monarchy, he said, was "a question for my people" and he would be "guided by the will" of Bahamians. Asked directly whether he was open to it, he replied: "I'm open to it, yes."

Mr Davis was careful. He described himself as "quite agnostic", noted that a referendum was not part of his mandate and acknowledged that many Bahamians did not want to "rid ourselves of part of our history".

But his message to Britain was unmistakable. To those who see no need for an apology, he said: "I think they have to appreciate the weight of that history and that ancestors like ourselves continue to bear."

Here lies the King's dilemma. He acts on the advice of his ministers, and the Government has ruled out both an apology and reparations, fearing a legal precedent that could open the floodgates for former colonies around the world.

‌



View 3 Images Charles during a visit to Umana Yana in Guyana (Image: Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

Mr Davis himself recognises that. He said the King "acts on the advice of his government", and conceded that financial reparations could be "challenging". Repair, he suggested, might instead mean acknowledgement, education and training, even pointing to the King's Trust scholarships as "a form of repair".

That is perhaps the most hopeful note for Charles. There is a path between apology and silence, and it is one he has walked for years.

He has also confirmed that Commonwealth leaders will discuss the legacy of slavery in Antigua next week, at a summit he will preside over.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Yet the ground is shifting beneath him. Barbados left in 2021. Jamaica is pushing towards becoming a republic and now the leader of a nation that welcomed him so warmly this week admits he is open to the King's departure.

None of this is of Charles's making. He has gone further than any monarch before him in confronting the past.

But history rarely judges kings on intentions alone. If Chogm ends with warm words and little else, the danger is that his reign in the Caribbean will be remembered not for the moments of reflection, but for the apology that never came.

‌

News.title: Laura Kuenssberg suggests male minister may have wanted a threesome with her
News.content:
Laura Kuenssberg suggests male minister may have wanted a threesome with her

BBC Presenter Laura Kuenssberg, whose book Pay Attention will be published next week, has suggested a male minister may have wanted a threesome with her and his partner

View 2 Images Laura Kuenssberg described meeting the minister in his hotel room (Image: BBC)

Laura Kuenssberg has suggested a male minister may have wanted a threesome with her and his partner.

‌



‌



The BBC presenter, whose book Pay Attention will be published next week, recounted a "very uncomfortable" encounter with an MP at a party conference.

‌



She described meeting the minister in his hotel room where she expected to find him and an adviser, only to find him sprawled on the bed with his shirt undone by several buttons. His partner was also there. Ms Kuenssberg said she swiftly finished her drink and left.

‌



Asked if she thought they were after a threesome, she told The Times: “Well, maybe they were and maybe they weren’t. As I say, maybe they weren’t and I got it completely wrong. It was very uncomfortable.”

Ms Kuenssberg - who was the BBC's first woman political editor - said she has concerns about people's behaviour in Westminster and worries about young people being "very vulnerable".

View 2 Images Laura Kuenssberg was the BBC's first woman political editor (Image: BBC)

‌



“People do things,” she continued. “And human behaviour is a complicated thing and sometimes people behave badly. And the concern … there is still a concern in Westminster that particularly young people starting out are sometimes very vulnerable.

In her book, the Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg presenter recalls several "weird" or "creepy" encounters with politicians. Describing a former minister who kissed her on the head every time he saw her, she said: “That was just weird. I never felt threatened. But it’s just a strange thing to do.” Her book also recounts someone who sent her a “really creepy text” complimenting her clothes on TV.

‌



“I’m not friends with politicians. There are lots of politicians who are perfectly nice people, but I don’t socialise with politicians,” she said.

Speaking about her decision to write a book, Ms Kuenssberg went on: “I suppose over a period of months thinking about whether or not I was going to write a book, having put it off for years and years and years, it sort of occurred to me that we were reaching a moment where I think I needed to come up for air and go, ‘OK, right. We had Brexit and the referendum. We’ve had social media emerging in incredible ways.

Article continues below

"You’ve had the phenomenon of Reform’s success exploding. You’ve had all of these different things that have been a big event for the country. And how can we sort of link them together? Are people really conscious of how we got to this place? And are people really conscious of the fact that politics is so different from what it was like when I started?’”

On her book, she added: “People will make of it what they will. I don’t know how people will react to it. I think for anybody writing a book for the first time, there’s a certain amount of trepidation.”

News.title: Son of Man Utd legend Nobby Stiles 'sickened' by theft from Munich Disaster Memorial
News.content:
Son of Man Utd legend Nobby Stiles 'sickened' by theft from Munich Disaster Memorial

John Stiles condemned thieves who stole from the memorial to the players who died in the disaster. German police are believed to be investigating the theft in Munich.

View 4 Images Detail shot of a wreath with the words "The Busby Babes" and "Rest in Peace" is seen after the commemoration for the 68th Anniversary of the Munich Air Disaster at the Manchesterplatz Memorial on February 06, 2026 (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

The son of Manchester United legend Nobby Stiles condemned the theft of valuable items from a memorial to the Munich Air Disaster today.

‌



‌



The items including medals were taken from a display case at Manchesterplatz in Munich, where the plane crashed on take-off on 6 February 1958 after refuelling on its return from a European Cup match in Belgrade.

‌



Munich Police told German media the glass was smashed with a stone and said the incident was believed to have happened between 08:00 and 13:00 local time on Monday, 26 October.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

Nobby Stiles was just 15 years old at the time of the disaster and an apprentice at United. But he spoke how deeply the tragedy had affected him. Eight Manchester Utd players were among the 23 who died.

Nobby's son John Giles, 62, of Doncaster, a former Leeds United player, said: "It is sickening to think that anyone could do that.

‌



"I am shocked and saddened that people could steal from a tribute which is such an emotional thing for so many. It is sad to find out that anyone could do such a thing."

Nobby Stiles died in 2020, aged 78, and a post mortem showed that he had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a brain condition caused by heading the ball.

‌



View 4 Images Flowers and wreaths are seen after the commemoration for the 68th Anniversary of the Munich Air Disaster at the Manchesterplatz Memorial on February 06, 2026 in Munich (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

The Manchester United Memorial Foundation said it was unclear exactly how many medals were missing "They don't understand the damage that they've caused," its chairman Ifty Ahmed said.

‌



He said the memorial had provided solace for families who lost loved ones in the crash. "And whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories," he said.

He urged those responsible to return the stolen items, saying they mean so much to Manchester United supporters and families of those killed in the Munich air disaster

‌



View 4 Images John Giles pictured with his dad in 2012 (Image: Mirrorpix)

Mark Salzmann, chairman of Red Docs Munich, a Bayern Munich supporters' group which helps care for the memorial, said his mother discovered the damage while driving past.

‌



Salzmann said a glass sculpture originally presented to Munich's former mayor, Dieter Reiter, was among the stolen items. About 1,500 people attended the annual remembrance service at Manchesterplatz in February, according to the memorial foundation

Ahmed said it was still unclear exactly how many medals were missing. He said Manchester United had offered to pay for repairs, but the foundation had already agreed to cover the costs itself.

‌



View 4 Images Flowers lie in front of a memorial stone commemorating the Munich air disaster. (Image: Bongarts/Getty Images)

The broken glass was replaced on the same day, according to the foundation. Ahmed said supporters of Liverpool, Manchester City and Leeds had also sent messages of support.

‌



Eight Manchester United players were among 23 passengers killed in the Munich air crash in 1958 A memorial stone was installed in 2004, while the display case was added in 2020 and officially inaugurated in 2023.

About 1,500 people from around the world attended the annual remembrance service at Manchesterplatz in February, according to the foundation.

Article continues below

Salzmann said the messages of support he had received showed how important the memorial was, adding that the connection between Manchester and Munich "will never go away".

News.title: Donald Trump has done 'fundamental' damage to US on the world stage, Alastair Campbell says
News.content:
Donald Trump has done 'fundamental' damage to US on the world stage, Alastair Campbell says

Alastair Campbell told The Mirror's new Youtube show Sense Check the US's reputation may never recover, even after erratic President Donald Trump is no longer in office

Donald Trump has done 'fundamental' damages to the US

Donald Trump has done "fundamental" damage to America's image on the world stage, Alastair Campbell has said.

‌



‌



The political commentator, best known for being Tony Blair's spin doctor, claimed the US's reputation may never recover, even after the erratic President is no longer in office.

‌



He told The Mirror's new YouTube show Sense Check: "I'm far from convinced that even if Trump goes, that America is ever going to go back in our minds to the place that it was. I think because that damage is fairly fundamental."

‌



The US-UK relationship has been under intense strain since former Prime Minister Keir Starmer refused to join Mr Trump's Iran war. Mr Trump repeatedly lashed out at him, accusing Mr Starmer of being "no Winston Churchill" over his reluctance to let the US launch attacks on Iran from British soil.

The US President also ridiculed UK aircraft carriers, calling them "toys", and lashed out at NATO for doing "absolutely nothing" to help the US in his conflict.

Andy Burnham pulled off a tricky first meeting with Mr Trump in September, though their differences were clear, including when the US President lashed out again at the “terrible deal” for the UK to hand over the sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius.

‌



View 2 Images Alastair Campbell spoke about the impact of Donald Trump when he appeared on the Mirror's new YouTube show Sense Check with host Nicola Thorp

Mr Trump, who faces tough midterm elections on Tuesday, has seen his popularity sink to record lows amid US citizens' worries over spiralling gas prices linked to his conflict with Iran.

‌



Mr Campbell told Sense Check's host Nicola Thorp the US would have to recognise the damage it's done to itself - and to the rest of the world - to recover its reputation.

Asked how America could build itself back up again in a post-Trump world, he said: " By recognising the damage that they're doing to themselves and the world. Now, some of them, probably a third of the people who are going to vote in the midterms, probably think that's just sort of arrogant European b******* from somebody who doesn't know America.

‌



"But I think they underestimate how much damage they have done to America and its reputation in the world, and I think by restoring the sense that standards in public life and trying to tell the truth and not seeing politics and public service as a place that's about grifting for yourself and your family and your friends.

"I've been genuinely shocked how that doesn't seem to matter as much as it does here in the States. Now you meet a lot of people in America who will say, I really, really care about it, but what can I do? The guy's got all the power at the moment. And that's why they're into the midterms to change things."

‌



View 2 Images Donald Trump faces tough midterm elections on Tuesday (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Mr Campbell, who hosts The Rest is Politics podcast with former Tory minister Rory Stewart, said it was a good thing that Nigel Farage and Reform UK is coming under scrutiny over their finances in the UK, suggesting that the US should ask more such questions of Mr Trump.

‌



He continued: "I think the reason why right now, whilst Trump has managed to become an even bigger multi-billionaire whilst serving as President, here, I think one of the reasons why [Nigel] Farage, Reform, are in trouble is because the public is saying, no you don't get £5million gifts. You don't do that. You don't get £72million off a couple of crypto guys and pretend that it's, you know, no strings attached.

"So I think we do have a hope, we have a deeper sense here of the importance of lack of corruption in public life. So I don't know what the Americans would do. I'm far from convinced that even if Trump goes, that America is ever going to go back in our minds to the place that it was. I think because that damage is fairly fundamental.

Article continues below

"And also it did to some extent on the foreign policy side of things, it kind of did start a little bit with Obama. Obama was, you know, and he's, look, they're not wrong to say that European, the Europeans should have done more to build up their own, our own defences. We should. But at the same time, I think there was a feeling that across America, that they, they see Europe now as kind of a bit of a tourist spot and nothing much else. And the other thing I've been shocked at is just the level of anti-Britain and anti-European propaganda that you get across the MAGA networks is mad."

News.title: Man accused of sexually abusing ex-Tory councillor's wife told cops he was 'trying out new things'
News.content:
Man accused of sexually abusing ex-Tory councillor's wife told cops he was 'trying out new things'

Connor Sanderson-Doyle is one of four men on trial for sexually abusing the wife of former Tory councillor Philip Young who had drugged and raped her

View 2 Images Mum-of-three Joanne Young has waived her right to anonymity (Image: Wiltshire Police/Press Association)

One of four men on trial for sexually abusing the wife of former Tory councillor Philip Young, who drugged and raped her, told police that he was "just a young guy trying out new things", a court has heard.

‌



‌



Young has pleaded guilty to multiple charges of drugging and sexually abusing his wife, Joanne Young, during a 13-year period, at their home in Swindon, Wiltshire.

‌



Four other men are on trial at Winchester Crown Court accused of sexually abusing her. Connor Sanderson-Doyle, 32, of Swindon, who is accused of sexual assault by penetration and sexual touching in June 2016, told a court today: "I thought I had her consent, I didn’t know she was drugged, I just thought I was doing a **** job."

‌



Sarah Jones KC, prosecuting, told the court that when Sanderson-Doyle was arrested at his home address on May 22, 2025, he told officers that he did not have sex with Mrs Young and added: "I remember this vividly, Jesus Christ."

The prosecutor said that the defendant told police that he had answered an advert on Craigslist, which had been posted by Young asking for people to have sex with his wife.

The jury was told that Sanderson-Doyle told police that he thought it was "just a married couple trying to live out whatever their kink is, I was just a young guy trying out new things".

‌



View 2 Images Philip Young pleaded guilty to multiple charges of abuse against his former wife (Image: CPS/Press Association)

He said that, when he arrived at the house, Young took him to their bedroom where he found Mrs Young "tied up and blindfolded" as she had been pictured in the online ad.

‌



He added: "I was a bit nervous by it all, I just started getting undressed and maybe I touched her body a bit."

He told the officer that he was wearing the balaclava from his motorcycle helmet because he did not want to be identified in the video recording that Young was making.

‌



The defendant went on to tell police that as he started to perform a sex act on Mrs Young he started to get a "vibe she wasn’t enjoying it or was not comfortable" so he stopped, got dressed and left.

He said there was "a clear line where I could tell she wasn’t comfortable. That's why I looked to him (Young) and he said 'Yeah, I don’t think she’s feeling it'".

‌



He added: "I just thought I was inexperienced and doing **** wrong and making her uncomfortable. I just thought I was young and maybe not reading the room right."

The defendant said that, at one point, he heard Mrs Young say "No" but he thought that she wanted him to do something different rather than stop completely.

‌



Sanderson-Doyle said that he had believed Mrs Young was consenting because "she just seemed relaxed, I couldn't see her eye or nothing like that, she was moving, she just seemed on the bed, bound, she seemed compos, she didn’t seem distressed at all".

When asked how consent can be confirmed, he said: "You can outright say it. 'Do you want to do this? Yes or no'. But then there's obviously levels of implied consent."

‌



He said that because of his communication with Young, he thought he had the joint consent of both of them and added: "This was a non-event to me, an encounter that didn’t pan out.

"It's upsetting this man has done this and involved me in it. I thought I had her consent, I thought I was joining a marital couple and doing what they wanted. I thought I was doing a bad job."

‌



The other defendants in the trial, who have been charged jointly with Young, are Norman Macksoni, 48, of Sharnbrook, Bedfordshire, who has denied one count of rape; Richard Wilkins, 62, of Toothill, Swindon, Wiltshire, who has pleaded not guilty to one count of rape and one of assault by penetration; and Mohammed Hassan, 38, of Swindon, who has pleaded not guilty to one count of sexual touching.

The jury was shown bodyworn video footage of the arrest of Wilkins, in which officers ask him to show his tattoos to see if they match those recorded in the video of the incident. Wilkins did not answer questions during police interview, Ms Jones said.

‌



In Macksoni's police interview, read to court, he said that he had got in contact with Young through the "Fab swingers" site.

The defendant said: "He said we want to do this, him and his wife, this is one of their fantasies.

‌



"So they tell me where they are, I get over there, he lets me in, he says, ‘She’s upstairs on the bed ready’.

"I go upstairs, then he sits on the bed next to her, he starts having a conversation with her and he’s saying, 'He's here, he's ready for you’.

‌



"She's got her face mask on, she doesn’t want to see who she’s sleeping with. So then we started having sex.

"I didn't know he was recording if I'm honest, and he’s talking to her, you know, ‘Are you enjoying it?’ and she’s, her legs move, are wrapped round me and then I finish, I get up and I leave. But there was no way that she was drunk or whatever (or) wasn’t coherent.="

‌



Macksoni, who said he MCed at music events, said that the sex had been consensual and added: "It was just a sex meet with a couple and I left.

"It wouldn’t be sleeping with someone who wasn’t coherent, I wouldn’t do that, that’s not what Fab swingers is about."

Article continues below

Young, 50, has pleaded guilty to a total of 56 charges, and a sixth defendant, Dean Hamilton, 47, of Street, Somerset, has admitted one charge of assault by penetration, two of sexual assault and one of rape.

They will be sentenced at the conclusion of the trial. The trial continues.

News.title: Zara Tindall plunged into Ellie Goulding diamond row after flogging 'toxic' gems
News.content:
Zara Tindall plunged into Ellie Goulding diamond row after flogging 'toxic' gems

Exclusive: Zara Tindall's jewellery range with Calleija features diamonds from Australia’s Argyle mine, where traditional owners say “forever chemicals” have destroyed the land

View 4 Images Zara Tindall talks to guests during a Royal Garden Party at Buckingham Palace wearing Argyle diamonds (Image: PA)

Zara Tindall has been selling the same pink diamonds from a pollution-hit mine at the centre of the Ellie Goulding row for tens of thousands of pounds, the Mirror can reveal.

‌



‌



The King’s niece, who has publicly backed ocean conservation, has her own jewellery range with Calleija which feature the stones from Australia’s Argyle mine, where traditional owners say “forever chemicals” have destroyed the land.

‌



She even attended a Buckingham palace garden party wearing the diamonds, in May 2025.

‌



Last week singer Goulding, who is a WWF ambassador, said she was left “mortified” after wearing a half a million pound necklace and earring set from Boodles containing the gems.

Calleija’s website lists at least four designs under Zara’s name containing Argyle pink diamonds, including rings, a pendant and earrings.

Its platinum Suprema Saddle ring contains 27 Argyle pink diamonds and is said to reflect Zara’s love of equestrian eventing. It costs £21,600. The Sunrise ring, made from 18ct white and yellow gold, contains an Argyle pink diamond surrounded by 20 white diamonds. Its description celebrates the stone’s “rare beauty”. A matching Sunrise pendant and Sunrise stud earrings also contain the same gems.

‌



A Calleija social media post says of her Buckingham Palace outing: “Zara Tindall attended the garden party at Buckingham Palace on Tuesday afternoon, wearing our gorgeous Sidra earrings featuring rare Australian Argyle Pink Diamonds.”

View 4 Images Zara Tindall by Calleija 18ct Yellow Gold ‘Sunrise’ Australian Argyle Pink™ and White Diamond Stud Earrings

‌



We revealed last week how environmental concerns over the mine are laid bare in a damning 2025 report from Gelganyem, the organisation representing traditional owners' interests. It said: "Land use will be permanently restricted due to soil, groundwater and surface water contamination from PFAS [known as forever chemicals] and hydrocarbons." Other findings identify serious erosion, fish needing chemical testing, as well as damage to indigenous sites including burial grounds and a ceremonial cave containing rock art.

Zara’s promotion of the pink diamonds appears at odds with her environmental credentials. She is a supporter of Tusk, the African conservation charity whose royal patron is her cousin Prince William, with her and husband Mike Tindall attending their awards at London’s Savoy hotel on November 26 last year. In his speech that evening, William praised “the indigenous communities and local conservation leaders who provide the practical solutions to how we can best sustain our precious natural landscapes”. She also attended the event in 2022.

‌



Her and husband Mike also launched a fundraising cycle ride for the conservation charity Blue Marine Foundation. The couple joined the opening stage of its third London-to-Monaco ride in September 2018, cycling from Herne Hill Velodrome in south London to Dover.

Zara said: “Our oceans are constantly under threat and it's for that reason that we are joining 100 brave cyclists in raising awareness around vital marine conservation projects like Blue's so that they can receive the funding and support they need.” Mike added: “Both myself and Zara believe its really important to help protect the oceans for our children and future generations to enjoy.”

‌



View 4 Images The Argyle diamond mine in the East Kimberley, Western Australia (Image: Fairfax Media via Getty Images)

Gelganyem, the organisation representing traditional owners' interests, said it was “hard to reconcile” the sale of the diamonds at such high prices when “funds to rehabilitate the Country to a high standard after mining are often lacking.”

‌



They said in a statement: “This is not about targeting individuals. It is about asking brands, suppliers and public figures who promote these products to support transparency - and ensuring that the people most connected to the land are heard.”

They added: “The questions raised by the promotion of Argyle diamonds are bigger than any one person or piece of jewellery. They are about whether the story of a product includes the people whose Country was mined, what happened after mining ended, and how we know commitments to rehabilitation are being met.”

‌



Thanking the Mirror for drawing attention to the issue, they added: “Traditional Owners welcome the fact that these stories are able to shine a light on the work that the Gelganyem Group is doing to ensure that the Argyle mine is closed responsibly and in a way that meets reasonable environmental expectations.”

The Argyle mine, in Western Australia’s East Kimberley region, stopped production in November 2020 after supplying around 90 per cent of the world’s pink diamonds. Mining giant Rio Tinto has been carrying out rehabilitation ahead of the eventual return of the land to its owners.

‌



Last week singer Goulding told the Mirror of her regret at wearing the diamonds. She said: "Protecting the environment is a cause close to my heart. I always strive to uphold those values. Regretfully, in this instance, I fell short. I was not aware of the concerns surrounding the Argyle mine and I am grateful that it has been brought to my attention.

View 4 Images Ellie Goulding wearing Argyle pink diamonds (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images for Boodles)

‌



"You will certainly not see me wearing diamonds originating from the Argyle mine again. The indigenous and local communities affected deserve better. While I am mortified to have made this error in judgement, I am letting this moment serve as a reminder and an opportunity to continue to question the status quo, learn and do better."

Calleija owner John Calleija said in a statement: “Calleija are a bespoke, luxury jeweller. Since opening our first boutique more than 40 years ago, we have always been fastidious about where our natural diamonds, gems and precious metals are sourced, hence our support of Positive Luxury and the Butterfly Mark for many years. We pride ourselves on working with ethically sourced materials, hand selecting the finest gems and the most beautiful, natural diamonds. Calleija has worked with Argyle Pink Diamonds for many years and our experience has been that careful custody of these beautiful diamonds, from the mine to the retailer, is treated seriously. Calleija is aware that Rio Tinto was a founding member of the Responsible Jewellery Council, which focuses on responsible sourcing and ethical practices throughout the jewellery supply chain, with the mine certified by the Council during the time it was operating. As we are not involved in the mine operations we would refer you to Rio Tinto's public reporting and governance regarding their rehabilitation of the Argyle mine, which is described in detail on their website and in Annual Reports. “

‌



Rio Tinto previously said in a statement: "Mining at Argyle ended in 2020, and we are undertaking major works including rehabilitation, with longterm monitoring and maintenance to follow. We acknowledge traditional owners as custodians. We are continuing to talk to them and their representatives, the Gelganyem Group, about closure, including PFAS. PFAS containing firefighting foams were historically widely used worldwide, including at Argyle. We continue to assess and manage environmental impacts associated with this historical use. Our priority is to deliver a safe, stable and culturally respectful closure while ensuring environmental outcomes are managed. Our focus is on meeting commitments we have made, being transparent about progress and working through concerns with traditional owners."

Boodles sources previously said they had “nothing to do with the mining or mine itself" when it came to Goulding.

Article continues below

Zara's agent didn't respond to requests for comment.

News.content:
Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, has been hit by a $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) hack - thought to be the biggest in history.

Half of the assets have been frozen but many remain in the hands of the hackers, the cryptocurrency giant said. It later added that it has "begun recovering" some funds.

Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit, though no one has claimed responsibility. Binance did not directly respond to questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea.
