News.title: Driver guilty of hitting cyclist and dragging him to death under car
News.content:
Warning: This article contains distressing content

A man has been found guilty of murdering a head teacher who was dragged to his death for more than a mile while trapped under the wheels of a car.

Simon Richardson crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins, who was cycling home from his job at Stretford Grammar School on the evening of 20 April in the village of Warburton in Trafford, Greater Manchester.

Prosecutors claimed Richardson, 35, fled the scene of the crash before stopping to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist and then driving on with Mr Mullins still lodged underneath the vehicle.

Richardson was also convicted of dangerous driving and will return to Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court to be sentenced on Monday.

There were shouts of "Yes!" from the court's public gallery as the guilty murder verdict was announced.

Others could also be heard crying.

The judge, Mrs Justice Brunner KC, told Richardson that there was only one sentence for murder, namely life imprisonment.

News.title: Police Scotland carrying out 'active inquiries' into Andrew and Epstein Balmoral visits
News.content:
Police Scotland is making inquiries into the activities of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislane Maxwell during their time at Balmoral Castle.

The Daily Express reported, external that the inquiry relates to allegations that women were trafficked to the royal residence in Aberdeenshire.

Sex offender Epstein - who died in 2019 - and Maxwell, who was jailed in 2022 for sex trafficking, are understood to have visited the castle with Mountbatten-Windsor, who has previously denied any wrongdoing.

Police Scotland said inquiries were at "a very early stage" and that it would be inappropriate to comment further.

Representatives of Mountbatten-Windsor have been contacted for comment.

News.title: Russell Brand accusers 'haunted' for years by alleged crimes, court hears
News.content:
Some of the women in Russell Brand's rape and sexual assault case have been "haunted" for years by what they allege he did to them, jurors have been told.

In her closing speech at London's Southwark Crown Court on Friday, prosecutor Reil Karmy-Jones KC said the women had "nothing to gain" from coming forward apart from "some closure".

Speaking for the defence, Polly Dyer told jurors Brand had pleaded guilty and been fined over possession of cannabis in 1995, but had no other "convictions, cautions, reprimands or warnings".

Brand, 51, is on trial facing seven charges; three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of attempted indecent assault. He denies the charges.

Karmy-Jones KC told the court that this case brings together six different women, none of whom knows each other.

She said that while all the alleged victims have since moved on with their lives, due to this trial they have been forced to "relive what has happened to them".

None of the women involved has "sought the limelight" or "any kind of publicity", she said, adding there was "no benefit to them from perhaps some closure."

Referring to Brand's accusers' evidence the prosecutor said "how many said he was nice and then there was a like a personality changeâ¦

"His eyes changed, he snapped, from charming to frightening to nasty," Karmy-Jones KC said.

She added that the complainant's evidence had been that "he didn't listen when I said no, he didn't stop, he didn't care, pulling pushingâ¦ thrusting".

"In the rape cases, he kept on going until he achieved his ultimate aim."

The prosecutor also dismissed the idea that a documentary had caused the women to "re-invent" what actually happened.

"There is no magic force in this documentary", she added.

"What in fact happened was these women have realised they are not alone and have bravely come before you to tell the truth."

She added: "Truth they have lived with, which in some cases has haunted them for years."

She told the jury: "The experience of people raped may be something that looms a little bit larger in your mind rather than the intricacies of the outfit.

"The defendant couldn't really remember anything when he was interviewed, in stark contrast to now when he suddenly seems to remember all sorts of details about the week."

News.title: Police watchdog to investigate Met over letter about Meghan's father
News.content:
The UK police watchdog is to investigate the Metropolitan Police's handling of a letter containing allegations against Thomas Markle that was handed to his daughter, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it had decided an investigation was required into the force's "failure to pass on allegations of serious offending... to relevant overseas authorities at the time".

The letter, written by Markle's first wife Roslyn Loveless, is believed to have contained claims about Meghan's father.

He has strongly denied recent allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse, describing them as "sick lies".

On Thursday the Met said it had voluntarily referred itself to the IOPC.

The letter at the heart of the IOPC investigation was sent to the Met's royal protection team by Loveless, who divorced Thomas Markle in 1975 and died in 2024.

The handwritten letter was then passed to Meghan in January 2019, with the duchess saying last week that it had "made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father".

Meghan did not provide any details but said it had given her sufficient reason to not visit Thomas Markle and not allow him to meet his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet.

Scotland Yard said the letter contained claims about offending outside the UK and that it had been forwarded to "the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness".

The IOPC will consider why the Met did not share the contents of the letter with other law enforcement agencies, in the UK or overseas.

The policing watchdog also said it had decided a further matter, relating to an alleged data breach in which information was passed on to a third party, "should be returned to the force to be appropriately dealt with". No details were provided about the circumstances of the alleged breach.

The Met said on Thursday that it intended to make further referrals to "relevant overseas law enforcement agencies", a process which it expected to be completed "in the coming days".

The letter was forwarded by officers to the Sussexes' royal office rather than to Meghan personally, while there have been reports that the Met did not keep a copy of the letter and had to ask for one from the Sussexes.

The watchdog will have to consider how the contents of the letter were treated by the force at the time.

Noel Rasmussen, Thomas Markle's granddaughter and niece of the Duchess of Sussex, previously told the BBC she was "deeply troubled by the questions surrounding the Metropolitan Police's handling of the information it received".

"If allegations of this seriousness were brought to the attention of authorities, it is reasonable to ask what steps were taken [and] why the information was not shared with other law enforcement agencies."

Reports of the Met's handling of the letter emerged as Thomas Markle's son had told the police in the Philippines about material which was alleged to contain sexual images of children, which he had claimed to have found in possessions belonging to Meghan's father.

Thomas Markle had been in the Philippines in December 2025, undergoing hospital treatment, when Meghan wrote to him to end all contact.

Authorities in the Philippines have begun investigating the claims. Police there have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from Markle's former home.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week.

However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they can examine the items.

Thomas Markle Sr has strongly denied all the allegations against him. He has been backed by his daughter Samantha, who has dismissed the claims against her father as "fake".

News.title: Democrats in the US have an identity crisis - it won't be an easy fix
News.content:
James Stevens calls himself a democratic socialist. The 24-year-old film student is the type of Democrat who recalls watching the provocative left-wing internet commentator Hasan Piker six years ago, "before he became relevant in politics". Last year, James flew up from his home in Georgia to New York City to canvass for Zohran Mamdani's mayoral campaign.

His mother, Tamara, 56, is a loyal Democrat too. But of a different ilk. She grew up Republican then switched to the Democratic Party after seeing Barack Obama on Oprah. These days, she's a loyal party woman, championing reproductive rights, attending campaign rallies and donating to local candidates.

Both mother and son want Democrats to win control of Congress at Tuesday's midterm elections, but they don't entirely agree on what they want their Democratic Party to be.

"I'm very sick of how compromising Democrats are to Republican policies that don't benefit a large group of people," James told me, as his mother looked on. "There needs to be a bold vision for the Democrats," he says, arguing that the party should adopt policies affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), a left-wing splinter group. In his view, that means anti-Zionism, getting corporate money out of politics, and government-run free healthcare.

The conventional wisdom in Washington is that Democrats are well-positioned to take control of the House, and possibly even the Senate, after the vote next week.

Underlying conditions are in Democrats' favour â Republican US President Donald Trump's approval rating is at a record low for a president heading into a midterm, comparable to George W Bush in his final term in 2006; the Iran war still isn't over and it's proving unpopular with American voters; and this has led to higher gas prices, which are frustrating an electorate that is already worried about the cost of living. Traditionally, the midterms are a referendum on a sitting president. In 18 of the last 20 US midterm elections, the party in power has lost seats in the House.

News.title: Set up to fail? Where England's World Cup campaign went wrong
News.content:
The northern hemisphere game has deep-rooted problems, and seems to be stuck in stasis when compared with the thriving NRL.

England had a record of being a major player at World Cups - having reached two finals and a further four semi-finals at the past six tournaments.

But when last autumn's 3-0 Ashes series defeat by Australia prompted the departure of head coach Shaun Wane, his successor was handed a near-impossible task.

Brian McDermott was appointed in April. Given just six months to prepare, the former Leeds Rhinos head coach had no mid-season international to work on a plan. Based in Australia because of his role as Gold Coast Titans assistant coach, he relied on virtual meetings to connect with his prospective squad and staff.

Four on-field sessions were planned in Australia before the World Cup. But only two were completed in full after his UK-based players were subjected to a 48-hour journey to Perth that left them exhausted - a situation McDermott compared to Planes, Trains and Automobiles, the 1987 road-trip comedy starring Steve Martin and John Candy.

It was a shambolic way to prepare for a pivotal opener against Tonga - one that always had the potential to consign the defeated team to an early elimination.

Following that 30-12 loss, McDermott said: "You give me another two or three weeks preparation or another couple of games of preparation leading into the tournament and I'd be really excited."

With the tournament organisers planning travel itineraries for the teams involved, any post-World Cup debrief ought to examine how that situation was allowed to occur.

It would have made more sense for England's opener to be against France - the only other team in the men's tournament made up largely of northern hemisphere-based players.

Wakefield Trinity's historic triumph may have delivered a wonderful sign-off story to the Super League season but it delivered another conundrum around England's squad selection.

Had McDermott known prior to 5 October that none of the Wakefield players in his thinking would be available, could arrangements have been made for his UK-based players to travel to Australia earlier?

In the end, only three of the 14 England-based players in the squad (George Williams, Matty Ashton and Ben Currie) participated in the Super League Grand Final on 3 October.

"If we come together next year as a group, we will be further down the track and we don't need to start from scratch," McDermott added.

"Bear in mind when we landed in Perth on the Friday [9 October], we are starting... like we didn't know each other.

"We were putting things in place about who we are as a group, what it means to us, how we are going to play, how we are going to attack and how we are going to defend. There's been a ton of work gone on."

News.title: How a passenger's confession helped convict her cousin of murder
News.content:
Warning: This article contains distressing content

One afternoon in April, a children's nursery worker approached her manager in what she described as an hysterical state.

Gabrielle Debotte said she had something serious to tell Nicola Goddard, adding: "You're going to hate me and I'm going to lose my job."

What the 27-year-old said next proved a turning point in the investigation into the death of popular head teacher Michael Mullins, who had been struck by a car the previous day and dragged under its wheels for more than a mile.

Debotte told the astonished Goddard she not only knew who was responsible for hitting the 56-year-old as he cycled home from work, but she witnessed what happened from the passenger seat.

That night, having initially been treated as a suspect, she sat in the interview suite at Stretford Police Station and named her cousin, 35-year-old former mechanic Simon Richardson, as the driver.

Thanks in part to the evidence provided by Debotte, Richardson was found guilty of murder after a two-week trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court.

News.title: Sir Ian McKellen leads tributes to 'beloved actor' Sir Patrick Stewart after his death at 86
News.content:
Comedian Ricky Gervais, whose BBC programme Extras Sir Patrick guest starred in, described him as a "legend".

Sharing a video of the pair giggling in a set of bloopers for the series, Gervais said: "I still can't believe he agreed to do this scene. And he didn't even mind when I ruined every take."

Sir Patrick was a lifelong supporter of English Football League club Huddersfield Town, which called him a "titan of his craft".

"Fiercely proud of his Yorkshire roots, Sir Patrick was a Terrier in every sense, and we're proud to have counted him as one of our own," the club added.

Alzheimer's is the most common type of dementia, while Lewy Body Dementia is another common form caused by abnormal protein deposits, which cause a loss of cognitive function.

The Alzheimer's Society CEO Michelle Dyson said Sir Patrick was an "extraordinarily talented and much-loved actor, admired by millions around the world", adding: "His death is a heartbreaking reminder of the devastating impact dementia has on people and families across the globe."

The actor became a campaigner on domestic violence in later life, including becoming an ambassador for domestic abuse charity Refuge in 2007, after witnessing his mother suffer violence at the hands of his father.

Hetti Barkworth-Nanton, Refuge's board chair, said it had been a privilege to "watch his endless devotion" to the cause, adding that he "broke down barriers and taboos on the subject".

Andy Burnham considered Sir Patrick to be "one of the very best" who "never forgot his working-class Yorkshire roots".

"He brought joy to millions," the prime minister's spokesman said on his behalf. "He always stood up for what he believed in, including through his campaigning to help those affected by domestic violence.

News.title: Stabbed boy felt Huntingdon train attacker 'was not sane', court hears
News.content:
A 14-year-old boy stabbed by a man who went on to attack people on a train said he did not feel the knifeman was "mentally sane", a court heard.

The teenager was attacked in Peterborough the day before Anthony Williams is accused of trying to kill 10 people on a train that had to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon in November 2025.

In a video recorded interview played to jurors at Cambridge Crown Court, the boy said: "This random guyâ¦ he just pulled out a knife and stabbed me."

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, denies 14 counts of attempted murder - four of which concern attacks prior to the mass train stabbing.

At the time of the attack, the boy, who cannot be named because of his age, was waiting with a friend on a footbridge over the River Nene, before going trick or treating.

Williams drew a knife from his waistband, he said, and "because I was closest to him, he's just stabbed me".

"I didn't feel like he was mentally sane. His eyes were wide open, like he was on something," he said.

"My friend said he was shouting something like 'are you involved?'."

"When he stabbed me, it's like he was there for a knife fight. Like he was waiting for me to pull out something."

The teenager said he had "so much adrenaline" that it felt "like a poke in the chest".

The jury heard the pair ran away and hid in some bushes, where they called the police.

News.title: 'No nation left behind' says Burnham after meeting first ministers in Glasgow
News.content:
Ministers and representatives at the summit discussed handing regions more powers to control employment support and funding for reindustrialisation.

"It's about creating those structures at a regional level and that is matter for Scotland and Wales to decide what that looks like in both countries," Burnham said.

He urged the Scottish and Welsh governments to "work jointly" with the UK government on "a model of deeper devolution".

In the context of reindustrialisation, Burnham added this could be more devolution of innovation funding.

Swinney, ap Iorwerth and Burnham also agreed during the meeting there are too many young people out of work in the nations.

The prime minister said the UK government would look at "arrangements for further devolution of employment support for young people in both Scotland and Wales".

Devolution has been at the heart of Burnham's policy agenda since he took his place in Downing Street this summer.

He claims "rewiring the state" and handing more control to regional mayors and authorities across England will boost economic growth.

The prime minister's devolution at the national level has so far been less clear but Burnham has said he will listen to the administrations' calls for further powers while advocating that they share more responsibilities with local authorities.

News.title: Wettest week for two years but still not enough rain to get out of drought
News.content:
The recent stormy weather brought England's wettest week in two years, according to the Environment Agency.

However, despite the rain, Wales and most of England are still in drought with parts of southern England in severe drought.

Met Office provisional statistics for October show that the UK received above average rainfall.

However, the National Drought Group have said it will take sustained and above average rainfall over a seven month period for conditions to improve to normal.

Over the last week we had the first two named storms of the season - Austen and Boelo - which gave much of the UK significant and much needed rain.

Rainfall totals ranged from 38mm in central England to 87mm in the south-west and according to Enviroment Agency (EA) monitoring, it was the wettest week across England since October 2024.

In some parts of southern England there was nearly 50% more rainfall than normal throughout the month.

As a whole, England has had 111% of its long-term monthly rainfall, according to the EA.

News.title: Ministers vow online safety action after teen sextortion victim took own life
News.content:
The UK government has said it remains committed to making the online world as safe as possible for young people following the death of a teenager who took his own life after he fell victim to an online sextortion scam.

Cai Davies, 18, died in June 2025 after he had sent messages to a woman he believed had a romantic interest in him.

South Wales Central Coroner's Court heard he had been targeted by scammers operating from Africa, who demanded money from him and said intimate photos would be sent to his friends and posted on YouTube.

The coroner addressed a Regulation 28 preventing future deaths report, external to the UK and Welsh government with her concerns about how Cai had fallen victim to the scam.

Assistant coroner Rachel Knight recorded a conclusion of suicide after Davies, from Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, died.

Knight said it was "more likely than not" that personal stresses in his life together with falling victim to the sextortion scam "more than minimally contributed" to his death.

She wrote of the scammers: "Conversation quickly turned sexual and she asked him for intimate images, which were then used to blackmail him for money by threatening to send the images to his family and friends, and to upload them to a YouTube channel.

"The images were indeed sent to at least one of Cai's Facebook friends by the scammer.

"Cai was bombarded with video calls and messages via Facebook Messenger and WhatsApp over a very short period of time making demands for money."

News.title: County Down man among three jailed for planning mosque attack
News.content:
A County Down man is among three men who have been jailed for attempting to engage in a terrorist activity, specifically damaging a mosque in Galway.

Garrett Pollock (36) of Kilhorne Greene in Annalong was sentenced to 10 and a half years with the last year suspended.

Darren Gorman (34) of O'Moore Place in Portlaoise was sentenced to eight years with the last year suspended and Karolis Peckauskas (39) of Newfoundwell Road in Drogheda was sentenced to eight years in prison with the last year suspended.

They had made advanced plans to blow up the Maryam Mosque on the Monivea Road between 4 and 5 November 2025 when they were arrested, the Special Criminal Court in Dublin heard.

Pollock also pleaded guilty to possessing an explosive substance which was found in four glass jars hidden in a drawer in his van on 4 November.

On Friday, Ms Justice Caroline Biggs said that modern Ireland is a multicultural and diverse country and that the actions of this group bring shame on the country.

It was, Biggs said, attempted arson with a terrorising message to be spread worldwide.

She added that it was clear that this was intended to be the first of many attacks.

News.title: Burnham's Number 10 North goes on multi-million pound hiring spree
News.content:
Andy Burnham's Number 10 North has gone on a multi-million pound hiring spree with dozens of new jobs being advertised.

The office in Manchester, set up by the prime minister in July, has launched 50 external job adverts, including a "rewiring the state deputy director".

It is the latest sign of how pivotal the government outpost - designed as a sister office to London's Downing Street - may prove to Burnham's aim to devolve power across the country.

Government sources say the roles will be paid for out of existing budgets.

The new recruits "will work with mayors and councils to identify barriers holding places back", but the Conservatives have described the office as a "gimmick".

There will be no redundancies elsewehere in the civil service as a result of the hiring spree, the BBC has been told, with some jobs expected to be relocated and other vacant roles closed.

The new roles, all based in Manchester, cover areas including strategy, communications, engagement, private office and policy.

BBC News has calculated they total up to Â£2.8m for basic salaries alone, excluding employer pension contributions in the civil service of 28.97%.

No10 North now has 120 members of staff, nearly half of the 280 staff who work in No10 London.

Among the highest paid of the roles are a "rewiring the state deputy director", with a salary band of Â£86,000 to Â£117,000, who will "lead the Rewiring the State Unit... shaping the government's approach to devolution across departments".

The government said it was launching a recruitment campaign for staff who would "bring fresh perspectives and knowledge of the places they serve, moving decisions closer to the people they affect".

No10 North "is driving the most significant transfer of power out of Westminster in a generation," the government added in a statement.

News.title: Men jailed for 'abhorrent' operation trafficking women from Europe into UK for sex work
News.content:
The "architect and organiser" of a group that trafficked Romanian women into the UK to become sex workers has been sentenced to eight years and two months in prison.

George Filip, 45, led an organised crime group responsible for the "prostitution" of at least 16 victims, earning hundreds of thousands of pounds, Cardiff Crown Court heard.

He was assisted by his wife Ionela Filip, 35, to bring the women to work as prostitutes in locations across Wales, England and Scotland. Alexandru Moco, 27 and Leonard Banica, 41, were also involved in the conspiracy.

Judge Francis said it was a "substantial and sophisticated criminal enterprise that operated over seven years".

The court heard that between June 2015 and October 2022, at least 16 identifiable victims had been brought to the UK from Romania and France to work in the sex industry.

Matthew Cobbe, prosecuting, said the operation was of a "significant scale" with women working in "Cwmbran, Hereford, a location near Alton Towers, Stoke-on-Trent, Aberdeen and Inverness".

Francis was told the women had not been brought under duress but George, of no fixed abode, had "plainly exploited the circumstances of these victims". Although there was "no suggestion of sexual violence" there were "very many customers", Cobbe said.

Francis said that some of the women, while coming to the UK to work in the sex industry had been "pressured to commit sexual acts they had not agreed to which had caused them considerable distress".

News.title: Colonial Massachusetts town’s ‘doomsday’ sewage problem might make it uninhabitable
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A picturesque Massachusetts town is facing a sewage crisis residents have dubbed a “doomsday scenario,” with experts warning that contaminated drinking water could eventually make its historic village center uninhabitable.

Carlisle, located about 20 miles northwest of Boston, has no public water supply or municipal sewer system. Instead, residents rely on private wells and backyard septic systems, many of which are aging. The problem is particularly concerning in the historic village center, where homes and businesses sit close together on small lots, some about the size of three basketball courts.

Conventional septic systems filter wastewater through surrounding soil, but limited space and the town's fractured bedrock can make it easier for contaminated wastewater to reach nearby drinking wells.

The contamination has already raised concerns across the community. Wells at Ferns Country Store, a general store that served Carlisle for more than 180 years, and Town Hall tested positive for E. coli in 2021 and 2023. The bacteria was also detected in the local public school's well last fall, while nitrate levels at the public library exceeded drinking water standards in 2016, according to an investigation by The Boston Globe.

Susan Murcott, a wastewater expert and lecturer at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, warned that if the situation remains unaddressed, it could become "deadly" in the coming decades. When asked by the Globe whether she meant the crisis could threaten property values, Murcott clarified that the danger was "to human beings."

open image in gallery The sewage crisis in Carlisle, Massachusetts, resurfaced when a couple seeking to reopen the shuttered Ferns general store (pictured) discovered its property could not safely accommodate a traditional septic system without risking contamination of nearby wells ( Google Maps )

The issue has gained renewed attention after Ben and Amy Pirri, a couple who moved to Carlisle during the COVID-19 pandemic, attempted to purchase and reopen Ferns, which closed in 2025.

The couple initially expected to reopen the business without major complications.

"We'll just turn it back on," Ben Pirri recalled thinking, he told the Globe.

Instead, they discovered the property could not accommodate a conventional septic system without potentially contaminating nearby wells. Ferns relied on a composting toilet because there was insufficient space to safely dispose of wastewater through a traditional septic system.

The Pirris initially set out to reopen Ferns as a cafe and community gathering place, but eventually expanded their efforts into a proposal to address the village's broader wastewater problems. The store remains closed for now.

They suggested connecting the property to an existing, town-owned wastewater treatment plant serving the public school, which would require approximately 2,100 feet of piping. Town administrator Ryan McLane initially called the idea a "moonshot," but subsequent investigation found the school's treatment plant had unused capacity that could potentially accommodate additional wastewater, according to the outlet.

McLane declined The Independent's request for comment.

The proposal has faced resistance from officials and residents concerned about the cost of new infrastructure and its potential impact on Carlisle's historic character. Some fear a municipal sewer system could encourage development and undermine the town's rural appeal.

During a May 27 Board of Health meeting, board chair Patrick Collins dismissed the possibility of constructing a municipal wastewater system, calling it "such a pipe dream."

Pirri pushed back, asking: "Is Carlisle town center not somewhat in crisis? Do we not need a better solution for wastewater in town? You don't think so?"

The controversy intensified after Pirri questioned an unexplained increase in wastewater passing through the school's treatment plant between November 2025 and March 2026. Records showed approximately 750,000 gallons of excess wastewater effluent passed through the facility during that period, according to the Globe.

Pirri suggested illegal dumping could have contributed to the increase. However, town officials and the private company operating the facility said they could not determine the cause and denied that illegal dumping had occurred.

After the Select Board declined to fund an engineering study examining the proposed connection, the Pirris offered to personally cover its $55,700 cost. Their efforts have since gained support from residents, with the local library committee also expressing interest in connecting to the school facility.

The Select Board has agreed to hold a townwide vote on November 16 to determine whether public money should be spent developing engineering and design plans for sewer pipes connecting the village center to the existing treatment plant.

News.title: Man who used hidden cameras to film young girls in the bathroom jailed
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A man has been sent to prison after using hidden cameras to secretly record young girls inside a bathroom.

Gaven Clarke, 41, from Norfolk, arried out the offending over a five-year period, capturing photos and video footage of children as they showered or used the toilet.

According to Norfolk Police, his actions between 2020 and 2025 came to light after one of the girls found a mobile phone hidden behind toiletries on a bathroom shelf.

Upon checking what was stored on the device, she discovered videos of herself that she did not know had been filmed.

She alerted her parents, who immediately reported the matter to officers.

Clarke was arrested in May 2025, when police seized his phone and digital equipment, the force confirmed.

A forensic examination of the devices revealed pictures of other victims, none of whom knew they were recorded, alongside hundreds of further downloaded indecent images of children.

The 41-year-old, of Drayton, near Norwich, previously admitted two counts of voyeurism, four counts of making indecent images of children and three counts of taking indecent images of children, police said.

At Norwich Crown Court on Thursday, Clarke was sentenced to three years and eight months in prison, Norfolk Police said.

open image in gallery Clarke previously admitted two counts of voyeurism, four counts of making indecent images of children and three counts of taking indecent images of children, police said ( PA Archive )

In a statement read in court, one of his victims said: “I felt disgusted by his behaviour. I was extremely shocked by what I had found. I was physically shaking.

“In the weeks after discovering the videos, I kept asking myself, why me?

“I couldn’t get my head around what had happened. Now when I walk into a public toilet I am constantly looking around to check if there are any devices.”

In a statement on Friday, Norfolk Police urged other victims of voyeurism to come forward.

Detective Sergeant Ash Parker added: “I’d like to thank the victims for their bravery and resilience throughout this investigation.

“Clarke’s offending was a deeply disturbing violation of the victims’ privacy and dignity.

“He deliberately invaded spaces where young girls had every right to feel safe, subjecting them to an experience that has had a lasting and significant impact on them.”

Clarke was also put on the sex offenders’ register for life and made the subject of an indefinite restraining order and a 10-year sexual harm prevention order.

News.title: We all are longing for the days of Obama. His latest mic toss proves it
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Barack Obama is back in the spotlight and Millennial Democrats are suddenly feeling something they have not in years — hope.

Having Obama back behind the podium brings a wave of intense nostalgia and longing for the days when a competent (and handsome) man resided at 1600 Pennsylvania Ave. His easy swagger and natural charisma feel like a warm hug from an old friend; a temporary balm to soothe our weary souls, exhausted from the unfiltered chaos of the current administration.

Watching him casually and effortlessly toss that microphone at the conclusion of the Michigan rally for Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed and gubernatorial candidate Jocelyn Benson — in a recreation of his viral mic drop at the 2016 White House Correspondents' Dinner — brings back memories of the good old days.

Online chatter praised 44’s “impeccable aura” and branded him “the coolest to ever do it.” Others said he’s “still charismatic, after all these years” and labeled him “the GOAT.” But it’s one Instagram comment — “Alexa, play Daddy’s Home by Usher” — that perfectly sums up how so many of us are feeling.

We used to wait with bated breath to see what Obama was going to do next; how he could possibly top whatever wry comment or heartfelt speech had us fawning. And somehow, he always managed to do just that, keeping us swooning over his unwavering confidence and ability to string multiple coherent sentences together back-to-back-to-back.

When our hearts were broken over senseless school shootings and violence, Obama always knew just what to say to get us to keep moving forward. When times were tough, he gave us reasons to feel hopeful. Even through the infamous tan suit and the (unhinged) Dijon mustard burger controversies, Obama continued to win us over. He showed us time and time again that he was a real, imperfect human being, which only earned him more respect.

open image in gallery Barack Obama's campaign rally speeches are giving Millennial Democrats hope once more ( AFP/Getty )

open image in gallery Obama tossed his mic to an aide after giving a rally speech in Michigan earlier this week ( Abdul El-Sayed )

That’s why he nearly broke millions of Millennial hearts in 2025 when whispers signaled the possible end of his marriage to Michelle Obama. Several solo appearances from the former president (sans everyone’s favorite first lady) at high-profile events like Jimmy Carter’s funeral left us panicked. Surely if they can’t make it through two presidential terms and the forced turnover of the White House to the orange guy, there’s no hope for the rest of us.

Thankfully they’ve continued their loved up Instagram posts marking milestone anniversaries and birthdays. Their relationship is just another reason why we desperately miss the Obamas.

No one is without flaws, and it takes a certain personality to want to be president in the first place. Obama wasn’t perfect, but as far as presidents go (and especially given what we have now) he was one of the best. No shady business dealings or criminal charges. Just a passion for America, the people who inhabit it, and those who dream of calling it home.

Imagine that! With all that we’ve endured as a country in the near decade since he left the White House, seeing Obama back where he belongs — slipping jokes and flipping mics — is the beacon of hope we so desperately need.

News.title: Broken tap at hospital ran for months and wasted a million litres of water before being fixed
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A broken tap ran at a hospital for nearly three months and wasted around a million litres of water, according to reports.

The tap at Ysbyty Glan Clwyd emergency department in Denbighshire, was fixed on 26 October, the Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board claimed, but the BBC’s Local Democracy Reporting Service said a sticker by the tap showed the matter was reported on 7 August.

A running tap uses 10 litres of water a minute, according to campaign group Let’s Save Water.

The tap was running for 81 days, according to the BBC, which means that as many as 1,166,400 litres of water may have been wasted while it was broken.

Not-for-profit group Waterwise said it was appalled by the waste of water.

Chief executive Nicci Russell told the BBC: “This is an absolutely horrific waste of water when we can scarcely afford to be wasting water.

“The climate change committee is telling us drought is one of our top three climate risks.

“Our current water systems are not even fit for the current climate, let alone what is coming – parts of Wales are still in drought.”

Denbighshire County Council member Chris Evans was sent a video of the tap, shot on 11 October, by a constituent, according to the BBC.

He said: “It sums up what is wrong with Betsi, that they can’t even sort a running tap that’s been running since August.”

The health board, which runs the hospital, said that consideration was given to the requirements of the emergency department but the drip “deteriorated to a more substantial flow” over time.

Betsi’s Arwel Hughes, operational estates chief at the health board, said: “The fault reported to our estates team was identified as a minor drip from a specialist clinical tap, which subsequently deteriorated to a more substantial flow.

“Although a replacement part was ordered from the manufacturer promptly, repair was delayed until Monday 26 October due to supplier lead times.

“Any decision to isolate or remove the facility from use had to be carefully balanced against the potential impact on patient care, including the availability of essential handwashing facilities within a busy clinical environment,” he added.

“We are currently working with our suppliers to review and improve the availability and lead times of specialist replacement parts, in order to reduce future repair times.”

News.title: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff file for divorce after 3 years of marriage: report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff have officially filed for divorce, according to a report.

The musician, 42, and The Substance actor Qualley, 32, separated over the summer after five years together, including three years married.

According to People, the pair officially filed for divorce on Friday (October 30).

“Jack and Margaret are filing for divorce jointly,” a source close to the couple told the publication. “This is a mutual decision.” The Independent has contacted representatives for Antonoff and Qualley for comment.

“They share a deep affinity and love for one another, and though their romantic partnership is ending, they will absolutely be lifelong friends,” the source said.

open image in gallery Jack Antonoff recently spoke about finding power in performing love songs he had written about Qualley after their split ( Getty )

Antonoff recently spoke in an interview about how he finds power in singing love songs originally written about Qualley.

The musician, a Grammy-winning producer who is known for his longtime collaborations with Taylor Swift, is currently touring with his band Bleachers. His set includes songs he had written about Qualley, like “Dirty Wedding Dress” and “You and Forever.”

Antonoff told The Guardian: “Songs which I wrote recently, I obviously was really worried about this specific thing, I sat long and hard with it and thought: ‘If I change the setlist …’ and in my gut there was a unanimous jury that said, ‘No, this is the deal.’”

He continued: “The deal I’ve made with my audience is that I’m going to tell you honestly how I feel and I’m going to risk at any moment having to stand behind it for f***ing ever.”

“Anyone could relate to the terrible sadness and pain, but there’s a great power to it also. It’s actually been really beautiful,” Antonoff added. “I mean, for people to come together, to know what I write a song about, to know how that must feel for me now, to know what that song means to you as an audience member, to just hold it all and sort of celebrate.”

He continued: “I don’t rewrite the past, I have no shame about the things I’ve said.”

He added: “I would rather live through something publicly than even escape it privately.”

Antonoff and Qualley met at a rooftop party in 2021 and were engaged the next year.

Their relationship was at the heart of several pop culture moments in recent years — including inspiring Lana Del Rey’s song “Margaret” and a star-studded New Jersey wedding in August 2023 with guests including Swift, Bruce Springsteen, Cara Delevingne, Channing Tatum and Zoë Kravitz.

News.title: Trump plans to deport dozens of Afghans back to the Taliban in first large-scale removal flight
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Donald Trump’s administration is imminently expected to forcibly remove dozens of Afghans from the U.S. to Afghanistan, marking the first large-scale deportation flight of Afghans back into the hands of the Taliban, aid groups and human rights lawyers warn.

Roughly 150 Afghans are reportedly scheduled for the removal flight, which is being routed from Louisiana to Pakistan, where officials are expected to expel them to their home country.

Afghans on the flight include family members of U.S. allies who worked alongside military forces and aid groups, among others who could face discrimination and violence upon their return — including at least one LGBTQ+ person.

By sending the flight to Pakistan, the Trump administration has found a legally dubious workaround to send vulnerable immigrants to the country they fled, according to attorneys and refugee aid groups.

“By creating arrangements with countries such as Kuwait, Qatar, and now Pakistan, the Trump administration is effectuating removals to active war zones and severe security crises where individuals may be at grave risk,” according to former U.S. diplomat Uzra Zeya, president of Human Rights First.

open image in gallery The Trump administration is imminently expected to remove dozens of Afghan immigrants from the US to Pakistan, where they are anticipating being expelled to their Taliban-controlled home country ( AP )

The administration also is reportedly preparing another deportation flight forcing Iranian immigrants back to Iran, marking the first such removal flight since the onset of the U.S. war in February.

“The administration’s cruel mass deportation agenda has swept up family members of Afghan allies and Iranian political dissidents” who face “grave” consequences in their home countries, Zeya said.

In Afghanistan, returning dissidents are at risk of imprisonment, corporal punishment or execution, according to Shawn VanDiver, president of AfghanEvac, which helps resettle refugees including wartime allies.

“The Taliban is a regime that jails, tortures and kills the people it considers its enemies,” VanDiver said Friday.

“It has hunted down former soldiers, police officers, and the families of anyone who worked with the United States. It has erased women and girls from public life. Sending someone there is not a deportation. It is a sentence,” he said.

“Whatever path brought them here, the danger waiting for them is the same.”

The Trump administration has not publicly announced plans for the removal flight; unnamed officials speaking to media outlets, court filings, and statements from lawyers and advocacy organizations who fear for their imprisoned clients have outlined tentative plans to send Afghans out of the country.

Court filings in the case of one Afghan detainee indicate that a flight is expected to leave Louisiana within the first week of November.

In a statement to The Independent, a spokesperson for Homeland Security said that Immigration and Customs Enforcement “does not comment on prospective removal operations, including flight schedules, passenger manifests, destinations, or individual case details.”

“For operational security reasons and the safety of our officers, we would not confirm future removal operations,” the person said.

The Independent has also requested comment the State Department.

open image in gallery Advocates and lawyers fear ‘grave’ consequences for Afghans who supported US war efforts if they are forced to return to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan ( AFP/Getty )

Last year, the Trump administration pointed to an increase in tourism under Taliban-controlled Afghanistan to justify the cancellation of humanitarian protections for more than 11,000 Afghans in the U.S.

The administration announced plans to strip Temporary Protected Status from Afghanistan following the U.S. withdrawal in 2021, which led to the evacuation of tens of thousands of people in the wake of the devastating years-long war.

“We’ve reviewed the conditions in Afghanistan with our interagency partners, and they do not meet the requirements for a TPS designation,” then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem said in a statement at the time. “Afghanistan has had an improved security situation, and its stabilizing economy no longer prevent [sic] them from returning to their home country.”

Homeland Security’s notice claims there have been “notable improvements” in Afghanistan’s national security and “requiring the return of Afghan nationals to Afghanistan does not pose a threat to their personal safety due to armed conflict or extraordinary and temporary conditions.”

The notice also claims that “the Taliban government is promoting tourism to shift its global image.”

“Tourism to Afghanistan has increased, as the rates of kidnappings have reduced,” the notice added. “Tourists are sharing their experiences on social media, highlighting the peaceful countryside, welcoming locals, and the cultural heritage, according to some reports.”

Pakistan, meanwhile, has launched its own mass deportation effort targeting Afghan refugees. More than 2.7 million Afghans have been expelled from the country since 2023.

The relationship between the two countries has continued to deteriorate following the withdrawal of U.S.-led foreign forces in 2021. Deadly border clashes and escalating attacks have resulted in closure crossings and growing fears of civilian casualties, while Islamabad has urged Kabul to dismantle militant groups including Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan accused of serving as proxies to launch attacks from inside the country.

It is, because they showed their quality and offered themselves a sniff with their Gallic heroics. They had to maintain that pace on Friday to put the pressure on Samoa, but after the ideal beginning they contracted a nasty case of white-line fever from which they could not recover. “It looks like we’re going out of the tournament,” McDermott said. “That second half got scrappy and we should have handled that a lot better.”

News.title: Everton give Burnham something to shout about by booking quarter-final spot
News.content:
David Moyes took a glug of water and glanced up at the big screen away to his right, almost as if he wanted confirmation that what he was seeing was true.

Had he looked behind him, Moyes would have seen Andy Burnham and his wife, Marie-France, in raptures, along with thousands of others. It was true, all right. Everton had scored their third goal and were bounding into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals, seemingly without a care in the world.

What a happy change of direction. Moyes has spent months spinning plates, dealing with owners who do not care about a proud club and want to sell up and a squad that was left criminally short in the transfer window. Then, before Newcastle’s visit, came more disruption.

Jack Grealish’s selfish and reckless decision to go Awol from training on Monday could have been a catalyst for more misery and invited Newcastle to deliver a hammer blow to Everton’s season, but again, Moyes fostered a siege mentality. He was rewarded in the most emphatic fashion.

True, Newcastle collapsed like a deckchair without hinges and this performance – which encouraged many of their 8,000 followers to head for the exits early – would not have done anything to convince those who view Matthias Jaissle, the head coach, with ambivalence to change their minds.

News.title: Trump administration loses grip on bird flu, experts warn
News.content:
The Trump administration has been criticised for losing control of a bird flu outbreak that has spread among mink and cattle farms across the United States.

The H5N1 virus has infected around 1,000 people since it was first detected in the late 1990s, killing roughly half of them. While it currently does not spread among humans, scientists have long worried that it could trigger a pandemic, and that each human infection raises the risk of the virus mutating.

A new variant emerged in 2020 and has since spread to millions of birds and hundreds of animal species across the globe, leading to devastating losses in both wildlife and farmed livestock and poultry.

While some countries have introduced tough measures to curb its spread, including mandatory culls of infected animals, “flockdowns” (where birds are kept indoors) and vaccination of farm workers who handle at-risk livestock, experts say the US is allowing the virus to run rampant.

For more than two months, an outbreak has raged unchecked on a Utah farm that raises thousands of mink for fur, news outlet ProPublica reported last week.

Mink in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of the farms give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

Mink have very similar respiratory systems to humans, increasing the risk that a virus can spread between the animals and people, and undergo a process known as “reassortment”, when two or more viruses mix together to make a new, more dangerous strain.

News.title: Britain faces unprecedented squeeze on incomes, IFS says

Thanks for joining me. John Healey has ruled out making “crude cuts” to welfare after he failed to tackle the rising benefits bill in Wednesday’s Budget.

The Chancellor acknowledged last night that the current benefits system is “unsustainable” but said he will only look to make cuts “in a Labour way”.

Speaking to the BBC in the wake of Wednesday’s Budget, Mr Healey promised that “there will be a reduction in the benefits bill” before the next election.

However, he said this will not include “crude cuts” to payments.

He said: “We will do that in a Labour way, and we will do that because it is simply not good for Britain, or progressive, to have a bigger and bigger benefits bills.

“This system is unsustainable. I’ve been clear about that. The Prime Minister’s been clear about that. It’s what you do about it.”

He added: “We have to bring the benefits bill down. You don’t do that by crude cuts, especially when people are feeling the cost of living pressures.”

His comments on welfare come after Tory leader Kemi Badenoch accused Labour of presiding over a Government that had left Britain “overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system”.

She said: “Next year, under Labour, the tax burden will be the highest in our country’s history and our benefits bill is going up by tens of billions of pounds because this Government has put welfare first.”

The latest figures from the Office for Budget Responsibility released on Wednesday revealed that benefits spending is expected to jump by almost 30pc to £431bn by 2032.

Almost half the total is pensions and disability benefits for pensioners, despite the planned abolition of the triple lock. Here is what you need to know.

News.title: Risk of Ebola spread in UK is low, experts stress
News.content:
Infectious disease experts have stressed the likelihood of Ebola spreading to the UK is low after the head of Africa’s health agency warned that the haemorrhagic fever could reach Britain.

The Democratic Republic of Congo is struggling to contain an outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain of the deadly virus that began in the volatile eastern region of the country. There have been 10,000 cases, including nearly 5,000 deaths, since the outbreak was first reported in May and it has now become the second largest Ebola epidemic in history.

In recent weeks the virus has spread to Kenya, where there have been nine cases including two deaths, and Nigeria. The case in Nigeria is concerning because the patient, the wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, the country’s capital, had no history of travel to the affected region of DRC. She has now been evacuated to Switzerland.

In comments reported by the Guardian Jean Kaseya, head of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, described the outbreak as “unprecedented” as it was the first time that the disease had spread to three geographic regions of the continent. He warned that there was scope for further spread.

“We shouldn’t forget that at the beginning of Covid, many countries said there was zero risk of being affected, but a few months later, they became the hotspot,” he said. “We don’t want to see the UK and other countries become the hotspot.”

On Wednesday the United States announced that travellers arriving by air would have to sign a statement affirming that they had not been in the DRC within the previous 21 days. Anyone found to provide false or misleading information would face imprisonment or a fine.

The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stressed that the risk to the UK is low. Dr Sam Collins, head of guidance, clinical and public health response at the agency, said the Ebola outbreak in DRC is serious but “the UK is well prepared to respond safely and effectively to the risk of imported cases arising here”.

UKHSA is monitoring travel routes from the affected countries and is providing information on symptoms.

The UKHSA said it is rare for Ebola to occur in returning travellers and the NHS has “well established procedures in place” for such a situation.

News.content:
As the Telegraph Fantasy Football season heads further into 2026-27, the award-winning experts at Fantasy Football Hub ccontinue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

Join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips.



Telegraph Fantasy Football: last week's insights



Joao Pedro owners face a dilemma

There was no prior indication that the game’s second most-owned player would miss out on Chelsea’s starting XI against rivals Spurs, leaving TFF managers with a potential transfer decision to make when the teams were announced. The Brazilian looks set to be out until the international break, with Alexander Isak (£6.0m), Nicolas Jackson (£4.1m) and Evanilson (£4.0m) all attracting attention as viable alternatives.



Bournemouth’s Old Trafford dominance

The south-coast club have now won on three of their last four visits to the Theatre of Dreams, each time by the same 3-0 scoreline. The biggest talking point for the home side was the omission of their captain, Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m). Poor form, concerns over a possible underlying injury and reports of a falling-out with the manager have now put the heavy-hitter firmly in the sell category.



Defensive bargains emerge

Eight teams kept clean sheets this weekend and there appears to be plenty of value in the budget defender bracket. Leeds, Bournemouth and Tottenham stand out thanks to their promising underlying data and favourable fixture runs, with Tarik Muharemovic (£2.7m), Antonio Silva (£2.8m) and Jan Paul van Hecke (£3.3m) emerging as the standout options.

Telegraph Fantasy Football Tips: Game Week 9



The Telegraph Fantasy Football player list has been analysed ahead of the upcoming games, and these look like the best players to transfer in:



1. Nicolas Jackson (£4.1m)

Many questioned whether the former Chelsea striker could fill Ollie Watkins’ boots, but his reunion with manager Unai Emery appears to be working perfectly. Fresh from a brace against table-topping Manchester City, the Senegal international is set to lead the line against Fulham this weekend and looks an ideal replacement for the aforementioned Joao Pedro.



2. Marcus Tavernier (£3.1m)

Despite being the sixth highest-scoring midfielder in the game, Tavernier is owned by just 12 per cent of TFF managers. The Cherries’ excellent fixture run begins at home to Leeds this weekend, presenting an ideal opportunity to invest for those who don’t already own him.



3. Johan Manzambi (£3.8m)

With ownership of just 2 per cent, the 21-year-old looks an excellent differential ahead of Villa’s favourable fixture swing. Doubling up with Jackson could help managers to climb their mini-league tables quickly.

News.title: Wesley Fofana’s Chelsea nightmare continues as Liverpool win shoot-out
News.content:
It is an all-Premier League tie at Anfield as Liverpool host Chelsea in the last 16 of the League Cup, with a place in the quarter-finals at stake. This will be the first managerial meeting between childhood friends Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso.

Liverpool beat Tottenham 3-1 at Anfield in the last round of this competition, which included a stunning goal from Dominik Szoboszlai to seal progression to the last 16. They earned their first home Premier League win of the season on the weekend as they beat Brighton 2-0. Iraola’s men come into this game off the back of four straight wins in all competitions.

“There will definitely be changes, but we want to win the game and we want to be competitive,” Iraola said ahead of this tie. “We have to see how the legs; we are not just in the Carabao Cup, but also in the Champions League and we have been trying to make changes from game to game. We want to be in the next round. We have been unlucky in the draw, playing Chelsea, and they have been unlucky also. But we want to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win. We need to rotate, all the top teams need to rotate when you are playing every three days. Sometimes you are forced to rotate due to injury or sometimes different demands in different games tactically. I am happy that everyone is involved. When we have had to use someone who has not played a lot of games, they have helped us. The more players we have in a good place, the easier my selection will be, even if it is hard to leave players out.”

News.title: Burnham rules out calling early election
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. John Healey has promised to offer households “breathing space” in his maiden Budget today.

The Chancellor insisted the economy has shown “resilience” in the face of the energy shock from the Iran war.

However, he admitted the conflict has pushed up the cost of living, “piling pressure on the families, on businesses, and on our public finances”.

Among the measures the Chancellor is expected to announce are plans to scrap standing charges on household gas bills – saving families up to £50 a year.

Mr Healey said: “We can’t stop these shocks that hit Britain, but we can make Britain more resilient when they do.

“So, this Budget is designed to give households breathing space from some of the everyday costs, provide targeted support for businesses and self-employed people, and to start the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Healey prepares to slash household gas bills by £50 | Chancellor to scrap standing charges on gas bills and curb Energy Secretary’s power

2) Minimum wage rise will drive up food prices, Healey warned | Manufacturers say they are already struggling to cover soaring production costs

3) Poundland directors quit in stand-off over administration | Board members fear owner wants to steer retailer into insolvency

4) Google attacks UK over ‘unlawful’ AI plans | Search giant fights plans by competition regulator to force it to promote rivals

5) Netherlands to cut 25,000 civil service jobs in AI push | Police and defence will be exempt from plans to trim 15pc of government workforce in next decade

What happened overnight

Ahead of the Budget, oil prices rose after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, which has renewed concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East.

Brent crude was up 1.7pc to nearly $116 a barrel, maintaining inflationary pressure on the global economy. It traded around $70 before the start of the Iran war.

Meanwhile, Asia stocks rallied amid fresh enthusiasm about AI.

South Korea’s Kospi surged more than 6pc and was on track for its largest one-day gain since July, after chipmaker SK Hynix reported a more than seven-fold jump in quarterly profit and said it would return about $75 billion to shareholders this year.

The AI rally faces its next test when technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft report earnings after market close later today, with investors looking for evidence of returns that would justify the hefty cost of the AI build-out.

In Asia, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was up 1.7pc, with Japan’s Nikkei adding 1.1pc and ⁠China’s CSI300 blue-chip index climbing 0.7pc.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez’s hand permanently disfigured as Chelsea goalkeeper reveals incredible sacrifice to play in World Cup

EMILIANO MARTINEZ has revealed how his hand is permanently disfigured and what he sacrificed to play at the World Cup.

The Chelsea goalkeeper suffered heartbreak at the tournament as Argentina were beaten in the final in New York by Spain.



Martinez, 34, almost did not play at the tournament after breaking his finger during Aston Villa‘s Europa League final victory over Freiburg.

The Argentine stopper was left distraught after seeing his X-rays, believing he would miss the tournament in the USA.



However, he was backed by national team coach Lionel Scaloni and received a special glove from Adidas that would allow him to play.



Martinez opted against surgery and did not train with normal balls until the quarter-final against Switzerland.

He revealed that he is still in need of an operation and suffering daily pain.

The goalkeeper has revealed that his hand is disfigured and that he can not properly close his fist during an interview with Los Edul.

He said: “I broke my finger in the Europa League final. When the doctor showed me the X-ray, I started crying because I thought I would miss the World Cup.



“Scaloni messaged me and said: ‘Whether you make it or not, I’ll back you… come anyway’.

“We decided not to have surgery. Adidas made me a special glove, and I played with my finger completely wrapped. I could only feel four fingers.

“I couldn’t even train with normal footballs. I trained with volleyballs until the Switzerland game.

“How much did it affect me at the World Cup? Ten out of ten.

“I was practically a zombie. Every time my hand touched the ground, I saw stars.



“I cried at the training camp because my finger was so swollen. After the World Cup, I had another X-ray and the finger was still broken in half.

“I still play through pain today. I’ll eventually need surgery.”

Following the World Cup, Martinez completed a £7.5million transfer from Villa to Chelsea.

LISANDRO MARTINEZ is being targeted for a free summer transfer by Atletico Madrid, according to reports.

SunSport exclusively revealed how the defender wants out of Manchester United following his public outburst against club chiefs in the wake of their Champions League defeat against Atletico.



However, the La Liga side are now said to be eyeing the Argentina World Cup winner to bolster their defence.

Martinez‘s contract at Old Trafford runs out in the summer, meaning he would leave for nothing unless he is sold in the winter window.



However, Spanish outlet AS claim neither the club nor player are eager to extend the relationship beyond this season.

The report adds both Atletico and Barcelona are positioning themselves to make a move for the 28-year-old, who is famed for his passing and technical ability on the ball.



Man Utd are in the midst of an eight-game winless run under Michael Carrick ahead of their early kick-off against Chelsea tomorrow.

Both Martinez, who targeted the board, and captain Bruno Fernandes, who blasted the coaching staff’s tactics after the loss to Como, have broken rank this month – showing that tempers in the United camp are boiling over.

Martinez has been injury prone for much of his time at United since joining from Ajax in 2022.

His persistent injuries have limited the centre-back to just 115 appearances in a Red Devils shirt over the course of four and a bit seasons.

Fans in the Stretford End made their thoughts clear by serenading Carrick as he walked off before aiming vicious boos at the players.

Martinez was included in the travelling squad to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, where United managed to win 1-0 last season under Carrick courtesy of a Matheus Cunha strike just before half-time.

JUDE BELLINGHAM’s dad has received a shock call-up for the England veterans.

Mark Bellingham has been called up for the team to take on Ireland – a massive seven years after he retired.



Bellingham Sr, 50, has football pedigree, having played in non-league during a 17-year career.

His playing days saw him play for 22 different clubs, including Leamington and Bromsgrove Sporting.



He also turned out for the likes of Cheltenham Town and Newport County in the late 1990s.

Mark hung up his boots in 2019 but continued to compete in veterans tournaments.

He has now been called up for the England Veterans Over 50s and could play this weekend.

He was announced in the squad to face the Republic of Ireland in Cambridgeshire.

England’s Over 60s will also be playing on Saturday at a later kick-off time.

The team wrote: “England Veterans have announced their squads for a double helping of international football against the Republic of Ireland on Sunday 1st November in Cambridgeshire

“The Over 50’s kick off at 2:15pm and the Over 60’s at 4:15pm at the Elite Football Complex, Cambridgeshire.”

The call-up is the first Bellingham Sr has received to represent the Three Lions.

He can now join his sons Jude and Jobe in playing for England.

Bellingham, 23, has become a key player for the first team under Thomas Tuchel and starred at the World Cup earlier this year.

Seven of his goals came in the World Cup as England finished in third place.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher tells Aston Villa fans ‘shut the f*** up, you’ll never be Man Utd’ as he tips Emery to replace Carrick
Sports.content:
Next

JAMIE CARRAGHER told Aston Villa fans to “shut the f*** up” after he was blasted for advising popular manager Unai Emery to take the Manchester United job amid Michael Carrick’s struggles.

Carrick, 45, is overseeing United’s worst league start in 40 years that has led to a total of six losses out of 13 matches in charge this season, of which he has only won three.



Man Utd‘s legendary midfielder has come under fire and club chiefs are said to have drawn up a managerial shortlist of possible replacements, which reportedly includes Emery, 54.

The Spanish tactician has transformed Villa from Premier League relegation strugglers to a Champions League side during his successful four-year stint, having also won last season’s Europa League.



Following other successful spells at Sevilla and Villarreal, Carragher, 48, is adamant the Spanish tactician would be perfect to turn Man Utd’s fortunes around – despite his failures at Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain.

That led to a furious reaction from Villa fans who are in absolutely no mood to part ways with Emery after he led them to two Champions League qualifications, one of which saw them reaching the quarter-finals.

However, Carragher is sticking to his guns and is adamant Emery should seriously consider that giant leap at Old Trafford if the opportunity presents itself.

And the Liverpool legend went as far as to tell Villa fans to accept that as they will “never be” as big as United.

Carragher told Stick to Football: “I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year.

“But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three of four times surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

“Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

“But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.

“So Real Madrid will take Manchester United’s best player, they did it with [Cristiano] Ronaldo.

“And there will be teams below Aston Villa, and they’ll take their players or manager, so shut the f*** up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United.”

Sports.title: Sport stars with the weirdest superstitions, including Chelsea icon’s URINAL ritual and tennis royalty’s unwashed SOCKS
Sports.content:
Next

SPORTS stars will do anything for a win.

Many have worked years for their moment, training hard, and psyching themselves up before they go out to a crowd to put on a show.



But, before they do so, some believe a superstition will give them that extra edge to perform.

That’s where the below come in. These sports stars have/had some incredible rituals that they believed would help them get over the line.



SunSport rounds up sports stars’ craziest superstitions

John Terry

Before he used to take the pitch at Stamford Bridge, the Chelsea legend would pee in the same urinal in the dressing room.

Amusingly, Terry did it once and the Blues won the game. Then, team-mates Ashley Cole and Frank Lampard got in on the act, sometimes delaying the team walking out on the pitch.

Terry told us: “Me and Frank started it a long time ago; in the Chelsea dressing room we have three urinals and me and Lamps started weeing in one. We won the game and that was it.

“The next week there was a queue of me, Frank and Ash. The next week there were four of us and the week after there were five. Even now, up until today, you have Cesar Azpilicueta and Cesc Fabregas, we are all there in one big queue.

“A few months ago the club secretary said to me: ‘we have had a few calls from the FA complaining because we have been going out late’ and I didn’t have the heart to tell him it was because we were all waiting to go for a wee.”



Sergio Goycochea

Staying on the peeing theme, Goycochea took his business outside of the changing rooms and certainly marked his territory.

Incredibly, before penalty shootouts the nutty Argentinian sweeper keeper would relieve himself in his penalty area.

He said: “I did it against Yugoslavia (in the 1990 World Cup quarter-finals) – we won, so then when the semi-final against Italy went to penalties I did it again – and it worked!



“From that moment on I did it before every shoot-out. It was my lucky charm.”

Goran Ivanisevic

In 2001, wildcard Ivanisevic won Wimbledon in one of the most remarkable sports stories of our times.

He did it with the help of several rituals, including watching Tinky Winky and Co of Teletubbies fame before his matches.



The Croatian told The Independent: “My coach one day said, ‘You have to watch this, this is so funny’.

“And I won my match that day. So then I couldn’t stop. My favourite was the purple one, Tinky Winky.”

Andre Agassi

Continuing the tennis theme, American tennis god Agassi let it all hang loose with his superstition.

From the 1999 French Open onwards, he decided to ditch underwear after forgetting to pack some before a match.



Agassi explained: “I got to the locker room and realised I’d forgotten my underwear.

“What can a man do? I just commandoed it. After that it was a case of ‘If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it’. It actually feels good.”

Jason Terry

NBA legend Terry had his own unique way of prepping for games.

It all unfolded before the NCAA national championship game between Terry’s Arizona Wildcats and the University of Kentucky.



After having trouble sleeping at night, he decided to put on his full kit for bedtime.

Terry said: “The next day, we ended up winning the national championship. After that, I was like, ‘OK, I think I’m superstitious and I need to keep this thing going.’”

Serena Williams

The greatest female tennis player of all time risked athlete’s foot with this superstition.



Serena was reportedly known to wear the same unwashed socks during a tournament.

She also made sure to use the same shower, it is believed.

Presumably, to give those feet a good scrub.



Kolo Toure

The former Arsenal and Man City star had a strict pre-match superstition where he insisted on being the absolute last player from his team to step onto the pitch.

However, that got him into bother during a Champions League last-16 tie against Roma at the Emirates.

Amusingly, the match began without him. Realising his error, he scuttled on as quickly as he could.



But, that only got him in trouble with the referee for entering the field without permission and earned the defender a yellow card.

Mariafe Artacho del Solar

Aussie volleyball star Mariafe Artacho Del Solar lost an earring during her opening match against Cuba at Tokyo 2020.

But, rather than replace it, she viewed it as a lucky omen and played the rest of the tournament wearing just one earring.



“Earrings are like my undies,” she joked.

“I can’t leave home without them.”

Marta Kostyuk

Kostyuk’s ​maiden WTA 1000 title in Madrid in May came courtesy of a laundry mix-up and some lucky pants.



As she explained to Spanish ⁠broadcaster Movistar Plus.: “We have a tournament laundry service and sometimes the clothes get ​mixed up and last year we ended up with this piece ​of underwear where in it was written ‘Lucky Shorts’. So we kept it.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“My coach Sandra (Zaniewska) kept it as a lucky charm.”

Kostyuk added: “We made this promise that if I’d ​win we would ​bring the ‘Lucky Shorts’ ⁠for the photoshoot with the trophy.” And, she didn’t disappoint parading the pants, in all their glory, as she did a backflip on the court.

Sports.title: Dejan Kulusevski told mum he might never play again as injury left Spurs ace unable to walk up STAIRS normally
Sports.content:
Next

DEJAN KULUSEVSKI told his mum that he thought his knee injury hell was going to wreck his football dream – because after 14 months he still could not walk up stairs normally.

The Tottenham star, 26, reached the point where he was preparing to hang up his boots when nothing was working to fix the broken cartilage that kept him out for 17 months.

Kulusevski sustained the complicated injury in an innocuous challenge with Marc Guehi during Spurs’ Premier League clash with Crystal Palace in May 2025.



Fortunately, his fears were not realised as the hard-working Swede returned to action after 526 days out against Coventry earlier this month.



On Saturday, he hopes to make his third appearance of the season at home to Palace – the exact same fixture in which he suffered the original injury.

Kulusevski recalled: “I broke my cartilage, and the cartilage flew out and went to another part of the knee, and they can’t fix cartilage.”

What followed was surgery and then a relentless and dedicated bid to recover seeing the world’s best specialists including a rehab expert in Serbia recommended by Zlatan Ibrahimovic.

But nothing seemed to work.

Kulusevski revealed: “You get stressed because now you try everything and nothing works still.

“I told my mother, I sat with her and I told her ‘listen, I don’t think this is going to work out’.
