“I had to prepare her, I don’t think I can play anymore.”



“I had to accept because it had been like one year and a couple of months and I still can’t walk on stairs like a normal guy (and) I have to play football.

“I’m not going to give up but I have to think if this doesn’t work out what am I going to do, because I’m 26 years old. I have to have some kind of plan.

“I have to know what I have to do if this doesn’t work out.

“I remember the day I sat with her on the couch. I told her, ‘Listen, I don’t think this is going to work out, I tried everything, I worked with all the best, it just doesn’t work’.”

But Kulusevski did not give up, kept on doing his rehab diligently, even when he suffered the devastating blow of missing out on the World Cup in the summer.



Then a trip to see a physiotherapist in his home country was the catalyst for his comeback.

The former Juventus winger explained: “I went to a physio in Sweden and he was able to change my nervous system and the knee felt different.

“When I did the exercises, I said, ‘I don’t have pain. This hurt yesterday, why is this not hurting today?’

“Then I did the next exercise and I said ‘This is not hurting’.

“I went into the room to my wife and I told her, ‘It’s over, we’re going to do this’.



“That’s when the grind started, in the summer, I started to play football, I got better every day, I was limping and everything but it was different now.

“I came here to Tottenham to do pre-season and they were also impressed of the progress I made. I got a lot of help from them, I got much stronger in a short time.

“I went from ‘this guy will not play football anymore’, to playing really good football just in a couple of weeks.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta warns Max Dowman he’s not at ‘DISNEYLAND’ after red card as Arsenal star told he ‘must earn right to play’
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA warned Max Dowman life in Arsenal’s first team is not “Disneyland” – and he will be held to the same standards as everyone else.

The forward, 16, was sent off during Tuesday’s shock Carabao Cup penalty exit to Fleetwood Town after reacting to a tackle from Harrison Neal.

Arsenal failed in their appeal of the red card and Arteta was “disappointed” by that, arguing the challenge could have left Dowman with a broken foot.



But the Gunners boss also stressed the need for the teen star to learn about the harsh realities of performing on the biggest stage.



Arteta said: “This is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise, we are in Disneyland.

“We are not in Disneyland. We are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine.

“But at the same time we are going to demand him, like anybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play.

“Otherwise, the rest of the boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.”

Arteta seemed angry with Dowman as he left the pitch on Tuesday night following his red card against the League Two side.

The Spaniard explained his reaction came in “a moment of heat and extreme frustration” because he had warned the teenager about being targeted and not reacting.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He added: “It’s something that we discussed just before we went out, because it’s not the first time that happened.



“It happened another time this month with England. And it will continue to happen, unfortunately, because of the way he plays and the way he attracts opponents.

“You want to see the reaction of his team-mates? When they have to play with ten, you want to see that? What do you expect?

“And whether it is right or wrong, that’s the reaction. But the reaction when I don’t win, you know what the reaction is? I’m p***** off, big time. So we need to be ready for that.”

Arteta expressed an understanding for Dowman’s reaction given the tackle he was on the receiving end of.

The Arsenal boss also held talks with the teenager on Thursday and insisted there was no fallout from the incident.



He said: “You have to read the context of the player, the age, and what happened previously.

“It could have been really bad, and we’re lucky today that he hasn’t had a broken foot – that’s clear.

“When you play for Arsenal, you’re going to have highs and lows. You have to be prepared for that. It doesn’t matter the age. So don’t feel sorry for yourself.

“I had a talk with him – no issues at all. I’ve done it, so I try to prevent that. That’s why I’m so protective of these things and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes.

“I want to protect [him] because if a player that weighs 95kg, 100kg, comes at 35km/h to Max and hits a bone, I don’t know what happens.”

Sports.title: Viral non-league boss tells Carrick how to fix Man Utd mess and reveals major mistake he made with Bruno Fernandes
Sports.content:
Next

MARC WHITE flipped a table twice during an explosive foul-mouthed half-time rant — and now he has offered to fix Manchester United’s soft dressing room.

The Dorking Wanderers boss went viral after footage emerged of him swearing 38 times and flipping a table twice in one half-time team talk.



And the manager — who also owns the National South club — insists Old Trafford’s multi-millionaires are hiding behind a rotten culture because modern bosses are too frightened to call them out.

White told SunSport: “When there’s a failure culture at a club, it gives players a good opportunity to hide behind it. The problem is the managers always get sacked before the players.



“If I was Michael Carrick, I’d go down on my own sword. I’d just get rid of what I consider bad eggs. I’d tell everybody that’s why they’re not playing and say: ‘He might be good on the pitch, but let me tell you, we can’t build around this guy’.

“It’s a brave thing to do as a manager, but somebody needs to be bold enough to take control.”

United have burned through managers and billions in transfer fees since Sir Alex Ferguson retired 13 years ago without fixing their fundamentally broken culture.

And White believes modern players are pampered by corporate suits who care far more about commercial value than winning matches.

He said: “That’s football’s biggest issue. There is so much money around that when you get these superstars, they are really difficult to manage.

“Commercially, when you have a big superstar in your changing room and it’s going wrong, the owner’s probably saying: ‘If you stop playing him, you’re losing his value’.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“If you kick him out and he looks like a bad egg, you lose his value. Look at Fergie — he was exemplary for that. When Jaap Stam or David Beckham became too big for the party, he kicked them out because the group was most important.”

White also criticised Carrick’s weak handling of skipper Bruno Fernandes during recent games.

He added: “I would have just left him out completely rather than bench him. I wouldn’t have had him sat behind me with his eyes on me during the game. Michael got that one wrong and Fernandes sat there thinking: ‘If we lose, you look stupid, Michael’.



“I think it would have been better to say: ‘I’ve taken him out because his job as my captain is not to say what he said’. Leaders have to lead and you’ve got to be strong.

“The whole world thought, ‘Just take him out of the side for a few weeks to teach him a lesson’.”

White built Dorking from scratch at Step 17 all the way to the National League, serving as owner, chairman and manager.



Such an aggressive blast seen on the video would have seen him sacked at almost every Premier League, EFL or National League club.

Instead, the wealthy self-made businessman answers only to himself — and the fans on the terraces.

His viral explosions have divided opinion online, but White insists players need old-school fire and autocracy to improve.

He said: “In any true performance industry, American football, football, netball, whatever, there are scenarios like that week in, week out. The only difference is that since football particularly has become a TV sport, less of it is seen or heard.

Too soft managers

“Even at the highest level, there are tough changing rooms and tough managers, but at Dorking we show it. That particular rant was pretty rare for me to lose the plot like that, but people have to see the fire.



“And if they don’t respond to the fire, then you’ve probably got the wrong people in the building.”

The non-league chief believes top-flight managers have become too soft, apologetic and terrified of challenging players who drop stinkers.

He added: “I think pay packets are too big and managers don’t want to upset the owners. They’re looking after themselves.

“If I’m a fan on the terraces, I sleep a lot better at night when the manager comes out and admits: ‘He didn’t run hard enough for the team today’. That is the refreshing honesty people want to see.

“Anyone can be honest in a balanced way, and if people see you being fair, you’re as likely to praise as criticise.”



White insists dressing rooms are human environments, and he would happily bring his fiery style straight into Old Trafford’s star-studded changing room.

He said: “Would I do exactly the same things with those players? 100 per cent. I’d love to test that. It’s not all about money — it’s about testing yourself and getting the best out of people.

“Look at Brian Clough or Jock Stein — real football people. There is room for football people in the game and I would never change a thing.

“I’d have no qualms walking up to superstar players and telling them a few home truths because that is what a great leader does. And let me tell you, that is exactly what the fans want to see as well.”

Man Utd owners warned

White believes United owners must stop looking for quick managerial fixes and commit to a long-term strategy.



He noted: “All the great teams craft a culture and that takes time and patience. Liverpool in the 80s, Chelsea under [Jose] Mourinho, [Manchester] City, Fergie at United — they crafted a culture.

“When you lose that set-up, it can take years to recover. Clubs default to new managers thinking that’s the answer, but the manager is almost the last piece of the jigsaw. They need an old-school three to five-year plan, stick at it and just leave it alone.”

United’s changing room, like many at the top level, has a number of nationalities. And White feels this makes traditional English management harder without a strong local core.

He said: “Recruitment is key. Premier League changing rooms are so international. If a star from abroad gets typical English hair-dryer treatment, they just think: ‘Okay, I’ll go back to Spain’.

“There’s not been any winning Premier League teams without an English core. Look at Arsenal, Declan Rice was a key signing. Look at United of old, or Chelsea with John Terry and Frank Lampard. You have to build around the culture of the game in this country.”



Despite his viral fame, White remains focused on taking Dorking into the EFL. The club was formed in 1999 by White and a group of friends, playing in the Crawley & District League.

And they have since won TWELVE promotions, climbing as high as the National League for a season before relegation back to the sixth tier two years ago.

For the last eight years the club has been involved in charting their exploits in a fly-on-the-wall internet documentary called Bunch of Amateurs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

White said: “It started with a guy asking to film a short documentary and he’s still here eight years later! Initially it meant nothing, but it turned into people being interested in how a club is run.

“If we get to the EFL from Step 17, it’ll be one of the world’s greatest sporting successes. People can moan about my team talks, but they should respect the fact we’re prepared to show the truth.”

Sports.title: Man Utd's January plan sums up summer's transfer failings as club make rare move
Sports.content:
Man Utd's January plan sums up summer's transfer failings as club make rare move

Manchester United are willing to make a rarely seen move by entering the January transfer market as they look to rectify their season, which began with some poor summer decisions

View 2 Images Manchester United's hierarchy are prepared to spend in January with their squad being exposed (Image: PA)

Manchester United are ready to act in January by making at least one signing as they look to try and rescue their season.

‌



‌



The Red Devils ploughed all their finances into improving their midfield in the summer, which ended with three new arrivals - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba. The latter has only just come into the first-team picture after struggling with injury.

‌



The aforementioned duo have question marks over them at this early stage of the season, contributing to the club's worst start to a campaign in 40 years, which has left Michael Carrick as a man under pressure.

‌



It seems the board have accepted their failings, as The Times report that they will look to make an addition in the New Year, with the holes in their squad being seriously exposed.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



But United are not a team who do such business in January, history suggests so. Even in the past under the likes of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag they've started poorly, but still stuck with the squad they had.

Bruno Fernandes is an example of a January signing proving a huge hit, but notoriously the first month of the year is a tough time to do successful business for the right fee. That is backed up by the fact United have signed only THREE new players in the January transfer window since their capture of Fernandes back in 2020.

‌



Amad was signed from Atalanta the year after, but allowed to remain with the Italian club for a period. More recently Ayden Heaven was captured from Arsenal, but he was another young player who was seen as more of a long-term project.

The only player signed with a view to going straight into the first-team is Patrick Dorgu. He joined from Lecce when Ruben Amorim was in charge.

‌



Dorgu had the profile to play as a wing-back, which was a major part of the system Amorim tried, but failed, to implement. Since his dismissal Dorgu has had positive moments, but is by no means a regular with United reverting back to a conventional back four under Michael Carrick.

View 2 Images Some of Manchester United's summer arrivals are already being called out (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Under Ten Hag, they signed the likes of Jack Butland, Wout Weghorst and Marcel Sabitzer on loan, but their impact was limited, and even those decisions copped criticism.

United's need to bolster all areas of their squad is well known, which will no doubt drive up the price. January signings can be overpriced with selling clubs often knowing that the buyer is in, something of, a desperate situation.

‌



The Red Devils need a left-back, which they failed to land in the summer, to cover for Luke Shaw. They've also not welcome a major centre-half since Leny Yoro in 2024.

In attack, they're without the injured Benjamin Sesko as there's no genuine No 9 to cover for him, leaving the likes of Marcus Rashford and Matheus Cunha to act as makeshift solutions.

Article continues below

Even in midfield their new trio have not lit the world alight, and frustration among fans and ex-players has only mounted by watching how impressive the likes of Elliot Anderson and Sandro Tonali have been. Two men who United backed away from due to their price tags.

Sports.title: Premier League icon breaks silence on being handcuffed at McDonald's for 'stealing a taxi'
Sports.content:
Gareth Barry has the most yellow cards in Premier League history. But he was shown a red by Spanish police when placed in handcuffs after joyriding in a taxi.

The midfielder starred for the likes of Aston Villa, Manchester City and Everton throughout a career that saw him rack up a whopping 54,439 English top-flight minutes. But in 2018, whilst playing for West Brom, Barry's number was up when he and three team-mates, Jonny Evans, Jake Livermore and Boaz Myhill, were caught after an infamous late-night joyride on a team bonding trip to Barcelona.

The 45-year-old has now broken his silence on the Taxi-gate incident and revealed that he was handcuffed after returning to a McDonald's to resolve the situation. Recalling the incident on All Out Football's In The Mixer, Barry said: "Four of us go to an Irish bar and it's past midnight. We broke our curfew.

"So we thought we'd have a couple more drinks and then head home, which we did. The lads are hungry. On the way home, we asked the taxi driver, 'Do you mind just stopping at McDonald's?' As you do. Typical professional footballer food.

‌



You can listen to brand new episodes of In The Mixer on Spotify and Apple Podcasts!

Harry Kane makes knighthood admission as he sets out demand for name change READ MORE :

Jack Grealish's Everton future uncertain as disciplinary issue casts shadow over positive impact READ MORE :

"For some reason, he got out of the car to order it, which was a mistake by the taxi driver. One of us decides to jump in and drive the taxi away as a bit of a joke and said, 'We'll drive it around outside, around in a circle and bring it back.'

"So all four of us are now in the car with no taxi driver, we drive it around, the plan's going well. But we go the wrong way. And the next thing you know, we're in traffic on a highway.

"I'm an experienced player. The experienced pro. I jump out the car and say, 'Right, I'm going to go and tell the taxi driver we're bringing the car back.' But by the time I get there, the police are there.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Barry and three team-mates were involved (Image: Getty)

"So I called the lads and said, 'Don't come back. The police are here.' They continued on and I think they go and take the taxi to the hotel like good boys.

"But then I'm in handcuffs looking for them. In the police car! So I'm ruling myself out of driving this taxi. So you can blame one of the other three.

‌



"Anyway, we got back to the hotel and I call the lads and say, 'Boys, what have you done with the taxi?' - 'We just parked it around the corner.' Fine. I think nothing of it. Just go to bed. The phones are ringing in the morning…

"Team meeting. Alan Pardew goes, 'What's going on lads? Somebody in this team has stole a taxi.' I say to the boys, 'Look, four of us have broken the curfew. We don't throw anyone under the bus.' We stayed in it together.

"We went down the police station and I don't know what they said. I know my side of this story. I protected everyone! But we broke curfew and it was unprofessional. Just one of those team bonding moments that got out of hand."

‌



The four Baggies players did not face any criminal punishment after the taxi driver dropped the charges but they were slapped with disciplinary action by the club. All of them were fined and Barry admitted he was docked two weeks' wages. They also issued a joint public apology, but Barry says that his team should never have embarked on the trip in the first place.

View 3 Images The Baggies played Southampton a few days after the incident and lost 2-1 (Image: Getty)

He continued: "We shouldn't have gone on [that trip], by the way. They booked it thinking we were going to be knocked out of the FA Cup because we were playing Liverpool away at Anfield.

"We ended up beating Liverpool and then we still go and the lads are like, 'We won't do this trip, shouldn't go on this trip because we're playing on the weekend and we're flying back in on Thursday.'

‌



"It's like poor preparation really, isn't it? But the team bonding. You know what happens on team bonding? It's important. So Alan Pardew was like, 'No, we'll continue doing it. We'll have one night out. A bit of team bonding, get some good training, warm weather training and come home.'

"Tuesday, we have the team night out. Fine. No curfew. Wednesday, the next night, Alan Pardew says, 'Right, go get some food lads and make sure you're back at midnight.' Them curfews are dangerous, aren't they?"

The Baggies went on to lose 2-1 to Southampton in their fifth-round clash, with Barry and Evans receiving a mixed reception from the crowd, while back-up keeper Myhill remained on the bench and Livermore was absent through injury.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick fires back at Jamie Carragher as Man Utd boss makes honest admission on future
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick fires back at Jamie Carragher as Man Utd boss makes honest admission on future

Michael Carrick is clinging onto his job as Manchester United manager, but he has put on a brave face ahead of Saturday's crunch Premier League game against Chelsea

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has vowed to fight on as Manchester United boss (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has insisted he is still enjoying managing Manchester United after Jamie Carragher said he wants to be "put out of his misery" by being sacked.

‌



‌



Carrick is desperate for a win having clung onto his job following crisis talks with the club's hierarchy earlier in the week. United sit 16th in the Premier League, having taken just seven points from their opening eight matches - the club's worst start to a league campaign since 1986/87.

‌



The dreadful start, which has included just two wins in 12 in all competitions, prompted United to consider replacements, including Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte. It leaves Carrick in dire need of victory when they play Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in Saturday's early kick-off.

‌



The 45-year-old held a clear-the-air meeting with Bruno Fernandes after dropping him for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last weekend as a response for his criticism of the tactics against Como. And he is relishing the chance to put things right against Chelsea, rejecting Carragher's assertion that he wants "to be put out of his misery" with a sacking.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Honestly, there's not a hardest thing about it," Carrick told TNT Sports. "It's a great position to be in. I love being in this position, I love the responsibility and having an element of control of trying to make a difference, and trying to guide this club in a certain direction.

"I still enjoy it. I know people question that at times, but I certainly do enjoy it. I still enjoyed this week as much as ever because that's when we've got to dig deep as a group and see sticking together as part of it.

‌



"It doesn’t change the motivation, and it doesn't change what we want to achieve. We can still be close to flipping things and moving forward."

Gary Neville was convinced that Carrick would be sacked following the defeat by Bournemouth at Old Trafford. His Sky Sports colleague Carragher went even further, saying Carrick would welcome the decision, just months after landing the role on a permanent basis.

‌



View 3 Images Michael Carrick appeared to have managed his final game on Sunday before being given a reprieve (Image: Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"I think he can never say publicly, but I think Michael Carrick would want to be put out of his misery. I really do," Carragher said on Stick to Football. "The thought of going into that training ground now... and trying to do that team talk before Chelsea, when you know the players just aren't having it at all.

"Those players know Michael Carrick's not going to be there in two or three weeks. He knows it, they know it, everybody knows it."

‌



Carrick met with director of football Jason Wilcox on Monday knowing that the club has been exploring their replacement options. He was given a stay of execution but is under no illusions about his perilous position.

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes is back in the fold (Image: Getty)

‌



"I don't need any assurances for anything, really," Carrick added. "I totally understand what’s needed here, so I don’t need any assurances from anybody. I’m just focused on winning games, and winning this one on Saturday."

He added: "I know that, I know what this role is, I know what the club needs. When you're in it, it's tunnel vision in terms of constantly trying to improve things.

Article continues below

"We know it's not been good enough… It’s always something that can flip, and we're the ones that control that. That's the beauty of it, for me. We’re in control of it, we can do something about it. That's what we're trying to do."

Sports.title: Man Utd Ineos takeover timeline emerges as Glazers handed major update
Sports.content:
Man Utd Ineos takeover timeline emerges as Glazers handed major update

The Glazers, who took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005, remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to Sir Jim Ratcliffe in 2024

View Image Sir Jim Ratcliffe could take full control of Man United in the future

The Glazers could potentially face a Manchester United takeover bid from Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Ineos during the latter half of 2029. The club's most recent financial arrangements provide a significant indication of when a shift in majority ownership might occur. Ratcliffe acquired a 25 per cent stake in United through a deal valued at approximately £1.2billion in 2024, with his Ineos group assuming responsibility for managing football operations.

‌



The British billionaire additionally committed a further £245million in investment, taking his overall financial commitment to roughly £1.5bn. Nevertheless, the Glazer family remains the majority shareholders and retains substantial control over any prospective sale of the club.

According to the conditions of their 2024 arrangement with Ratcliffe, the Americans possess the authority to compel him to dispose of his stake, which has subsequently risen to approximately 28 per cent, should they agree to sell United to a third party under specific circumstances. The Glazers previously placed United's value at around $6bn (£4.5bn) while considering a possible sale, though the club's continuing financial challenges have prompted doubts about whether that valuation remains achievable.

Glazer family angry at Sir Jim Ratcliffe for breaking Man Utd 'promises' READ MORE :

Harry Maguire has already given Man Utd green light for blockbuster January transfer READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

According to The Telegraph, United's recent £411m refinancing deal offered a telling indication of when Ineos might look to increase its shareholding and potentially wrest majority control from the Glazers. The agreement points to 2029 as a potentially pivotal year for the club's ownership structure, positioning United better to settle existing debts while raising funds for their proposed 100,000-seater stadium.

Under the terms of the arrangement, United could settle certain loans without incurring early repayment penalties from 10th June 2029, provided the repayment forms part of the financing arrangements for a new stadium. This could enable the club to clear a portion of the debt stemming from the Glazers' deeply controversial leveraged takeover in 2005, which has continued to heap financial pressure on United ever since.

A further crucial date is 31st December 2029, when a separate credit facility United uses to manage its cash flow is due to expire. With both milestones falling within the same year, financial experts believe the latter half of 2029 could present the perfect opportunity to overhaul the club's debt structure entirely.

Such a development could also pave the way for Ratcliffe to acquire further shares from the Glazers, potentially enabling Ineos to obtain majority control while helping to fund the new stadium. Nevertheless, no arrangement currently confirms that the Glazers plan to relinquish their controlling interest, meaning 2029 represents a potential takeover opportunity rather than a definite date for an ownership transition.

Since finalising his minority investment in February 2024, Ratcliffe has implemented substantial changes behind the scenes at Old Trafford, including cost-reduction initiatives designed to strengthen the club's long-term financial standing.

Yet recent reports indicate the Glazer family has become progressively dissatisfied with how United has been managed under his stewardship, despite granting Ineos responsibility for football operations.

A source with social connections to the American family told the Mail that the situation at Old Trafford represented a 'travesty', asserting it was not what the Glazers had anticipated or been assured of when Ratcliffe became involved. The source also maintained that the Glazers had never run the club in such a fashion, prompting further doubts about their faith in the British billionaire's strategy.

Meanwhile, ESPN reported that another source claimed the Glazers believe Ratcliffe 'couldn't have masterminded a worse situation,' as his cost-cutting measures and changes across several departments reportedly contradict the strategy he initially outlined.

United's woes have also spilled onto the pitch, with the Red Devils enduring a dreadful eight-match winless streak across all competitions. Having secured just a single Premier League victory this season, the club are suffering their worst start to a campaign in nearly 40 years.

Their alarming slump has left them a mere two points above the bottom of the table ahead of Saturday's showdown with Chelsea, heaping further pressure on Ineos and those at the helm of football operations.

The club's dismal performances and mounting financial worries have additionally cast doubt over United's valuation, potentially throwing a spanner in the works should Ratcliffe attempt to secure majority ownership from the Glazers further down the line.

Sports.title: Club owner suing EFL side for £2m over 'cheating' as bitter feud takes ugly twist
Sports.content:
Club owner suing EFL side for £2m over 'cheating' as bitter feud takes ugly twist

Tensions are bubbling over in the English Football League, with a National League team owner taking legal action after accusations of being 'cheated'

View 2 Images Forest Green Rovers owner Dale Vince is suing Peterborough United (Image: PA)

Dale Vince is suing Peterborough United and their head coach, Robbie Savage, for £2million in damages. It comes after the head coach left Forest Green Rovers for Posh earlier this month, with the club's owner Vince claiming that an illegal approach was made.

‌



Speaking with Sky on Friday, Vince was asked if his feud with Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony had been resolved. There, the 65-year-old explained that he is taking legal action against Peterborough, seeking £2m in compensation - the figure which was the buyout in Savage's contract.

He told the broadcaster: "It’s not all sorted. It’s now gone legal and we are suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for £2 million which was the buy out clause we were cheated out of.

"That process started last week. What has come to light in the last two weeks is an abundance of evidence of an approach made by the chairman of Peterborough himself, while he’s been denying any such approach was made.

England U15s rush to protect referee from being attacked by opponents in extraordinary scenes READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"That’s quite aggrieving really. I know people will say, ‘It’s just football’, but we shouldn’t just shrug our shoulders and allow badness to happen."

Sharing a message on his personal X account, meanwhile, Vince shared a further update with Forest Green fans. He said: "Early start this morning, for me anyway.

"Up before 8am, here at Forest Green. Doing a little bit of TV, just done Sky. Doing ITV and BBC next, and I'll show you what it's all about.

"It's about the changing rooms and it's all about plants. A little bit about Peterborough as well, the news that we've begun a legal process for the tapping up of our manager, ex-manager now, Robbie Savage.

View 2 Images Robbie Savage joined Peterborough earlier this month (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"And that's the day so far. Plants, and what would you call it? Hassle. Hassle that we didn't want, but what are you going to do?"

The camera then cut away to Vince in the Forest Green dressing room, which featured plants in abundance above player lockers. The owner added: "Here it is, check it out. Changing room, chocka full of plants."

At the time of writing, Forest Green sit 15th in the National League after 13 games played, with five wins, as many losses and three draws to show for their efforts. They face Harrogate Town at Eco Park on Saturday, October 31 at 12.30pm.

Peterborough, meanwhile occupy 21st in League One with a record of two wins, four draws and six losses. Savage has held tenure with the club since October 2, having replaced Luke Williams following a dire start to the season.

Up next for Posh is a 3pm clash with Luton Town on Saturday. That game will take place at the Weston Homes Stadium on London Road, the home of Peterborough United.

Sports.title: England U15s rush to protect referee from being attacked by opponents in extraordinary scenes
Sports.content:
England U15s rush to protect referee from being attacked by opponents in extraordinary scenes

More drama ensued at the U15 World Cup during England's match with Bolivia

View 2 Images The referee came under attack after his controversial decision (Image: DAZN)

England's Under-15s found themselves at the centre of another controversy after a contentious penalty decision in their World Cup clash with Bolivia. Their South American opponents refused to face a last-minute spot kick, which saw the Young Lions claim a 3-2 victory.

‌



‌



The referee, who immediately blew the full-time whistle, then came under attack, with the England players rushing to his defence. He'd deemed a foul on West Ham's Emmanuel Famokun to have been in the box.

‌



The Bolivian players and staff were adamant that contact had been made outside the area, with the referee surrounded and one coach marching onto the pitch to point at where the foul had occurred. Multiple cards were issued but the decision stood.

‌



As a result, their goalkeeper leaned against his right-hand post and let Famokun score the penalty uncontested. England's players celebrated regardless, while the Bolivians once again directed their frustrations at the match official.

FIFA issue statement as England walk off pitch at U15 World Cup after alleged racism READ MORE :

Harry Kane makes knighthood admission as he sets out demand for name change READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

They sarcastically clapped before one made a beeline towards him, prompting the England players to run back and attempt to break up the skirmish. The referee brandished a red card to the substitute who had tried to attack him before he was escorted away as tensions boiled over between the two sides.

‌



England's players were seen further angering their defeated opponents by celebrating in front of their bench, with FIFA officials attempting to calm the situation before the two sides were ultimately separated.

It comes days after the U15s walked off the pitch against the Republic of Ireland due to an allegation of racist abuse. The match was abandoned with Ireland leading 4-1 at the time after an England player accused one of the opposition of a discriminatory comment.

‌



View 2 Images England were allowed to score an uncontested last-minute winning penalty (Image: DAZN)

The FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival is a new tournament founded this year as part of the international governing body's commitment to promote youth football. Azerbaijan have been hosting the inaugural event, which started on October 22 and concludes on Saturday, October 31.

‌



Over 3,000 players from 189 FIFA member nations have been involved, with 8-a-side matches and 20-minute halves. England have beaten Nicaragua, Montenegro, Cambodia, Zimbabwe, El Salvador and Georgia, while they've suffered defeat against Zambia and Turkey.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher makes U-turn on Liverpool title chances after 'inconceivable' Man City charges
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher makes U-turn on Liverpool title chances after 'inconceivable' Man City charges

Jamie Carragher has reversed his initial stance on Liverpool's Premier League title chances under Andoni Iraola this season ahead of their game against Arsenal

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has changed his stance on Liverpool's title chances (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Jamie Carragher has changed his original position on Liverpool's title prospects under Andoni Iraola, having initially cast doubt on whether the Spaniard could handle the transition to managing one of England's elite clubs. This follows ongoing speculation surrounding Manchester City's 115 financial rule breaches, with Carragher claiming it is 'inconceivable' that a substantial punishment wouldn't affect their ability to win the Premier League title.

‌



‌



Iraola joined Anfield in the summer after a remarkable three-year tenure at Bournemouth, where he garnered considerable acclaim for his achievements on the south coast. Nevertheless, with his Premier League credentials confined to a club beyond the established big six, questions remained about whether he could reproduce that form at Liverpool.

‌



The 44-year-old has delivered four wins from his first eight Premier League fixtures, while Liverpool have also enjoyed a flawless start to their Champions League campaign, triumphing in all three matches to occupy third place in the table.

‌



Carragher reckons that any substantial points deduction imposed on City could effectively eliminate them from the Premier League title race, potentially offering Liverpool a stronger chance to regain the trophy they secured under Arne Slot during the 2024/25 campaign.

5 Brazilian wonderkids Liverpool's new transfer chief may attempt to sign READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Although Carragher now believes his former club have a realistic chance to challenge for the title ahead of the weekend fixture with Arsenal, he acknowledged he initially harboured doubts about Iraola's appointment and whether the Spaniard could succeed at the elite level.

‌



Writing in his column for The Telegraph, Carragher explained: "I count myself as one of those on a journey with Iraola from initial scepticism following his appointment towards cautious optimism having seen his vision starting to take shape. My fear at the start of the season was that Liverpool employed a manager who had never won a trophy, nor managed in European competition.

"These did not strike me as solid credentials for a job of such stature. It felt like a gamble to opt for someone who would have to learn how to manage a big club rather than arrive ready-made. There was a lot to do, and some unanswered questions about what made Iraola the standout candidate, particularly given those who picked him – Michael Edwards and Richard Hughes – were about to announce their own departure as chief executive and sporting director, respectively."

‌



View 2 Images Iraola's Liverpool are title contenders says Carragher (Image: Getty Images)

Yet as the campaign has unfolded, Carragher has changed his position. The Liverpool legend explained: "There are several reasons why there are those who believe Iraola's side might push Arsenal closer than anticipated.

‌



"First and foremost, the guilty verdict in the Manchester City case has altered the complexion of the season, and emboldened those who want to seize the initiative. When Iraola replaced Arne Slot last summer, it was difficult to envisage how Liverpool could get past both Arsenal and City within a year.

"Now we expect City to be punished soon. Given the nature and severity of their misdemeanours it is inconceivable they will be a title contender if that happens. The door is open for those in the chasing pack with the capacity and will to walk through it.

Article continues below

"But if Iraola repeats Slot's Premier League success during his Anfield career, Hughes and Edwards can expect more applause for getting it right for a successive time having done so when Jurgen Klopp left. Iraola has made a fine start in eradicating doubts about his relative inexperience."

Sports.title: Harry Maguire has already given Man Utd green light for blockbuster January transfer
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire has already given Man Utd green light for blockbuster January transfer

Harry Maguire has given his seal of approval

View 2 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin has emerged as a target for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are reportedly eyeing up a move for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, whose qualities have previously impressed Harry Maguire. With problems persisting at the top of the pitch, the Red Devils are keen to strengthen their frontline in January and the Leeds striker is one of several names under consideration.

‌



‌



The 29-year-old has been on Manchester United's radar for some time and, according to The Athletic, recruitment staff are trying to establish whether a move for him is possible when the transfer window opens in two months.

‌



Maguire would likely welcome the prospect of playing alongside Calvert-Lewin, having spoken highly of the striker during his time at Everton. Back in 2021, the former United captain warned his team-mates about the threat posed by the England international ahead of a clash against the Toffees.

‌



"I know Dom from our time with England and he's very physical and a handful," Maguire said. "We'll need to be right on our game to keep him quiet."

Youri Tielemans sends message to board with Man Utd players' feelings on Michael Carrick clear READ MORE :

Man Utd manager agreement 'reached' over three options as Roy Keane gets approval READ MORE :

Calvert-Lewin scored 16 Premier League goals that season, the best return of his career. He struggled to maintain those standards during the final years of his Everton spell, but has rediscovered his goalscoring touch since joining Leeds in 2025.

The striker netted 14 times in 35 league appearances during the 2025/26 campaign and has already scored four goals this season, including one against Manchester United earlier this month.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

By contrast, United's primary No. 9, Benjamin Sesko, has scored just one Premier League goal this season and only three in the competition since mid-March. The Slovenian joined from RB Leipzig in a £70million deal last year but has struggled to establish himself as a regular starter.

‌



Instead, manager Michael Carrick has preferred using Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha as makeshift centre forwards. With Sesko also sidelined by a shin injury until the New Year, United are short of options in attack and could look to add reinforcements in January.

Other names reportedly on their shortlist include Jean-Philippe Mateta, Igor Matanovic and Victor Osimhen. Marcus Rashford is another potential option, although the England international has predominantly been deployed on the left wing.

‌



View 2 Images Harry Maguire is a fan of Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Image: Getty Images)

Calvert-Lewin, however, appears to be emerging as a leading candidate, with United's interest in the Leeds forward having gathered momentum ahead of the January window.

‌



A move would be particularly sensitive given the historic rivalry between Leeds United and Manchester United. Players switching between the two clubs have rarely been welcomed by supporters, with Eric Cantona, Rio Ferdinand and Alan Smith among those to have made the controversial move in the past.

Leeds currently sit nine places and four points above Manchester United in the Premier League table. United head into the weekend down in 16th, just one point clear of the relegation zone, while Leeds occupy seventh spot and are only four points adrift of the Champions League places.

Sports.title: Leclerc dominates Mexico City GP first practice
Sports.content:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was fastest from champion-elect Kimi Antonelli in first practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Leclerc was 0.659s quicker than Antonelli to underline the expectation that Ferrari will be strong at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez due to their small turbo working well at high altitude.

Lewis Hamilton was fourth after a scruffy soft-tyre lap but will be buoyed by his team-mate's pace as Ferrari look to win only their third race of the season.

It should not majorly impact Antonelli on the weekend where he is likely to become world champion on Sunday as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure the drivers' title.

Ten rookies replaced the usual full-time drivers in first practice as most teams took advantage of the relative simplicity of the circuit and it not being a Sprint weekend to fulfil a regulation that a rookie most run in both cars at least twice in the season - only Ferrari ran both regular drivers in the session.

Mercedes reserve driver and 2023 Formula 2 runner-up Frederik Vesti was the best of the rookies in third, less than one tenth behind Antonelli, and Ayumu Iwasa impressed in Max Verstappen's Red Bull in fifth, less than one second off the pace on the medium tyres.

Sports.title: Zverev repeats Wimbledon victory over Fery to reach Vienna semi-finals
Sports.content:
Alexander Zverev repeated his Wimbledon victory over Britain's Arthur Fery in the quarter-finals of the Vienna Open.

Fery's dream run at the All England Club this summer came to an end against Zverev in the semi-finals and the German was ruthless again, eliminating Fery in two quick sets.

Fery was outclassed by the top seed at the event, losing 6-0 6-2.

Reigning French Open and US Open champion Zverev is set to replace Jannik Sinner as world No 1 on Monday.

The 29-year-old, who will become the second German man to top the rankings after Boris Becker in 1991, hit 19 winners as he breezed through in just 59 minutes.

Zverev revealed he had struggled to sleep on Thursday night after securing his rise above Sinner in the global standings by beating Dutchman Tallon Griekspoor in the last 16.

He will face either Matteo Berrettini or fifth seed Alex de Minaur in his 12th semi-final of the year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz and Fery reflect on winning the Laver Cup with Team Europe

"I definitely felt good," Zverev said in his on-court interview. "I think Arthur is a bit of a different opponent than I had yesterday, he doesn't have the same firepower but he plays tactically extremely well and he's extremely fast.

"I feel like when I have the ball on the racket like that it's just a good day for me. He has the score 6-0 6-2 but he shouldn't put himself down too much, he's 35 in the world, it's his first full year on tour, and he's doing amazing things.

"For him, I hope he keeps his head up and continues the work he's doing."

Medvedev into ATP Finals

Daniil Medvedev secured a place at the ‌season-ending ATP Finals for the seventh time after overwhelming Adrian Mannarino 6-2 ‌6-3 to also reach the Vienna Open semi-finals.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniil Medvedev lets his frustration out on the court during his match against Cameron Norrie at the Vienna Open

The ​30-year-old Russian, who missed out on the season finale last year after qualifying ​every year from 2019 to 2024, ‌joins Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton in the eight-man ​field.

Sinner has also qualified but will not compete due to injury, leaving four places still ​available.

Medvedev has enjoyed a resurgent season ⁠in which he has surpassed ⁠the 50-win mark for the first time since 2023 and claimed four ‌titles.

Medvedev took control early against Mannarino with a break of serve and eased through the opening ‌set.

The former US Open champion broke again at 3-3 in the second set and closed out the match with another break.

Medvedev will next face Alcaraz, who ⁠defeated Tommy Paul 6-4 7-6 (7-2).

Sports.title: Rickelton, Mulder hit tons as South Africa set Australia 288 to win decider
Sports.content:
Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder struck centuries as South Africa were bowled out ‌for 387 to close day four of the decisive third Test against Australia, setting the touring ​side a victory target of 288 on the final day.

Australia toiled, taking a single wicket in the opening two sessions before a burst after tea, but ​it was still very much the home side's day and sets up ‌an intriguing tussle on Saturday.

Mulder top-scored with 115, his fourth Test century, while Rickelton amassed 101 as the pair ensured Australia ​will need to complete the second-highest successful run chase in 137 years of Test cricket at Newlands.

"It was about trying to win the small moments," Rickelton said. "We knew we ​were effectively 40 for four this morning and that Australia would come hard ⁠at us.

"It was about spending time at the ⁠crease rather than worrying about scoring runs or getting too far ahead of ourselves. We had our plans and needed to stick to them.

"We ‌knew the longer we batted, the more frustrated Australia would become. Perhaps they expected things to happen quite quickly because of the deteriorating wicket."

The pitch is starting to show signs of wear, ‌with Australia batter Josh Inglis saying on Thursday a chase of over 200 would be a difficult one batting last.

They will need considerably more than that at more than three runs an over against a South African bowling attack that has had its feet up for more than a day and a half.

South Africa ⁠resumed on the fourth morning at 140-4 and lost only ​Matthew Breetzke (43) in two sessions as he fell to a pull shot ​off Pat Cummins (2-71) and was caught on the boundary by Mitchell Starc, a familiar mode of dismissal for the home ​side this Test.

Sports.title: Carrick's last chance? The fixes Man Utd may need at Chelsea
Sports.content:
You would be forgiven for wondering how much longer Michael Carrick will remain in the Manchester United dugout.

A run of eight games without a win has left Carrick searching for answers, with the performances raising as many questions as the results.

The energy and organisation of his interim spell last season has been replaced by a team struggling to find their identity.

Chelsea away is next on Saturday. Carrick needs to find solutions, and quickly. But what can he actually change?

Stop the high press and make United harder to play through

One of the biggest problems facing Carrick is that Manchester United are making life too easy for their opponents.

The intention to be more aggressive out of possession is understandable, but the execution has been off. United have repeatedly been pulled out of position, with gaps opening between the forward line and midfield that opponents have exploited to progress through the centre or find space out wide.

United are among the Premier League's most frequent users of a high block, employing it for 36 per cent of opposition build-up phases. Only Tottenham and Liverpool have used it more often, with Manchester City level with United.

But pressing high is one thing, making it work is another. United have won the ball high up the pitch 52 times this season, but only 10 of those occasions have led to a shot. They have yet to score from one.

Defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como exposed those weaknesses. United's attempts to press have lacked the coordination and intensity required to make the approach effective, leaving defenders exposed when the first line is bypassed.

Bruno Fernandes questioned the decision not to press man to man against Como, arguing that opponents were being given too much time to build attacks. But the answer is not necessarily to press higher and harder. United must first establish a structure they can execute consistently.

There were encouraging signs against Leeds, when Carrick's side looked more disciplined and compact, even if they could not turn a 1-1 draw into victory.

There is also a wider issue with United's defensive shape. They have spent just 56.5 minutes in a high defensive compactness structure this season, the 18th-lowest figure in the Premier League.

A similar approach to the Leeds game at Chelsea would make sense. United need shorter distances between their defensive and midfield lines, better protection in central areas and a clearer understanding of when to engage.

Until United can defend as a unit, their tactical confusion will continue.

Fernandes must return to the starting XI

Leaving Fernandes on the bench against Bournemouth was a significant decision, particularly after the captain questioned United's tactics following the Champions League defeat to Como.

Carrick insisted it was a football decision, but the midfielder's absence was impossible to ignore as United suffered another damaging defeat. Fernandes was not even introduced as the situation deteriorated, leaving questions over whether the decision was based purely on performance or also reflected a power play from Carrick.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Warren Barton was on the Premier League show panel to discuss how Carrick can unlock the best out of Bruno Fernandes

The clear-the-air talks between the pair this week appear to have drawn a line under the disagreement. Carrick has reiterated that Fernandes remains captain and said the club can move forward together.

There is no guarantee Fernandes alone can transform United's fortunes. His own performances have not consistently reached the levels of last season, and the team cannot continue relying on individual quality to compensate for collective shortcomings.

However, he remains one of United's most influential players, capable of creating chances, progressing possession and providing the decisive pass in transition. When he is on song, his ability to connect midfield and attack is particularly important when United struggle to break down organised defences.

Carrick needs his best players on the pitch, especially when results are this poor. If Fernandes is fit and ready, leaving him out again would be difficult to justify.

Turn to youth?

What is ironic about Manchester United's recent struggles is that the senior players Carrick relied on during his impressive interim spell last season are now struggling to deliver the same levels of performance.

Image: Shea Lacey's only start this season came during Man Utd's Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton

Fernandes must return to the starting XI but reinstating the captain should not mean ignoring the youngsters who could inject some much-needed energy into a team that has looked short of intensity and conviction.

Harry Amass impressed during pre-season and deserves an opportunity to compete for a place at left-back. With United struggling to find consistency in that position, there is a case for giving the youngster a chance to show what he can offer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lacey scored an incredible goal against Brighton

Shea Lacey is another option. The 19-year-old has had limited opportunities since scoring in the Carabao Cup against Brighton, but has shown the enthusiasm and willingness to take responsibility that United have lacked at times.

Introducing young players is not a solution to every problem, and throwing them into a struggling side comes with its own risks. But if experienced players are not delivering, Carrick must be willing to look elsewhere.

Fernandes can provide the quality to complement that youthful energy. United need a balance of experience and enthusiasm - and Carrick should not be afraid to give the next generation an opportunity to make their mark.

Go back to basics and stop moving players around

Man Utd this season appear to be spending as much time adapting to new positions as they are trying to find form.

Diogo Dalot has operated at both right-back and left-back, while Leny Yoro has been used at right-back as well as centre-back. Mason Mount has featured on the right, and Youri Tielemans, previously viewed as a deeper-lying midfielder, has recently been pushed into more advanced positions.

Further forward, Matheus Cunha has been asked to operate from the left and through the middle, while Bryan Mbeumo has predominantly featured on the right despite producing some of his best football centrally last season.

Players out of position? Square pegs in round holes? How familiar does that sound?

There are understandable reasons for some of these changes, including injuries and the need to find a winning combination. But the constant reshuffling has made it difficult for United to establish consistent partnerships and give players a settled understanding of their roles.

Carrick's willingness to experiment was one of the positives of his interim spell, especially in the transition away from what Ruben Amorim was often critiqued for.

Against Chelsea, he needs to identify the strongest available XI and give players the best opportunity to perform in positions that suit them. That does not mean abandoning tactical adjustments, but United need a reliable foundation before they can start building something more ambitious.
