Sports.title: HYROX world-record holder who unapologetically soiled herself mid-race U-turns to admit she was wrong to put rivals at risk
Sports.content:
HYROX world-record holder who unapologetically soiled herself mid-race U-turns to admit she was wrong to put rivals at risk

The HYROX athlete who soiled herself mid-race before going on to win has opened up on unwittingly becoming the centre of a global story and finally admitted she was wrong to put rivals at risk.

Joanna Wietrzyk, a 24-year-old Australian endurance competitor, performed while suffering bowel incontinence caused by food poisoning while using equipment shared with other competitors at the race in Beijing last month.

Footage at the time showed the HYROX world record holder running, doing burpees and carrying heavy bags with excrement running down her leg.

While organisers apologised at the time, the athlete herself opted not to show remorse, until making a U-turn and apologising on Thursday.

Wietrzyk says she has experienced a 'traumatic' backlash following the incident and suffered personal abuse but accepted she should not have continued racing.

She told the BBC: 'It was a very sudden experience. It wasn't until about halfway through the race where everything did transpire.

Joanna Wietrzyk apologised for continuing to race after soiling herself at a HYROX event

Wietrzyk posted an image to Instagram from her hospital bed after the race - but her victory has sparked backlash and it took two months for any show of contrition

'In that moment, right then and there, as a very competitive person… and an elite athlete that I am, my only focus is on racing. Obviously I did put other people at risk.'

She added: 'Yes, I did make the wrong decision but I don't believe I should have received such backlash and such scrutiny online. At the end of the day I'm only human.'

Wietrzyk did not offer contrition after the event, posting on Instagram from her hospital bed: 'Go hard or go home they say... a win is a win. In all seriousness, thank you all for the support. I'll be back soon.'

HYROX bosses apologised and pledged to implement immediate rule changes but the athlete herself took longer.

When questioned over why she took more than a month to then say sorry and whether it was an attempt to rehabilitate her image, she said: 'I needed those days to reflect on it and process it.'

In an Instagram video shared on Thursday, Wietrzyk said: 'So I've had some time to reflect over the past six to eight weeks of everything that happened in Beijing.

'And, I just want to say that I'm truly, truly so sorry to everyone that I affected, whether they were spectators or participants out on that race floor for my decision to choose to continue to race.'

The Melbourne athlete won the women's HYROX Pro event in Beijing in 1:01:23, but footage of her continuing through the course prompted questions about why officials had allowed her to remain in the race.

Images showed faecal matter running down her legs as she competed at stations involving communal equipment.

Joanna Wietrzyk apologised for continuing to race after soiling herself at a HYROX event

The incident placed organisers under scrutiny, with fellow competitors raising concerns about hygiene, contamination and the speed of the response.

HYROX said affected lanes were isolated, contaminated equipment was removed and cleaning and carpet replacement took place overnight before competition resumed.

Wietrzyk faced personal abuse, prompting HYROX to warn that people directing abuse or threats of violence towards her would be banned from future events.

Her coach, Chris Bayens, defended her against attacks while acknowledging that decisions made during the event could be reviewed.

'Decisions were made under competition conditions by an athlete, judges and officials, all responding to a situation none of them could reasonably have prepared for,' he wrote on Instagram.

'It is very easy to construct the perfect response once the moment has passed. Hindsight gives people time, information and distance that simply did not exist for those actually living it.'

Australian fitness star Wietrzyk won her event despite suffering bowel incontinence

Wietrzyk said she was ‘super excited’ to get back on the race floor and do what she loves

Bayens urged people to distinguish scrutiny of the incident from attacks on the athlete.

'Sport occasionally produces moments that are imperfect and deeply human,' he said. 'Discussion is legitimate. The hatred and personal attacks that have followed are not.'

HYROX combines eight one-kilometre runs with eight workout stations, including sled pushes, rowing, sandbag lunges and medicine ball throws.

Wietrzyk's next scheduled appearance is in the opening race of the 2026-27 HYROX Elite Series in Hamburg on Friday, October 30.

Sports.title: PREMIER LEAGUE LIVE: Xabi Alonso on Estevao's future with Chelsea, Roberto De Zerbi confirms James Maddison IS available for Tottenham - and Andoni Iraola on why Liverpool fans can dream
Sports.content:
LIVE PREMIER LEAGUE LIVE: Xabi Alonso on Estevao's future with Chelsea, Roberto De Zerbi confirms James Maddison IS available for Tottenham - and Andoni Iraola on why Liverpool fans can dream

It's another action-packed Premier League weekend ahead and the managers have been having their say. Follow the best of it here with Daily Mail Sport...

Xabi Alonso discusses Estevao's future with Chelsea

Xabi Alonso insists there are zero talks being held inside Chelsea about allowing Estevao to leave in January on loan for game time, despite the Brazilian wonderkid struggling for chances to impress.

The 19-year-old stayed sat on the bench during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup shootout-loss to Liverpool on Wednesday. In the Premier League, he has been a late substitute six times, and unused twice. It has seen questions asked of Alonso’s plan for a highly-promising talent.

There is no shortage of rivals who would be willing to take Estevao temporarily. As revealed by Daily Mail Sport this week, multiple clubs at home and abroad are watching his situation.

Before Manchester United visit Stamford Bridge for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off, Alonso was asked if they would consider finding him a temporary home in this winter window.

‘No, no, no,’ Alonso said. ‘No discussions about that. The season is long and there will be moments for everyone. It's a process for the team, for Este, for myself, but I'm sure that in the season, he will have his games, his minutes. We are still early in the season, but he will be there.

Xabi Alonso insists Chelsea are not discussing sending Estevao out on loan in January

‘It's not about attitude. It's been about the context of games, it's been about the start of the season, and he's a great guy. We are still in October and he will be important.’

Chelsea fans feel as if they have heard this before, and then watched as he failed to come on as a substitute in their Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool. The Blues signed Estevao from Palmeiras for £29million rising to £55m, and he is tied down to a deal lasting into the 2030s.

He had some magic moments in his first season, including scoring a stoppage-time winner against Liverpool in the Premier League and upstaging Lamine Yamal of Barcelona in the Champions League. His lack of opportunities this term has come as a surprise to supporters, who sang his name at Anfield, and led to speculation in Brazil that the youngster is frustrated.

‘It is no secret that all players want to be on the pitch,’ Alonso added. ‘When any of them haven't had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that, that they are not as happy as they could be. But everyone has to be ready because in any game, they could be important, they could be part of the team, and Este, his training and his attitude has been good.

‘We are back in Premier League mode, and that is, for me, the main competition for us this year, and it's a big one. It's one that we didn't have that much time to prepare, but it's really important after the last home game that we had (a 2-0 loss to Tottenham).’

Meanwhile, Maxence Lacroix has a hamstring injury which will sideline him for several weeks. Moises Caicedo and Pep Chavarria are fit to face United, but Jorrel Hato is injured. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez may return sooner than expected – perhaps even before the international break – as Alonso said: ‘In case he's ready to play, he will need a face mask probably.’

KIERAN GILL

Enzo Maresca hits back at 'lucky' claims against Brighton

Enzo Maresca has shrugged off Fabian Hurzeler’s thirst for revenge and the suggestion that Manchester City were lucky to beat Brighton in midweek as the managers face off for the second time in four days.

City progressed to the Carabao Cup quarter finals via penalties on Wednesday night, with the Brighton boss insistent that they had created more than enough to knock out the holders.

Maresca’s side are looking to open up an eight-point gap with the Seagulls, who are flying high in third. Hurzeler has confessed to being a ‘bad loser’ but has moved on from Wednesday night.

‘Revenge is more about him [Hurzeler] and not about us,’ the Italian said. ‘This is what he said. Every manager can say something different.

Enzo Maresca does not feel that his side were merely lucky to beat Brighton in midweek

‘It depends on what you see with your eyes. But I respect what he said. Probably the reason why it's so difficult to play against them is because they are always front foot, aggressive and their attack is also very good.’

Instead of returning to the south coast between fixtures, Brighton have remained in Manchester through the week and trained locally on Friday.

Maresca added: ‘If you see the Premier League games they have played, they scored three, four, five goals against any team. That's why I was so happy after Wednesday.

‘It's because yes, they scored two goals, they had some more chances. We also created chances. But we knew that it was a difficult test for us. We dealt quite well.’

Meanwhile, Maresca has claimed that no City star has a guaranteed place in his team despite revealing that shootout hero deputy Geronimo Rulli is not rivalling Gianluigi Donnarumma for the No 1 spot.

‘I think one thing is to say that in this moment Gigio is plus 10 others,’ he said. ‘And another thing is to say undroppable. Yes, there are two different things. There is no player who is undroppable. But in this moment it is Gigio plus 10. In this moment I see it like this.’

JACK GAUGHAN

Roberto De Zerbi on James Maddison's availability

Tottenham playmaker James Maddison is available for Saturday’s visit of Crystal Palace despite an injury scare during the victory at Chelsea.

Maddison sparked more fitness fears when he limped off in the 51st minute of Spurs’ 2-0 victory at Chelsea.

After Maddison had endured a slow start to the campaign with caution preached over his fitness following a May return from anterior cruciate ligament damage, his substitution last Saturday looked to be another setback.

But, ahead of the Palace game, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi said: 'James is available. This week he didn’t work like the other players, but for tomorrow he is available and he is a special player for us. A special player because of the character and he has unique characteristics.

James Maddison is available for Tottenham despite an injury scare suffered against Chelsea

'For James Maddison or the players who are coming from a long injury, they have to work more than the other players, but he has already four or five weeks he is working very hard and consistently.'

'So, I think it’s not a problem if he loses two days (training), but then we have to analyse if we take risk or not.

'If we take risk like Pedro Porro (against Aston Villa) or (Dejan) Kulusevski.

'We are lucky to have a big squad and it’s important to not take risk with new injuries.'

MATT BARLOW

Andoni Iraola: Fans can dream of Liverpool title challenge

Andoni Iraola is happy for Liverpool fans to start dreaming of a Premier League title challenge ahead of Sunday’s clash with champions Arsenal, but insisted it is too early for him to start looking at the table.

Victory at Anfield would see Liverpool move to within three points of the Gunners as they look to continue a five-match winning run in all competitions, but Iraola said his focus remains on improvements in performances early in his reign.

'It is still October,' Iraola said. 'We have to take one game at a time and I always say the reference is more or less when we’ve played against each other once so halfway through the season. That’s when you can start to look at the standings.

'Right now, we are in a position where we need to improve and keep getting better.'

Liverpool supporters are able to dream of winning the Premier League - but Andoni Iraola isn't getting ahead of himself

But when asked if he welcomed the growing optimism amongst Liverpool supporters, Iraola added: 'For fans, it is good if they have expectations or they think we can win.'

Arsenal moved level with Manchester City at the top of the table last weekend with a 2-0 win over Everton, but were then on the wrong end of a huge cup upset in midweek, dumped out of the Carabao Cup when they were beaten on penalties by League Two Fleetwood.

'We know Arsenal and how good they are,' Iraola said. 'They have very good players, working a lot in synchronicity and we have to be ready for that challenge.

'It’s going to be a demanding game but we also trust our players, trust ourselves and in the good atmosphere we will for sure have on Sunday. I hope we will be at level to win this game.'

LEWIS STEELE

Sports.title: The Bushtucker dressing room! 'Woke' football club to make players change in a sea of 60 HOUSEPLANTS 'to reduce stress' - after banning meat pies and making their kit vegan
Sports.content:
Forest Green Rovers' changing room has undergone a dramatic transformation and been left looking more like an I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! set.

The National League football club, renowned for their quirky and unconventional approach and often branded the world's most 'woke' team, have installed more than 60 plants in a bid to improve the players' mental health.

Environmentalist owner Dale Vince – who is worth around £100million – has had his club team up with Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland and a psychologist in a bid to help the squad relax in what can be a high-pressure environment.

Footage of the new-look changing room shows greenery everywhere, with the lockers themselves filled by vegetation.

While it may appear to be Rovers' latest wacky publicity stunt, the club insist there is science behind their re-design.

A statement on the carbon-neutral football club's website explained: '30% of Brits report that having living houseplants in a room noticeably lowers their stress levels and restores a sense of calm.

Forest Green Rovers have installed 60 plants in their changing room to reduce stress

The club are renowned for their environmental practices and quirky schemes

'Despite this, ‘plant paranoia’ is holding many back, with over a quarter of Brits (27%) put off by buying greenery because they are terrified the plants will die despite their best efforts.

'To prove that introducing greenery doesn't have to be a high-stress commitment, Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland is testing the theory in one of the most notoriously stressful indoor environments possible: an elite football changing room.'

The move coincides with International Stress Awareness Week ahead of their fixture against Harrogate and Dr Josephine Perry, a sports psychologist, said: 'Living greenery acts as a natural buffer, actively reducing nervous system arousal, which helps sharpen our cognitive abilities, allowing us to focus and perform better.

'Adding greenery to high-pressure spaces is one of the simplest, low-effort and accessible habits anyone can adopt to stay in control when the pressure mounts.'

Vince posted a video on X on Friday morning explaining: 'Up early this morning doing TV interviews. I'll show you what it's all about, it's in the changing room, all about plants. There's a little bit about Peterborough as well, the news that we have begun a legal process for the tapping up of our ex-manager Robbie Savage. That's the day so far, plants and what would you call it... hassle.'

He then moves into the newly decorated changing room and says: 'Here it is, chock full of plants. Quite chilling, really.'

Regarding the Savage lawsuit, Peterborough chairman Darragh MacAnthony previously denied that his side had made an illegal approach. Vince told Sky Sports on Friday: 'We're suing Peterborough and Robbie Savage for two million quid which was the buyout clause we were cheated out of and that process started last week.'

Controversial owner Vince, praised by some for his eco-focus and dismissed by others for what they perceive as 'woke' management, has found his club in the spotlight on numerous occasions for their unorthodox practices.

Their kits are made from recycled, sustainable materials and are officially certified as vegan.

The food in the canteen is completely vegan, with players also provided with vegan meals to take with them to away matches. Meat is completely off the menu and everything provided to players, fans and staff is plant based.

The players are seen in their new environment, with plants in each locker space

Rovers' pitch is maintained without chemical pesticides, herbicides, or synthetic fertilizers and cut using solar-powered mowers.

There's even a urine filtration system from the away toilets that is used to irrigate and water the turf.

There are also plans to build a new stadium made of timber with the lowest carbon footprint of any ground in world football. The club also promote cycling to matches and have electric charging points at the ground.

Vince, an eco tycoon who made his money in renewable energy, came under fire earlier this year after the club often branded the world's 'wokeist' made the decision to scrap their women's team, hardly the most progressive move.

The Gloucestershire-based outfit are spending their third consecutive season in the fifth tier, having failed to achieve promotion back to League Two at the first time of asking.

The club reached a record high of League One in 2022 but suffered consecutive relegations, ending their seven-year stint in the English Football League in 2024.

Vince has chosen not to directly replace Savage, who left on October 2, instead opting for a three-man coaching team from existing staff.

Sports.title: Kumar Sangakkara opens up on Ryanair 'race storm': Cricket legend reveals how 'rude' Dublin staff berated him and his wife before boarding - as he submits 2,000-word complaint to budget airline
Sports.content:
Kumar Sangakkara has opened up on what he believes was the racist treatment he and his family received during an argument at check-in at Dublin airport after a member of Ryanair staff told them: ‘You people with your kinds of passports should expect this.’

Sangakkara, who scored 12,400 runs in a glittering 134-Test career with Sri Lanka, was preparing to fly back to Bristol following a two-day trip to celebrate his 49th birthday when he says he was spoken to rudely by a woman at the check-in desk following confusion over an e-visa.

He says he went out of his way to make ‘doubly sure’ he was following the correct procedure with his family’s Sri Lankan passports.

But despite being assured two hours earlier by staff at the visa check desk that he didn’t need to reproduce the e-visas on his mobile phone at the boarding gate – a process that can take several minutes – and despite already clearing security, he was still told to step aside and download the e-visas after he arrived at the gate.

Sangakkara told Daily Mail Sport: ‘I said to one of the lady’s colleagues, “I will do this, but it is a bit of a procedure.” I also said: “We went to your visa desk just to avoid this confusion. They gave us one message, and it’s a bit confusing to passengers. But give us time.”

Kumar Sangakkara has hit out at Ryanair over an alleged racism storm at Dublin Airport

The cricket legend claims a member of staff berated him and his wife during boarding

‘As I was accessing the e-visa on the side, this lady from behind the desk raised her voice so the entire area could hear and said: “Hurry up! Hurry up! You have to do this quickly, otherwise I’m going to close boarding. Hurry up and get this done. Step aside now.” Sangakkara asked for more time to access the e-visas, only to be told once again to hurry up, at which point he told the lady she was being ‘very rude’.

He says she responded by saying he was being ‘argumentative and aggressive’, adding: ‘I’m going to treat you as a threat to other passengers on board and not board you.’

Sangakkara says: ‘And then she made the comment that you people with your kinds of passports should expect this.’

At this point, Sangakkara’s wife, Yehali, said: ‘You do realise what you said is so offensive, right? We are trying to access our passports, and you are shouting at us here in front of all these people. And you just made a very offensive comment. We’ve had such a good trip to Dublin, met such nice people. The only rude person we have met is you.’

The Sangakkaras were eventually allowed to board, but not before Kumar asked for the lady’s name so he could register a formal complaint. He says she replied: ‘I don’t have to give you my name. And if you keep asking for this, I’m not going to board you because I will consider you a threat.

‘Then my wife explained step by step why we were in Ireland, all of which she didn’t even have to do. But she was very calm, very measured, and she explained to her how rude it was, how offensive her remark was, because to us, I would take that as a very racist comment.

Sangakkara has filed a 2,000-word complaint to the budget airline over his treatment

‘Ryanair said I had refused to show my visa, which is completely untrue. I would completely understand if I had been an a** and refused, but I never play the race card for the sake of it, and this was an offensive comment.’

Earlier, Ryanair had insisted: ‘This passenger refused to provide the required visa documentation when requested by a gate agent carrying out mandatory immigration checks. Following completion of these checks and verification of this passenger’s eligibility to travel, this passenger travelled on this scheduled flight from Dublin to Bristol (28 Oct).’

Sangakkara has since filled out a Ryanair complaint form, explaining in 2,000 words the events of Wednesday, and says he was told to expect a response from the airline within eight days.

He added: ‘We had a lovely time in Dublin. It’s a beautiful city and we had two great days. And this one person on the way back does this, and then says that I refused to show my visas. It is a very bad representation.

‘I didn’t go into this looking for any publicity. It’s just a case of this is wrong, and it shouldn’t have happened – to me or to anyone.’

Sports.title: Jack Grealish has let his team-mates down: This self-inflicted episode shows he lacks the hard graft and humility so desired by David Moyes - and the team were better off without him, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Hard graft, humility and fighting for team-mates: three qualities not shown by a certain Jack Grealish this week. They are also a trio of traits demanded by the Premier League's most experienced boss, David Moyes, who banished the once £100million man Grealish to the naughty step for missing training without permission. News of his latest act of ill-discipline dominated every conversation on the Merseyside waterfront before this full-blooded contest with Newcastle but Grealish was not missed a jot as his youthful and energetic replacements put on a show. Goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry were enough to send Moyes and Co to the Carabao Cup quarter-final and within sight of their first trophy since 1995, something the 63-year-old boss and these loyal fans crave above anything. Moyes made the decision to drop and fine Grealish alongside chief executive Angus Kinnear. It is unknown if he will return for Monday's league game, also against Newcastle. The boss would not comment on the situation but said he supported the club decision to drop him. 'The one thing about Everton is that we have got really good values behind it,' he said. 'All the players stand up to the values and accept the values, on the pitch and off the pitch. Jack Grealish let his Everton team-mates down, with the star suffering another setback 'From that point of view, I think the players did a brilliant job. It's a small squad we have got, we are limited in some areas but we are doing our best to keep challenging. You can see what it meant to the supporters, this is a big moment for them. There's humility about us tonight.' Giant-slayers Fleetwood Town are up next. Given the way they toppled champions Arsenal on Tuesday, that will be no easy feat, but a trip to Highbury is all that stands between the Toffees and a first domestic cup semi-final since 2015-16. Newcastle, meanwhile, look a pale imitation of the great team that beat Liverpool to win this competition in 2025 and the jury remains out on Matthias Jaissle. He lambasted his side's lack of maturity and said: 'It is shocking and it is frustrating as well. 'You need to be more mature and more clinical in these situations. Just clear it. It is a learning process but we don't have the time, we need to learn fast, especially with these young lads which is not an excuse any more.' Fans around the country have tended to see the Carabao Cup as a chance to save some money in recent years and Everton supporters have grumbled at Moyes and former boss Sean Dyche for having a similar attitude with line-ups. But a full house of 51,894 here – including 8,000 of the travelling Toon army – indicated that both teams were taking this seriously. Both mid-table with inconsistent form, this was a real chance for success. Even the Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, knew that and was in attendance alongside his wife Marie-France. There was an obvious joke to be made around this week's budget, which has given a helping hand to those in need this winter. Given the Grealish-shaped hole in Moyes's team and the obvious lack of numbers in multiple positions, the Everton top brass might have fancied getting in Burnham's ear to get the chancellor's phone number and ask for a leg-up too. Hackney volleyed in his first goal for the club following his summer move from Middlesbrough Thierno Barry added Everton's third in the second half to set-up a tie against Fleetwood Town Matthias Jaissle's side will seek revenge when the sides meet again in the league on Monday Prime Minister Andy Burnham was among those celebrating as Everton bid to end their trophy drought Moyes has had to muddle through the season with a dearth of outfielders following a botched transfer window, but he has made the best of a tricky situation – one that was not helped by Grealish's actions. Any frustration at those off-the-field issues was parked on the night, though, as Everton found themselves two ahead at half-time. It was a scoreline to leave Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle cursing after a string of missed chances. MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS EVERTON (4-2-3-1): Pickford 7; Rohl 6, Tarkowski 7, O'Brien 7, Mykolenko 7 (Maitland-Niles 86); Hackney 8, Garner 7; Dibling 7 (Johnson 77), Dewsbury-Hall 8 (Norgaard 86), George 8 (Alcaraz 77); Barry 7. Subs not used: Travers, King, Keane, Armstrong, Graham. Scorers: Garner 34, Hackney 45, Barry 69. Booked: Hackney, Dewsbury-Hall, Mykolenko, Pickford, Tarkowski. Manager: David Moyes 8. NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5, Schar 5, Burn 6, Hall 6; Gonzalez 5 (Steur 81), Ramsey 5 (Joelinton 46); Murphy 5 (Toure 67, 6), Willock 5, Barnes 7 (Elanga 46, 6); Osula 5 (Wissa 46, 6). Subs not used: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Thiaw. Scorers: Burn 88. Booked: Schar, Burn, Joelinton. Manager: Matthias Jaissle 5. Referee: Farai Hallam 7. Attendance: 51,894. As it was, Everton weathered the storm thanks to Jordan Pickford and several last-ditch blocks. Despite Newcastle's territorial advantages, the Toffees settled and were first to strike on 34 minutes. It came through Grealish's direct replacement for a starting berth, Tyrique George, winning possession and, via Hackney, feeding Garner to pass into the far corner. Hackney soon turned from provider to goal-scorer, although referee Farai Hallam might claim an assist. Good officiating saw him play an advantage when Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall was hauled down when charging goalwards. Barry picked up a loose ball and fed Hackney who volleyed home, making it look easy when he could have easily fired over the bar. Seconds earlier, Harvey Barnes had been denied by Pickford but Newcastle were undone by a motoring counter-attack. Moyes would be delighted with the two goals but arguably more buoyed by the defensive rearguard that followed. Jaissle responded by throwing on three half-time changes in Yoane Wissa, Joelinton and Anthony Elanga. None of them worked as Everton played with their hearts on their sleeves in a warrior-like defensive display that had this new stadium rocking like rarely before. James Tarkowski put his body on the line and Sunderland lad Pickford made several inspired stops. Barry put the icing on the cake on 69 minutes when Garner robbed Amar Dedic of possession and Dewsbury-Hall teed up the No9 to finish with composure and help his team one giant step closer to ending that trophy drought. No Grealish? No problem. The Manchester City loanee, who showed his admirable side earlier in the day when he gave £10,000 to help an ill fan, has let his team-mates down with this latest episode. But with a collection of young talents thriving, mixed with some soldier-like experienced heads and a boss with an appetite for silverware, Everton do not need Grealish right now. This night was one to forget for him and Jaissle's work-in-progress Newcastle, who are a shadow of the halcyon days of Eddie Howe's cup-winning side, despite pulling one back late on through captain Dan Burn's header. Everton fans including Mr Burnham, meanwhile, will have March 21 and a potential final at Wembley circled in their diaries.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola drops hint over double Liverpool injury boost for Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola drops hint over double Liverpool injury boost for Arsenal clash

Liverpool welcome Arsenal to Anfield on Sunday and the Reds could welcome back two players in what would be a boost for Andoni Iraola's side and their chances of beating the Premier League champions

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola has provided an update (Image: This Is Anfield)

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says that Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz could be available for Sunday's clash with Arsenal. Szoboszlai and Munoz have both been missing since the Reds' 2-1 win away to Brentford earlier this month.

Iraola's side have won all three games in their absence, but the pair would provide extra firepower when the Premier League champions rock up at Anfield with injury concerns of their own. "I think they have a chance," the Liverpool manager replied when asked about Szoboszlai and Munoz.

"But I don't know for sure if they will be involved or not. We still have two days, so I think they have a chance, yes."

Liverpool will, however, be without Jeremie Frimpong until after the November international break. Meanwhile, Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Hugo Ekitike remain sidelined with long-term injuries.

"We have a training session tomorrow, let's see if he can complete the full session. After that, we will know if he's available."

Sports.title: The teenagers hoping to beat Luke Littler and win £501k as harsh Netflix reality emerges
Sports.content:
The teenagers hoping to beat Luke Littler and win £501k as harsh Netflix reality emerges

A total of 20 contestants will take on Luke Littler in a bid to win a cool £501,000 by beating the World No.1 in a single leg of darts - and some of them are teenagers

View 4 Images Netflix's Beat Luke Littler airs on Friday (Image: Netflix)

Five British teenagers have the chance to make history when they take part in the hotly anticipated 'Beat Luke Littler'. Exactly what it says on the tin, a total of 20 (whittled down from 24 on the night) amateurs, rising stars and avid darts fans have been chosen to face-off against the World No.1 live on Netflix at 7pm on Friday.

‌



‌



Should they beat Littler - still only 19 himself - over a single leg, they'll walk away with the staggering grand prize of £501,000. The two-time world champion, who's gone through a rough spell of form lately, is under pressure to deliver and keep the show as close to its three-hour runtime as possible.

‌



The harsh reality for viewers is that the action could be over inside three minutes if Littler loses his first match. He'll also be walking away with a healthy pay packet from Netflix regardless of how he performs.

‌



You might recognise a few of the contestants including Fallon Sherrock, who famously became the first woman win a match at the PDC World Championship in 2019. Lesser-known entrants include a Nando's restaurant manager, a bricklayer and a driving instructor.

But some of them aren't even old enough to have full-time jobs - nevermind be a professional darts player.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Makinley Cooper-Johnson, 14

"I respect Luke for what he's done. But at the end of the day, he knows he's good – but he doesn't know how good I am."

‌



That's quite the statement for a 14-year-old to make, but Makinley Cooper-Johnson is a confident lad. From Wrexham, 'Mighty Mak' was chosen by a panel which included darts icon Phil Taylor, who's been giving him tips on how to beat Littler.

"My best mate Phil! I was in bed half-asleep when Mum came in with the phone," Cooper-Johnson told BBC Wales. "When I heard who it was, I was out of bed, stood up, almost saluting, and he personally told me I had a place in the live show."

‌



The Welsh teenager added: "Look, I'm not saying I'm world class or anything, but I can hold my own. I've got a shot at this."

Will any of the contestants beat Luke Littler? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Jayden Walker, 14

The joint-youngest competitor, Jayden Walker, comes from Christchurch, Dorset and is no stranger to beating darts players with a World Championship on their CV. When he was just 12, Walker beat Luke Humphries by averaging 102.

‌



His remarkable performance prompted 2024 world champion Humphries to label Walker 'the best 12-year-old [player] I've ever seen in my life'. Despite being dubbed the 'next Luke Littler', Walker is level-headed and comes from a family who have their priorities in order.

"My mum always tells me I have to finish my homework before I can go out to a night of darts," he explained to Sky Sports. "Because I love darts so much, I sort of make myself do the homework.

‌



"[One of my favourite subjects is] maths - it helped me in darts, because during lockdown when I first started playing, I started focusing on it.

"The only schoolwork they set us was maths. I just did maths and all those mental arithmetics helped me with my game, with all the shots out."

‌



View 4 Images Jayden Walker gets his homework done before stepping up to the oche (Image: PA)

Mitchell Lawrie, 15

Hailing from the town of Renfrew in Scotland, Mitchell Lawrie is another darts prodigy. The 15-year-old has already won the World Youth Championship twice.

‌



While Lawrie admits that he'll be nervous when live on Netflix at such a young age, he's got the confidence of having beaten Littler before.

"It was at the World Cup junior darts in Gibraltar in 2023, Scotland against England and we beat the team that Luke Littler was in," he recalled to BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast.

‌



"We beat them 4-3 in a deciding leg and it's one of those memories that sticks with you forever. We also went on to win that tournament."

Will history repeat itself?

‌



View 4 Images Mitchell Lawrie was part of a team that beat Luke Littler in 2023 (Image: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock)

Kasey Smith, 16

The most local contestant, Kasey Smith won't far to travel in order to reach the Manchester Central Convention Complex. She's recently been chosen to play for Greater Manchester County Youth, reflecting how highly she's rated.

‌



What's more is that Smith has only been playing darts for a year, having been encouraged to take up the sport by a pub colleague. Previously, the 16-year-old was a competitive Morris dancer. Away from the oche, Smith is an aspiring criminologist.

View 4 Images Kasey Smith will have home support in Manchester (Image: gmdartscoaching/INSTAGRAM)

‌



Taylon Forrester, 18

Last but certainly not least, Taylon Forrester might boast the best nickname of all the contestants. A rubbish collector from Bedford, he's known as The Trash Man.

Should Forrester take home the jackpot, he'll fly his family to Jamaica to meet relatives they've never met. Forrester is also a huge fan of the The Inbetweeners has rewatched every episode.

Article continues below

He'll be hoping to tell his friends: "Beat Luke Littler? Completed it, mate."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta doubles down on Max Dowman anger and reveals new disappointment
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta doubles down on Max Dowman anger and reveals new disappointment

Max Dowman found himself sent off during Arsenal's loss to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday evening, with Mikel Arteta opening up on Michael Salisbury's decision

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has spoken about Max Dowman's red card (Image: Beanyman Sports)

Mikel Arteta has explained that he remains "very disappointed" that Max Dowman was sent off against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday evening. Arsenal suffered a shock penalty shootout loss to the Fishermen in the Carabao Cup, with the game having finished 1-1 in normal time.

‌



‌



Summer signing Bruno Guimaraes squandered a crucial spot kick, with Jay Lynch diving low and hard to his left to make the save. Conor Haughey then converted coolly to tip the shootout 5-3 in Fleetwood's favour, as the League Two side advanced to the quarter-finals.

‌



There, they will take on Everton on December 15. However, the shock defeat wasn't the only headline; Dowman's red card late on sent football fans into a frenzy. With just four minutes remaining, the 16-year-old was dispossessed by Harrison Neal on the byline, and the Fleetwood defender trapped Dowman's leg in the process.

‌



The teenager reacted instantly by kicking out at Neal, sparking a fracas among players. Salisbury then responded by brandishing a red card Dowman's way, with Arteta seemingly furious at the decision.

And now, the Spaniard has doubled down on his criticism of the official. Speaking in his pre-Liverpool press conference on Friday, he said: "Very disappointed to be fair especially with the reckless tackle that he received.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



"His reaction is minimal in compared to the action. It is what it is, we have put every argument on the table to make a case for it. Max's action is clear, obviously we have a very different opinion, you have to read into the context, the age, the player. It could have been really bad and we're really lucky today that he doesn't have a broken foot."

Speaking about his fiery reaction toward Dowman, meanwhile, Arteta added: "My reaction comes in a moment of heat and extreme frustration because I know the consequences of that, especially for Max. We discussed it just before we went out and it will continue happen unfortunately because of how he attracts opponents.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"He's 16 and we have to be very protective of him but also very straight with what we expect from him towards the team, individual and the clubs."

Arsenal had appealed the three-match ban that Dowman faces as a result of his red card, only to see their challenge rejected. His dismissal resulted from 'violent conduct,' which, according to the rules of the game, occurs when a participant "uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball."

‌



View 2 Images Max Dowman was sent off (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

It means that the midfielder will miss Sunday's trip to Anfield, as well as their upcoming matches against Hull City and Newcastle United. However, he is not the only expected absentee.

Article continues below

Bukayo Saka will miss the clash as a result of a muscular injury sustained during Arsenal's Champions League draw with Bayern Munich earlier this month. Arteta said of the winger: "He needed another scan to see the amount of fluid there was resolving, afterwards we will know more about it."

Sports.title: Jake Paul has ready-made excuse if he loses next boxing fight
Sports.content:
Jake Paul has ready-made excuse if he loses next boxing fight

YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul will end a year-long hiatus after revealing he is set to make a return to the boxing ring later this year

View Image Jake Paul after being knocked down against Anthony Joshua (Image: Ed Mulholland, Getty Images for Netflix)

Jake Paul already has an excuse in his back pocket should he fall short in his return to boxing later this year.

‌



‌



The YouTuber-turned-boxer revealed he will be making a stunning comeback - a year after breaking his jaw against Anthony Joshua. Paul has been recovering since his brutal sixth-round knockout defeat to the former two-time heavyweight world champion.

‌



Over the last few months, the American has been spotted back in training and seemingly has the itch to compete again. The 29-year-old took to social media to announce that he will be fighting on Christmas Eve in Dubai - with an opponent yet to be officially confirmed.

‌



Speaking of his comeback, he said: "I've spent years proving people wrong, taking risks, and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I'd face. Nothing that's happened has changed my belief in myself or what I'm working toward. I'm hungrier than ever, and on Thursday, December 24, I'm returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

FOLLOW OUR FIGHTING FB PAGE! Latest boxing and MMA news, analysis and much more via our dedicated Facebook page

"Dubai is a city that thinks big, breaks boundaries, and doesn't believe in limits. That's exactly the kind of place I want to make my comeback. We've got plenty of names on the list; let's see who signs the contract. Merry Christmas, Dubai. Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody's getting knocked out."

‌



But Paul has some very bad memories of the Middle East - having suffered his first professional career loss to Tommy Fury in Saudi Arabia three years ago. Despite scoring a knockdown in the dying embers of the Saudi showcase, it was not enough to get the nod on points.

And rather than accepting the defeat, Paul claimed he struggled to physically adapt to the conditions during his training camp in Dubai - which he believes ultimately led to his demise on fight night against his bitter rival in Diriyah. "I was going through things outside the gym," Paul told Stephen A Smith.

‌



"A breakup, mentally, getting sick. Not being on point and trying to jam pack a camp in six or seven weeks, there just wasn't enough time for someone at my level to prepare. I get to Dubai and there's dust in the air that I'm apparently allergic to, so I'm sick for another 10 days.

Anthony Joshua told why he could be badly hurt by Tyson Fury READ MORE :

Conor Benn accepts Conor McGregor boxing fight READ MORE :

"Everything that could have went wrong in that fight went wrong, it is what it is. I'm not sitting here and making excuses, I lost. I was the one who chose to get in the ring and put everything on the line, no one is going to remember the excuses I make. I lost fair and square but I'm going to come up stronger and eventually I want to go back after Tommy Fury."

‌



Several names have been thrown into contention regarding Paul's next fight, including Chris Eubank Jr and Darren Till. A rematch with Fury, though, appears to be off the cards. The Brit wants to settle his rivalry with the 'Problem Child' once and for all but was simply not ready to fight in December.

He wrote: "Just wanted to make it very clear as to why the rematch with Jake hasn’t happened yet. His team came to me when I already had an agreed date in place elsewhere. Why would I then agree to a fight with Jake or anyone of that fact when I had already committed to another fight.

Article continues below

"He made me an offer knowing full well about the other date. I said publicly that I would fight Jake anytime after that date. Jan, Feb, March literally any time. Jake and his team love to play out to everyone that it’s me running from this fight when it’s very much the other way around."

Sports.title: 5 Premier League stars Man Utd can target as January plans take shape
Sports.content:
The summer transfer window closed less than two months ago and Manchester United are already desperate for January.

United spent £155million to reshape their midfield in the summer but have seen their 2026/27 campaign start disastrously under Michael Carrick. The arrival of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba has not had the desired impact and Carrick's future as manager is under threat following a run of just two wins in 12 games.

The team sits 16th in the Premier League, having gone eight matches without a win. Already the plan for the season is being torn up, with club chiefs looking for a new manager while also pondering transfers in January.

Injuries have struck, leaving United's squad brutally exposed. Their failure to sign a left-back in the summer, with top target Lewis Hall unavailable from Newcastle, has come back to bite them, while the lack of depth up front is another obvious issue that needs to be addressed.

‌



The problems may be obvious but the solutions are less so. Here Mirror Football takes a look at the players United could move for in January.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Tyrick Mitchell

United needed a left-back before the season kicked off. They need one even more now, with the injuries to Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu further highlighting their lack of depth in the position.

‌



Shaw is in his 13th season for United and the club need to find his long-term successor. Mitchell should be on the United recruitment department's radar for two reasons: he has plenty of Premier League experience and has a contract with Crystal Palace which is due to expire in June.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 6 Images Tyrick Mitchell's Crystal Palace contract expires in June (Image: MB Media/Getty Images)

The 27-year-old has made 256 appearances for Palace and is comfortable playing as a conventional left-back, or as a left wing-back. A tough-tackling defender with a good engine, his move to Old Trafford could have echoes of Aaron Wan-Bissaka's transfer from Palace back in 2019.

‌



Palace are aware of the interest in Mitchell and reportedly want to tie him down to a new contract, but their early-season struggles under Pierre Sage could play into United's hands. If they can land him before he signs a new contract, the fee involved should please INEOS, who are unlikely to sanction big deals as a mid-season rescue mission.

Rayan Ait-Nouri

View 6 Images Rayan Ait-Nouri is seeking a move due to a lack of game time (Image: Vince Mignott/MB Media)

Ait-Nouri's move to Manchester City from Wolves has not gone to plan, with the Algeria international failing to hold down a place in the starting XI. The arrival of Enzo Maresca this summer has not helped matters, with Josko Gvardiol and Nico O'Reilly his preferred options in the position.

There doesn't appear to be a way back and City are reportedly ready to sell in January, with sporting director Hugo Viana already working on an exit. United have been linked with Ait-Nouri before and it would appear to be a good solution for all parties, if the club rivalry can be put to one side. However, the fact he still has over three years left to run on his City contract and moved for £31million in 2025 could complicate things.

‌



Ait-Nouri is still only 25 years old and, at his best, is an exciting attack-minded left-back, shown by his nine assists in 35 games for City.

Adrien Truffert

View 6 Images Adrien Truffert helped Bournemouth thrashed Manchester United (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

The most ambitious of the three left-back targets. While Mitchell's contract is running down and Ait-Nouri wants to move for more football, Truffert is happy at Bournemouth, who thrashed United 3-0 last weekend.

Truffert was on United's radar before he helped the Cherries win at Old Trafford. The 24-year-old has been an ever-present and ever-impressive player at left-back for Bournemouth since his £14m move from Rennes last year and looks set to be another success story on the south coast.

‌



United are not the Frenchman's only admirers and competing with rivals is not likely to be easy for the club. Bournemouth will also be extremely reluctant to sell mid-season. If they are to stand any chance of landing Truffert then United would surely have to wait until the summer.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin

View 6 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin has been in form for Leeds (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

Left-back isn't the only area of need for United, who are also thin on the ground up front. Carrick confirmed on Thursday that Benjamin Sesko would be sidelined until January with a shin injury, making their decision not to sign a striker in the summer appear foolish.

Club chiefs have reportedly identified Leeds' Calvert-Lewin as a target. The former Everton centre-forward has impressed in Daniel Farke's side, scoring five times this season to add to his 15 strikes in his debut campaign.

‌



Calvert-Lewin's current contract runs until the summer of 2028, but Leeds could extend it to ward off interest. It seems very unlikely that Leeds would sanction a move for their first-choice striker to their fiercest rivals mid-season.

Jean-Philippe Mateta

View 6 Images Jean-Philippe Mateta is keen to leave Crystal Palace (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Mateta's future at Crystal Palace has been a near constant source of speculation in 2026. The Frenchman very nearly joined AC Milan in January, only for the deal to collapse due to a knee injury and there was more speculation over the summer. Ultimately, Mateta stayed put, but the rumour mill is churning once more.

Palace sold Marc Guehi in January to Manchester City, instead of losing him for free in the summer, and now face a similar decision with Mateta, whose contract expires in June.

‌



The 29-year-old is understood to be open to joining United in January, but his injury record is a consideration. Mateta has only played four times, scoring once, this season due to a hamstring issue and would appear to be only a short-term solution if he were to move to United.

Sports.title: The Unai Emery reality that Jamie Carragher ignored in Manchester United row
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher suggested Unai Emery cannot win the Champions League with Aston Villa and should therefore take a job elsewhere to prove himself "at an absolute giant of a football club."

What Carragher appears to suggest is that Emery would have a better chance of winning the Champions League at a club with more money to spend. But that cannot be proven, and it also ignores the Spaniard's record in European competition with the clubs he has managed.

At Villarreal, he reached the Champions League semi-finals in 2022, before Villa were knocked out by eventual champions Paris Saint-Germain in the quarter-finals two seasons ago.

Had it not been for an inspired goalkeeping performance from Gianluigi Donnarumma and a goal-line clearance in the final minute of the second leg, Villa would have taken PSG to extra time, with the momentum behind them as they looked to reach the semi-finals and face Arsenal.

Man Utd manager agreement 'reached' over three options as Roy Keane gets approval READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

In fact, beyond Villarreal, the likes of Ajax, Tottenham, Monaco, Roma and RB Leipzig have all reached the Champions League semi-finals in the past decade.

Villa have an outstanding record in Europe under Emery, boasting a 73% win rate after playing their 44th match last week against Viking FK. Their Champions League record now stands at 11 wins from 15 games.

At PSG, one of the giants Carragher refers to, Emery failed to progress beyond the round of 16 in either of his two Champions League campaigns. At Arsenal, he managed in the Europa League in both of his seasons, losing the final in his only full campaign in charge at the Emirates.

View 4 Images Emery failed to reach the latter stages of the Champions League with PSG

In contrast, he won all three Europa League finals he contested with Sevilla before beating Freiburg in May to end Villa’s 30-year wait for silverware, claiming his fifth Europa League title after also beating Manchester United as Villarreal manager in 2021.

The idea that Emery must manage a club with greater resources to win the greatest prize in club football, then, does not necessarily stand up.

Emery’s success at Villa has been built on the environment and culture he has created at Bodymoor Heath. He is the best coach in the Premier League, improving players and delivering results because he has not only earned their full commitment and respect but also enjoys full power and control at Villa.

Nassef Sawiris gave Emery a blank canvas within the financial parameters in which the club can operate. Mateu Alemany, who was due to be appointed president of football operations, warned Emery that he would face restrictions because of the club’s limited revenue. Emery did not mind.

View 4 Images Unai Emery led Aston Villa to Europa League success last season (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

He knew what he was signing up for at Villa, but, more importantly, he understood what he could build. And he has done just that.

He would be foolish to trade all of that for the poisoned chalice that is Old Trafford - or for any other club searching for a new manager, for that matter.

Carragher, though, believes Emery will have an itch to scratch at a “giant” club and will want to prove himself at one.

“He is a manager I look at when I think about Manchester United," he said on Sky Sports. "I think Emery is the best manager in the Premier League. But I've got this thing with him.

“Yes, his record in the Europa League is amazing, but surely somebody who is that successful wants to be known in the Champions League. He wants to win the Champions League. He's not going to do that at Aston Villa.

"He's had two experiences that haven't gone particularly well for him, Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal. And I just think surely he would want that opportunity to prove himself at an absolute giant of a football club. Sorry, Villa fans."

View 4 Images Carragher thinks Man Utd could help Emery scratch an itch (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Back in December last year, Emery outlined his dream, and admitted that he was getting closer to achieving it.

“Dreams are free. Everyone has to dream. I have my dream and I am here getting my dream,” he said. “My huge dream here or as a coach is to win the Champions League. That is my dream, all my life.

“But 20 years ago I started as a coach, in League One in Spain. Speaking now in my progression as a coach, I am a privileged man to manage the level I have.

“I am feeling proud of everything I did but also I have a huge responsibility to the club, the supporters, the players and the owners. The level I am, my dream is still to win the Champions League.

“I don’t know if I can have again this opportunity. Last year, we played quarter-final. Four years ago we played semi-final. I am getting close!”

Is it more likely that Emery could win the Champions League at a club like Real Madrid, Barcelona or Bayern Munich? Possibly, yes, but his record at PSG, where he had plenty of star players, and at Villarreal does little to support that argument.

Equally, we're talking about Man United. The state of that club, and the mess it's in, stands in stark contrast to what Emery has built at Villa. It would take years to achieve what he has at Villa at United, if it were possible at all.

Sports.title: Legendary 75,800-seater stadium to be demolished as stunning images of replacement emerge
Sports.content:
Legendary 75,800-seater stadium to be demolished as stunning images of replacement emerge

A 100-year-old stadium - one of the most iconic in world football - is set to be demolished, with a shiny, new replacement ground set to be constructed

View 8 Images The San Siro is set to be razed to the ground (Image: AC Milan via Getty Images)

The San Siro, one of football's most recognisable and revered stadiums, is facing its final chapter after plans to demolish the iconic ground and replace it with a new state-of-the-art arena were officially confirmed.

‌



‌



The 75,817-capacity stadium, which has been home to both AC Milan and Inter Milan for nearly a century, will be torn down to make way for the Generali Stadium, with the new venue scheduled to open in time for the 2031/32 season.

‌



The naming rights have already been snapped up by Italian insurance giant Generali, with the company reportedly agreeing to a staggering £540million deal spanning 20 years.

‌



Another Premier League star robbed DURING match as partner shares 'distressing' statement READ MORE :

Mystery surrounds Jack Grealish after David Moyes gives blunt response to Everton axing READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

On Wednesday, both Serie A giants offered supporters a glimpse of the future, sharing a series of images and a video on social media showcasing what their new home is expected to look like.

And the contrast with the San Siro could hardly be greater. The famous spiralling towers and towering red girders that have defined the stadium's unmistakable silhouette will be consigned to history.

‌



In their place will stand a sleek, futuristic arena - which will be able to house 71,500 spectators - complete with a sweeping double-curved roof and a striking concrete X-frame structure encircling the ground.

8 View 8 Images The first images of the stadium that will replace the San Siro have been released (Image: @acmilan/X) 8 View 8 Images The Generali Stadium will be opened in 2031 (Image: @acmilan/X)

‌



The unveiling also offered a tantalising glimpse of some of the features planned for the new stadium, including what appears to be a transparent players' tunnel designed to bring supporters closer to the action before kick-off. Football, meanwhile, will not be its only attraction, with the venue also earmarked for concerts, fashion shows and other major events.

There is undoubtedly plenty for Milan and Inter supporters to look forward to, but the unveiling has also brought an uncomfortable reality into sharper focus.

‌



8 View 8 Images Like the San Siro, the stadium will be home to both AC Milan and Inter Milan (Image: @acmilan/X) 8 View 8 Images The new design does not feature the San Siro's iconic spiralling staircases (Image: @acmilan/X)

‌



For all the excitement surrounding the Generali Stadium, many fans are struggling to accept that one of football's great cathedrals is approaching the end of the road.

The San Siro's place in football folklore is difficult to overstate. Since opening in 1926, it has witnessed some of the sport's greatest players, biggest occasions and most memorable nights, becoming a landmark not just for Milan but for football supporters across the world.

‌



8 View 8 Images AC Milan and Inter Milan have shared a stadium since the 1940s (Image: @acmilan/X) 8 View 8 Images The Generali Stadium is set to be one of the very biggest in Europe (Image: @acmilan/X)

‌



Its imposing stands have provided the backdrop to countless derbies between the Rossoneri and Nerazzurri, with the fierce rivalry between the two clubs adding another layer of history to an already remarkable venue. From European Cup triumphs to domestic title celebrations, the stadium has seen it all.

It has also welcomed some of the game's most celebrated figures, with the likes of Paolo Maldini, Marco van Basten and Ronaldo all having graced its pitch. For visiting supporters, walking out into the San Siro's enormous bowl has long been one of the most intimidating experiences in European football.

‌



View 8 Images The San Siro, pictured here during the opening ceremony of the 1990 World Cup, remains one of the most legendary grounds in all of sport (Image: Getty)

It has hosted countless Italy international fixtures, three matches at the 1934 World Cup, three at Euro 1980 and six at the 1990 World Cup, as well as the tournament's opening ceremony. Rugby matches and boxing events have also been staged there, while the likes of Michael Jackson, The Rolling Stones and Bob Marley have performed there.

‌



There is a strong argument that the stadium's unique character cannot be replicated. Its towering concrete structure, steep stands and distinctive architecture have given it an atmosphere unlike almost anywhere else in the game.

While the Generali Stadium promises to usher Milan's two clubs into a new era, the challenge will be ensuring that the soul of their old home is not lost along the way.
