Sports.title: Russell believes tyre pressures and less “efficient” driving style hurt him in 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell believes two key aspects of this year’s cars are the reason why he hasn’t been able to perform as well as his team mate.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli goes into this weekend’s race virtually guaranteed to seal the championship.

Russell began the season with victory in Australia. But he has only won twice more since then while Antonelli has amassed nine wins.

“I think there’s just a few factors with the cars this year that potentially favour or hinder a certain driving style,” Russell explained

“I’ve always been a driver that focuses on the mid to the exit of the corners, which often means I’m on the throttle earlier than most. And with these new power units, that means I am spending more energy and it is sometimes not the most efficient way to drive for the power unit.

“Secondly, the tyre pressures this year, especially on the rear, have been very, very high. Pirelli are taking a few PSI margin, especially in the rear axle. So again, that sort of has hindered me a little bit by pushing the exits. The rear tyre can’t cope with it as well, and there’s been a bit of a hindrance on the power unit side.

“So it was kind of these two factors that just really hampered my natural driving style, and I’d say that’s probably been the biggest thing of the season.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Although Russell has had a handful of strong weekends, he has also struggled on other occasions.

“I came out of Monaco earlier this year and it was a very difficult weekend for me and I went to Barcelona and was quickest in every session and put it on pole,” he said. “I went to Austria, the next race, was on pole again and then a few races later I was qualifying down in P5 and P6.

“In Baku, on pole by eight tenths, then in Malaysia I qualified I think was P8, maybe, [seventh] in Malaysia.”

Russell said his results were more consistent in other seasons when he had a less competitive car.

“I feel in the years gone by I had a pretty high hit-rate of reaching the potential of the car and maybe at the end of the season there were four or five races I feel that were not maximised. I remember in 2022, we finished in the top five more than any other driver in the whole season, I think it was 19 from 22 races and that was the third-best car on the grid.

“Now this season we have the best car and I’m not able to achieve these results. So it’s quite strange and certainly scratching our head a little bit and it’s definitely not through a lack of trying.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Although he is on the verge of losing the championship to his team mate, Russell said the relationship between him and Antonelli remains positive.

“On a personal level, Kimi is obviously a great guy and has lots of energy,” he said. “We’ve had no reason this year not to continue a good relationship.

“I think a lot of these rivalries start because of on-track incidents or actions. The truth is he’s been at a higher level than me this year so we’ve not really been in that situation too often, we have had one or two races.

“When it comes to the race in itself, we sort of keep ourselves to ourselves and work with our individual engineers to try and get the most out of it.”

With his championship defeat virtually assured, Russell said he would take no consolation from claiming the runner-up spot.

“I think for every driver on the grid, there’s only one position that matters, and it’s P1. To be best at the rest is not really something you dream of as a kid.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Looks Shaken At Weigh-In: Body Language Betrays Former King
Sports.content:
Christian Mbilli plans on doing far more than just hanging onto his WBC super middleweight title against Canelo Alvarez in Riyadh. He claims he intends to beat the former champion at his own game, a risky declaration against a technician who thrives on catching aggressive punchers reckless enough to leave gaps.

Canelo answered at Friday’s weigh-in by pointing directly to his 21 years in the ring. The clash boils down to a classic style collision: Mbilli trying to swamp the veteran with sheer volume versus Canelo using veteran ring savvy to time incoming attacks.

That was not the swaggering, unflappable Canelo who used to smirk on the scales and mentally dismiss opponents before the opening bell even sounded.

The body language told the real story. When a fighter has to constantly recite their resume like a rehearsed script, it usually means they are trying to convince themselves just as much as the crowd. Canelo repeating that he has been doing this for 21 years sounded less like an intimidating warning and more like a fighter clinging to past glory to mask present doubt.

The physical reality is staring him right in the face. Canelo knows his gas tank is not what it used to be; his punch output drops every year, and resting on the ropes against a relentless engine like Mbilli is asking for trouble.

Mbilli throws punches in bunches, does not care about reputation, and attacks the midsection with bad intentions. Canelo looked like a veteran who fully realizes he signed up for an absolute grueling night at the office, where his mind might know the right counters to throw, but his legs and reflexes might not respond in time.

“You’re going to see on Saturday what’s going to happen. Tomorrow night, I’m going to beat him in every way. The better the technique, the better the punch. It will change my life a lot. After the victory, my life will change more. Fight of the year, an amazing fight. It will be incredible,” Mbilli stated at the scales.

A victory over Canelo brings instant worldwide credibility that owning a belt by itself never secures. Still, trying to prove he can outbox the Mexican star inside the pocket invites trouble. Mbilli operates best when crowding opponents, digging to the ribs, and forcing a relentless pace that drains older legs.

“This is very important for me. I’ve been doing this for 21 years. It’s important for me to take this title. Well, my experience is obviously very different. He’s never fought anyone like me. Tomorrow, he’s going to fight me,” Canelo said.

Ring mileage only works if Canelo makes Mbilli second-guess his charges. Sharp counterpunches can blunt the champion’s momentum and carve out breathing room between exchanges. Should Mbilli walk through those shots without blinking, ring wisdom alone will not generate the work rate needed to capture rounds on the cards.

Both men made weight without incident. Canelo tipped the scales at 167½ pounds, while Mbilli checked in at 167¾.

If Canelo cannot hurt Mbilli in the first four rounds and force him into retreat, he is in for a miserable evening trying to survive a non-stop wave of pressure.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Crawls Back To Bob Arum After Zuffa Disaster
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson catching up with Bob Arum feels like a smart play on familiar ground. Walking the free agent path lets him call his own shots, yet he still requires deep pockets to bankroll his ring returns plus a broadcaster ready to air them. Sitting idle for nearly twelve months makes those requirements impossible to brush aside.

Stevenson posted a picture flashing a wide grin next to his former promoter out in Houston. Coming off a quiet stint with Zuffa Boxing that failed to deliver an actual ring appearance, seeing Arum in person beats trading insults online over his market value.

🥊‼️Shakur Stevenson meeting with Bob Arum who has Raymond Muratalla the WBO MANDATORY on his stable‼️😳 https://t.co/Y7IRu55hBC — Hassan (@Hassanwellss) October 30, 2026

What Arum will do is facilitate business that serves Top Rank. The WBO ordering Shakur to face Raymond Muratalla at 140 pounds handed Arum all the cards. Muratalla is Top Rank’s guy. Arum can either negotiate a single-fight arrangement to put Shakur on a Top Rank card or push the bout to a purse bid, daring Shakur to find outside financiers willing to outbid ESPN’s ecosystem.

A permanent reunion will happen only if Shakur accepts a massive haircut on his financial expectations. If he still insists on purses detached from gate receipts and pay-per-view buys, Arum will simply use him for the Muratalla mandatory and let him drift back into the market to test reality all over again.

Arum bringing him back under a full, multi-fight promotional banner is another story entirely. Bob knows Shakur’s ceiling down to the exact dollar. Top Rank famously offered him a five-fight deal worth roughly $3 million a bout before he walked away, an offer Shakur rejected because he fancied himself a bona fide pay-per-view attraction. Arum will not bid against himself, nor will he overpay for a style that struggles to move tickets or drive commercial subscriptions.

What matters now is an official fight confirmation. Stevenson has spent enough time arguing about his worth from the sidelines. Whether Arum signs on for the long haul or just finances one night, sitting down together might finally get him back under the arena lights.

For the fighter, the upside makes total sense. Steering his own promotional ship grants creative freedom, but it leaves him hunting for funding, television clearance, plus opponents willing to accept realistic paydays. Total freedom never guarantees an actual fight night on its own.

Arum understands Stevenson’s talent inside the ropes, having spent years selling his headline slots. At the same time, he knows the financial ceiling. If Shakur continues demanding the massive purses reserved for pay-per-view draws, lunch together will not magically fix that gap.

Still, that photo blows up the narrative that Stevenson ran off every ally in boxing. Arum traveled to check in on him, and Shakur made sure the entire sport took notice.

Shakur found out the hard way that self-promotion requires somebody willing to write the check. He rode the wave on Turki Alalshikh cards against Zepeda and Teofimo Lopez, banking huge paydays while assuming that level of funding was the new industry baseline. Then came the Zuffa Boxing detour.

Dana White and company quickly realized what others already knew: paying an artist who fights safety-first eight figures while waiting out catchweight demands makes zero business sense. Zuffa cut their losses, showing him the door without staging a single fight.

Sitting inactive since January with zero broadcast platform and asking for money nobody wants to guarantee leaves him backed into a corner. That Houston photo with Arum was pure PR damage control. Shakur desperately needs the public to believe he has suitors, options, and warmth from the old guard, rather than looking like an isolated fighter out on an island.

Sports.title: Pointless Warburton Clash Wastes What Little Time Carlos Adames Has Left
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames begins his Zuffa Boxing journey with a matchup tailored to set up future UK bouts rather than create instant box office excitement. Ring Magazine officially confirmed that the WBC middleweight champion will meet Gerome Warburton on November 14, headlining Riyadh Season Zuffa Boxing 13 in Saudi Arabia.

This non-title contest takes place above the middleweight limit. Former bantamweight champion Jason Moloney meets Andres Teran on the undercard. News of the matchup leaked on October 19, so today’s press release simply rubber stamps what everyone already knew.

Adames (25-1-1, 18 KOs) gets his chance to make an impression with his new promoter. Building real buzz with Warburton in the opposite corner remains a tough sell. The Welsh fighter sits at number seven in the WBA middleweight rankings, though that ranking looks better on paper than it resonates with mainstream fight fans.

Warburton (18-2-2 KOs) comes into the fight with back-to-back wins over Nathan Heaney. Those victories opened the door for this spot, yet Adames marks a massive upgrade in difficulty. With only two knockouts on Warburton’s entire resume, the promotion cannot rely on a knockout artist angle.

The real motive here seems clear. Zuffa wants to prep Adames for bouts against stablemates Denzel Bentley and Aaron McKenna. Warburton serves as the first British obstacle before Zuffa rolls out bigger names from across the pond. While neither matchup is official, the blueprint makes sense.

Zuffa already has these fighters under contract. Adames gives Bentley and McKenna a legitimate champion to target. A dominant showing against Warburton hands the promotional team fresh footage to roll out for the next phase.

Still, convincing audiences to tune in for the current plan is a different story. Bentley and McKenna give British spectators a hometown reason to care, but domestic ties do not guarantee a massive gate or monster television ratings. In the United States, neither matchup feels like a breakout attraction for Adames.

Bentley’s status complicates things even further. He risks losing his WBO belt after failing to secure a date with mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez. Strip away that belt, and an Adames clash loses much of its luster.

McKenna presents another route, yet the middleweight division continues struggling with star power. Matching in-house talent creates reliable action, but it rarely draws casual viewers into the weight class.

This is classic in-house recycling that completely ignores both the clock on Adames’ career and what actual ticket-buying fight fans care about.

Adames is 32, fights roughly once a year, and carries zero commercial crossover. Handing him Gerome Warburton in a non-title catchweight does nothing. It does not sell tickets, it does not draw eyes to a broadcast, and it certainly does not move the needle for casual viewers who have never heard of the guy. Fans know a glorified sparring session when they see one, so they simply tune out.

The logic of using Warburton as a stepping stone to Denzel Bentley or Aaron McKenna is just as flawed. That entire sequence assumes the public is clamoring to see Adames clean out the British domestic scene. They are not. Bentley and McKenna are solid operators, but neither is a global draw capable of transforming Adames into an attraction.

If the payoff at the end of the tunnel is lukewarm to begin with, burning four to six months on a preliminary warm-up against Warburton makes zero promotional sense.

Time is working against them. With his history of lengthy layoffs, Adames cannot afford to spend prime months ticking boxes for low-profile regional setups. If Zuffa wanted to make a real statement with their middleweight investment, going after recognized names like Tim Tszyu or Vito Mielnicki Jr. would have delivered immediate legitimacy.

Putting Adames in with names fans actually follow forces attention onto the division, creates genuine stakes, and gives Zuffa an immediate return on their money.

Instead, they went the safe, budget-conscious route. The problem is that safety breeds indifference. When the opening move fails to capture anyone’s imagination, the matches lined up behind it end up dead on arrival anyway.

Sports.title: Ben Davison: Help Or Hindrance To His Heavyweights?
Sports.content:
It is rare for a trainer to attract as much publicity as his fighters. However, that is precisely what Ben Davison has succeeded in doing this year. For the uninitiated, Briton Davison is the trainer of heavyweights Moses Itauma, Fabio Wardley and Anthony Joshua.

Ben Davison’s profile as a trainer of heavyweights, though, really skyrocketed when he trained Tyson Fury from 2017 – 2019. During this time, many credited Davison for being responsible for The Gypsy King’s successful return to the ring after an absence of two and a half years, which Fury spent battling his demons and putting on weight.

Indeed, Davison was Fury’s trainer for his world title fight against Deontay Wilder in Los Angeles on 01 December 2018, resulting in a draw, and Wilder retaining his WBC title as the defending Champion. Fury performed well in this fight, proving that he is a talented boxer.

However, he felt there was something missing, and adjustments needed to be made. This fight demonstrated Fury’s skills as a boxer. The Gypsy King was, though, astute enough to know that just being a good boxer was not going to win him any rematch with The Bronze Bomber, famous for his legendary right hand.

Fury therefore changed trainer, enlisting the help of SugarHill Steward, the nephew of the famous Emanuel Steward, who had trained former World Heavyweight Champions Lennox Lewis and Wladimir Klitschko. The Brit did this in the hope that he would be not just a skillful boxer, but also become a ferocious puncher to combat the threat Deontay Wilder posed.

This plan worked. When Fury fought Wilder in their rematch on 22 February 2020 in Las Vegas, Fury beat Wilder by TKO in the 7th Round to win the WBC world title and the vacant The Ring heavyweight title.

Then, again with SugarHill Steward as his trainer, Fury successfully defended his WBC world title and The Ring heavyweight title against Deontay Wilder. This time, Fury went one better and beat Wilder by knockout in the 11th Round of their world title fight on 09 October 2021, also in Las Vegas.

Up to Fury’s last two fights against Wilder, The Gypsy King was not known to have the punch power to become a knockout artist. Under Steward’s tutelage, this situation changed, and Fury’s decision to leave Ben Davison was vindicated.

After Tyson Fury, Davison became the trainer of former World Champion Anthony Joshua. This is where things become interesting, as Davison was in AJ’s corner for his challenge for the IBF world title against then-champion Daniel Dubois. This all-British clash took place on 21 September 2024 at Wembley Stadium in London, England.

Joshua was having trouble in this fight, suffering knockdowns in the 1st, 3rd and 4th Rounds. In the break between the 4th and 5th Rounds, Davison seemed to advise Joshua to take a chance, coming out with the now-infamous “roll the dice” comment to his fighter.

When Davison was questioned about what he meant by this comment in a recent interview with the boxing commentator Spencer Oliver, Davison informed Oliver that the intention was for Joshua to throw a double jab and then a right uppercut at Dubois. Doing this, however, would leave Joshua’s chin exposed.

As the insightful YouTube channel Chris Talks Boxing explains, it would have been better for Davison to have advised AJ at that stage to stay out of trouble for a couple of Rounds, and rely on the jab, giving both trainer and fighter a chance to review tactics at the end of the 5th Round. In this way, Joshua would have conserved energy for the later Rounds, which was necessary, given that he had been in the wars up to that point.

As we know, however, Joshua tried to throw a right uppercut early in the 5th Round, but was caught on the chin by Dubois, forcing the former two-time World Champion to the canvas, and unable to beat the count in the same Round. It would therefore appear that Ben Davison’s tactics in this fight were at best clumsy, and at worst reckless.

Turning now to Moses Itauma, Davison has been his trainer since 2023, and was in Itauma’s corner for his fight for the vacant IBF world title against Filip Hrgović on 29 August at The O2 Arena in London, England. Up to this fight, Itauma had not been past the 6th Round in any professional fight.

Further, Itauma admitted publicly that he had not sparred 12 continuous Rounds, which is bizarre to say the least. On fight night, Itauma ran out of gas and lost to Hrgović by TKO in the 9th Round. In his recent interview with Spencer Oliver, Ben Davison mentioned that Moses Itauma is inexperienced, inferring that this is a possible reason for his loss to the Croatian.

As Chris Talks Boxing again rightly states, however, Itauma may be inexperienced, but it is his trainer Ben Davison’s responsibility to “manage” this lack of experience to get the best out of his fighter. Inexperience on the part of Itauma is therefore no excuse for Davison not preparing the young man adequately for a 12 Round fight.

Finishing with Fabio Wardley, Ben Davison was his trainer for both Wardley’s world title fights against Daniel Dubois this year. Both fights ended in TKO losses for the Ipswich man. Wardley lost his WBO world title to Dubois by TKO in the 11th Round on 09 May at Co-op Live in Manchester, England.

It was a respectable performance by Wardley. However, the rematch on 17 October at The 02 Arena in London, England was a much more one-sided affair, with Dubois winning by TKO in the 2nd Round. This last fight prompted former three-weight World Champion Duke McKenzie to go on the record saying that Ben Davison should seek help from “someone more technically minded” in training Wardley – hardly a ringing endorsement of Davison as a trainer.

Taking Davison’s record with all these heavyweights into account, it is clear that a pattern is emerging. The pattern is that Ben Davison seems unable to step up to the plate when it comes to training heavyweights for world title fights. Boxing is a results-driven sport, or at least it should be. In this regard, Davison has been found wanting, with one draw and four losses in all the Heavyweight world title fights he has been a trainer in.

This represents an 80% loss ratio with not one win. It is, of course, easy to criticize. In his last two Heavyweight world title fights, however, Ben Davison has thrown in the towel to save his fighters from further punishment. You don’t need to be a rocket scientist to come to the conclusion that there is definitely room for improvement.

Ultimately, though, it is for Davison’s heavyweights to decide whether he stays or goes!

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

UK

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Must Get Ben Whittaker’s Next Move Right
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn needs to find Ben Whittaker a fight that prepares him for a world title shot, and Conor Wallace remains the obvious choice. At 29, Whittaker needs meaningful rounds against opponents who can expose his weaknesses, followed by evidence that he can correct them.

Anthony Yarde is among the opponents Hearn has mentioned for Whittaker, although the meeting does not establish that a fight between them is being negotiated.

Plotting what’s next 🌎 https://t.co/AWWFNVJk3p — Eddie Hearn (@EddieHearn) October 29, 2026

Whittaker earned his IBF mandatory position by beating Wallace on October 3, but the closing rounds weakened the case for sending him straight into a title fight. He controlled much of the contest before fading and getting hurt late, leaving a very different impression from the one he had built earlier.

“For me, no, he needs another fight,” Hearn said after the bout, naming Yarde, Wallace and the Joshua Buatsi–Willy Hutchinson winner as possibilities.

That leaves Hearn with a decision about what Whittaker actually needs. Another quick stoppage against an overmatched opponent would offer little preparation for championship opposition. Wallace forced him to work over the distance and exposed weaknesses that a better fighter could punish earlier.

A rematch would give Whittaker the chance to show he can finish strongly against someone who already knows how to hurt him. Wallace would have reason to attack sooner, having allowed Whittaker to collect too many of the early rounds before making his strongest effort.

Trainer Andy Lee cited COVID during the buildup to their first fight. If illness contributed to Whittaker’s late decline, facing Wallace again would provide an opportunity to demonstrate the difference a healthier preparation makes. It would also address the controversy surrounding a chaotic final round in which Whittaker went to the canvas three times without a knockdown being scored.

Yarde would bring a bigger domestic name and a heavier punching threat. That makes him an interesting option, but potentially a dangerous choice for someone who just struggled when Wallace increased the pressure. Whittaker would need to retain his concentration and defensive discipline when tired.

The Buatsi–Hutchinson winner would provide another demanding route. However, Hearn should be careful about treating any of these opponents as a convenient bridge to a title shot. Whittaker’s last performance showed why he needs the work.

Moving away from Wallace could also carry a cost with fans. Hearn has mentioned the rematch, but choosing someone else would leave the impression that his unbeaten fighter is leaving unfinished business behind.

Whittaker has time to improve at 29. His next fight needs to show that improvement, and beating Wallace more decisively would give Hearn something firmer to sell when the world title opportunity arrives.

At Whittaker’s age, a fighter does not develop an engine or an iron will out of nowhere. Those traits are either built into the foundation during the amateur days, or they simply do not exist. Whittaker entered the professional ranks with massive fanfare, an Olympic pedigree, and a style built entirely around showboating, reflexes, and athletic arrogance.

That works beautifully against overmatched opposition or journeymen who stand frozen in front of him. The moment a fighter stops watching the dancing, plants their feet, and marches forward with hard physical pressure, the entire facade begins to crack.

Liam Cameron proved it first. Cameron is a gritty, durable operator who made Whittaker uncomfortable by simply refusing to respect the theatrics, dragging him into physical trench work until that bizarre spill out of the ring brought a premature end. Instead of treating that as a warning light on the dashboard, Matchroom went right back to soft touches.

The Popeye Rivera matchup in Brooklyn was prime evidence of Hearn trying to protect the investment with harmless opposition rather than preparing him for genuine world caliber operators.

Conor Wallace brought that reality back to the surface in vicious fashion. It was not just a case of getting tired. Whittaker looked completely depleted, mentally rattled, and physically incapable of handling heavy incoming fire once the fight entered the championship rounds. Spending the twelfth round touching the canvas multiple times without the referee counting knockdowns was embarrassing for a guy calling out the division’s elite.

Whittaker does not possess the luxury of two or three developmental years to rebuild his gas tank and learn how to fight inside a phone booth. If he steps into the ring with a puncher like Anthony Yarde, or goes anywhere near the division monsters like Artur Beterbiev or Dmitry Bivol, the outcome is predictable. Those men do not wait around for nine rounds before turning on the pressure. They hunt you down from the opening bell.

If Hearn sends him into a rematch with Wallace and Whittaker runs out of gas again, the entire promotional work pops for good. What we saw down the stretch on October 3 might simply be Whittaker’s absolute ceiling under real pressure.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Gets Showcase Treatment Against Nikita Zon
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia against Nikita Zon looks thin for a pay-per-view co-feature. Munguia supplies the name recognition, but Thursday’s press conference offered little proof that his challenger can keep the second biggest bout on Saturday’s Riyadh card competitive.

Richard Schaefer confirmed Munguia against Zon will take place immediately before Canelo Alvarez faces Christian Mbilli. That gives the WBA super middleweight title bout a prime broadcast position, yet the promotional pitch leaned on Zon entering with twelve victories and ten knockouts.

“I watched some of his fights. He’s strong, incredible power, as obviously 10 knockouts show,” Schaefer said during the media session. “I call him actually the new Siberian Rocky.”

Schaefer praised Zon’s power and stoppage record without naming a single credible opponent who proves he belongs in the ring with Munguia. Buyers heard he possesses danger, yet received zero evidence to evaluate that claim.

From a competitive standpoint, it is a gross mismatch. Munguia has logged 48 professional bouts, headlined major cards, and shared the ring with elite competition. Zon has exactly 13 fights, spent his entire career on regional Russian cards, and has never faced anyone remotely close to world class.

Slapping the moniker “the Siberian Rocky” on a completely untested fighter does not make him a threat. It is a fabricated sales gimmick designed to distract from the reality that Zon has done nothing to earn a shot at a belt on a massive international stage. Munguia should blow right through him inside five rounds, and anything less would actually look bad for Munguia.

“I came here to win and I’m leaving with nothing less than a victory. I will become the new world champion,” Zon said through a translator.

That served as his loudest quote, delivering standard bravado expected during fight week. He provided zero tactical detail on what vulnerabilities he intends to target against Munguia.

Munguia kept his comments just as brief. Asked if taking on a challenger with twelve bouts invites complacency, he pointed to his work with trainer Eddy Reynoso.

“I can just say that I’m ready. I had a great camp along Eddie. We prepared strongly,” Munguia stated through a translator. “It will be a great fight. You will see the best version of Jaime Munguia.”

The fighters offered little interest for the event. Schaefer tried filling that void by selling Zon as a raw puncher receiving a life-changing shot against an established Mexican name.

For viewers spending money on the broadcast, that pitch sounds empty. Munguia scoring a routine knockout over an untested opponent helps his record, but a premium slot requires legitimate drama. Watching an established contender cruise through a soft assignment leaves little intrigue.

As for why this fight is happening, it comes down to this. It is about keeping Munguia winning while minimizing any real risk. After picking up the WBA title against Armando Resendiz in May, his team wants him active and collecting paydays without putting him anywhere near dangerous 168-pound contenders like Osleys Iglesias, Diego Pacheco, or Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zon represents the path of least resistance for Munguia: an opponent with zero profile who will stand in front of him and provide highlight-reel footage. Boxing fans are completely exhausted by this specific brand of cynical matchmaking, which is exactly why the fight has generated virtually zero pulse online or in ticket sales.

Promoters seem to operate under the delusion that casual fans will see a gaudy knockout record, hear a goofy nickname like the “Siberian Rocky,” and instantly buy in. Today’s boxing public is far too savvy for that trick. Everyone recognizes an artificially manufactured record compiled in remote regional shows when they see one.

Sports.title: Tim Bradley Gives Shakur Stevenson A Muratalla Escape Route
Sports.content:
Tim Bradley just offered Shakur Stevenson a convenient exit, one that spares him from a dangerous matchup with minimal reward. Raymond Muratalla brings serious heat without anywhere near the $15 million purse Bradley claims Stevenson wants. Stevenson could get caught, maybe even stopped, or grind out a safety-first decision that leaves fans booing anyway.

Heading back down to lightweight might not double his money, but it gives him cover. It lets him chase a different target under the banner of championship glory. Bradley basically handed him the script: drop back to 135 pounds, then unify the division.

“Now if he says, ‘I’m not going to fight him, and I’m going to go down, and I’m going to fight Zepeda for a belt,’ I’m cool with that. I’m cool with that. Stay at 135 and clean up the division. That’s what you should do,” Bradley said on his channel.

That backing carries weight while critics blast Stevenson over whether he will actually take the WBO mandate against Muratalla. Bradley opened by claiming there is “no hiding,” only to lay out the exact road map for Stevenson to walk away with his blessing.

Muratalla creates a tactical nightmare where even a victory might fail to win over frustrated fans. If Stevenson chooses to stand his ground, he gives a heavy hitter chances to connect. If he gets on his bicycle to protect the zero on his record, he only fuels the talk about being boring.

A knockout loss is a real danger here. Bradley insists he expects Stevenson to win, but picking him to prevail does not remove the physical threat, nor does it guarantee the performance builds any future buzz.

The money also looks shaky according to Bradley.

“He’s going to have to take a little bit less. It ain’t going to be $15 million. It’s going to be a lot less,” Bradley said.

From a business standpoint, retreating to lightweight makes plenty of sense. Stevenson does not even need a massive raise to justify the switch. Taking similar cash against someone his camp feels better about beats stepping into Muratalla’s crosshairs.

Dropping to 135 guarantees nothing simple, of course. Bradley’s plan means hunting down titleholders, specifically giving the green light to a tilt with William Zepeda. The real value comes down to the matchup details rather than just stepping on the scale at a lighter weight.

When a fan noted that Bradley pushed for a 135-pound return before the sanctioning body stepped in, the analyst stood firm. Stevenson can leave junior welterweight behind, but he has to plant his feet at lightweight instead of bouncing right back up after ducking Muratalla.

That bargain works for Bradley, but skeptical fight fans who want to see Muratalla get his shot will be a much tougher crowd.

Bradley supplied the public excuse by urging a chase for undisputed glory at lightweight. The real payoff is ducking a punishing clash for a paycheck that falls flat. Both realities can coexist, yet picking up another strap somewhere else will not silence the whispers about Muratalla.

Shakur’s silence is deafening, especially coming from someone who usually treats social media like a live microphone. When a fighter makes noise 24/7 about nobody wanting to get in the ring with them, going completely dark the second an actual mandatory gets called creates an awful look. It looks like battlefield freeze.

Usually, the moment a sanctioning body steps in, guys start chest-thumping about easy work, post-training clips, or talk about who is getting exposed. Instead, crickets. In combat sports, sudden radio silence often signals hesitation rather than quiet confidence. Stevenson knows Muratalla is not an aging name brought in to pad a highlight reel or a blown-up featherweight looking for a payday.

Muratalla is big, physically imposing, applies relentless forward pressure, and throws with spite. He does not care about fancy footwork or playing a game of tag to lose a decision.

Taking on a heavy-handed, high-volume puncher with everything to gain and nothing to lose requires digging into the trenches. When the reality sets in that there is no massive eight-figure check waiting on the other side to justify that kind of physical punishment, battle nerves kick in fast.

Right now, his camp is likely running the numbers and looking for every possible exit route. Dropping back down to 135 to claim an undisputed crown sounds a lot more heroic in a press release than admitting you want no part of an absolute buzzsaw at 140.

Sports.title: Richard Schaefer Oversells Canelo Alvarez’s Christian Mbilli Choice
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez looks to have picked the softer option in Christian Mbilli, though nobody expects an easy night at the office. Mbilli gives Canelo clear lanes to time counters, letting him steal rounds on the scorecards even if he gets outworked. Osleys Iglesias, on the other hand, represents a far more unforgiving matchup.

Promoter Richard Schaefer repeatedly praised Canelo at Thursday’s final press conference for picking Mbilli to give fans the best fight possible. That narrative ignored how slim the pool really was. With WBA titlist Jaime Munguia practically off the table due to gym loyalty, plus a vacant WBO belt, Canelo really only had Mbilli or IBF champion Iglesias to consider.

“Because I do not believe in shortcuts. I have been a champion for many years. I just want to fight the best,” Canelo said when asked about the decision.

Even if Mbilli throws a hundred punches a round, Canelo knows how judges score fights. A crisp, explosive counter shot that snaps an opponent’s head back often wins rounds over flurry work that lands to the body, head, or gloves. Against Mbilli, Canelo has a clear path to win rounds on the cards.

Iglesias is an entirely different problem, and arguably a far more punishing one. The Cuban is a rangy, hard-hitting southpaw who controls real estate with a stiff jab and detonates with a lead right hook. Canelo struggling against disciplined boxers with length and movement is well established.

Following Iglesias around the ring while absorbing straight lefts, right hooks, and jabs would be grueling, with very few clean openings to fire back. Iglesias brings real knockout danger without needing to smother himself on the inside to get it. Iglesias brings the bigger punch, but he also possesses the technical skill to dominate without hunting for a knockout.

Canelo risks trailing, missing, and soaking up damage without landing enough in return to keep pace. Reaching the final bell would still leave him battered. That is a projection, yet the Cuban’s length, precision, and power make it a very real danger.

Mbilli brings heat of his own. His swarm could pin Canelo against the ropes for long stretches. The difference is that Mbilli’s relentless forward motion keeps him squarely in range for Canelo’s signature counter rights and body hooks.

That gives Canelo a realistic path to victory. Mbilli can throw and land three times as many punches, but judges often reward Canelo’s cleaner, harder single shots. Activity does not guarantee points, and Mbilli will offer plenty of targets for flashier work.

Canelo would get far fewer looks against Iglesias. He would need to evade the jab, close the gap, and connect before Iglesias moves away or fires back with something harder.

“I just need to be myself, and that is how I am going to win this fight,” Mbilli stated.

He could be right. Mbilli’s furious engine could easily overwhelm the veteran if Canelo cannot punch with enough authority to slow him down. Calling him the better option is far from guaranteeing a Canelo win.

Canelo never admitted to dodging Iglesias over stylistic concerns, and this remains a personal breakdown of the matchup. Still, Schaefer’s spin invites a reality check. Between the two champions on the table, Canelo selected the opponent who gives him room to land and a much clearer route to a victory on the cards.

It still could be controversial if Canelo wins a decision against Mbilli, but at least he would see the final bell, and his face wouldn’t be as beat up as it would be against Iglesias.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest 40-year-old man with 91 parcels of suspected Indian hemp at Circle
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 40-year-old man, Roger Borbobli, after allegedly finding 91 parcels of substances suspected to be Indian hemp in his possession at the VIP Bus Terminal at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra.

The arrest was made on October 29, 2026, by officers from the Office of the Special Operations Assistant to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), following information that the suspect had been spotted at the terminal with three suitcases containing the suspected narcotics.

According to preliminary investigations, some loading boys at the terminal detected an unusual smell coming from the suitcases and alerted the Police.

A team of officers subsequently arrived at the scene, arrested the suspect and retrieved the three suitcases, which contained 91 parcels of compressed dried leaves suspected to be Indian hemp.

The suspect reportedly valued the seized substances at GH¢33,600.

During interrogation, Mr Borbobli allegedly told investigators that he was a farmer from Sovie Kudzra, near Kpando in the Volta North Region.

He reportedly admitted cultivating Indian hemp but said the parcels found in his possession had been acquired from another farmer, identified as Benjamin, from the same community.

The exhibits are expected to be forwarded to the Police Forensic Crime Laboratory for analytical examination.

The suspect remains in Police custody, assisting investigations, and is expected to be brought before the court to face justice.

Ghana News.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
Ghana News.content:
Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.

"Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation," Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said.

Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus.

Melania Trump said that "all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders".

Speaking to journalists on Friday evening, Lantratova put out a joint request with her Ukrainian counterpart "to the US First Lady... that humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump".

A ceasefire - the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined.

Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay, despite the widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

"Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to do so safely," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Friday morning.

"At the same time, those who decide to remain will be able to stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian assistance."

Ukrainian military positions lie 5km (3.1miles) from Oleshky, but the evacuees will first have to travel into Russian-occupied territory and then to the southern Russian city of Anapa.

They will board a Russian government plane to Gomel in Belarus, and then drive across the border into Ukraine's Chernihiv region.

Others are expected to choose to stay in Russian-occupied territory.

Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova travelled to Oleshky together on Friday, setting off from Armiansk, in the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula.

Lubinets is the first Ukrainian official since the start of the war to visit Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. He will also become the first to visit Russia when he escorts the evacuees back into Ukraine on Saturday.

The Oleshky ceasefire has required close cooperation with Lantratova, which Lubinets said he carried out in the interests of saving lives.

But some in Ukraine have recoiled at the sight of him standing beside a representative of the Russian occupying power which has killed so many of the city's residents and made life unbearable for the rest.

Both Lubinets and Lantratova posted videos from Oleshky on their social media channels, saying people were given the chance to form two groups depending on whether they wanted to be taken to Russian-controlled territory or to Ukraine.

In one video, Lubinets can be seen meeting tearful locals. "The problem is that a lot of people are staying," he can be heard saying. "I was told that it was their own choice, we will do everything possible for the humanitarian aid to arrive."

Russia said on Thursday that it had prepared "dozens of tonnes" of aid for the residents who do not wish to leave, including food, medicine, hygiene products and fuel for generators.

An Oleshky resident told the BBC she had decided against leaving because "they wouldn't take my animals, so that's it."

Olena, who now lives in Kyiv, said her grandmother and wider family in Oleshky were also staying behind.

"The older generation does not want to leave," she told the BBC. "I've barely managed to persuade my father - and only because I've just had a baby, who he would never see otherwise."

Olena's grandmother's sister died in Oleshky last winter.

"She lost her legs after stepping on a landmine, covered in snow... People took her to the hospital in a garden wheelbarrow," Olena said.

"That's how locals transport all wounded and dead people in Oleshky to the hospital and the hospital's morgue: in garden wheelbarrows."

The ceasefire is due to be in force until the end of Sunday 1 November. It has provided the first few days of peace in the Kherson region since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Residents of Kherson told the BBC they were "overjoyed" by the ceasefire. However, they are concerned the truce has given Russia time to build up its military presence on the banks of the Dnipro river, which could result in a renewed assault once the ceasefire expires.

On Friday, the Kremlin made it clear that the success of the Oleshky ceasefire should not be interpreted as willingness to extend the truce to the rest of Ukraine.

A handful of foreign journalists have been invited to witness the evacuation of the town, which Moscow is expected to present as a humanitarian mission conducted with mercy to protect the people of Oleshky.

Many Ukrainians suspect Russia's real intention is to earn credit with the White House, and to provide US President Donald Trump with a boost ahead of next week's midterm elections.

Ghana News.title: Konongo, Juansa chiefs back revocation of Northern Ashanti Mines license
Ghana News.content:
Traditional authorities in Konongo and Juansa have backed the revocation of the mining license of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited in its catchment.

They cite poor performance, environmental degradation and neglect of responsibilities towards local communities.

This comes after the Minerals Commission terminated the company's mineral rights following allegations that portions of the concession were given to illegal miners.

Staff have since been asked to vacate the concession as the mine is non-operational.

Chief of Konongo, Nana Dr. Awuah Abedimsa II, supports the Commission.

"Minerals Commission is the statutory body responsible for mining and they have performance indicators which they use in measuring the performance of all Mining Companies. So the action taken by the minerals commission on behalf of the Konongo mine, I agree with it," he said.

He added that "the Northern Ashanti Mines in my opinion didn't have the resources to mine the deposits and it has given rise to the environmental degradation that we fought and continue to fight against."

He wants the mine given to credible investors.

Chief of Juansa, Nana Tweneboah Kodua Bempah, also backs a reset.

"The illegal miners have destroyed some water bodies in the area. Our community largely depend on farming and whoever mines there should do it responsibly. We need people who will mine responsibly so we can protect our river bodies," he said.

Government intervention

The lease was granted to Owere Mines in January 2010 covering 595 cadastral blocks. Under Section 24 of Act 703, it was bound to pay Annual Mineral Right fees, which it failed to do so.

The Minerals Commission says it exercised persistent forbearance issuing a Notice to Remedy Breach in May 2020 when arrears exceeded US$4 million.

The company, transitioning to BCM Investments, proposed payment in four tranches which it failed to meet its own plan.

The Commission issued successive notices between 2020 and 2025. Debt rose from US$5.5 million in October 2022 to US$6.1 million in December 2022, and to US$8.33 million for mining leases plus US$49,928 for prospecting licences by April 2025. The company failed to make payments.

On April 7, 2026, the Commission deemed the breach flagrant and deliberate and requested the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources to terminate. The Minister approved and the rights were terminated.

The Commission rejects claims that the US$8 million figure is wrong and disputes the company's claim of paying US$1 million. Its records show only US$300,000 paid.

"For a company that claims to have spent US$200,000,000 on the mine, what prevented it from paying the US$8,000,000 owed to the people of Ghana?" it queried.

Under Section 70 of Act 703, terminated rights revert to the State. The State will secure the assets and pursue all outstanding liabilities.

"A mineral right is not a gift, and it is not an inheritance! It is a privilege conferred by the State on terms, and those terms must be honoured," the Commission said, insisting it acted lawfully and with due process.

The military remains stationed at the facility as the government is expected to announce next steps.

The taskforce fears that the lack of cooperation from residents could compromise its operations.

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian creatives losing funding opportunities over poor documentation – Sustainable finance expert
Ghana News.content:
The Head of Sustainable Financing at Consolidated Bank Ghana (CBG), Eva Ackuaku, has expressed concern over the inability of many Ghanaian creatives to access available funding opportunities due to poor documentation and a lack of formal business structures.

According to her, many talented individuals in the creative industry, particularly photographers and other content creators, struggle to secure financial support because they operate without registered businesses, bank accounts or proper financial records.

Speaking at the Climate x Culture Summit organised by CultureJoint in partnership with the Ministry for Climate Change and Sustainability on Thursday, October 22, 2026, Ms Ackuaku urged creatives to formalise their operations and adopt sustainable financial practices to attract investment.

She explained that although Ghana's creative industry has enormous economic potential, many practitioners remain in the informal sector, making it difficult for financial institutions to assess their eligibility for funding.

“The creative industry is a viable industry. However, most of these people are found in the informal sector,” she stated.

Citing photographers as an example, Ms Ackuaku noted that some creative professionals who have worked for several years are unable to provide basic documentation, including invoices and proof of business registration.

“I have employed some of them within the bank. And then they ask you, oh, madam, I don't have an invoice. Madam, I don't have a business,” she recounted.

She questioned why creatives with established careers continue to operate without formal registration or bank accounts, explaining that such records are essential for assessing their financial activities and determining their eligibility for support.

“Why haven't you registered your company? Why don't you have a bank account? If I want to help you scale, it means that I should have your bank account to tell me the inflows and the outflows in your bank statement,” she said.

Ms Ackuaku further emphasised that creative professionals seeking financial assistance must demonstrate the sustainability of their projects through proper research, financial planning and viable business models.

“How do we scale if the business is not sustainable? And so we must ensure that whatever projects that you are bringing to us, it is sustainable,” she stressed.

She explained that financial institutions have a responsibility to ensure that funds are invested prudently so that resources remain available to support other creatives and emerging entrepreneurs.

“As a bank, we work for the public. The funds are not for the bank. It's for everyone who is seated here,” she stated.

“And we owe that obligation to ensure that we put it to good use and make it very sustainable,” she added.

Ms Ackuaku also expressed concern that Ghana continues to miss out on funding opportunities because potential beneficiaries, including creative professionals, are often unable to meet the necessary requirements.

“Funds come to Ghana and we're unable to assess the funds. And it goes back,” she lamented.

Other panellists included Robert Klah, Head of Public Relations at Charterhouse; Kofi Adjei, Head of Research at the Multimedia Group; and African art curator Nuna Adisenu-Doe.

The Climate x Culture Summit brought together stakeholders from the creative, financial and environmental sectors to explore the role of culture and creativity in advancing climate action and sustainable development.

Ms Ackuaku urged creatives to take advantage of available financing opportunities by registering their businesses, maintaining proper financial records and developing sustainable projects capable of attracting investment and supporting long-term growth in Ghana's creative industry.

Ghana News.title: NPP petitions US to suspend privileges for Ghanaian diplomatic, service passport holders
Ghana News.content:
Justin Frimpong Kodua

The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has called on the United States to review its treatment of Ghanaian diplomatic and service passport holders following allegations that some travel documents were secured using false or inaccurate official designations.

The party has identified six individuals whose service passport applications were approved by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as officials of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) and the Fisheries Commission, but whom it claims do not hold the positions stated in the approval documents.

In a petition dated October 30, 2026, and signed by General Secretary Justin Kodua Frimpong, the NPP asked the US Chargé d’Affaires in Ghana, Rolf Olson, to suspend diplomatic courtesies for the individuals concerned and introduce stricter checks on Ghanaian diplomatic and service passport holders.

The party cited two Ministry of Foreign Affairs letters issued on August 6 and 7, 2026. The first approved service passports for Twumasi Francis Kwame, Shaibu Alhassan Abu and Gyabaah Anthony, described respectively as Deputy Director of Climate Change, Director of Hydro and Director of Geology at NADMO.

However, the NPP claimed that those positions were occupied by Ebenezer Vandyke, Dr Bertha Kusimi and Bright Atama respectively, raising questions about the accuracy of the designations used to secure the approvals.

The second letter covered Issah Ayisha, Bennor Yussif and Adom Emmanuel Kwabena as officials of the Fisheries Commission.

The party alleged that the designation Deputy Director of Aquaculture Specialist did not exist, the Deputy Director of Information Technology position was held by another officer, and the Commission had no Assistant Finance Manager position.

The NPP argued that the alleged discrepancies undermined the basis for issuing the passports, which the Ministry's letters indicated were strictly for official use. “A passport cannot be for official use where its bearer holds no office that calls for official travel,” the party stated.

It further described the approvals as irregular, arguing that they “rest on a misdescription of the applicants’ positions, and the passports issued on them are irregular.”

Beyond the six cases, the party wants the US Mission to introduce enhanced verification for Ghanaian diplomatic and service passports issued from January 7, 2025.

It says the process should include direct confirmation of passport holders’ positions with the institutions they are alleged to represent.

The NPP has also urged the government to suspend passports issued to ineligible persons, publish a full list of diplomatic and service passports issued since January 2025, and commission an independent audit of the issuance process.

It wants the Auditor-General or another independent body to conduct the exercise and make its findings public.

The party is further demanding the revocation and recovery of passports found to have been issued irregularly, as well as investigations and possible prosecution of anyone found culpable.

It said the petition was intended to protect Ghana’s national interest rather than inconvenience officials travelling on legitimate state business.

The NPP also referred to recent drug seizures linked to consignments from Ghana and romance fraud cases prosecuted abroad, which it said had contributed to international embarrassment for the country.

Ghana News.title: Ghana vows to pursue justice for 15-year-old boy shot dead in New York
Ghana News.content:
The Government of Ghana has pledged to pursue justice for 15-year-old Ghanaian teenager Javits Frimpong, who was fatally shot in the Bronx, New York, on Thursday, October 29.

Javits was reportedly shot by unidentified assailants at about 9:20 a.m. while on his way to school.

In a statement issued on Friday, October 30, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned the killing and assured the bereaved family of the government's commitment to ensuring that those responsible are brought to justice.

According to the Ministry, Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa personally contacted the victim's father, Thomas Frimpong, on Friday morning to express condolences and assure him of the government's support.

“We will pursue justice, and we will make sure that those who did this do not get away with it,” the Minister assured the grieving father.

Mr Ablakwa, on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama, also extended heartfelt condolences to the family, describing the teenager's death as devastating.

“We are all saddened. We are all distraught. He did not deserve this,” he stated.

The Ministry disclosed that officials from Ghana's Permanent Mission in New York had visited Mr Frimpong at his residence to commiserate with the family and convey the government's solidarity.

It further called on authorities in the Bronx to conduct a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the shooting and ensure that the perpetrators face justice.

The Ministry emphasised that Ghana's diplomatic mission in New York would work closely with US authorities to pursue justice while providing the necessary legal and consular assistance to the family.

It reaffirmed the government's commitment to protecting the safety, dignity and wellbeing of Ghanaians living abroad.

“Ghana remains steadfast in its unwavering commitment to the safety, dignity and well-being of our citizens everywhere, any time, and in all circumstances,” the statement said.

The government also extended its sympathies to the teenager's relatives and loved ones in Ghana and the United States, particularly his mother, Doris Adu Gyamfi, who resides in Kumasi.

Meanwhile, investigations into the shooting are ongoing as authorities work to identify and apprehend those responsible.

Ghana News.title: Chinese hospital ship concludes seven-day medical mission in Ghana, treating 5,909 people
Ghana News.content:
The Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy hospital ship, Auspicious Ark (Hull 868), has concluded its seven-day humanitarian medical mission in Ghana after providing healthcare services to 5,909 people.

The mission ended with a farewell ceremony at the Tema Port on Friday, October 30, 2026, marking the conclusion of the vessel’s visit under China’s Mission Harmony 2026 initiative.

During its stay, the medical team provided free services to Ghanaians and Chinese nationals living in the country, covering general consultations, dental care, eye treatment, dermatology, cardiovascular examinations, orthopaedic care and physiotherapy.

The team also conducted laboratory investigations and performed approximately 40 surgical procedures.

According to the Ghana Armed Forces, a total of 5,909 people received medical attention both aboard the hospital ship and through its community outreach activities.

The visit also facilitated professional exchanges between Ghanaian and Chinese medical personnel, with discussions and engagements focusing on specialised healthcare delivery, naval medicine and emergency medical response.

The Director of Medical Logistics, Brigadier General Michael Addy, joined other officials at the Tema Port to bid farewell to the crew and wish them a safe voyage.

The Ghana Armed Forces expressed appreciation to the Chinese People’s Liberation Army Navy, the mission commander and the medical team for their dedication and contribution to healthcare delivery in the country.

The mission forms part of efforts to strengthen medical cooperation and bilateral relations between Ghana and China, while promoting professional collaboration between the two countries’ healthcare personnel.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
