World.title: How cuts under Colombia’s de la Espriella threaten a key human rights court
World.content:
Bogota, Colombia – Angela Cordon was only a teenager when her father and uncle disappeared.

They were among a string of farmers and merchants to go missing in the southwestern department of Huila in Colombia.

First came her uncle Reynaldo Cordon Herrera's kidnapping. A grocer by trade, he had been travelling by truck on January 22, 2003, when he went missing.

The next month, Guillermo Cordon Herrera — Angela's father — set out to discover what happened to his brother, tracing his whereabouts through rural Colombia.

Guillermo called home one night with news: He had made contact with the rebel fighters he believed to be responsible for his brother's abduction.

It was the last time his family would ever hear from him. His body was never found, nor was his brother's.

Angela's father and uncle are among the more than 450,664 people killed as part of Colombia's six-decade-long internal armed conflict.

In the 23 years since their disappearance, Angela and her family have sought any information they could find about their loved ones' last days. "I have dedicated my life to this search," she told Al Jazeera.

She credits one institution in particular with helping her find answers: Colombia's Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP), a transitional justice court.

Set up in 2016 as part of a peace deal between the government and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), the country's largest rebel group at the time, the court handles the prosecution and investigation of crimes committed during the conflict.

But victims, their loved ones and even some former fighters fear that budget cuts could gut JEP, leaving the court unable to fulfil its mission.

This month, the administration of right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella announced it would enact a 2027 budget with dramatic reductions for government bodies like JEP.

The total cuts to JEP were valued at around 181 billion Colombian pesos, or roughly $57m.

On Wednesday, a Senate committee also advanced a bill to eliminate JEP altogether by March 2028, with a proposal to transfer its functions to the general court system.

Angela, however, credits JEP with offering closure that the criminal justice system was never able to provide. She worries that slashing the court's funding — much less shuttering it entirely — could derail its work.

Through JEP, Angela learned about her father and uncle's time in captivity, as well as the site of their execution. JEP has also worked with former FARC members to try to locate their remains.

"Fewer resources mean fewer missions to the field to find answers, less humanitarian personnel," Angela said, bracing for the cuts.

"It probably means that we will never be able to return to the site."

World.title: Report reveals campaign promoting racist, Islamophobic, anti-Qatar views
World.content:
Investigation finds that years-long operation sought to portray Qatar as driving force behind mass migration to Europe.

Share Campaign pushes racist and anti-Qatar ads across Europe, US: Report on social media

A years-long, paid-for influence operation promoting racist, Islamophobic and anti-Qatar views has been uncovered by two academics, with the evidence suggesting the campaign was intended to serve Israeli interests.

The investigation, which took three years, was published on Thursday. It detailed an operation that likely cost more than $11m and was carried out across 30 countries, including in Europe, the United States and Lebanon.

As part of the campaign, several million internet users were exposed to s on sites like YouTube, TikTok and Facebook that pushed an agenda, according to the report titled Manufacturing the “Great Replacement”.

Marc Owen Jones, a professor at Northwestern University’s Doha campus, and independent researcher Sohan Dsouza, the academics who published the report, called it “perhaps one of the biggest digital influence and disinformation operations ever documented”.

Their report uncovered at least 533 million exposures of social media s promoting anti-Muslim, anti-migrant, racist and anti-Qatar views between October 2023 and October 2026. It added that the s were launched ahead of elections in some of the target countries.

One example, also reported by French newspaper Le Monde, looked at how the campaign had targeted France and found that “a historical analysis of the ads pushed by the campaign’s backers suggests that they repeatedly sought to align with national electoral calendars”, the newspaper said.

“Buying in France ran through the months before the June 2024 European Parliament elections, and UK buying stopped on 17 May 2024, days before the general election was called,” the researchers said.



“Its sustained promotion of anti-Muslim and anti-migrant narratives raises concerns about attempts to shape the political environment ahead of these votes, beyond the formal election campaign period,” they added.

Additionally, the report warned that “the campaign remains active in countries approaching major elections, including France and Italy in 2027”.

Qatar targeted

France accounted for about a third of the total number of  placements, the highest share among the countries targeted, the report said. Meanwhile, the s recorded the largest number of exposures in the United Kingdom, at 154 million. The US came second, with 100 million.

“In Europe, the ads use the structure of the Great Replacement conspiracy theory, that white people are being replaced by immigrants,” Jones said.

“Qatar takes the role that anti-Semitic versions give to George Soros: a hidden power directing Muslim immigration to ‘Islamise’ Europe,” he noted, referring to the Jewish billionaire philanthropist and frequent target of anti-Semitic conspiracy theories.

Separately, one of the campaigns that appeared on TikTok promoted regime change in Iran to audiences in Europe. The ads first began running on February 24, four days before the US and Israel launched their war on the country, the investigation found.

According to the report, the evidence suggests with “moderate to high confidence” that the influence operation was launched from within Israel and sought to portray Qatar as the driving force behind mass migration meant to allegedly “Islamise” Europe.

The researchers said metadata shows that video editors working on the campaign did so in the Israeli time zone. It also reveals that they used machines with Hebrew drive and folder names.

Qatar has been the focus of Israeli-linked campaigns before. Last month, the Israeli newspaper Haaretz found that a group of Israeli influence experts and political advisers had worked on a secret campaign targeting Doha in the weeks after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks.

Israeli politicians have also lashed out at Qatar several times in recent years, with former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett calling for the country to be declared an enemy state.

Most recently, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party accused Doha, without evidence, of interfering in Israeli elections held on Tuesday. The Qatari Foreign Ministry has denounced the allegations as a “disinformation campaign”.

World.title: Barcelona’s Flick praises Yamal’s ‘mentality’ after missing out on Ballon d’Or
World.content:
Lamine Yamal was tipped for the Ballon d’Or which went to Harry Kane, but his Barca boss ‘proud’ of teenager’s reaction.

Share Barcelona’s Flick praises Yamal’s ‘mentality’ after missing out on Ballon d’Or on social media

Lamine Yamal has “reacted very well” following the disappointment of the Ballon d’Or being awarded to Harry Kane, Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said on Friday.

Despite winning La Liga with the Catalan club and lifting the World Cup with Spain, the 19-year-old winger came third in the vote for the best player in the world on Monday, behind Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

“Harry Kane deserved it, but you already know what I think about Lamine. He’s at the level required to win this award,” Flick said ahead of the La Liga leaders’ home match against Alaves.

“I’m very proud of Lamine. He reacted very well and was very focused in training.

“That’s the way to respond. His mentality is very good for the team.”

Yamal will have a chance to put any lingering disappointment behind him on Saturday when Barcelona look to correct course at home to Alaves following two high-profile defeats.

After winning their first 11 matches in all competitions, Barcelona were flying but then came undone when they travelled to PSG in the Champions League last Tuesday.

That 4-2 reverse in the French capital was swiftly followed by a Mbappe-inspired 2-1 loss at home to Real Madrid in La Liga last weekend.

“The most important thing tomorrow is to win,” Flick said.

“The team is playing well and we believe in our strengths. I’ve seen a good training session and a positive mood. We have to show that tomorrow.

“Alaves are a team that know how to defend well, but we’re Barca and we want to show our best version.”

Barcelona still hold a two-point lead at the top of La Liga ahead of their meeting with Atletico Madrid.



While the German coach admitted he does not like losing, he insisted that the campaign is “a long road”.

“It’s at the end of the season that we can win trophies,” he added.

“We have to deal with it. We could have won, but we have to accept defeat and learn from it.”

World.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
World.content:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist.

The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider.

Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (Â£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit.

The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds.

America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI.

While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort.

The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle â cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar.

Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss".

It had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected".

World.title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution
World.content:
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee paused all executions for the remainder of the year and ordered an independent review to "determine exactly what occurred".

Lee was asked by reporters this week about a potential second execution attempt. "I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts," he responded.

Speaking about the state's response to what happened to Pike, Mann said: "I find it deeply troubling that, even after what Christa endured, Governor Lee has shown little public willingness to reconsider the death penalty itself, rather than simply the procedures used to carry it out."

She added: "What happened to Christa is not an isolated tragedy, nor should this conversation begin and end with her."

The Tennessee Department of Correction has not explained why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used.

It declined comment on Pike's statement when contacted by the BBC.

Slemmer's mother, May Martinez, was among those pushing for Pike to be put to death and attended the botched execution, later calling it a "mess".

She told a local ABC News affiliate in Florida, where she lives, that she thinks the state owes her an apology.

"All I wanted was justice," Martinez said.

Pike was the first woman scheduled to be executed in the state of Tennessee in over 200 years.

Her lawyers have spent decades appealing her case. In the days leading up to her scheduled execution, both the US Supreme Court and Lee declined to block the execution.

The attempted execution of Pike was not the first in Tennessee in 2026 that did not go to plan.

The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein for a lethal injection. He was granted a year's reprieve by the governor.

In 2022, more than a third of executions across the US were botched or highly problematic, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, which does not take an ethical stance on the penalty.

World.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
World.content:
Speaking to journalists on Friday evening, Lantratova put out a joint request with her Ukrainian counterpart "to the US First Lady... that humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump".

A ceasefire - the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 - has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined.

Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility.

Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay, despite the widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water.

"Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to do so safely," Ukraine's human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Friday morning.

"At the same time, those who decide to remain will be able to stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian assistance."

Ukrainian military positions lie 5km (3.1miles) from Oleshky, but the evacuees will first have to travel into Russian-occupied territory and then to the southern Russian city of Anapa.

They will board a Russian government plane to Gomel in Belarus, and then drive across the border into Ukraine's Chernihiv region.

Others are expected to choose to stay in Russian-occupied territory.

World.title: Prominent Russian newspaper shuts down under pressure from authorities
World.content:
For the last three decades, Novaya Gazeta has been one of the most high-profile independent news outlets in Russia.

Now it's shutting down - and it has accused the Russian authorities of the "murder" of a newspaper.

"They've killed us," reads a statement on the Novaya Gazeta website.

"The newspaper is no more. The Russian authorities and Russian special services have forced the paper to stop its work."

Novaya Gazeta has received an eviction order. Crucially, at the same time, the system that had allowed the paper to receive donations from readers was disabled.

That leaves no way to fund the publication.

Novaya Gazeta had developed a reputation for fearless investigative reporting on subjects such as corruption, human rights violations and abuse of power by officials and bureaucrats - dangerous topics in Russia.

World.title: Spain transport minister says he won't resign over high-speed rail disaster
World.content:
Spain's transport minister says he won't resign over the high-speed rail collision that has left at least 69 people dead.

Ãscar Puente told a news conference in Madrid he had "nothing to hide" while repeating the government's vow to get to the bottom of the disaster, saying many questions needed to be answered.

"My duty right now is not to talk about whether I should remain in my position, but to resolve the problem," Puente said.

The transport minister has been facing calls to step down in the aftermath of the tragedy, including from political rivals, a trade union and demonstrators who protested outside the transport ministry on Wednesday night.

Dozens were killed and many more injured when a state-operated Renfe high-speed train smashed into the back of another stationary train operated by the Iryo company near the town of Urda, in the central Toledo province, on Wednesday morning.

A preliminary report released by transport investigators late on Thursday found the Renfe train was travelling between 160km/h (99.4mph) and 200km/h when the collision occurred, causing its front carriage to become embedded in the tail of the stationary train.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez said earlier on Friday that public trust in Spain's high-speed rail network had been broken and repeated it was "unacceptable" that there had been two similar tragedies within a year.

World.title: Pope Leo XIV becomes first pontiff to vote in a US election
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has submitted his mail-in ballot in Illinois, for the midterm elections, becoming the first-ever pope to vote in a US election.

"The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in democratic processes," the Holy See Press Office said in a statement.

The Chicago-born pontiff is the first US citizen to hold the Vatican's highest seat, after his selection in May 2025.

Since then, he has clashed with the Trump administration over various issues, including immigration enforcement and the US-Israel war with Iran.

"Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so," the press office said, including during his years in Peru.

The US midterm elections will determine which political party controls Congress and have a significant impact on the final years of Donald Trump's presidency.

Elections will be held nationwide on 3 November, but early voting has begun in most states.

According to NBC News, the Pope requested his mail-in ballot from the Will County Clerk's Office on 3 October.

Less than two weeks later, the Vatican announced he had surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung after he was diagnosed with lung cancer.

The Vatican confirmed last week that the Pope, aged 71, will travel as planned to Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru in early November.

Tensions escalated between the Pope and the US president in April, after the Pope called for peace in the wake of US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

"I don't think he's doing a very good job," Trump said about the Pope afterwards.

"We don't like a Pope that's going to say that it's OK to have a nuclear weapon," he continued. "I'm not a big fan of Pope Leo."

Pope Leo followed with his own remarks later, saying: "The mission of the Church is to preach the Gospel, to preach peace," according to Reuters.

"If someone wants to criticise me for preaching the Gospel... I hope simply to be listened to because of the value of God's words."

World.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
World.content:
Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).

Shares in Intel plummeted by as much as 30% on Friday, following Google owner Alphabet's stock price plunging by more than $500bn (Â£374bn) in the previous day's trading.

Other tech stocks including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, sank more than 3.5%.

While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.

Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800.6bn between them in 2026.

Alphabet's stock market value plunged on Thursday after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.

At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI.

Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 2.2% after Thursday's slide of more than 12%.

The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value as its shares continued to fall in Friday trading.

The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors.

On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

"Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.

In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.

World.title: G20 'family photo' cancelled after protests over presence of Russian minister
World.content:
Relations between Ukraine and the US have been particularly tense this month, with a diplomatic standoff between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Donald Trump over Kyiv's strikes on oil infrastructure within Russia.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is present and a diplomatic source confirmed the UK was among the countries which refused to participate in the picture.

One British official said: "The UK has a longstanding policy not to have direct, bilateral engagement with Russian ministers since the invasion of Ukraine and we are not about to change that".

A US official said the photo was cancelled "after it became clear some of the delegations were unwilling to participate in a joint photo".

"Rather than allow a ceremonial photo opportunity to become a diplomatic distraction, the US decided to forgo the photo and keep the focus on the substantive discussions," the official said.

In contrast to Ukraine, relations between the US and Russia appear to have partially thawed in recent weeks, as Trump waived some sanctions and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the American market.

The move comes as Trump attempts to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of mid-term elections at the start of November, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war.

Ukraine and its European allies have heavily criticised Trump's deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Zelensky called it "a gift" to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged".

Trump said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table in the war between Russia and Ukraine.

Putin has said Russia, which introduced a ban on diesel exports earlier this year, is willing to supply both the US and global markets with oil and petroleum products.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and currently controls approximately a fifth of Ukrainian territory.

Moscow has in recent weeks intensified its deadly missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities.

World.title: Chris Okafor: Doris Ogala remains in custody as court postpones bail ruling
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Lagos on Friday adjourned the bail hearing of actress Doris Ogala until 6 November in the case involving her and Chris Okafor, founder of the Mountain of Liberation and Miracle Ministry.

PREMIUM TIMES had earlier reported that Justice Akintayo Aluko ordered the remand of Ms Ogala, the African Action Congress (AAC) governorship candidate in the forthcoming Abia State election, at Ikoyi Correctional Centre.

The actress appeared before the court over allegations bordering on cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion, lawyers representing both parties told this newspaper.

Ife Ajayi, who represents Mr Okafor, and Nzeakor Atulomah confirmed that the judge adjourned the bail hearing to 6 November, leaving Ms Ogala in custody pending the court’s decision.

“The case was adjourned till 6th Nov 2026 for ruling on her bail application. She continues to remain in the correctional facility, Ikoyi Prison”, Mr Ajayi said.

Mr Atulomah expressed confidence that his client would secure bail when the court resumed proceedings.

“My juniors were in court. The bail application was taken today and adjourned to 6 Nov for ruling. We’re hopeful the court would admit the defendant to bail. As we argued before the court, the charges are ‘bailable,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ruling

Meanwhile, Justice Aluko said the actress’s actions disrupted the court’s schedule, leaving more than seven other cases listed for that day unheard.

He revealed that he initially considered committing her for contempt following the incident but eventually spared her, despite believing that her behaviour justified such a punishment.

According to the judge, Ms Ogala could have faced at least two months in prison for obstructing the court’s proceedings.

Justice Aluko said, “She should have been given some form of imprisonment, right, on that day, but I kept my cool, and I rose. Why do you have to start shouting and start singing in the open court? You conducted yourself in a manner that forced the court to rise. That’s what you did, and it’s already recorded.”

The judge also criticised the defence counsel for failing to acknowledge the incident and explain the defendant’s conduct before presenting arguments in support of the bail application.

He recalled that he had personally ordered an expedited hearing of the application and taken steps to ensure that the court heard it within 48 hours.

He said he was disappointed that Wednesday’s disruption occurred despite his efforts to fast-track the proceedings.

Ogala speaks

Speaking after the court ordered her return to prison, Ms Ogala alleged that Mr Okafor and others had deliberately frustrated her bail hearing.

She maintained that she neither feared nor felt intimidated by anyone involved in the case.

She further alleged that some individuals had politically motivated her continued detention to distract her from her campaign to become Abia State governor.

“This thing here is already prepared, but one thing you must know about Doris Ogala is that I am not perturbed. They said the bail ruling is on Friday, but that Friday, they will still send me back. You know why? Because they don’t want me to come out. First, they don’t want me to campaign. This is politically motivated. More than four pastors and the government come together to keep me down here.

“But whether they like it or not, bail is my right. They will leave me. If they like, let them keep me here for 10 years; I am not afraid of them. You see this court? I’m disappointed that our judicial system has reduced itself to this level. Imagine a judge doing the bidding of a pastor who did not even attend school. I am ashamed of the judicial system of this country”, said the actress.

Disappointment

The actress further expressed displeasure with the Ministry of Justice over its involvement in what she called a “boyfriend and girlfriend” affair.

She maintained that prison differed from what people generally imagined and stressed that she remained unconvicted. She accused influential figures in the case of using the law as a weapon against her.

“I’m ashamed of the Ministry of Justice to reduce themselves to this level of now fighting boyfriend and girlfriend matters in the name of the federal government. This case is between the federal government and Doris Ogalla. I am not afraid of them. Every powerful man you see in this life has gone into prison, and they came out strong. Doris is not afraid. I am going back to prison.

“I’m not afraid of Chris Okafor. And you will not bend me. I want you guys to know that it is Doris today. It will be you tomorrow. You are sitting down there saying that Doris is guilty. I am not guilty. If Chris Okafor is not afraid, why don’t he stop putting me in prison with his resources and come let us face the court. Let’s go to the trial and see who is guilty. But you see this matter? I will not stop it. I will get to the end of it. You know me now.”

Ms Ogala vowed to get to the root of the matter and urged her fans and supporters not to listen to the negative things people are saying.

“They cannot intimidate me. Alex Otti, I am not afraid of you.”

World.title: Nigeria, Russia move to replace 59-year-old aviation agreement
World.content:
Nigeria and Russia have agreed to replace a 59-year-old aviation agreement, aiming to update air transport relations and create opportunities for stronger connectivity between the two countries.

The agreement to renegotiate the Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA), which dates back to 1967, was reached during a meeting between Nigeria’s Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and Russian officials on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow.

Mr Keyamo disclosed the development in a post on his X account on Friday, saying both countries had agreed to complete negotiations within six months and sign a new agreement in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in April 2027.

He said the Nigerian delegation met with Dmitry Stanislavovich Zverev, the State Secretary and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Russian Federation.

“We resolved to renegotiate our last Bilateral Air Service Agreement that was made in 1967. We set a timeline of six months to conclude the negotiations and sign a new one in Saint Petersburg in April 2027,” Mr Keyamo said.

He added that both countries had formed negotiating teams to begin work toward an agreement within the agreed period.

The proposed renegotiation is expected to update the framework governing air transport between Nigeria and Russia, reflecting changes in the international aviation industry over the past six decades.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

What the agreement means

A Bilateral Air Services Agreement provides the legal framework for scheduled air services between two countries. It generally sets out the conditions under which airlines from both countries can operate international flights, including routes, traffic rights, designated airlines and other operational arrangements.

Nigeria’s Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development says its Air Transport Management Department negotiates and reviews new and existing air services agreements and monitors their implementation.

The ministry also works with the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority and other aviation agencies to facilitate international air links and regulate airline operations.

The proposed replacement of the Nigeria-Russia agreement could therefore create opportunities for improved air connectivity and cooperation between their aviation sectors.

However, neither Mr Keyamo nor the ministry disclosed proposed flight routes, designated airlines or the frequency of possible operations under the new agreement.

Wider cooperation

Beyond the aviation agreement, Mr Keyamo said the meeting also examined other areas of cooperation between Nigeria and Russia.

He said both sides had resolved to explore additional opportunities in the coming months.

The Nigerian delegation included the Director-General of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority, Capt: Chris Najomo, and the Registrar of the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology, Dr Danjuma Adamu Ismaila.

Directors from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA also participated in the discussions.

Nigeria and Russia have maintained diplomatic relations since shortly after Nigeria gained independence in 1960. Their relationship has included cooperation in areas such as defence, trade, science and technology.

According to the Nigerian Embassy in Russia, the Soviet Union provided political and military assistance to Nigeria during the 1967–1970 Civil War. Cooperation between the two countries has also extended to space technology, including the launch of Nigeria’s satellites aboard Russian rockets in 2011.

The planned aviation agreement is expected to form part of broader efforts to deepen bilateral relations and identify further areas of cooperation.

Both countries are expected to begin negotiations through their respective teams, aiming to conclude the process and sign the new agreement in Saint Petersburg in April 2027.

World.title: BUA Foods’ nine-month profit rises to N450 billion
World.content:
Leading maker of sugar, pasta and edible oils, BUA Foods, recorded an 11.2 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit for the first nine months of the year, its unaudited financials published on Friday showed.

The company generated N1.1 trillion in turnover, down from N1.4 trillion a year ago, following weaker sales from its bakery flour and fortified sugar businesses.

That notwithstanding, the manufacturer sharply reduced its spending on raw materials by 37.2 per cent as a key strategy in bringing down cost of sales, which, in turn, helped lift gross profit by N32.2 billion to N552.9 billion.

Moreover, the strong performance was also driven by other cost-management measures.

Administrative expenses, for instance, dropped by more than one quarter to N22 billion, while selling and distribution expenses dropped by 15.4 per cent to N45 billion, easing cost pressures on operating profit.

BUA Foods is majority-owned by billionaire magnate Abdulsamad Rabiu, and carries a market value of N13.7 trillion.

In December 2021, the company announced the combination of its sugar, rice, oil, flour and pasta divisions into a single entity as it moved to leverage economies of scale in its food processing business.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In the period under review, EBITDA margin, a key performance indicator, jumped to 43.6 per cent from 31.3 per cent.

Profit before tax accelerated by 11.1 per cent to N480.5 billion, while profit after tax climbed to N450.5 billion from N405.3 billion.

“Despite a 19% decline in revenue to ₦1.15 trillion, driven by softer pricing conditions and subdued consumer demand, we maintained a substantial improvement in profitability through effective cost optimisation, improved productivity, and rigorous execution across the business,” CEO Ayodele Abioye said in an earnings release document.

“Looking ahead, we remain focused on driving profitable growth, enhancing market penetration, and maintaining operational efficiency,” he added.

World.title: Mohbad’s family seeks delay in Liam’s DNA test, requests US lab details
World.content:
The family of late singer Ilerioluwa “Mohbad” Aloba has asked the authorities to postpone the tissue-based DNA test scheduled for 31 October at Mainland General Hospital/IDH, Yaba, Lagos, as part of efforts to establish the paternity of the singer’s son, Liam.

The authorities scheduled the examination for 10 a.m. to help resolve the protracted dispute over Liam’s paternity.

In a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Friday, the family head, Samuel Aloba, expressed concerns about transparency, sample handling and adherence to existing court orders.

The family stressed that its demands were not meant to frustrate the investigation or prevent the use of scientific methods to establish the truth. Instead, it wants the authorities to conduct the exercise independently, transparently and in strict compliance with the court’s directives.

The family statement read: “The Aloba family respectfully calls for the postponement of the DNA examination scheduled for 31 October

2026, pending adequate clarification of the outstanding concerns. The family reiterates that its position is not an attempt to obstruct the judicial process or frustrate a scientifically valid DNA examination. Rather, the family insists that an exercise of such profound personal, legal and public significance must be conducted transparently.

“Independently and in strict compliance with the order of court. Given the history of the matter and the concerns previously raised by the family regarding the handling of biological samples in the post-mortem process, the family considers it imperative that every reasonable safeguard be put in place to protect the integrity of the proposed examination and the credibility of its eventual result.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Court directives

Furthermore, the family said its concerns stemmed from a 5 May court order directing the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre to conduct the examination using biological tissue recovered from the late singer.

The family expressed reservations about plans to collect the samples in Lagos and transport them to an unnamed laboratory in the United States for analysis.

It questioned whether the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre would conduct the examination itself or merely arrange the transfer of the specimens to the foreign laboratory.

The family maintained that allowing another laboratory to analyse the samples without first securing the necessary court approval could violate the court’s directive.

“This raises a fundamental question that must be answered before the exercise proceeds: Is the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre itself going to conduct the examination contemplated by the court, or is it merely going to collect and dispatch samples to another laboratory? The distinction is material. Where a court has directed that a scientific examination be conducted at a particular institution, the parties are entitled to clarity regarding the manner in which that directive will be implemented.

“If the designated centre intends to rely on a foreign laboratory to perform the actual analysis, the precise arrangement should be transparently explained and, where necessary, presented to the court for clarification or further directions. No party or institution should unilaterally substitute a materially different arrangement for the one contemplated by a subsisting court order without appropriate judicial clarification.”

“Family demands disclosure of laboratory details”

The family further urged the authorities to provide comprehensive details of the overseas laboratory expected to receive the biological samples, including its registered name, physical location, contact details and the identity of the institution undertaking the DNA testing.

They also requested verifiable evidence of the laboratory’s accreditation, staff qualifications, technical capabilities and track record in analysing tissue samples recovered from human remains.

The family argued that confidentiality should not stop concerned parties from confirming the laboratory’s competence or scrutinising the methods it intends to use.

“The precise scope of the examination: a clear explanation of the proposed scientific procedure, the samples to be examined, the tests to be undertaken and the manner in which the results will be generated and reported. The chain of custody: complete documentation showing how the samples will be collected, identified, labelled, sealed, preserved, transported, received and examined, including the persons responsible at each stage.

“Verification of receipt and examination: a reliable mechanism for confirming that the samples collected are the same samples received by the overseas laboratory and that those samples are the ones actually subjected to analysis. Reporting and accountability: clarification of who will issue the final report, to whom the report will be delivered, and what arrangements will be available to authenticate the report and address any legitimate questions concerning the methodology or findings”, said the family.

“More demands”

The family said its requests sought to establish basic safeguards that would ensure the exercise produced credible findings that could stand up to scientific and judicial scrutiny.

It further requested detailed information about the overseas laboratory, including its identity, accreditation and technical capacity to conduct the tests.

“Clear documentation and verification of the collection, preservation, transportation, receipt and examination of the samples. Confirmation of the precise role of the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre in implementing the court’s order.

“Adequate notice to all parties and their legal representatives of any rescheduled exercise. Judicial clarification or further directions wherever necessary to ensure that the examination proceeds in accordance with the court’s order. The family’s position is simple: there must be no room for avoidable doubt about the integrity of the process through which the truth is to be established.”

Possible interference

The family further warned that without adequate protective measures, someone could interfere with, replace or mishandle the samples.

While emphasising that it had not accused anyone of tampering with the specimens, the family insisted that the authorities must make the entire process transparent and subject every stage to independent scrutiny.

“For the avoidance of doubt, the family is not presenting the possibility of manipulation as a fact, nor is it asserting that the proposed examination has already been compromised. Its concern is that an inadequately transparent process could create opportunities for doubt, disputes or allegations concerning the authenticity and reliability of the eventual result.

“In a matter as sensitive as Mohbad’s DNA, the result must not merely be announced; it must be demonstrably reliable. The process must be independently verifiable, from sample collection to the final laboratory report. A credible DNA examination requires more than assurances from the institutions involved.”

The family said it would insist on answers to all outstanding questions and reject any process that denies the parties a fair opportunity to verify the eventual findings independently.

It argued that it had every right to put protective measures in place to guard against possible contamination, sample substitution, mishandling or other forms of interference.

It added that seeking such safeguards did not imply wrongdoing by any person or institution.

DNA examination

The family reiterated its willingness to use scientific testing to settle the paternity dispute but said transparency and accountability must guide every stage.

It further explained that its concerns extended to unresolved issues from the earlier post-mortem examination.

In support of its position, the family pointed to previous inquiries involving Dr Richard Somiari, Director of the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre.

It said the earlier autopsy failed to establish conclusive findings and alleged that subsequent checks showed that the foreign laboratory had no record of specimens submitted or registered in Mohbad’s name.

“The family’s apprehension is also informed by concerns arising from the earlier post-mortem examination conducted in connection with the death of Ilerioluwa Aloba. The family has raised questions regarding the role of one Dr Richard Somiari, whom it identifies as the Director of the Lagos State DNA and Forensic Centre and as a pathologist involved in the collection of samples during the Coroner’s Inquest. The family is concerned that the earlier autopsy result was reported to be inconclusive.

“Furthermore, the family maintains that, following enquiries, it received information indicating that the laboratory to which the samples were purportedly sent had not received the samples or any specimen registered in the name of Ilerioluwa Promise Aloba.

These assertions represent the family’s account of matters that require appropriate clarification and verification. They are not presented in this release as findings of a court or as independently established proof of wrongdoing by any named person or institution.”

The Aloba family called on the relevant authorities to address its concerns and meet its demands before conducting the examination.

The family said a transparent, well-documented procedure would safeguard the credibility of the DNA test, maintain public trust, and help resolve the paternity dispute fairly.

Backstory

This newspaper earlier reported that the court had postponed the paternity proceedings until 16 November and appointed a new officer to resolve the family’s concerns over the choice of DNA testing facility.

The adjournment followed the Ikorodu Magistrates’ Court’s approval of three DNA tests in February after singer Mohbad’s father, Joseph Aloba, renewed his demand for a court-supervised test to establish his grandson’s paternity.

The court selected two testing centres in the UK and another in the US.

World.title: OPay lists on NYSE, raises $304m in IPO at $4 billion valuation
World.content:
OPay, a Nigeria-focused digital financial services company, has listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), raising $304 million in its initial public offering (IPO) and securing a market capitalisation of more than $4 billion.

The company began trading on Friday, pricing its offering at $19 per American Depositary Share (ADS). It sold 16 million ADSs, with each representing 10 ordinary shares.

According to the company, the United States Securities and Exchange Commission declared its registration statement effective on 29 October, and the offering was expected to close on 2 November.

Lars Boilesen, OPay’s co-chief executive officer, said the listing marked a significant milestone for the company and Nigeria’s financial technology sector.

“Today, OPay serves over 50 million monthly active users across Nigeria, Egypt, Pakistan, and Indonesia. Since launching in Nigeria eight years ago, we have pioneered seamless digital payments to become the country’s leading digital financial platform,” he said.

Mr Boilesen said the company had recorded a 9.9 per cent market share across Africa and the Middle East based on monthly average users in the first half of 2026.

He said OPay saw further growth opportunities in Nigeria, where an estimated 40 million adults remained outside the formal financial system.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Our journey is just beginning. In Nigeria, an estimated 40 million adults remain outside the formal financial system,” he said.

He added that the company intended to apply its experience in Nigeria to other emerging markets, where young populations and increasing mobile internet access were expanding demand for digital financial services.

Stephen Wen, another co-chief executive officer of OPay, said the company was positioned to expand across emerging markets, citing growing smartphone penetration and demand for accessible financial services.

“In Nigeria, more than 60 per cent of the population are underserved by traditional banks and rely on cash. As we grow, we will stay focused on solving our customers’ pain points to make financial services accessible and convenient,” he said.

James Perry, OPay’s chief financial officer, said the company had reached a $1 billion revenue run rate in the second quarter of 2026.

He said OPay recorded 137 per cent year-on-year growth and a 19 per cent net margin in the first six months of the year.

ALSO READ: How OPay is taking financial inclusion closer to more Nigerians

“OPay enters the public markets from a position of financial strength, reaching a $1 billion revenue run rate in Q2 2026. For the first six months of 2026, we grew 137% year-on-year and reached 19% net margin,” Mr Perry said.

He said the company planned to use the IPO proceeds to invest in technology and support growth in Nigeria and other African markets.

OPay has expanded beyond payments into savings, credit and merchant services, with plans to develop a broader financial and lifestyle platform.

Launched in Nigeria in 2018, OPay operates an integrated digital financial platform serving users in Nigeria, Egypt, Pakistan and Indonesia.

World.title: Friday Sermon: Nigeria is bigger and greater than any politician!, By Murtadha Gusau
World.content:
In the name of Allah, Most Merciful, the Bestower of Mercy.

All praise belongs to Allah, the Owner of absolute Dominion. He gives power to whom He wills, and He strips power from whom He wills. He exalts whom He wills, and He abases whom He wills. In His Hand is all good.

Dear servants of Allah! Please, look at the soil beneath your feet. This rich, resilient Nigerian earth has outlived empires, colonial masters, military regimes, and democratic administrations.

Respected brothers and sisters! The enduring reality is that Nigeria—as a land, a collective soul, and a divine trust and amanah—is immeasurably bigger, greater, and more permanent than any politician, leader, or transient power broker. While leaders come and go like shifting shadows, the land and its people remain accountable to a higher cosmic order.

Sincerely speaking, politicians are merely brief tenants on a land owned entirely by the Creator, Allah. They occupy offices for a few short years, but the consequences of their stewardship — and the collective destiny of over 200 million souls — endure long after they are gone.

Allah Almighty warns us in the Noble Qur’an about the intoxicating nature of worldly power and wealth, He says:

“Know that the life of this world is but amusement and diversion and adornment and boasting to one another and competition in increase of wealth and children…” [Qur’an, 57:20]

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

When a politician walks the corridors of power, surrounded by sirens, wealth, and praise, psychology tells us they often fall into the trap of the “hubris syndrome.” They begin to believe that the nation cannot survive without them. But the religion of Islam shatters this illusion through ascetic teachings.

Lets ask ourselves, where is Pharaoh today? Where is Qarun? Where are the powerful monarchs of yesterday? They entered the earth with nothing but a shroud, leaving behind a legacy that is either cursed or blessed. Nigeria will not fall because a politician fails; Nigeria belongs to Allah, and its people are its true heartbeat.

Dear Muslim believers! We must shift our mindset from political dependency to spiritual agency. We have elevated flawed, mortal men to the status of national architects, forgetting that true change begins within our own psychological and spiritual architecture.

We complain about corruption, yet we participate in micro-corruption in our marketplaces, in our schools, and in our offices. A nation is simply a mirror of its collective souls. If we want a greater Nigeria, we must realise that our duty to this land is a religious obligation.

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) said:

“Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.” [Sahih Al-Bukhari]

Fellow brothers and sisters! Nigeria’s rivers, forests, mineral wealth, and brilliant minds are blessings we will be questioned about on the Day of Judgment. Some politicians use ethnic and religious fault lines to divide us for temporary electoral gains. Wallahi, to succumb to this is a sign of spiritual disease. Our strength does not come from Aso Rock Villa; it comes from the sweat of the market woman in Kano, the brilliance of the tech youth in Lagos, the endurance of the farmer in Benue, Zamfara, Kogi etc, and the prayers of the righteous people across this land.

Imagine a billionaire politician who held the fate of millions in his hands. He signed budgets, decided who ate and who starved, and walked with an army of guards. Now, fast forward a few decades. He lies in a quiet, dark grave in a local cemetery. The sirens are gone. The wealth is distributed. The political parties have moved on to new faces.

Above his grave, the ordinary citizens of Nigeria—the ones he ignored—continue to walk, to build, to live, and to survive.

Here who was bigger? The man who thought he owned the country, or the country that swallowed him back into its soil?

Nigeria is an idea etched into the divine decree. It is a tapestry of over 250 ethnicities woven together by Allah’s wisdom. Allah Almighty says:

“O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another…” [Qur’an, 49:13]

Fellow servants of Allah! To move from emotional reflection to real-world activation, every Nigerian citizen must adopt three spiritual-psychological shifts as follows:

1. De-deify the Politician

Stop treating elected officials as masters. In Islam, the leader is the servant of the people, The Khadimul-Ummah. Hold them accountable, but never tie your hope, your livelihood, or your patriotism to their names.

2. Kill the Ghost of Cynicism

Despair is a sin. The moment you say “Nigeria can never change,” you have doubted Allah’s power to transform hearts. Keep building, keep educating, and keep doing good in your immediate circle.

3. Vote and Act with Conscience

On the day of elections or civic duties, sell not your soul for a bag of rice, sphagetti or petty cash. Wallahi, that momentary transaction paralyses the future of your children. Act as a guardian of the amanah.

O Nigerians! Lift your head high. Know that, governments will rise and fall. Policies will change. Budgets will be spent. But your faith, your resilience, your unity, and your devotion to the Almighty Allah are unshakeable. Do not let transient men ruin a permanent blessing. Build your homes on righteousness, raise your children with integrity, and remember that this giant of Africa is held up by the hands of the Almighty Allah, not the whims of politicians.

Dear brothers and sisters! Fear Allah, and know that power belongs solely to Al-Malik, The True Sovereign.

And know that, our great country Nigeria is an enduring trust and amanah from Allah, a vast land of millions of souls, and an estate far greater than the fleeting shadow of any single politician.

We look at our nation today and see a people consumed by the names of men. We anchor our hopes, our anger, and our entire futures to individual politicians—mortals who breathe the same air we breathe, who sleep, who err, and who will inevitably return to the dust.

Respected brothers and sisters! Politicians are but brief actors on a stage. They are transient. They occupy an office for four years, eight years, or a lifetime, and then they disappear into the pages of history. But Nigeria—with its over 200 million souls, its innocent children, its hardworking mothers, its resilient youth, and its spiritual heritage—is a sacred trust.

Therefore, do not trade your brotherhood, your peace, or your eternal soul for the temporary ambitions of a mortal leader. When politicians stoke the fires of division, remember that they are small, but the collective destiny of this Ummah and this nation under Allah is immense. Nigeria is bigger than any politician’s ambition.

My dear brothers and sisters! Look at the reality of this world through the lens of Zuhd and asceticism. The Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) said:

“What have I to do with this world? The relation between me and this world is like a traveler who sits under the shade of a tree and then walks away and leaves it.” [Tirmidhi]

If this entire world is just a temporary shade, what then is the seat of a governor, a senator, a president, a house of representative member, a state assembly member, a local government chairman or a councillor? It is a shadow within a shadow.

Please, why do we allow our hearts to be broken by their failures? Why do we allow our communities to be fractured by their campaigns? Why do we bleed for men who do not know our names?

Fellow Nigerians! Remember, a politician is just one person. But Nigeria is a tapestry of millions of prayers rising to the heavens every single night. Please, do not elevate a servant to the status of a master. Your loyalty belongs to Allah, and your duty of care belongs to your neighbours, your community, and your country.

There is a profound lesson from our righteous predecessors, as-Salafus Salih. A powerful leader once rode through his kingdom in grand pomp, surrounded by bodyguards, demanding total subservience. He passed by a wise, ascetic Islamic scholar sitting in the dirt. The leader demanded:

“Do you know who I am?”

The Islamic scholar calmly replied:

“Yes. I know your beginning and your end. Your beginning was a dropped drop of fluid, and your end will be a decaying corpse in the earth. And between the two, you are merely carrying waste.”

The leader wept.

Let this be our reminder when we look at the political landscape of Nigeria. No matter how loud a politician’s convoy, no matter how vast their wealth, they will face the Grave alone. The land they rule over will outlive them. The people they govern will survive them. The nation is the canvas; the politician is merely a passing drop of ink.

Awaken, Nigeria citizens and Muslim believers! Stop waiting for a political messiah to save Nigeria. The salvation of our nation lies in the reformation of our own hearts, our honesty in our marketplaces, our kindness to our neighbours, and our collective turning back to Allah Almighty.

Wallahi, a politician cannot fix a home where character has decayed. A politician cannot bring peace to a community that has abandoned justice.

Nigeria will stand long after the current political elite are forgotten names in a textbook. Protect the nation, serve the people, and fear none but Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala!

Dear servants of Allah! When the Prophet Muhammad (Peace be upon him) was forced to leave his birthplace, Makkah, he stood at the edge of the city, looked back with tears in his eyes, and declared:

“How sweet you are as a land, and how dear you are to me! If my people had not driven me out from you, I would not have dwelt anywhere else.” [Tirmidhi]

This is not mere sentimentality; it is a divine template. The spiritual heart does not exist in a vacuum. It is rooted in the soil that sustains it. To love Nigeria, to prioritise its survival, and to labour for its resurrection is a direct expression of the values taught by Islam. You cannot claim to love the Creator if you actively despise or destroy the cradle of His creation in which He placed you.

Our collective suffering—the economic hardship, the insecurity, the fracturing of social trust—is a material reflection of a deeper spiritual drought. The Noble Qur’an provides an unyielding psychological law. Allah Almighty says:

“Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a population until they change what is in themselves.” [Qur’an, 13:11]

We have fallen into the trap of looking outward for saviours while harbouring the very diseases that collapse nations from within: greed, selfishness, mutual distrust, apathy, and the pursuit of individual survival at the expense of the collective.

A nation is nothing more than the sum of its individual souls. If we are corrupt in our small daily transactions, our leadership will inevitably reflect that collective deficit. The reform of Nigeria does not begin at the Eagle Square in Abuja; it begins in the quiet chambers of your own conscience.

Do not forget! Nigeria is a trust and amanah from Allah. Every resource, every citizen, and every public space is an amanah. Betraying the nation through bribery and corruption, through cutting corners, through nepotism or tribalism is a direct betrayal of this divine trust.

Stop asking what Nigeria can do for you when the soil is parched. Ask what you are pouring into the ground. And please, before you point fingers at the leadership, audit your own integrity in your workplace, in your home, and in your community.

Also despair is a spiritual failure. To claim Nigeria is beyond redemption is to limit the mercy and power of Allah Almighty. We must actively cultivate hope as a form of resistance against chaos.

There is a profound lesson in the classical histories of the righteous predecessors, The Salafus-Salih. A companion once found an old sage painstakingly repairing a community wall in a city plagued by civil strife, insecurity, corruption, and failing governance.

The companion asked:

“Ya Sheikh, why do you exhaust your remaining days fixing a wall for a city whose foundations are rotting and whose people have abandoned virtue?”

The sage did not stop his work. He wiped the sweat from his brow and replied:

“When the angels look down upon this city, let them find at least one soul building while everyone else is tearing down. I do not fix this wall because the city deserves it; I fix it because the Lord of this city demands righteousness from me, regardless of what the crowds choose to do.”

Dear brothers and sisters! Nigeria will not be saved by systemic overhauls alone. It will be saved when its citizens experience a psychological and spiritual awakening. It requires an ascetic detachment from immediate, selfish gains in exchange for the lasting legacy of a stable society.

Dear brothers and sisters! Let this be your reminder: You were placed in Nigeria by divine decree, not by accident. You will be questioned about what you did with the piece of earth allotted to you. Stand up, reform your heart, build your community, and put the survival of your homeland first.

Fellow Nigerians! Know that, the destiny of a nation is carved in the secret whispers of its citizens’ prayers. When hands are raised in sincere supplication for a homeland, a profound spiritual activation takes place—transforming despair into hope, friction into unity, and stagnation into progress.

Dear servants of Allah, O citizens of a land rich in soil, vibrant in spirit, and heavy with human potential!

Look around you. A nation is not merely a collection of borders, infrastructure, or political entities. A nation is a living soul, woven together by the collective hearts of its people. Nigeria—our home—stands at a monumental crossroads. We face trials that test our patience, economic hardships that strain our resolve, and fractures that threaten our unity. Yet, as Muslim believers, we do not despair. Despair is the language of the forgotten, and we belong to Al-Hayy, The Ever-Living and Al-Qayyum, The Sustainer of All Existences.

Allah Almighty reminds us in the Noble Qur’an. He says:

“And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'” [Qur’an, 40:60]

Remember, Du’a is not a last resort for the helpless; it is the ultimate weapon of the powerful. It is a spiritual catalyst capable of altering the Divine decree, shifting geopolitical realities, and softening the hardest of hearts.

Let us reflect on the profound wisdom of the great ascetic Islamic scholar, Imam Fudail Ibn Iyad (may Allah have mercy on him), who famously said:

“If I had a single supplication that was guaranteed to be answered, I would make it for none other than the leader, or the Sultan.” When asked why, he replied: “If I make the Du’a for myself, the benefit stops with me. But if I make it for the leader, and he is reformed, then through his righteousness, entire nations, communities, and citizens will find peace, justice, and prosperity.”

This is a heart-softening psychological shift. It is easy to criticise, to speak words of anger, and to curse those who govern. But anger breeds chaos; Du’a breeds rectification. Our leaders are human beings tested with immense burdens. When we pray for their guidance, their fear of Allah, and their wisdom, we are actively investing in our own security, our economy, and the future of our children.

We are a nation of diversity—a beautiful mosaic of tribes, tongues, and cultures. But diversity without a unifying spirit becomes a weapon of division. Allah Almighty commands us:

“And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided.” [Qur’an, 3:103]

Progress cannot thrive in a house divided against itself. Our development relies on mutual empathy. We must make Du’a that Allah cleanses our hearts of tribalism, nepotism, and religious animosity, replacing them with collective patriotism and love for our neighbours.

Peace and economic sustenance are intertwined twins. Without peace, businesses cannot grow, farmers cannot harvest, and children cannot learn. We must beg Allah for security across every state, from the creeks to the savannahs. We must invoke His name, Ar-Razzaq, The Provider, to pour down His blessings upon Nigeria, turning our natural resources from tools of exploitation into streams of shared prosperity.

Raise your hands, clear your minds, and let your hearts cry out to the Lord of the Worlds with absolute certainty.

Ya Allah, Lord of the Heavens and the Earth! We turn to You on this day, acknowledging our shortcomings, but placing our absolute hope in Your infinite mercy. We ask You to grant complete, lasting, and beautiful peace to our nation, Nigeria.

Ya Allah, Safe-Keeper of the Vulnerable! Heal our lands from the wounds of insecurity, violence, banditry, and terrorism. Let every corner of Nigeria, from the North to the South, from the East to the West, become a sanctuary of safety, where the young can dream and the old can rest in tranquility.

Ya Allah, Guide of the Confused! We lay the affairs of our leaders before You. Ya Allah, touch the hearts of our President, our Governors, our Lawmakers, and our Traditional Rulers. Grant them profound wisdom, empathy, and an unwavering fear of You. Let them see leadership not as a privilege of luxury, but as a heavy trust and amanah for which they will be questioned on the Day of Judgment. Guide them to policies that alleviate poverty, foster justice, and drive sustainable development.

Ya Allah, Creator of Diversity! Unite our hearts as citizens. Eradicate the diseases of tribalism, regionalism, and hatred from our souls. Bind the citizens of Nigeria together with the cords of mutual respect, love, and common purpose. Let our diversity be our greatest strength, not our downfall.

Ya Allah, Ar-Razzaq, The All-Providing! Open the gates of sustenance for the millions of struggling households across Nigeria. Bless our farmers, our entrepreneurs, our workers, and our youths. Let our economy flourish through honest means. Deliver us from the hardships of inflation and scarcity, and grant us barakah and blessing in our resources.

Ya Allah! Uplift the spirit of the Nigerian youth. Grant them patience, focus, creativity, and avenues to excel so that they may build a brighter tomorrow.

Ya Allah! Do not punish us for the sins of the corrupt among us, but forgive us, rectify our state, and change our condition from hardship to ease.

Respected brothers and sisters! Wallahi, change never begins at the presidential villa; it begins in the mirror.

If we want an honest country, we must be honest in our market transactions. If we want a peaceful country, we must stop spreading malice on our social media platforms. Use this Du’a not just as words spoken, but as a blueprint for personal reformation.

Finally, I pray, may Allah Almighty heal the land of Nigeria, purify the hearts of all its leaders, bless all its citizens with prosperity, and make our love for righteousness greater than our fear of tyranny. Amin Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum!

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May the peace, blessings and salutations of Allah be upon our noble Messenger, Muhammad, and upon his family, his Companions and his true followers.

Murtadha Muhammad Gusau is the Chief Imam of Nagazi-Uvete Jumu’ah and the late Alhaji Abdur-Rahman Okene’s Mosques, Okene, Kogi State, Nigeria. He can be reached via: [email protected] or +2348038289761 or +2348024192217.
