World.title: Government recommits to promoting sustainable agriculture
World.content:
Seed Control and Certification Institute (SCCI) Senior Seed Officer, Zombe Sikazwe, says Government reaffirmed its commitment to promoting sustainable agriculture, crop diversification and the empowerment of women farmers as part of efforts to strengthen Zambia’s food security and agricultural resilience.

Speaking during the Zambia Traditional Seed and Food Festival, Mrs Sikazwe said the government is shifting its agricultural agenda from focusing mainly on production to promoting sustainable, resilient and inclusive agricultural practices.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government had identified agroecology, agricultural diversification and women empowerment as key priorities in transforming the agricultural sector.

She said the Eighth National Development Plan and the National Agriculture Policy prioritised agroecology as a pathway towards sustainable agriculture.

Mrs Sikazwe said the Ministry of Agriculture is promoting farming practices that restore soil health, conserve water, encourage the use of indigenous seed varieties and reduce dependence on expensive external inputs.

She said SCCI will continue ensuring that farmers have access to certified, diverse and climate-resilient seeds, including traditional and improved varieties suitable for agro ecological farming systems.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government is moving away from overdependence on maize production by promoting crops such as soybeans, sunflower, groundnuts, cowpeas, sorghum, cassava and high-value horticultural crops.

She said the diversification agenda also included integrating livestock and aquaculture into farming systems to create additional income opportunities, employment and resilience against climate-related shocks.

Mrs Sikazwe said the Comprehensive Agriculture Transformation Support Programme (CASP) has placed crop diversification at the centre of its implementation strategy.

She further said the government recognised women as key players in the agricultural sector, noting that they contributed more than 60 percent of farm labour and played a central role in household food security.

Mrs Sikazwe said the government is prioritising support for women-headed households through the Farmer Input Support Programme (FISP), improved access to finance and land, women-focused agricultural extension services and training.

She said deliberate efforts are also being made to ensure women are included in seed systems and agricultural value chains.

Mrs Sikazwe added that sustainable agriculture could only be achieved through the combined efforts of government, farmers, the private sector, non-governmental organisations and cooperating partners.

Meanwhile, Gabriel Mapulanga who was representing a Consortium of Civil Society Organizations has called for increased investment in traditional seed systems, saying indigenous seeds are critical to strengthening Zambia’s food security, improving nutrition and building resilience to climate change.

Father Mapulanga said traditional seeds such as sorghum, millet and cowpeas had the potential to help communities withstand drought and other climate-related challenges.

He said the loss of indigenous seed varieties is gradually threatening Zambia’s agricultural heritage, as some traditional crops are becoming less common in farming communities.

Father Mapulanga noted that the disappearance of traditional seeds also meant losing indigenous knowledge on how to grow, preserve, store and prepare traditional foods.

He said women play a critical role in preserving indigenous seeds and traditional food knowledge, describing them as key custodians of the country’s food systems.

Father Mapulanga said traditional foods such as sorghum, millet, cowpeas, bondwe and wild fruits such as masuku are important sources of nutrition but are increasingly being marginalised due to changing food consumption patterns.

He observed that the growing consumption of highly processed foods has contributed to reduced dietary diversity and increased nutrition-related health challenges.

Father Mapulanga said traditional seeds should not be viewed as outdated, but rather as practical solutions to climate change and food security challenges because of their ability to withstand harsh weather conditions and their nutritional value.

He, however, said farmers continued to face challenges such as the high cost of irrigation equipment, limited access to affordable processing technologies, inadequate agricultural extension services and restricted access to seed markets.

He called for increased investment in farmer-managed seed enterprises, affordable agricultural technologies for rural women and policies that protect farmers’ rights to save, exchange and sell traditional seeds.

Father Mapulanga said farmers should be given the freedom to preserve and use their own seeds, adding that seed sovereignty is important to achieving national food sovereignty.

He urged policymakers to integrate gender-inclusive agroecological approaches into national agricultural strategies and support farmer-led seed systems alongside conventional agricultural methods.

He has also called on the private sector, academic and research institutions to work with women-led cooperatives in developing markets and affordable processing technologies that would help retain economic value within local communities.

Women farmers have called for greater recognition and support for traditional seed systems, saying indigenous crops are essential to strengthening food security, preserving agricultural knowledge and building resilience to climate change.

The women farmers’ representative Esther Mumba said women are not merely beneficiaries of agricultural development but key leaders, innovators and custodians of traditional seed and food knowledge.

Mrs Mumba said women play a critical role in selecting, preserving and exchanging seeds, as well as passing indigenous farming knowledge from one generation to another.

She said women farmers remained central to household food security through the production of vegetables, legumes, small grains and other traditional crops.

She however, noted that farming had become increasingly challenging due to unpredictable rainfall patterns, declining soil fertility, rising input costs, increased pest attacks and limited access to reliable markets.

Mrs Mumba said the severe drought experienced during the 2023/2024 agricultural season had exposed the vulnerability of the country’s food system when it depended heavily on a limited number of crops.

She also highlighted indigenous vegetables such as bondwe, chiwawa, kalembula and katapa, saying they contributed to dietary diversity and represented an important part of Zambia’s food heritage.

Mrs Mumba said traditional seeds carried valuable knowledge and biodiversity, adding that some indigenous crop varieties had characteristics that made them suitable for different local growing conditions, including dry environments.

Mrs Mumba said increased support for farmer-managed seed systems, community seed banks, seed conservation and the exchange of traditional seeds among farming communities and young people.

She further urged stakeholders to recognise and protect farmers’ rights while ensuring that women’s knowledge and experiences are represented in agricultural policies and programmes.

Mrs Mumba said women farmers are also adopting agro ecological practices such as compost making, crop rotation, intercropping, mulching, tree planting and water harvesting to improve soil fertility and protect the environment.

She said combining traditional farming knowledge with modern technologies and scientific research will help farmers improve productivity, conserve biodiversity and reduce dependence on expensive external inputs.

Mrs Mumba has since called for stronger support for traditional seeds and farmer-managed seed systems through policies and programmes that recognise community seed banks, indigenous seed varieties and farmers’ knowledge.

She has also urged the government to increase investment in agro ecology and climate-resilient agriculture through practical extension services, water harvesting technologies, small-scale irrigation, soil restoration initiatives and affordable farming equipment.

Mrs Mumba further called for improved access to land, finance, training, technology and decision-making opportunities for women farmers, including young women entering the agricultural sector.

World.title: ZAQA commends public for exhibiting positive compliance levels
World.content:
The Zambia Qualifications Authority (ZAQA) has commended members of the public and other stakeholders for the high levels of compliance with their qualifications verification process.

In an interview with ZANIS TV, ZAQA Corporate Communications Specialist, Inutu Mwanza, says the authority’s mandate is being adopted, as they continue to receive applications from people seeking to pursue higher education and employment opportunities.

“Many people are complying, as we all know, it’s mandatory for you to verify your qualifications,” she said.

Mrs Mwanza stated that the authority is collaborating with higher learning institutions to enforce a system integration that will enable the availing of learner records to the authority to avoid delays in verification.

“Legally we are the custodian of all qualifications in the country,” she said.

Mrs Mwanza noted that the system has significantly improved learner record availability by digitizing the verification process.

She further encouraged all those who have not yet verified their qualifications with the authority to do so, stating that once verified, their certificates will have no expiry.

World.title: ECZ announces resignation of three candidates for Mandevu Parliamentary by-election
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ), has announced the resignation of three candidates from the Mandevu Parliamentary by-election.

According to a public notice issued by ECZ today, 30th October 2026, the candidates who have resigned are Mr Ntazana Musukuma Mutungwa of the Leadership Movement (LM), Mr Daniel Chisenga of the Forum for Democracy and Development (FDD), and Mr Daniel Daka, an independent candidate.

The Commission disclosed that the three candidates resigned through letters dated 28th October 2026, which were served on the Commission on 29th October 2026.

Following the resignations, Mr Adrian Banda of the United Party for National Development (UPND) remains the only validly nominated candidate in the race.

However, in accordance with Regulations 20(3) and 52(2) of the Electoral Process (General) Regulations, 2016, Mr Banda will be declared duly elected as Member of Parliament for Mandevu Constituency without the need for an election, effective 5th November 2026.

World.title: Malawi: Police Confirm Egyptian Deputy Ambassador Beaten in Lilongwe Attack
World.content:
A senior Egyptian diplomat has been hospitalised after being attacked and beaten in Lilongwe, sparking a police investigation into the shocking assault.

National Police spokesperson Gladys Chiwaula confirmed that Egypt's Deputy Ambassador to Malawi was admitted to a hospital in the capital after the attack.

"Police are following up on the matter and will give more details later," she said.

Chiwaula gave few details.

She did not say where the attack happened, what led to it, or how serious the diplomat's injuries are. Police have also withheld the deputy ambassador's name.

Officers say they are investigating, but the incident is likely to raise alarm over the safety of foreign envoys in the country.

World.title: Africa: From Commonwealth Connections to Economic Opportunity - Expanding Africa-Caribbean Trade Linkages
World.content:
guest column

When Commonwealth leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda this November, they will confront rising trade tensions, geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruption alongside longstanding challenges, such as high debt, limited affordable finance, climate exposure and poor connectivity.

Across Africa, the Pacific and the Caribbean, these pressures make diversifying markets, attracting productive investment and building resilience through trade even more urgent. They also increase the importance of regional and cross-regional value chains that can withstand disruptions to established trade relationships.

One opportunity lies in plain sight: stronger Africa-Caribbean economic connections. Shared history, culture and diaspora relationships provide a foundation, as do common ambitions to diversify exports, add value locally and create opportunities for small businesses, including those led by women and young entrepreneurs.

The institutional landscape is also changing. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is building a framework for trade including goods, services, investment and digital commerce, while the Caribbean is deepening the CARICOM Single Market and Economy.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Connecting these integration efforts across the Atlantic could help firms aggregate supply and demand, build scale, and develop regional value chains. and access larger markets. A bigger, more integrated market can improve the commercial case for investment and the economics of cross-regional trade.

Forthcoming analysis by the International Trade Centre (ITC), undertaken with the support of Afreximbank, points to considerable unrealised trade potential between Africa and the Caribbean. But the numbers tell only part of the story.

In a survey of 1,175 businesses and business support organisations only 10% of African companies and 12% of Caribbean companies reported trading with the other region. Yet among those that did, 79% of African firms and 82% of Caribbean firms described their experience positively or very positively. The challenge is less about potential than removing barriers to scale.

Businesses struggle to access reliable market information, trusted partners and appropriate finance, as well as to navigate standards and move goods efficiently.

These constraints are not new. Low trade volumes weaken direct transport links; poor connectivity raises costs; limited commercial relationships restrict information; and smaller transactions are harder to finance.

The priority is to tackle these challenges in a comprehensive way.

Physical distance remains particularly costly. ITC estimates freight costs on African exports to the Caribbean at almost 20% of shipment value, compared with just over 8% for African exports globally. Caribbean exports to Africa face costs approaching 22%. Limited routes and fragmented networks continue to undermine viable trade. Scheduled direct air services between Lagos and Barbados, launched in 2026, illustrate how improved connections can support business travel, tourism and wider services.

Access to finance depends not only on the availability of capital, but on whether viable opportunities can be connected to appropriate financing. Businesses need guidance on available funding and lender requirements, and financial institutions need appropriate instruments and ways to manage risk. Trade finance, working-capital facilities, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms can all bridge these gaps.

Payments also matter, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Slow, costly or uncertain transfers can derail transactions. More efficient cross-border payment systems would reduce both transaction costs and risks. Africa's Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) offers useful lessons for simplifying payments as financial links with the Caribbean deepen.

Beyond trade volumes, value creation extends beyond goods. Services, digital solutions and the creative industries can generate more value within both regions. Africa and the Caribbean have globally recognised cultural assets and extensive diasporas, yet much of the creative value is captured elsewhere. Creators and firms need finance, workable payments, intellectual property expertise, distribution channels and direct access to buyers and investors. Supporting creative businesses, rather than only promoting cultural exchange, would generate more revenue and help jobs remain in local economies.

Governments and institutions can create the enabling environment, but businesses will ultimately determine whether a new chapter in Africa–Caribbean economic relations succeed, especially for SMEs.

Commonwealth trade and investment platforms can connect policymakers, investors, entrepreneurs and business leaders. They offer a way to identify obstacles that no single firm or government can resolve alone. Success, however, means introductions becoming contracts, investment reaching viable enterprises and businesses entering new markets.

The Commonwealth brings an existing economic advantage to this endeavour. The opportunity is to make that advantage work more deliberately for Africa–Caribbean commerce, where physical distance, limited market information and still-thin commercial networks continue to constrain trade.

Through its Working Group on Trade and Investment, member countries are developing a workplan to expand intra-Commonwealth commerce. Cooperation on compatible regulations, mutual recognition of standards and qualifications, and simpler border procedures can help realise these gains.

Close 

ITC's work on investment promotion and digital trade to women's economic empowerment, small-state resilience and emerging Africa–Caribbean business linkages can advance this agenda. Afreximbank's Global Africa vision brings the finance, investment and commercial infrastructure required to turn diaspora ties into sustainable economic relationships.

These capabilities are complementary. Trade policy can open markets; finance helps businesses act; and enterprises sustain commercial relationships.

The practical test is clear: identify viable opportunities, mobilise investment, resolve logistics, finance and payment barriers, connect SMEs to customers and investors, use digital trade to overcome distance and retain more value within regions. Progress should then be measured in transactions, market access and sustainable business relationships.

As leaders gather in Antigua and Barbuda, they can demonstrate how a connected Commonwealth can convert partnerships into investment, enterprise and shared prosperity.

World.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Kill Police Inspector, 11 Others in Kebbi
World.content:
Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities.

The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse.

A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts.



He said, "the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities," he said.

Though the police said five people were killed in an attack on October 26, while seven others died in attacks on October 28 in the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi area of the state, bringing the total to 12, including a police inspector, locals who spoke under condition of anonymity said over 23 people actually lost their lives in the Lakurawa/Mamudawa attacks on the communities of Koko Besse and Shanga areas of Kebbi.

A source said, "They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted."

He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026.

A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, "I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities. Some of them who fled for safety during the attack are just returning on the assurance by the security agents and government that measures are being put in place to ensure our safety."

He called on the government to come to their aid as some of the residents have nowhere to stay.

Another resident, Aliyu Tailor Besse, said the attack was carried out by the Lakurawa terrorists group.

"What happened was that after attacking communities in Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government, they started moving along the River Niger up to Koko Besse area.They were attacking communities along the River Niger as they moved towards Besse community. Many people were killed in the attacks. Prior to the attacks, those who saw them moving along the River Niger banks had raised an alarm calling on residents of the communities along the area to vacate. Some left, but many others stayed behind," he said.

Daily Trust gathered that a few days before the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi attacks, suspected members of the Lakurawa group also attacked Lafagu and other communities in Boya area of Kaoje, killing the village head, Alhaji Saidu Mujeli, and six others before leaving the area through the River Niger bank to attack other communities in Besse and Shanga.

It was gathered that despite the establishment of an army battalion in Kaoje to curtail the activities of terrorists, attacks have continued.

Police confirm attacks

Speaking to our correspondent, the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, said "it's true that the attack happened but it did not happen in one day and not in one community. It started from the 22nd of this month. The casualties recorded was not in a single attack. They attacked many of the communities in the riverine area and that's why the figure of those killed rose to 12. A police inspector and 11 others were killed in the attacks."

He said members of the Lakurawa terrorists group had earlier attacked communities along the Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi axis on 22nd of October, but security operatives repelled them. He said they later carried out attacks on the communities of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi on October 26 and 28.

"Although the joint security teams repelled the attacks, seven people unfortunately lost their lives, including a police inspector," he said.

He added that earlier, members of the Yan Sakai, had invaded Samanaji Market and killed Fulani traders.

"Our police tactical teams deployed by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Besse, responded promptly to restore peace and prevent further carnage. However, three Fulani people lost their lives, while a police inspector sustained injuries in the line of duty," he said.

The state police spokesman said a tactical team of the police had been deployed to the troubled communities and normalcy is gradually returning to the area.

"The police have launched investigation into the attack and is following up on the attackers," he said.

'Attacks sign of frustration'

A security expert, who retired as a Captain in the Nigerian Army, Shehu Abubakar, told our correspondent that the attacks carried out by suspected members of the Lakurawa group in some communities of Kebbi, is a sign of frustration.

"You should understand that a battalion of the Nigerian Army was recently established at Kaoje area of Bagudo Local Government to curtail activities of the bandits and Lakurawa, operating in the area. The Lakurawa must leave the area to find a convenient place as base to carry out their attacks. They carried out their attack on the communities along the River Niger bank while migrating to another area to avenge the presence of the army base at Kaoje.

"They can no longer stay close to the area where the battalion is located. They migrated from Kaoje, through the bank of the River Niger, moving through communities of Samanaji, Dutsinmari, Zaria Kalakala, to where they started their attacks at Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi. Now that they seem to have been displaced, the security agencies operating in the state should follow them up in every move they make so that they don't get a convenient place to settle. That way, they may be frustrated to move out of the state," he said.

Military bases in Kebbi

In the last two years, six Forward Operation Bases were established in Sakaba,Zuru,Yauri, Augie and Kaoje. The Battalion in Birnin Kebbi was upgraded to an Armoured Brigade, just as there is a battalion in Zuru.There are also army units in parts of Kaoje and other areas to strengthen military operations in the troubled communities of Augie, Danko Wasagu, Mahuta, Argungu, Arewa, Bagudo and Dandi, but the spate of killings occasioned by bandits and Lakurawa attacks remain a growing concern among residents.

Close 

Kebbi's killing fields

On Wednesday of last week, a large number of bandits invaded Dirin -Daji in Sakara Local Government Area of the state. It took the combined efforts of the security agencies in the area to disperse the attackers.

A week before the Kaoje district attack, three people were killed at Kasabo, a community in Saminaka, Yauri Local Government Area of the state. The community was attacked by the bandits in the early hours of the day when people were preparing to go about their daily activities. A resident, Aminu Usman, said their attackers came in large number to invade the community and that they killed three people while many others escaped through the bush.

A few days before the attack at Kasabo, suspected members of the Lakurawa terrorists group attacked the site of the construction company handling the Badagry-Ilela Supper Highway project at Gubba in Maiyama Local Government Area of the state, killing two soldiers and a Chinese national. The attackers were said to have crossed into Kebbi from Kebbe area of Sokoto, to carry out the attack, it was gathered.

Efforts to get comments from the state government proved abortive, but a top government official who does not want his name in print told our corespondent that the state government was working closely with security agencies to identify and apprehend those responsible for the attacks.

He said, "Governor Nasir Idris has been up and doing on issues of security on the state. No fewer than 109 armoured vehicles and other logistics have been procured for security agencies to fight insecurity in the state."

World.title: Africa: AFCON Every Two Years Again As CAF Reverses Decision
World.content:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle.

The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation's Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026.

The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition.

CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation's 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent.

"The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa," he said.

Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition.

He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future.

Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament.

The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year.

Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries' ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027.

He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa's cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together.

"The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa's rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa's 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world," he said.

"The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF's 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa," he added.

World.title: Maggie Sajak looks like a million bucks for Halloween, Billy Napier makes horrible history & Tim Duncan votes!
World.content:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Happy Halloween Eve to all who celebrate! Big day. Big Friday. Big weekend in front of us.

Like I said earlier this week ... this is our last big push until the holiday season suffocates us starting Sunday morning. Everything will flip in the blink of an eye.

You'll go to bed with the Halloween theme song in your heads, and wake up to jingle bells. Whether you like it or not, it's coming. There is no stopping it.

I can already see Mariah Carey's stupid "All I Want for Christmas" social media post now. It's coming. There's nothing we can do about it. We're cornered.

That's a Sunday problem, though. For now, we respect the fall. We respect Halloween.

Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where poor Billy Napier joined Mike Norvell in making some embarrassing history last night at James Madison.

Dukes fans aren't thrilled today!

CASUAL BASKETBALL FANS GOBSMACKED AT HORRIBLE ANGEL REESE HIGHLIGHTS FROM AN ACTUAL WNBA FINALS GAME

What else? I've got Maggie Sajak looking like a million bucks for Halloween, Angel Reese giving us one more highlight reel before this WNBA season mercifully ends, and can we quit complaining about "injury protection" in sports gambling?

I'm admittedly at fault, too, but enough is enough already. You know what? Society went DECADES gambling on sports with no such thing as "injury protection," and it worked pretty well. And now every sports book is supposed to issue refunds if a player gets hurt?

Why?

Grab you your favorite Michael Myers mask (I'm partial to Rob Zombie's "Halloween" mask), and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

Billy Napier's JMU tenure is going well!

I don't know how many "Halloween" buffs we have in class today, but those of you who have been around here long enough know it's my favorite movie franchise of all time.

LSU’S MIKE THE TIGER STALKS REFEREE WHILE DRESSED AS MICHAEL MYERS, APPEARS TO BE STEERED AWAY BY STAFFER

I did the Mount Rushmore of Halloween movies a few weeks ago, so I won't rehash that today. BUT, I did find out this morning while doing the award-winning OutKick newsletter that the original "Halloween" mask from 1978 was ... a Captain Kirk mask?

Seriously:

The more you know ...

Anyway, I will be watching the original "Halloween" (1978) tomorrow night, as per usual. I save that one for Halloween night, like any sane person would do.

It's the only way to close out October. Sad. Winter is coming.

OK, let's get class started by checking in on someone who is very much looking forward to flipping the calendar ...

Billy Napier!

Angel Reese wasn't her best last night

Amazing stat.

James Madison joined Florida State last night as teams to lose back-to-back games as double-digit favorites. Incredible.

Do we have any Dukes fans in class today? I'd imagine so. I come from a James Madison family. My grandma went there way back when it was simply called "Madison." My dad went there. I toured the campus as a high school senior and loved it.

That town deserves way better than Billy Napier, and I'm speaking now as a Florida fan. I'm so sorry, JMU fans. We've been there before. I promise. We spent the last four years feeling exactly how you've felt the last two weeks.

What kind of play call was that on fourth down in overtime? Just awful. But, that's Billy Ball for you.

Embarrassing.

Speaking of ... let's check in with Angel Reese after yesterday's big Game 6 win!

Maggie, sports betting & election szn is almost over!

Lordy.

Look, it was a tough game for Angel Reese. No sugarcoating it. No hiding it. Just to show you how truly bad everyone else was, Reese somehow finished with a +/- of +10, which is stunning given she turned the ball over six times and made just 27% of her shots.

Feels like that shouldn't equate to positive play on the court, but what do I know?

Anyway, this will be my final non-Sophie Cunningham WNBA story for seven months. The season, mercifully, ends tomorrow night. It feels like it's dragged on FOREVER. It just won't end!

But at 8 p.m. tomorrow night — a COLLEGE FOOTBALL SATURDAY — we'll get a Game 7. Who's watching?!

Show of hands ...

Anyone?

Bueller?

Okeedokee! Moving on ...

Let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big Halloween weekend, and start it off by celebrating the end of something else: Election season.

Four more days, folks. We're almost there.

That's one of the funnier pictures I've seen in a long time. Just amazing stuff. Well done to whoever took it.

Are you guys getting inundated with calls and texts right now? Lord knows I am. Hand to God, I got a text last night from James Talarico asking for money.

James Talarico! I live in Florida. These people are NUTS. They're just unrelenting. Freaking Byron Donalds texts me 14 times a day making sure I'm gonna vote.

Byron, you got my vote, pal. I promise. You're good. I'd prefer we just stick with DeSantis, but I realize that's not possible, so you're next in line.

For the love of God, please leave me alone. I'm begging you.

Next? Let's quickly check in with Christian Watson after last night's game in which he left in an ambulance, and then returned like nothing happened:

So, there's a big debate over on Elon's app right now about injury protection, which is a fairly new thing sports books have come up with over the past few years. Basically, they'll void straight bets and parlay lines if the player you bet on gets hurt and doesn't return to the game.

It sounds great on paper, right? Again, it's bailed me out a few times.

But now everyone is in an UPROAR because Watson looked to be voided last night, only for him to miraculously return to the game.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

I think it's hogwash. About a month ago, I was complaining to my dad about a player getting injured and tanking one of my bets, and I mentioned injury protection.

"Huh?" he responded. "Why would the books refund you? You lost. Tough nuts."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

He was right. The bellyaching over injury protection is insane to me. Frankly, I don't think any book should do it. I'm glad they do, but it seems like a lose-lose for them, no?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Toughen up, buttercup! Gambling ain't for the faint of heart!

OK, that's it for today — and this week. And this month.

Happy Halloween, everyone. Farewell to October.



And, of course, hello to Maggie Sajak.

See y'all Monday.

World.title: 'Punt' on this year's quarterback draft class, take Jeremiah Smith, says college football expert Brooks Austin
World.content:
While the NFL Draft isn't until next April, that never stops general managers, scouts and even fans from opining on what their teams will do in the spring.

It's the main reason why mock drafts exist and are created nearly a year in advance, because everyone is dying to know who their favorite team is going to select with their first round pick.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Of course, because it's the most important position on the field, the quarterback draws the most amount of eyes when it comes to the first round of the draft, and the 2027 edition is no exception.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

There are several draft-eligible signal callers who are generating plenty of buzz, but one expert thinks this might be the year to skip out on the position altogether if a team holds a top pick.

Brooks Austin has made a living studying college football film, so much so that he's earned the moniker "The Film Guy."

His YouTube channel, "The Film Guy Network," has over 135,000 subscribers, and he's recently parlayed that into a partnership with the college football media giant On3.

Suffice to say, Austin knows ball, so when I sat down with him to talk about the college game, and more specifically, the quarterback class for the 2027 NFL Draft, he gave a surprising assessment.

"Can I punt on the entire class," he asked, half jokingly.

As Austin points out, there are some solid quarterbacks in this class, but none are the "can't miss" prospects that would necessitate a top-five pick like in years past.

Most experts figured Oregon's Dante Moore would be the first QB off the board in '27, given he was already projected to go high last year before deciding to return to Eugene.

An injury might have derailed that for Moore, but as Austin points out, the injured Duck wasn't without some limitations of his own even before exiting for the season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Dante Moore is a really good football player," he explains. "But (he) gets stuck on reads and makes his mind up pre-snap, and that scares me. He's also a little up and down, like from a fundamental standpoint, from a mechanics standpoint, he just kinda gets away with a lot of it in college football."

Moore wasn't the only one giving Austin some pause.

Ole Miss's Trinidad Chambliss, one of the preseason Heisman favorites, has had a fine season statistically, but his build makes Austin nervous about him at the next level.

"I love him, but there are some physical questions about that one as well, like, is he gonna work at his stature when we get to the league?"

Other quarterbacks like Texas' Arch Manning and LSU's Sam Leavitt get mentioned as well, with Austin stating question marks about their decision making and turnover problems.

The prospect who Austin believes should go number one overall shouldn't come as a shock to anyone who watches football on Saturday.

"If I had the number one overall pick, I'd draft Jeremiah Smith," Austin admits. "And then next year I try to find a quarterback."

Austin explains that Smith, the Ohio State wide receiver, is a "guarantee" and one of the only truly generational prospects we've seen in the game since Andrew Luck in 2012.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"I would draft Smith, and I'd be like, 'I've got the best prospect and most known prospect that's come out of college football... since maybe like Andrew Luck,'" Austin claims. "I would just draft him if I was bad enough to be the number one overall pick."

World.title: Cooling mattresses for hot sleepers: Why Nectar?
World.content:
There's nothing worse than waking up at 3 a.m. sweating, and desperately searching for the cool side of the pillow. If that's you, the solution might just be a mattress from Nectar. All of Nectar's mattresses have cooling fibers woven into the surface fabric, designed to cool down your body temperature and keep you sleeping through the night, regardless of the season.

Original price: $1,567

Cool to the touch all night long

Nectar memory foam mattresses are ideal for hot sleepers, with a cool-to-the-touch sleeping surface. The foam relieves pressure on your joints, conforms to your body and responds to your movement through the night, helping support your body while cooling you (and minimizing movement for a partner sleeping in the same bed).

You can choose from Classic, Premier and Luxe memory foam mattresses. As you move up the line, the cooling and pressure-relieving properties double and triple.

If you're an especially hot sleeper, consider the Ultra memory foam mattress, which has four times the cooling properties of the Classic model. It contains a separate sheet of phase change materials layered on top of the memory foam to help regulate temperature.⁠ Phase change materials in the Nectar Ultra can absorb or release heat as they change phase. That means it pulls heat away from your body when you're too warm and releases heat back out towards your body when you're too cold, so you always stay at the perfect temperature throughout the night.

There are more than 200 5-star reviews, many of which praise the cooling properties. "Absolutely the best mattress I have ever laid my head on," said one reviewer. "First night was the best night's sleep I have had in years. The comfort of the mattress helped me fall asleep quickly and the cooling effect helped me sleep all night."

All of Nectar's foam used is CertiPUR-US certified, which means it's free from ozone-depleting substances and harmful pollutants.



What about hybrid mattresses?

Hybrid mattresses combine the pressure-relieving support of memory foam with innerspring coils. These help with reducing motion transfer, which is perfect for those sleeping with partners. Nectar's Hybrid Luxe mattress would be ideal for extremely hot sleepers who toss and turn or have partners that move in their sleep.

The coils allow for more airflow in your mattress, rather than air getting trapped in the dense memory foam. There are Premier and Luxe versions of the hybrid mattress, which get more and more cooling as you move up the line.

NectarCool technology: The optional upgrade

For an additional cost, NectarCool is an optional cover upgrade on eligible Nectar Classic, Premier, and Luxe memory foam and hybrid models. It adds cooling polyethylene fibers to the cover for a cooler-to-the-touch feel, designed to bring down your temperature as you sleep.

How the NectarCool upgrade fits each tier

Classic: The standard cover has a cool-to-the-touch feel; NectarCool adds more cooling fibers.

Premier: The standard cover has about 60% more cooling fibers than Classic; NectarCool adds more to that cover.⁠

Luxe: The standard cover has about twice as many cooling fibers as Classic; NectarCool adds more to the Luxe cover.⁠

Ultra: The separate NectarCool cover upgrade isn’t offered since Ultra already includes top-tier cooling with four times more cooling fibers and phase-change material as the standard.⁠

Try it first

Nectar has a generous trial period and warranty, so you can be absolutely sure you love your mattress.

You can sleep on the mattress for up to a year and return it for a refund if you don’t like it. Call or email Nectar, and the company will help you find a charity to donate it to.

If a mattress develops a problem within 10 years, Nectar will replace it. After 10 years, the company will repair it.

For more deals, visit www.foxnews.com/deals

Original price: $599

On top of the mattress deal, you can snag Nectar's Serenity Sleep Bundle for 66% off when you bundle it with your mattress purchase. It comes with a mattress protector, a sheet set and two cooling pillows for $179.

The waterproof mattress cover protects it from spills and stains, without taking away from the breathability of your sleeping surface. Plus, it's machine-washable for easy cleanup.

The two included pillows have cooling fibers woven into the foam, similar to the brand's foam mattresses, to keep you even cooler through the night. With a classic sheet set, you have everything you need to completely make your bed for one budget-friendly price.

World.title: Luka Doncic brings extra motivation to Lakers vs Warriors NBA Cup clash on ESPN tonight
World.content:
The start of the NBA season has actually been a lot of fun. The teams have looked good; they are enjoyable, and the betting has gone very well for me. I have a major move tonight in the Hornets-Wizards game, and I'm looking to score more in another early-season matchup. We've already seen this one play out this season, but I have a lot of excitement for the game between the Lakers and Warriors that takes place tonight at Golden State.

The Lakers are now the Luka Lakers. There is no more LeBron, and the keys have been handed over to one of the top assets in the entire league. How has that worked out for Los Angeles through the early portion of the season? The team is 4-1, with the lone loss coming against a surprisingly good Portland team. To start the season, they've beaten the Warriors by 22, the Clippers by eight, the Jazz by nine, and the Clippers by 16. None of those three teams will be playoff contenders.

They now take on the Warriors for the second time in the early season as part of the NBA Cup Group Play. This is the third game in four nights for the Lakers, but not a back-to-back. Still, legs could be a bit tired. However, this is almost certainly a game that Luka circled on the calendar. On Opening Night, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg was yapping at Luka for much of the game, and then doubled-down with comments about him in the media. Luka does not back down, and Luka does not forget.

LUKA DONCIC BUYS OUT ENTIRE PARKING LOT TO GIVE LAKERS FANS FREE PARKING FOR SEASON OPENER

In fairness to Lendeborg he was quite effective when guarding Luka directly. However, the Lakers crushed the Warriors and moved on. Now the Warriors get a chance to return the favor. It hasn't been a great season for Golden State so far with two wins and three losses. However, the Warriors did win back-to-back games on the road with very good performances against the Nuggets and the Timberwolves. World.title: Unvetted foreign workers at AI firms raise national security alarms, advocates warn
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Tech advocacy groups are sounding the alarm, warning that the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence and a lack of federal oversight for foreign nationals working at AI firms pose a major national security risk.

Amy Kremer, chair of Humans First, a group focused on establishing democratic oversight, safety protocols, and local control over artificial intelligence, said AI technology has virtually no federal guardrails compared to other tech sectors.

"This is a national security threat. These companies hold and have access to a lot of sensitive information," Kremer told Fox News Digital. "You don't have to steal an entire AI model to get information. You can just find out what they're working on, who their partners are, and who their adversaries are. That is not the kind of thing that we need getting out."

MAGA MOM'S DIRE WARNING OVER TECH GUARDRAILS AS TRUMP PUTS PEDAL TO THE METAL ON RACE WITH CHINA

"If America wants to lead the world on AI, and we want America to have this AI advantage, then we have to put national security at the top," she added.

Kremer's concerns come as AI continues to expand, even as many Americans and lawmakers remain wary of the fast-moving industry.

WATCH: AI SAFETY SCARE SPARKS CAP HILL FIGHT OVER GUARDRAILS: 'CHINA'S GOING TO EAT OUR LUNCH'

In early October, an engineer at OpenAI, one of the world's most prominent AI companies, was arrested after allegedly planting a recording device inside a conference room at the AI giant's San Francisco office.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, a Saudi Arabian citizen, allegedly researched how to construct a recording device and where to place it inside OpenAI, eventually concealing a customized audio recorder behind a television in an executive conference room in late September, according to the Justice Department.

BEYOND KILLER ROBOTS: CHINA'S REAL AI THREAT TO AMERICA IS ALREADY HERE, EXPERTS WARN

Searches of his home and electronic devices uncovered similar components and photographs that appeared to show reconnaissance of other locations inside OpenAI, including another conference room used for sensitive meetings, federal prosecutors said.

Alfozan, who was a lawful permanent resident in the United States, was terminated by OpenAI following his arrest.

FBI OVERHAULS TECH BACKBONE TO COUNTER AI THREATS FROM FOREIGN ADVERSARIES, REDUCE RESPONSE TIMES, PATEL SAYS

In January, a former Google software engineer was convicted of stealing thousands of pages of the company's trade secrets related to AI to benefit China.

Even the AI firms themselves have expressed concerns about the technology. In September, OpenAI and Anthropic warned that their advanced systems could pose a direct threat to humanity. The CEOs of both firms stated that their AI models should be regulated and rigorously tested.

TRUMP'S AI RACE WITH CHINA COULD BECOME THE BIGGEST MISTAKE OF OUR TIME

Despite calls for greater controls, in his September speech to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, President Donald Trump rebuffed calls for international regulation.

"The United States … totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control the artificial intelligence being spoken of so much now," Trump told various heads of state and their delegations. "Yet the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming ... these are the same people that are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us, that everything is going to be a total disaster."

MORNING GLORY: SPARE US THE AI APOCALYPSE RHETORIC. LET CONGRESS DECIDE WHAT COMES NEXT

Among the other mounting concerns are rogue agents, autonomous or semi-autonomous AI programs whose behavior diverges from their design intent or safety constraints.

In the spring, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell held emergency briefings with major Wall Street bank CEOs to warn about severe cybersecurity risks posed by Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview AI model.

AI COULD GO ROGUE. WASHINGTON NEEDS ANSWERS TO THESE FIVE QUESTIONS ASAP

In July, OpenAI revealed that rogue AI agents hacked into the systems of tech startup Hugging Face.

Some elected officials have called for increased AI regulation.

"There is now a growing alarm about the future of humanity and creating technology that human beings cannot control," Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., told reporters in September. "And I'm happy to tell you that I think there is a growing sense of urgency upon members of Congress that this has to be done."

That same month, Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., blocked a bill that would require artificial intelligence companies to have a kill switch for rogue AI.

"I think it would be crazy to get on the floor one day and regulate an entire industry," Paul told reporters at the time.

In addition to the AI firms themselves, critics of the technology have raised concerns about how it could be exploited by America's adversaries and bad actors.

TRUMP INTEL CHIEF WARNS AI FIRMS ON HACKS, SAYS NEW DEPARTMENT IS THE 'COP ON THE BEAT'

A model created by Chinese firm Z. AI carried out several complex cyberattacks in controlled simulations and repeatedly ignored safety instructions in separate tests, according to a report by AI security research firm Irregular, Reuters reported.

In addition, U.S. intelligence agencies raised concerns regarding contact between Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, and NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang, The New York Times reported. Alice Huang, no relation to Jensen Huang, was deemed by American officials to be a Chinese intelligence asset, according to the report.

"Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected," a NVIDIA spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year."

"Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security," the statement continued. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know."

Kremer is calling for an investigation into whether Jensen Huang's conduct warrants federal review.

"Jensen Huang has questioned whether it matters who gets to advanced AI first. It matters to America," she said. "He should be barred from the White House, and Nvidia’s government contracts should end until he is no longer affiliated with the company. America’s national security must come before corporate profits."

Fox News Digital's Alex Miller contributed to this report.

World.title: Treasury flags $8B in suspicious foreign-directed transfers through US money services firms
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Trump administration uncovered what it says is more than $8 billion in potentially fraudulent cross-border wire payments that were made under foreign agents’ direction, issuing new guidelines for nonprofits who take foreign money, executing multiple FBI search warrants and building out a large-scale indictment.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) within the Treasury Department said it identified suspicious wire payments from 2021 to 2025 that were sent through U.S.-based money services businesses at the direction of foreign agents.

"When greed meets negligence, the American people suffer," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "Under President Trump and Vice President Vance’s leadership, Treasury stopped nearly $190 million in funds tied to overseas fraud and returned more than $100 million to U.S. victims. We are working with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud to help prevent this kind of abuse from happening again, in Minnesota or anywhere else."

WHITE HOUSE LAUNCHES INTERACTIVE MAP TRACKING BILLIONS IN SUSPECTED FRAUD

At a Friday press conference, Bessent said: "In the weeks following my visit, Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, known as FinCEN, issued a geographic targeting order to trace criminal networks.

That diverts funds overseas and ensures that taxpayer dollars go to the American people, not terror groups like Al Shabaab."

He added that the Treasury Department has investigations in the U.S. and abroad into "Al-Shabaab, its networks and its enablers. Since the start of the Trump administration, FinCen data have also supported the law enforcement effort that led to the arrest and charging of 115 fraudsters, as well as 75 convictions and nearly 3,000 subpoenas across Minnesota."

Bessent said that on Thursday, "IRS-CI assisted with investigative activity at several sites suspected of fraud. I want to give a shout-out to our great officers at IRS-CI. They don't get much press, but they are quietly one of the most affected groups in the United States government for fighting fraud."

Bessent, FBI Director Kash Patel, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz and Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson held a news conference in Minnesota to detail the substantial fraud uncovered and FBI Minnesota's actions.

"This FBI follows the money," Patel said at the Friday press conference. "This FBI will put in prison anyone who commits fraud anywhere in the world against any American citizen. Thanks to President Trump, we finally have a commander-in-chief who prioritized the initiative to go after the fraudsters with the full force of government."

The Treasury Department issued a notice urging banks to scrutinize nonprofits’ donors, funding streams and ties to other groups and governments. FinCEN says the arrangements could obscure the ultimate recipients and potentially be exploited for money laundering or terrorist financing.

WATCHDOG UNLEASHES DATABASE TO EXPOSE 'LOOPHOLES' AS $5B IN FOREIGN CASH FLOODS US NONPROFITS

The notice noted that bad actors commit fraud in three forms of abuse: sham charities allegedly diverting funds to illicit activity, charity-related fraud that enriches the people running the scheme, and embezzlement by insiders at legitimate organizations.

Salim Said, a co-conspirator in the Feeding Our Future case, was sentenced to 30 years in prison this week after being convicted on 21 counts tied to a scheme that defrauded a federal child nutrition program of $49 million.

At the end of last year, reports and social media coverage by Shirley exposed a network of daycare centers, like the "Quality Learing (sic) Center," that were allegedly fraudulent and operated mostly by Somali immigrants.

MINNESOTA MAN CAPTURED IN SOMALIA AFTER ALLEGEDLY HELPING ORCHESTRATE $250M CHILD NUTRITION FRAUD SCHEME

The reports sparked swift action from the administration, and former Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem deployed DHS and ICE agents to the streets of Minneapolis to catch and deport Somali immigrants in the country illegally. The deployment sparked a clash between local residents and federal agents that exploded into violent riots across the Twin Cities.

The Treasury secretary has previously taken aim at fraud and bad actors funding nonprofit organizations in the U.S. In April, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) tightened tax-exempt reporting requirements in an effort to uncover nonprofit funding being used for "extremist activity" and "hiding fraud."

"Tax-exempt status is not immunity from scrutiny," Treasury Assistant Secretary and acting IRS chief counsel Ken Kies wrote in a statement. "If an organization receives public funds or tax-deductible donations, it should be prepared to show who controls the money and where it goes."

CRUZ PUSHES BILL TO HOLD TAX-EXEMPT SPONSORS ACCOUNTABLE AS DOJ PROBES SINGHAM NETWORK

Bessent has also been involved with the Department of Justice’s grand jury probe into the nonprofit network of Neville Roy Singham. Sources at Treasury told Fox News Digital that Bessent met with Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon and discussed Singham’s previously held accounts at the bank, which Singham used to distribute funds to a number of nonprofits.

HOUSE PANEL WARNS SINGHAM-LINKED NONPROFITS: COMPLY WITH SUBPOENAS OR FACE CONGRESS

Singham, a 72-year-old American who sold his tech company for $785 million in 2017 and now lives in Shanghai, has funneled $278 million into the broad network of nonprofits since 2017, according to a Fox News Digital investigation. These groups regularly organize and participate in anti-ICE, anti-Israel and pro-Iran demonstrations.

World.title: Binance says user funds are safe after thieves make off with billions in largest-ever crypto hack
World.content:
A record-setting cyberattack targeting the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange rocked the digital assets industry Friday, delivering another blow to a sector already struggling to achieve mainstream adoption.

The exchange, Binance, announced late Thursday that more than $6 billion appeared to have moved through wallets connected to a security breach. Around $3 billion of that had potentially been located and frozen across several exchanges, though it was not immediately clear if those funds were recoverable.

It did not appear that the hackers were able to access customer accounts or holdings. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng released a video statement Friday morning that sought to reassure platform users.

“Your assets are safe,” he said, adding “we never use customer funds, so they are not impacted.”

Instead, Binance’s corporate holdings were affected, he said. The company said it had set aside $5 billion to cover the losses and was working with partners to purchase an additional $1.34 billion in cryptocurrencies to cover the total amount believed to have been stolen.

In a statement, the Secret Service said it was working with private-sector partners, including U.S.-based crypto group Circle, to identify, freeze, trace and recover funds stolen from Binance. It also said it was coordinating with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia and other law enforcement partners to identify those responsible. It said its investigation remained in early stages.

The hack is the latest setback for crypto, which continues to reckon with a reputation for being too volatile — and too vulnerable to criminal activity — for widespread use. The scale of the hack echoes collapse of crypto exchange FTX, which, though not the result of a cyberattack, caused billions in losses.

The renewed doubts were reflected in Bitcoin’s value Friday, which fell more than 5% overnight to approximately $77,000, accelerating its month-long downturn. Other affected cryptocurrencies fell as much as 9%.

The crypto industry was already reeling from the failure in Congress of the Clarity Act, a bill that would have granted comprehensive legal protections for crypto assets in the U.S.

Despite bipartisan support for the core elements of the legislation, its passage was torpedoed by a battle over conflict-of-interest rules for elected officials, notably President Donald Trump.

The president has disclosed in filings that he earned more than $1 billion from crypto last year.

The Binance hack stands to prolong this reckoning, experts said.

“There will be an imperative for Binance to cover losses not only for its own reputation and value, but I expect there will be a level of co-operation within the space as they look at the collective reputational harm this may, rightly or wrongly, cause to the sector,” Laura Clatworthy, head of digital assets at the law firm Edwin Coe, said in a statement.

That cooperation was seen in the immediate reaction of other mainstream crypto players.

Crypto firms Tether and Circle, which operate the two-largest stablecoins, worked quickly to freeze assets implicated in the hack.

However, U.S. blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs estimates that $2.4 billion in Bitcoin and Ethereum will never be recovered.

As of Friday morning, the hack’s origins remained murky. The whole heist unfolded in just 20 minutes starting at approximately 4 p.m. ET Thursday.

Binance initially said the attack involved a compromised laptop.

“However, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach,” ‌it said in a statement on X, without elaborating.

Multiple blockchain analysis firms said the hack had attributes associated with previous operations believed to have been carried out by North Korean actors.

Teng, the Binance co-CEO, said Binance’s investigation had not yet identified the attackers.

At least one prominent tech CEO could not resist making light of the situation. Elon Musk left a “yikes” emoji in response to an X user who noted that the collapsed crypto exchange FTX had initially also told users their funds were safe amid a wave of losses.

Binance co-founder CZ Zhao responded:“Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop.”

Zhao noted that his SpaceX shares — the product of a Binance-related $500 million investment in Twitter, were now worth more than $1 billion.

“Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!”

World.title: Trump uncancels weekend rallies in Iowa and Kansas with Senate control at stake
World.content:
The White House has rescheduled weekend rallies in Kansas and Iowa after briefly canceling them Thursday.

The president will now attend rallies on Sunday in Salina, Kansas, and Dubuque, Iowa, the Republican National Committee announced Friday afternoon.

Less than 24 hours earlier, the president said he would not attend either rally and would opt instead for a series of tele-rallies that could reach more voters ahead of Election Day.

Now, it appears the president will be attempting to do all of the above.

NBC News earlier Friday reported the rally reversal, citing a White House official and another source familiar with the plans.

“President Trump loves his supporters, and in addition to nearly 20 tele-rallies, he will hold back-to-back rallies in Kansas and Iowa on Sunday,” the source familiar with the plans said Friday. “No one works harder, fights harder, or loves the American people more than President Donald J. Trump!”

“The rallies were rearranged for scheduling purposes to accommodate nearly 20 additional tele-rallies that were recently added to the President’s schedule,” the source added.

A Trump adviser said that the team thought it might be better to get Trump “in as many places at once” by doing more tele-town halls, but that the president wanted to do in-person rallies instead.

“He wants to be out with his people,” the adviser said. “No one does a rally quite like him, and that’s how he wanted to close out the cycle.”

Asked after the cancellations Thursday on why he wasn’t going to Kansas anymore to support GOP Sen. Roger Marshall, the president told reporters: “Because I think he’s doing well. We’re going to do a tele-rally for him instead. He’s doing, he’s doing very well.”

When asked whether the return to Kansas marked an acknowledgment of Marshall’s tighter-than-expected re-election race, one of the sources responded that the White House is “feeling bullish about both states, but it’s about giving the people what they want.”

This weekend’s rallies are part of the president’s planned midterm travel blitz, in which he said he would travel to 35 places across the country to help boost turnout for Republican candidates.

Trump has repeatedly touted what he believes is the positive impact of his rallies on GOP candidates, going as far as to suggest that his presence in battleground states has boosted Republicans in the polls.

Concerns over high costs connected to the Iran war have helped turn the Kansas Senate race into a toss-up in a state that hasn’t sent a Democrat to the Senate for nearly a century.

Trump, who has campaigned at 25 rallies in the past month, has admitted that the blitz has not been “easy,” saying through a hoarse voice Monday that “God didn’t make your vocal cords to do a rally every day.”

But he insisted Thursday that he felt “perfect” and lashed out at a reporter who pressed him about whether the rally cancellation in Kansas was tied to his health.

“You’ve been following me for two weeks. I feel perfect. You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape. You look like hell,” Trump said to the journalist.

He canceled Iowa’s rally hours after that interaction, after a White House official and a person familiar with the matter confirmed that Trump’s appearance was off.

The Republican National Committee said in a news release Thursday that the rallies were canceled with the goal of “maximizing opportunities for President Donald J. Trump to speak to voters across the country.”

GOP operatives in Iowa, where all congressional races this year except one are competitive, told NBC News before the rally there was rescheduled that in-person rallies would have been helpful. Trump’s rally is scheduled to take place in Dubuque, in the contested 2nd Congressional District.

“A tele-rally will be helpful in boosting turnout, but an in-person rally would have been really helpful,” an operative said.

Another operative said he “would love to have the president,” but he said, “Iowa’s in pretty good shape.”

Trump is also scheduled to hold an event in Daytona Beach, Florida, on Friday. He will be campaigning for Republican Rep. Randy Fine and Sen. Ashley Moody, who are running in races rated solidly Republican by the nonpartisan Cook Political Report.

No events have been announced for Monday.
