What Voters Will Face

Voters can cast special votes on Monday and Tuesday, 2–3 November 2026, from 08:00 to 17:00. Special voting is for people who cannot get to a station on election day, such as the elderly, the disabled and election workers.

Ordinary voting takes place on Wednesday, 4 November 2026, from 07:00 to 21:00 South Africa Standard Time (SAST, two hours ahead of Universal Time). The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC), the independent body that runs the vote, says voters need a smart ID card, a green barcoded ID book or a temporary identity certificate.

Cooperative Governance Minister Velenkosini Hlabisa set the date in Government Gazette No. 55162, the official state notice, published on 7 August 2026. The IEC says 136,790 candidates were cleared to contest.

What Prediction Markets Say

Traders on Polymarket, a prediction market where users bet real money, are betting on mayoral races rather than national results. Their prices, read on 30 October at 1:25 p.m. ET, are shown below.

Johannesburg, mayoral contenders: Helen Zille 57.5%, David Makhura 13.0%, Frank Chikane 7.5% (US$136,259 traded).

Cape Town, mayoral contender: Geordin Hill-Lewis 95.9% (US$13,375 traded).

Durban (eThekwini), mayoral contenders: Apostle Mxolisi Phakathi 52.9%, Haniff Hoosen 36.0% (US$44,788 traded).

These prices are bets, not polls, and each candidate’s price is the market’s implied probability. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely.

We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

Americans with business, family or travel ties to Johannesburg, Durban or Cape Town should expect a heavy police presence around polling day. The three cities are where most of the flagged stations are, and a disrupted vote there would draw attention to how stable the country’s big cities are.

The 4 November voting window starts at midnight Eastern and closes at 2 p.m. Eastern, so results will begin arriving during the US morning. Local elections decide who runs water, electricity and housing services, issues that sit behind many of the protests police are watching.

What Is Not Known

The reports reviewed do not say how many officers will cover the flagged stations or what changes voters will see there. They name no specific threat, and none reports an incident, arrest or closure linked to the assessment.

It is also unclear what happened to the remaining three stations in the national total. The inter-ministerial committee, the group of ministers overseeing election readiness, flagged in early October that El Niño weather risks, such as heat and low rainfall, could affect voters queuing on the day.

Frequently Asked Questions

When are South Africa’s local elections?

Special voting is on 2–3 November from 08:00 to 17:00. Ordinary voting is on Wednesday, 4 November from 07:00 to 21:00 South Africa time.

How many high-risk voting stations did police name?

Police named 331, with 165 in KwaZulu-Natal and 119 in Gauteng. The reason given is possible protests and unrest.





Sources: South African Police Service statement of 30 October 2026; Electoral Commission of South Africa; Government Gazette No. 55162 via gov.za; Polymarket (prices as of 30 October 2026, 1:25 p.m. ET).

World.title: Swahili Fashion Week Returns Without a Venue
World.content:
TANZANIA · CULTURE GUIDE

Key Facts When Friday 4 to Sunday 6 December 2026, the 19th edition; Dar es Salaam is 8 hours ahead of New York.

Where Dar es Salaam, Tanzania’s largest city; the organiser has not yet published the venue.

Tickets On sale at selected outlets and online through the festival site; prices are not published.

Extra A one-day Pop Up Shop for the public runs Saturday 14 November, 12 to 8 p.m. local time.

Entry US visitors need a visa costing US$100 and a passport valid for six months.

Swahili Fashion Week, East Africa’s long-running runway and design festival, returns to Dar es Salaam from Friday 4 to Sunday 6 December 2026, and tickets are on sale. This guide covers what is confirmed, what is not, and how a US visitor gets there.

The organiser calls the 2026 event its 19th year and says it is one of the biggest annual fashion events in Africa. Two details that a traveller needs, the venue and the ticket prices, are still missing from the festival’s own pages.

What Swahili Fashion Week Is and Why It Matters

Swahili Fashion Week was founded in 2008 by the Pan-African couturier Mustafa Hassanali, according to the festival’s own site. It gives designers from Swahili-speaking countries, the region around Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda, a stage to show work and meet buyers.

The organisers frame fashion as a business as well as an art, with the aim of taking African designers into the global industry. The festival’s forum is organised by the Fashion Association of Tanzania, the industry body, together with 361 Degrees Africa, a fashion and events group.

For US readers the draw is a rare chance to see East African design in person, and to meet designers whose labels sell abroad. Buyers, stylists and members of the African diaspora are the natural audience.

The Schedule

The organiser lists the main event for 4 to 6 December 2026, which runs Friday to Sunday. Dar es Salaam is on East Africa Time, three hours ahead of Greenwich time all year, so it is 8 hours ahead of New York and 11 hours ahead of Los Angeles in December.

The official runway schedule says only that it is coming soon, so show times and the designer line-up by night are not yet published. The festival’s site already lists more than 30 Tanzanian designers and six international ones, including a label from Kampala, Uganda.

A Pop Up Shop opens to the public on Saturday 14 November 2026 from 12 noon to 8 p.m., and the organiser describes it as a one-day retail space. Its location is still to be confirmed, and it aims to connect designers with business, diplomatic and expatriate communities.

The Tanzania Fashion Forum, a business conference under the same banner, was listed for Tuesday 27 October 2026 in Dar es Salaam, and the organiser’s page does not yet report how it went. The Embassy of Italy in Dar es Salaam supported it, according to the organiser.

Tickets

The festival’s ticket page says tickets are available now at selected physical outlets and online. The page does not list prices or ticket types, so we do not quote any.

Buy only through the festival’s own site, swahilifashionweek.com, and keep the confirmation. If you cannot see prices at checkout, ask the organiser at [email protected] before paying.

Getting to Dar es Salaam From the US

US citizens need a Tanzanian tourist visa, which costs US$100 for a one-year multiple-entry permit, according to the immigration service fee list. You can apply for an e-visa online before travel or buy a visa on arrival.

Your passport must be valid for at least six months and have a blank page. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you arrive from a country with the disease, including after a layover of 12 hours or more.

Since 1 October 2026, Tanzania also requires mandatory travel insurance for visitors to the mainland, which costs about US$44. Check the current rule with your airline or the immigration service before you fly.

Most US travellers will connect through a hub in Europe, the Gulf or elsewhere in Africa, so check routes and times with the airlines. The city’s airport is Julius Nyerere International Airport, and getting around at night is easiest by taxi or ride-hailing app, as in our Dar es Salaam events guide.

Safety and Costs

Reports say the State Department lowered its Tanzania advisory to Level 2, Exercise Increased Caution, on 16 October 2026. Read the current advisory on the State Department site and enrol in the embassy’s alert programme before you book.

December is hot and humid on the coast, so plan indoor evenings and carry water. Use cards and cash sparingly in crowded places and keep valuables out of sight.

Add a few days in Zanzibar if you can, where our guide to Sauti za Busara shows the island’s biggest music festival. Fashion fans can also compare Kenya Fashion Week in Nairobi on 22 November.

What It Means for You

This is a niche cultural event rather than a mega festival, so plan it as part of a longer East Africa trip. Tickets are open, but you cannot yet price the evening or choose a hotel by the venue.

Wait for the venue and the runway schedule before you book flights, and check the visa and insurance rules. Our Tanzania coverage follows travel and security news.

What Is Not Known

The organiser has not published the 2026 venue, ticket prices, show times or the nightly line-up. Rely on the festival’s own dates of 4 to 6 December.

The location of the Pop Up Shop is also unconfirmed. We will update this guide when the organiser publishes the schedule.

More: Tanzania news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When Is Swahili Fashion Week 2026?

It runs Friday 4 to Sunday 6 December 2026 in Dar es Salaam, according to the festival’s site. Dar es Salaam is 8 hours ahead of New York.

Where Is Swahili Fashion Week Held?

The festival is in Dar es Salaam, but the organiser has not published the 2026 venue. Check the festival site before booking.

How Do I Buy Swahili Fashion Week Tickets?

The festival says tickets are on sale at selected outlets and online through its website. Prices are not published.

Do US Visitors Need a Visa for Tanzania?

Yes, US citizens need a tourist visa, which costs US$100 for a one-year multiple-entry permit. It can be requested online or bought on arrival.

World.title: Hilary Duff VIP Tarot Cards in San Juan
World.content:
File photo, 2013. (Photo: JacksonvilleDistrict, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

PUERTO RICO · MUSIC GUIDE

Key Facts When Tuesday 10 August 2027, 8 p.m. in San Juan, which is also 8 p.m. in New York.

Where Coliseo de Puerto Rico, 500 Arterial B, Hato Rey, San Juan, a seated arena.

Tickets On sale through Ticketera, the arena’s ticket seller; the arena lists no prices yet.

Travel Puerto Rico is US territory: no passport and no currency exchange for US citizens.

Rules Clear bags only, tickets in a phone wallet, and under-16s need an adult over 21.

American singer and actress Hilary Duff brings her Lucky Me Tour to San Juan, Puerto Rico, on Tuesday 10 August 2027, and tickets are on sale now. This guide covers the schedule, the VIP package, entry rules, and how a visitor from the mainland gets to the arena.

Puerto Rico is a US territory, so this is the easiest Latin American stop on her tour for US fans, with no passport check and dollars everywhere. The arena’s own page lists the date, the seller and the rules, but not the prices.

Who Is Hilary Duff and Why It Matters

Hilary Duff is an American actress and pop singer who rose to fame as a teenager in the 2000s and now plays arenas again with the Lucky Me Tour. The tour has Latin American stops in 2027, and our guides cover her shows in São Paulo and Santiago.

For a US reader the San Juan night is a short, simple trip, and Tuesday 10 August 2027 falls in the summer break for many families. The show is an English-language pop night, so no Spanish is needed to follow it.

The show is a seated event, so each ticket comes with a seat, and the arena provides a seating chart on its event page. Children aged two and older need their own ticket.

Date and Times

The arena lists the concert for Tuesday 10 August 2027 at 8 p.m. Puerto Rico stays on Atlantic Standard Time all year, which is the same as New York in August, so the start is also 8 p.m. Eastern.Chicago and Houston are an hour behind, and Los Angeles is three hours behind.The arena does not list door times, a support act or an end time.

Tickets and the VIP Package

Tickets are sold through Ticketera, which runs on the TiX.By platform, and the promoter is No Limit Entertainment. The arena’s page does not show any ticket prices, so we do not quote any.

Resale sites also list this show, but their figures are not official face values and can change at any time. Buy through the arena’s own link, listed on the arena’s event page, to avoid fake tickets.

A VIP package is on sale in limited numbers, and its price is not shown. It includes one premium reserved ticket, early entry, a merchandise pack, a Lucky Me wine glass set, tarot cards, a limited-edition bag, a commemorative laminate and lanyard, and priority merchandise shopping.

The seller emails the VIP details about three days before the show. The packages cannot be transferred, cannot be bought through fan-to-fan resale, and cannot be refunded.

Getting There From the US Mainland

US citizens fly to San Juan as a domestic trip, so they need no passport, visa or customs form, but they do need the photo ID that airlines require. Non-US citizens follow the same entry rules as for any US airport.

The main airport is Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport, known by its code SJU. The arena is in the Hato Rey district of San Juan, and a Tren Urbano rail station named Hato Rey sits next to it, as the photo above shows.

The island is in the Atlantic hurricane season, which runs from 1 June to 30 November. Buy travel insurance that covers storms, and check the forecast a week before you fly.

Entry Rules and Safety

Tickets must be downloaded to a phone wallet, and the arena says it does not accept photos of tickets. Only small clear vinyl or PVC bags up to 12 by 6 by 12 inches are allowed, or a small clutch up to 4.5 by 6.5 inches.

The arena bans weapons, cans and bottles, e-cigarettes, lighters, video and professional cameras, tablets and computers, selfie sticks, perfume, and outside food and drink. Children aged 15 and under must stay with an adult over 21 at all times.

Seats in the accessible sections need a valid disability card or ID at the door. At any big event, keep your phone in a front pocket and agree on a meeting point with your group.

For the wider island, read our guides to Puerto Rico culture and Puerto Rico news. They explain the music scene and the island’s current issues for visitors.

What It Means for You

Because Puerto Rico uses the US dollar and needs no passport for US citizens, this is a low-friction concert trip. Watch for the ticket prices to appear on the seller’s page, and compare them with her US dates before you decide.

Book flights only after you hold tickets, and plan around the hurricane season. If you are travelling with children, remember the adult-over-21 rule for those aged 15 and under.

What Is Not Known

The arena has not published ticket prices, door times, a support act or the length of the show. The VIP package price is also not listed.

It is not known whether a second San Juan date will be added. We will update this guide when the seller or the arena publishes more.

More: Puerto Rico news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When Does Hilary Duff Play San Juan?

She plays Tuesday 10 August 2027 at 8 p.m. at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico. That is also 8 p.m. in New York.

Where Do I Buy Hilary Duff Tickets in San Juan?

Tickets are sold through Ticketera, linked from the arena’s event page. The arena has not listed prices.

Do I Need a Passport to See the Show?

US citizens do not need a passport to fly to Puerto Rico, only the photo ID that airlines accept. Non-US citizens follow the entry rules for the United States.

What Can I Bring Into the Arena?

Only small clear bags up to 12 by 6 by 12 inches, or a clutch up to 4.5 by 6.5 inches. Tickets must be on a phone wallet, not as photos.

Sabaneta, the town south of Medellín where the new DAVIarena stands. File photo, December 2012. (Photo: Jpsalazaro, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

COLOMBIA · MUSIC GUIDE

Key Facts When Saturday 17 April 2027: doors 6 p.m., show 9:30 p.m. Medellín time, which is 10:30 p.m. US Eastern.

Where DAVIarena, a new arena in Sabaneta, in the Medellín metro area, five minutes on foot from a Metro stop.

Tickets Tuboleta, the arena’s only authorised seller: from 120,000 Colombian pesos (COP), about US$38, to COP 7,280,000 (about US$2,313).

Rules Minimum age 12, at most 4 tickets per order, and foreign-card buyers collect tickets at the box office.

Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

Carlos Vives and his band La Provincia play Medellín on Saturday 17 April 2027 at DAVIarena, with tickets on sale now through Tuboleta. This guide covers the schedule, prices, how to buy from the United States, and how to get to the arena.

Vives is one of Colombia’s best-known pop and vallenato singers, and this is his first tour of the country in eight years. The Medellín night is a new date for a show first announced for 17 October 2026, so fans with older plans should check their tickets.

Who Is Carlos Vives and Why It Matters

Carlos Vives is a Colombian singer who built a modern pop sound on traditional vallenato, an accordion-led folk style from the country’s Caribbean coast. La Provincia is the band that plays with him, and the Tour al Sol is the name of the current tour.

The tour was announced in February 2026 as his first national tour in eight years, and it also played the United States and Puerto Rico earlier in 2026. The Medellín date is one of several shows moved from 2026 to 2027.

For US readers the draw is simple, because this is the home-country version of a tour that also crossed the United States this year. Seeing it in Medellín adds a trip to a city that many American visitors and remote workers already know.

Date, Doors and Start Times

The concert is on Saturday 17 April 2027, with doors at 6 p.m. and the show at 9:30 p.m. Medellín time, according to the Tuboleta listing. Colombia stays on UTC minus five all year, while New York is on daylight time in April, so the show starts at 10:30 p.m. Eastern.

Doors at 6 p.m. in Medellín equal 7 p.m. in New York and 4 p.m. in Los Angeles. The listing gives no end time or set length.

Tickets and Prices

Tuboleta says it is the only authorised ticket operator for DAVIarena, and Promotora Colombia S.A.S. is named as the organiser. Tickets are on sale to the general public, with a limit of four per order.

Tuboleta lists the prices below on 30 October 2026, in Colombian pesos with the service fee included, converted at about 3,148 pesos per US dollar, the official rate of 28 October. Prices can change with demand, so treat them as a guide.

Cheapest seats: fourth tier, sections 402 and 403 and 417 and 418, COP 120,000 (about US$38).

Most of the arena has numbered seats, while the General and VIP zones are standing. Some sections, numbered 301, 315, 401, 402, 418 and 419, can have a restricted view depending on the stage set-up, and Tuboleta says it will not accept complaints about that after purchase.

How to Buy From the United States

Tuboleta has two checkout buttons, one for cards issued in Colombia and one for cards issued abroad, and a US credit card goes through the second. Tuboleta says buyers with international cards get their tickets only at the box office, handed to the card holder.

Tickets for foreign cards are handed to the card holder at the box office. Bring the passport and the card used for the order, and leave time to collect the tickets before doors open.

Buy only from Tuboleta or its authorised sales points, which are listed on its site. Resale listings are not guaranteed and can cost far more than the face values above.

Getting to Medellín and the Arena

US visitors fly into José María Córdova International Airport, which serves Medellín from Rionegro in the hills above the city. US citizens need no visa for tourist stays of up to 90 days, and the passport must stay valid for the whole trip.

DAVIarena is at Carrera 49 number 52 Sur-200 in Sabaneta, a town in the south of the metro area. Tuboleta says the nearest station is Itagüí on Line A of the Medellín Metro, about five minutes on foot.

Check the Metro’s closing time before relying on it for the ride back, because the show starts at 9:30 p.m. and may end late. Our guide to Medellín for expats covers neighbourhoods and getting around.

Entry Rules, Safety and Costs

The minimum age is 12 years, and Tuboleta says visibly pregnant women are not allowed in, following recommendations of the authorities. Sections 305, 306, 310, 311, 405, 406, 414 and 415 are alcohol-free zones.

At any big night out in a large city, keep your phone in a front pocket and carry only the cards and cash you need. Book the ride home through an app or the hotel rather than hailing a taxi on the street late at night.

The ticket is the main cost, with a hotel in the city and a transfer on top. Our Colombia coverage tracks the peso and travel news, and the Colombia culture guide explains the music behind the night.

What It Means for You

If you plan the trip, buy the ticket first from Tuboleta and then book flights and a room, since prices can change with demand. Arrive a day early, because the show ends late on a Saturday night.

The same arena hosts other big nights, and the transport and entry notes are similar. Our guides to Fonseca on 6 February and Laura Pausini on 7 March cover them.

What Is Not Known

No opening act, set length or end time has been published, and the arena has not said what happens with tickets bought for the earlier October 2026 date. Holders should ask the seller where they bought.

The Metro’s late-night timetable for the day is not confirmed, and prices can change. We will update this guide when the organiser publishes more.

More: Colombia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When Does Carlos Vives Play Medellín in 2027?

He plays Saturday 17 April 2027 at DAVIarena, with doors at 6 p.m. and the show at 9:30 p.m. local time. That is 10:30 p.m. US Eastern.

How Much Are Carlos Vives Tickets in Medellín?

Tuboleta lists prices from COP 120,000 (about US$38) with service included. Premium zones run higher, up to COP 7,280,000 (about US$2,313) for a box.

Can a US Visitor Buy Tickets With a US Card?

Yes, Tuboleta has a checkout for cards issued outside Colombia. Tickets for those orders are handed over at the box office to the card holder.

How Do I Get to DAVIarena?

The arena is in Sabaneta, about five minutes on foot from Itagüí station on Metro Line A. Taxis and ride-hailing apps also serve it.

World.title: Botafogo vs São Paulo in Rio on 23 November
World.content:
BRAZIL · SPORT · RIO DE JANEIRO

Key Facts The match Botafogo host São Paulo in round 36 of 38 of the Brazilian league on Monday 23 November 2026.

Where and when Nilton Santos Stadium, Rio de Janeiro; kick-off 8 p.m. in Rio, 6 p.m. US Eastern.

Tickets The club sells through Ingresse, a Brazilian ticketing platform; this match was not yet listed on 30 October, and no prices are published.

Watch in the US The league lists Amazon for Brazil; a US broadcaster is not confirmed.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Botafogo, a Rio de Janeiro club, play São Paulo, one of Brazil’s biggest clubs, at the Nilton Santos Stadium on Monday 23 November 2026. The league’s governing body, the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF), set the date, the 8 p.m. kick-off and the stadium in its detailed fixture list of 29 October 2026.

For US readers this is a Monday-evening game that starts at 6 p.m. Eastern, with the Brazilian league title and a place in next year’s South American cup competitions still being decided. Our guide to living in Rio de Janeiro covers the city beyond the stadium.

What the Match Is

The Campeonato Brasileiro Série A, usually called the Brasileirão, is Brazil’s top league, with 20 clubs that each play 38 games. This game is round 36, so only two rounds remain afterwards and every point can move a club between the title race, a South American cup place and the relegation fight.

The CBF fixture list shows Botafogo of Rio hosting São Paulo, a club from the city of the same name about 270 miles (430 km) away. The same round also holds Palmeiras against Flamengo on Saturday 21 November in São Paulo, which our Palmeiras vs Flamengo guide covers.

Standings change every week, so we do not quote a table here. Check the league table on the day you book, because the stakes for both clubs may look very different by 23 November.

We never share your email.

The Clubs in Plain English

Botafogo are a Rio club that won South America’s top club competition, the Copa Libertadores, in 2024. Their home is the Nilton Santos Stadium, a municipal arena in the north zone of Rio that the club uses for league games.

São Paulo, often called São Paulo FC, are a club from Brazil’s largest city with three Libertadores titles. They usually play at the Morumbis stadium, and this trip to Rio is an away game for them.

Schedule in Rio and US Eastern Time

Monday 23 November 2026, 8:00 p.m. in Rio de Janeiro (Brasilia time, UTC-3).

Monday 23 November 2026, 6:00 p.m. US Eastern, 5:00 p.m. Central, 3:00 p.m. Pacific.

Gates and exact opening times are not published yet.

Brazil does not use daylight saving time, and the United States has moved back to standard time on 1 November, so Rio is two hours ahead of New York on this date. The kick-off can still be moved by the CBF or the broadcaster, so check again in the week of the game.

How to Buy Tickets

Botafogo’s official ticket page, linked from the club’s own website, runs on the Ingresse platform at botafogo.ingresse.com. On Friday 30 October 2026 that page listed no event for this game, so sales have not opened.

The page links to the club’s Camisa 7 membership programme, but gives no details on its benefits or on early access. We have no confirmed prices, sectors or sale dates and will not guess them.

Buy only through the club’s page or its verified links, because resale offers for Brazilian league games often appear on social media. Bring your passport, because Brazilian clubs often ask for identification when a ticket is bought or checked.

How to Watch in the US

The CBF’s fixture list marks this game for Amazon, whose Prime Video service shows selected league games in Brazil. It does not say who holds the rights in the United States.

US broadcasters often announce Brazilian league games only a few days ahead. Look for the match in the listings of Spanish- and Portuguese-language sports services in the week of 16 November, and do not pay for a subscription before the game is listed.

Getting There

The Nilton Santos Stadium stands in Engenho de Dentro, a residential district in Rio’s north zone, a long way from the beaches of Copacabana and Ipanema. Allow extra time for the trip, because evening traffic in Rio is heavy and no match-day transport plan has been published for this game.

Most visitors use licensed taxis or ride-hailing apps and agree on the return trip before the game ends. Fly into Rio’s Galeão airport or the downtown Santos Dumont airport, and book a hotel on the south-zone side if you want a beach stay as well.

Fans coming from São Paulo can reach Rio by a flight of about one hour or a road trip of about six hours. The match ends late on a Monday, so a flight home on Tuesday morning is a safer plan than a late-night departure.

Safety and Costs for Visitors

US citizens need a Brazilian e-visa for tourism, which they apply for online before the trip. Our guide to the Brazil e-visa for US citizens explains the process, and the US State Department publishes the current Brazil travel advisory.

Football crowds in Brazil are loud and passionate, and rival fans are separated by the police inside the stadium. Wear neutral colours, carry only the cash and card you need, and keep your phone out of sight on the street after dark.

Do not buy from street sellers outside the stadium, and do not accept tickets sent as screenshots. Our guide to what to do in Rio in November 2026 lists other events that month.

What It Means for You

If you plan a trip, the date is firm enough to book flights, but wait for the ticket sale before you pay for a non-refundable hotel. The 6 p.m. Eastern start makes it easy to follow from the United States on a Monday evening if a broadcaster picks it up.

Fans who follow Brazilian football from the US can pair this game with the other round-36 matches that week. Our Corinthians vs Botafogo guide covers Botafogo’s trip to São Paulo five days earlier, on Wednesday 18 November.

What Is Not Known

The ticket sale date, the prices, the sectors and the rules for visiting fans are not published. A US broadcaster, the gate times and any match-day transport plan are not announced either.

The CBF can still move the kick-off, and a result in an earlier round can change what is at stake. We will refresh this guide when Botafogo open the sale.

Frequently Asked Questions

When Do Botafogo Play São Paulo?

The match is on Monday 23 November 2026 at 8 p.m. in Rio de Janeiro. That is 6 p.m. US Eastern time.

Where Is the Game Played?

It is played at the Nilton Santos Stadium in Engenho de Dentro, in Rio’s north zone. It is not at the Maracanã.

How Do I Buy Tickets?

Botafogo sell tickets through the Ingresse platform, linked from the club’s website. The game was not listed on 30 October, so check again closer to the date.

Can I Watch the Match in the United States?

The league lists Amazon for Brazil, but no US broadcaster is confirmed. Check sports listings in the week of the game.

GUATEMALA · ECONOMY

Key Facts The country Guatemala, Central America’s largest economy, is led by President Bernardo Arévalo.

What happened The Banco de Guatemala, the central bank, published its October 2026 survey of private analysts.

Inflation Analysts expect inflation of 4.42% in December 2026, up from 3.94% in the September survey.

Growth They forecast growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027, both unchanged from September.

Confidence The confidence index fell to 54.38 points, 3.19% below September and 6.77% below October 2025.

Private analysts in Guatemala now expect inflation of 4.42% at the end of 2026, nearly half a point above what they expected a month ago. The Banco de Guatemala (Banguat), the central bank, published the result in its October survey of an analyst panel.

For US readers, higher prices in Guatemala cut the buying power of the dollars that migrants send home, which came to about US$25.5 billion in 2025, as our guide to foreign money in Guatemala explains. The same survey shows that the analysts see slower growth than the 4.3% the economy recorded in 2025.

What Happened

Banguat ran its Survey of Economic Expectations of the Panel of Private Analysts between the second and fourth weeks of October 2026. The survey asks national specialists where they think prices and output are heading.

The panel expects inflation of 4.33% in October, 4.37% in November and 4.42% in December 2026. For December 2027 and December 2028 it expects 3.93% and 3.82%.

In Plain English Banguat The Banco de Guatemala, the country’s central bank.

Inflation How fast prices rise over twelve months, shown as a percentage.

Confidence index A score from 0 to 100 built from the analysts’ answers about business and the economy.

We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

What Analysts Expect for Prices

The forecast for December 2026 rose by 0.48 points from the 3.94% expected in September, while the forecast for December 2027 barely moved. Over longer horizons the panel expects 3.99% in twelve months, 4.00% in two years and 3.69% in five years.

The analysts named energy prices as the most important factor behind the 2026 inflation forecast, followed by weather conditions and inflation in Guatemala’s trading partners. Fiscal and monetary policy also appear on their list.

What They See for Growth

The panel estimates real growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027, with no change from the September survey. For the third quarter of 2026 it expects growth of 3.8%.

Banguat’s preliminary figures put growth at 4.3% in 2025 and 3.7% in 2024. Analysts listed energy prices and fiscal policy as the main factors that could change the pace this year.

The Confidence Index

The index of confidence in economic activity stood at 54.38 points in October, below 56.17 in September and 58.33 in October 2025. Its 2026 high was 62.21 points in February, and its low was 51.53 points in April.

In the poll, 43.8% of analysts expect the economy to improve over the next six months, while 56.2% do not. Only 18.8% called this a good moment for companies to invest, and 75% said they were not sure.

Most analysts, 87.5%, expect the business climate to stay the same over the next six months. Half of them, 50%, think the economy is better than a year ago.

What It Means for You

If you send money to Guatemala, higher inflation means each dollar buys somewhat less, even if the exchange rate holds. Families that depend on remittances feel this first in food and transport.

If you do business there, the survey points to slow but steady growth and a cautious investment mood. Our guide to foreign investment in Guatemala shows that US companies are the largest foreign investors.

What Is Not Known

The survey reflects the opinions of private analysts and not Banguat’s own forecast, so it can differ from the central bank’s official path. The text of the report does not discuss the latest actual inflation reading.

It is not known how much of the rise in expected inflation comes from oil prices and how much from the weather. The size of the panel is also not stated in the summary we reviewed.

What Inflation Do Guatemala Analysts Expect?

Private analysts surveyed in October 2026 expect inflation of 4.42% in December 2026. That is up from 3.94% in the September survey.

What Is Guatemala’s Confidence Index?

It is a score built from analysts’ answers about business and the economy, run by the central bank. It fell to 54.38 points in October 2026 from 56.17 in September.

How Fast Will Guatemala Grow?

The analyst panel forecasts real growth of 3.9% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027. Both figures are unchanged from the September survey.

World.title: High Tides Flood Homes in Costa Rica’s Puntarenas
World.content:
High tides flooded homes in Puntarenas on Thursday, October 29, with authorities warning that elevated tides could continue along Costa Rica’s Pacific coast through Saturday, October 31. The National Emergency Commission (CNE) reported flooding in Barrio El Carmen and the community of 20 de Noviembre in Chacarita.

Seawater entered homes, and photographs from the affected areas showed flooded patios and corridors, with furniture and household belongings standing in water. Members of the Puntarenas Municipal Emergency Committee visited the communities to assess damage, identify families’ needs and coordinate assistance. Initial reports did not specify the number of homes affected or provide an estimate of financial losses.

Thursday’s flooding followed repeated high tides earlier in the week. Residents of El Carmen described moving appliances and other belongings off the floor and staying awake to monitor water entering their homes. Flooding was also reported earlier in the week at Playa Zancudo in Golfito and Playa Preciosa in Puerto Jiménez, extending the effects beyond the city of Puntarenas.

The University of Costa Rica’s Oceanographic Information Module, known as MIO-Cimar, warned that the period of unusually high tides could last through Saturday. The CNE urged residents of coastal communities with a history of tidal flooding to watch local conditions and take steps to protect their belongings.

The conditions are associated with spring tides, the higher tides that occur around the new and full moon when the gravitational effects of the Sun and Moon reinforce one another. These events occur regularly and are unrelated to the spring season. MIO-Cimar coordinator Rodney Mora said warmer Pacific waters associated with El Niño were also contributing to higher sea levels, worsening the effects in vulnerable coastal communities. Water expands as it warms, allowing high tides to reach farther into low-lying areas.

El Niño does not cause spring tides, but the combination can increase the risk of flooding along the coast. Mora also warned that similar conditions could recur in November and December, urging coastal residents to prepare for further episodes.

World.title: Costa Rica Gas Prices Jump Sharply as Regular Fuel Becomes More Expensive Than Premium
World.content:
Drivers in Costa Rica will soon be paying considerably more at the pump after the public services regulator approved yet another round of fuel price increases, including a 12.38% jump in regular gasoline that will make it more expensive than premium fuel. The Public Services Regulatory Authority (ARESEP) approved the adjustment a couple of days ago, with the new prices announced yesterday. Regular gasoline will increase by ₡89 per liter, climbing from ₡719 to ₡808, while premium gasoline will rise by ₡42, from ₡764 to ₡806.

That creates an unusual situation at Costa Rica’s gas stations. Regular gasoline, traditionally the cheaper option, will cost ₡2 more per liter than premium, while diesel will also reach ₡808 following an increase of ₡23. The higher prices have been approved but will not take effect until the regulatory resolution is published in the official government newspaper, La Gaceta. Under the resolution, the new rates begin the following day. An exact implementation date had not been confirmed as of Friday morning.

At the new price, filling a 40-liter (10.6-gallon) tank with regular gasoline will cost ₡32,320 (about $71), up from ₡28,760 (about $64) today, an increase of ₡3,560 (about $8) per fill-up and with regular. Drivers filling a larger 60-liter (15.9-gallon) tank will pay ₡5,340 more than before.

For those who commute daily, operate delivery vehicles or regularly travel between Costa Rica’s major cities, the additional expense could quickly add up. The increases are not limited to gasoline and diesel. Households that use propane gas for cooking will also face higher costs, with the price of a standard 25-pound cylinder rising by ₡549, from ₡7,172 to ₡7,721.

ARESEP estimates that approximately 53% of Costa Rican households use this type of cooking gas. Restaurants, small food businesses and other commercial establishments that depend on propane will also be affected. The regulator says the adjustments reflect rising international fuel costs, which have been influenced by instability in global energy markets.

Costa Rica imports all of its finished petroleum fuels, making domestic prices especially sensitive to changes in international supply, shipping costs and the exchange rate between the colón and the U.S. dollar. Energy officials pointed to disruptions involving oil shipments from the Middle East, declining global inventories and higher refining and transportation costs. Diesel supplies have faced particular pressure as demand and supply conditions fluctuate internationally.

The latest adjustment was calculated using fuel purchases made by the Costa Rican Petroleum Refinery (RECOPE) between September 11 and October 8. The exchange rate also played a role. ARESEP used an average rate of ₡456.66 per dollar for the new calculation, compared with ₡450.41 in the previous adjustment. Because fuel purchases are made in dollars, that difference increases the amount paid in colones even when the international price of a product remains unchanged.

For Costa Rican businesses, higher fuel prices can create expenses that extend well beyond the cost of filling a vehicle. Transportation companies, agricultural producers, delivery services and businesses that distribute goods throughout Costa Rica depend heavily on diesel and gasoline. When those costs rise, companies may face pressure to adjust their operating budgets or eventually pass some of the increases on to customers.

Tourism operators could also feel the effects. Rental car companies, shuttle services and tour providers frequently travel long distances between Juan Santamaría International Airport, the Central Valley and popular destinations such as La Fortuna, Manuel Antonio, Tamarindo and the southern Pacific coast.

Tourists coming here and are renting cars will find the same regulated fuel prices as Costa Rican motorists. However, any increase in tour prices, transportation fares or rental rates would depend on decisions by individual businesses and where applicable, additional regulatory approvals.

The latest adjustment comes after earlier fuel increases in October, adding to transportation expenses as Costa Rica approaches the busy end-of-year holiday and tourism season. The approved changes also highlight how fuel prices can move differently depending on the type of petroleum product. Although regular gasoline is typically cheaper than premium, international market conditions and the formulas used to calculate domestic prices can occasionally reverse that relationship.

For those who don’t have a diesel car, once the new rates become effective, premium gasoline will actually be slightly cheaper than regular gasoline, but you should still follow the fuel specifications recommended by your vehicle manufacturer. The regulator’s decision covers nearly two million vehicles circulating in Costa Rica, including private cars, motorcycles, buses, trucks and other commercial transportation.

While our government regulates retail fuel prices, those prices are reviewed periodically and can increase or decrease depending on the cost of imported petroleum products and other factors included in the pricing formula. For now, drivers have a short period before the latest adjustment takes effect. Once the new prices are officially published and implemented, a liter of regular gasoline and diesel will both cost ₡808, marking another increase in the cost of getting around Costa Rica.

World.title: Heading Out for Halloween in Costa Rica? Expect More Police on Patrol
World.content:
Heading to a costume party, a beach bash or a masquerade parade this Saturday? Expect to see more police than usual. Costa Rica’s national police are stepping up patrols across our country for Halloween and they will concentrate on the places where crowds gather. The Public Security Ministry said officers will focus on cemeteries, churches, shopping centers and the streets around bars hosting costume parties.

The goal is to prevent vandalism, spot unauthorized parties and head off trouble at large gatherings. When the national police first outlined the plan, it said it would deploy 1,500 officers from today through Sunday. The ministry’s latest statement, issued yesterday, did not give a number of officers.

Because halloween falls on a Saturday, many parties start Friday night, and that three-day window is meant to cover them. Why cemeteries and churches? Police said incidents in past years, including vandalism and rituals at cemeteries, are the reason officers will patrol them through the weekend. César Anchía, deputy director general of the national police, outlined the weekend operations.

If you’re going out, expect police at the party too. Themed Halloween events and other mass gatherings will see preventive checks and patrols at venues and meeting points. Part of the aim is to catch parties held without permits. Shopping centers, which draw families in costume on Halloween, are also on the patrol list.

If you’re driving, watch for the Caravana del Payaso, or Clown Caravan, a Halloween ride that draws hundreds of motorcyclists. Police will watch the route and the gathering points, and the ministry said highway patrols are meant to prevent crashes. Give riders room and allow extra time where the caravan passes.

Taking kids trick-or-treating? Police are asking parents to stay with their children and keep them in sight the whole time they go door to door. Before you head home, make sure the car you get into is the ride you actually booked. Lat night, the Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ) said it had detained four men suspected of drugging and robbing people outside bars and nightclubs in San José.

According to the OIJ, one of the suspects allegedly posed as the ride-hailing driver victims had requested, then offered them drinks laced with a sedative. Investigators said other members of the group then withdrew cash and moved money out of victims’ accounts and spent it on goods and services, including fuel.

Saturday is also Costa Rica’s National Masquerade Day, when towns celebrate with giant-headed mascareros, cimarrona bands and dancing in the streets. Police said those community events fall under the same security operation. In beach towns, Halloween runs all weekend. Tamarindo has costume surfing, parades and beach parties on the calendar. Big crowds also draw thieves, so keep valuables with you and out of parked cars, where a rental can be emptied in minutes. In an emergency, call 911.

Halloween has grown steadily in Costa Rica alongside our own masquerade tradition, blending a centuries-old holiday with local customs. Authorities are betting that a visible police presence will keep this year’s celebrations safe for everyone who takes part.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Cambronero Bridge to Reopen
World.content:
The Cambronero bridge on Route 1 is scheduled to reopen Tuesday, November 3, restoring traffic through a stretch of the Inter-American Highway closed since a truck damaged the structure in September. The reopening is planned for noon, nearly two weeks ahead of schedule. The bridge is at kilometer 71, on the road connecting San Ramón, Alajuela, with Esparza, Puntarenas.

The crossing has been closed since the night of September 7, when a tractor-trailer struck the modular steel bridge. Crews had to dismantle parts of the structure, replace damaged components and remove and reinstall the bridge deck. Before those repairs could begin, workers built a support tower to hold the bridge’s weight while damaged pieces were removed. Some parts of that temporary support had to be manufactured specifically for the work.

Additional work will continue after the bridge reopens, but those remaining tasks are not expected to interrupt traffic. Drivers should slow down and use caution around crews at the site. The reopening will restore passage through Cambronero while preparations continue for a permanent solution to the ground instability affecting this section of Route 1.

Bids for that project are under review, with construction expected to begin in early 2027. The planned work includes stabilizing the slope, removing the modular bridge and restoring the road’s two lanes. A possible third lane is also being studied, but it has not been approved for construction.

World.title: Tamarindo Celebrates Halloween Weekend With Costume Surfing, Parades and Beach Parties
World.content:
Tamarindo is getting ready for a Halloween weekend that promises everything from surfers riding waves in costumes to trick-or-treating, costume contests, live music and beach parties. The popular Guanacaste destination will host the fifth annual Tamarindo Halloween Fest, with its main celebrations taking place this Friday and Saturday.

Organized by the Tamarindo Development Association (ADIT), the festival brings together local families, tourists, businesses and community organizations for two days of activities designed to offer something for just about everyone. There will be events for children, contests for pets, a nighttime running race and plenty of entertainment for adults looking to celebrate Halloween at the beach.

The celebration has grown since it began in 2022, with Tamarindo’s hotels, restaurants and local businesses joining the festivities. Organizers hope the event will also bring more people to the community before Costa Rica’s busy tourism season gets underway. This year, Halloween falls on a Saturday, giving everyone a full weekend to enjoy the celebrations without having to rush home the next morning.

The main family activities begin Friday at 5 p.m. with a costume parade through downtown Tamarindo, starting near Hotel Tamarindo Diria and continuing toward Parque Oneida, where much of the evening’s entertainment will take place. Children and adults are encouraged to dress up, with costume competitions planned for kids and families. Even dogs will have their chance to compete, as organizers invite pet owners to bring their four-legged companions dressed in Halloween outfits.

The Friday celebration will feature a crazy hair competition, trick-or-treating, music and activities for younger children. The traditional Payasos Los Alegres will also join the parade, bringing a touch of Costa Rican entertainment to the festivities. For those who prefer something a little scarier, Journey School will operate a haunted house at Parque Oneida beginning at 6 p.m. Admission to the haunted house carries a fee, with proceeds supporting scholarships for students at the school.

Those looking for food will find local vendors participating in the Tama Market, offering a variety of dishes and refreshments throughout the evening. A dance competition will add another element to the celebration, with participants performing routines inspired by Halloween characters and popular horror-themed entertainment. Organizers are encouraging groups to put together their most creative performances for a chance to win prizes.

Friday will also feature a recreational 5-kilometer (3.1-mile) race organized by Tama Run. The event combines exercise with Halloween fun, rewarding runners who show up wearing the most creative costumes. After the family celebrations, Tamarindo’s nightlife will take over. Crazy Monkey will host its Haunted Paradise party on Friday beginning at 9 p.m., featuring several DJs and three stages with dancehall, reggaeton and electronic music.

The festivities continue Saturday morning with a free Halloween reading event at the Tamarindo Children’s Community Library. From 10:30 a.m. until 12:30 p.m., children can enjoy themed stories and collect candy. One of the weekend’s most unusual events takes place Saturday afternoon when surfers head into the Pacific Ocean wearing Halloween costumes.

The costume surfing event is scheduled from 3:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. in front of Witch’s Rock Surf Camp, bringing together local surfers, instructors, residents and visitors for an afternoon of waves, music and prizes. Participants will be judged in different categories, adding a playful twist to a sport that has helped make Tamarindo one of Costa Rica’s best-known surfing destinations.

Several local surfing organizations are participating, including the Tamarindo Surf Association, the Tamarindo Sports Committee and the North Pacific Surf Association. For anyone who would rather watch than paddle out, the beach will provide a chance to see surfers attempt to catch waves while dressed in costumes not normally associated with the ocean.

Saturday evening will bring another round of parties and competitions. Sharky’s is planning a Halloween celebration with $1,500 in costume prizes, while Iguana Surf and NAIA restaurant will hold a sunset gathering featuring music and additional costume contests. A pickleball tournament organized by 15 Love Tamarindo is also part of the festival’s activities, with prizes that include a two-night hotel stay for two people.

Beyond the entertainment, the festival is intended to support Tamarindo’s tourism businesses during a traditionally slower period of the year. Hotels including Pasatiempo, Mar Rey, Hideaway Costa Rica and Las Guapas are offering special accommodation promotions, with some deals extending into November.

Restaurants and shops are also participating, giving everyone more reasons to spend the weekend in town. Several beachwear and fashion retailers have announced discounts ranging from 10% to 70%. Elizabeth Cole, president of the Tamarindo Development Association, said the goal is to make the community a destination people associate with Halloween celebrations in Costa Rica.

The combination of beaches, restaurants, nightlife and family entertainment makes Tamarindo well suited for a festival that appeals to different age groups, while providing additional business for local merchants ahead of the high season. Although many of the community activities are free, some attractions, races and private parties may require advance registration or paid admission.

Anyone planning to attend should check individual event details, particularly for nighttime entertainment and competitions with limited participation. The main family celebration at Parque Oneida runs from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. Friday, while the Saturday program offers activities from the morning through late evening.

For travelers already visiting Guanacaste, Halloween weekend provides another reason to spend time in Tamarindo. And for those living in Costa Rica who want something different from the usual Halloween party, watching costumed surfers catch waves in the Pacific might be difficult to beat.

The complete schedule, registration details and any last-minute changes are available through the Tamarindo Development Association’s official website and its social media accounts.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Native Stingless Bees at Center of Supreme Court Fight
World.content:
Costa Rica’s tiny native bees have become the center of a legal battle that could affect beekeepers, honey producers and efforts to protect some of the country’s most important pollinators. The Constitutional Chamber of the Supreme Court (Sala IV), has agreed to review a challenge against government regulations that limit the commercial use of native stingless bees. The case raises questions about whether the rules are protecting biodiversity or making it unnecessarily difficult for people who have raised these insects for generations.

Costa Rica is home to 58 recorded species of native stingless bees, but regulations introduced in November 2025 allow commercial production without additional scientific studies for only two species. Anyone hoping to commercially produce honey, wax or other products from the remaining species must first provide scientific evidence showing that doing so will not threaten their survival.

The legal challenge was accepted last week following a complaint filed by Yandry Johanna Alvarado Castro. The lawsuit questions several provisions of the Executive Decree which regulates facilities where stingless bees are raised and managed. Unlike the familiar European honeybee, Costa Rica’s native stingless bees lack a functional stinger. Many are much smaller, and some live in colonies inside hollow trees, fallen logs and other natural cavities.

Two of the best-known species are the mariola (Tetragonisca angustula) and soncuano (Scaptotrigona pectoralis). Both are included among the species permitted for commercial production under the regulations. Their honey is produced in relatively small quantities and has long been valued by Costa Rican families, particularly in rural communities where raising native bees has been passed down through generations.

The practice is known as meliponiculture, a type of beekeeping that focuses on stingless bees rather than the imported honeybees commonly used in large-scale commercial honey production. But these insects do much more than produce honey. They pollinate native plants and agricultural crops, helping forests regenerate and supporting the reproduction of vegetation throughout the country.

That ecological importance is one reason the government introduced the regulations. Officials say the rules are intended to protect native bee populations, prevent overexploitation and preserve genetic diversity. However, beekeepers and researchers have questioned whether some of the restrictions are supported by sufficient scientific evidence.

One of the most controversial measures limits commercial operations to 30 colonies and noncommercial operations to just five. The legal challenge argues that these limits fail to consider differences between species, regional environmental conditions and the availability of food sources.

A beekeeper working in the humid forests of Limón, for example, may face very different conditions from someone maintaining colonies in the dry forests of Guanacaste. Critics argue that applying identical limits to both operations may not make sense without additional research.

The regulations also require beekeepers to maintain minimum distances between their colonies and agricultural operations using pesticides. Depending on the size of the bee species, those distances range from 500 meters (1,640 feet) to 3.5 kilometers (2.2 miles). Even greater distances are required in some circumstances, including where aerial spraying takes place.

Although the intention is to protect bees from potentially dangerous chemicals, the lawsuit questions how those distances were established and whether they are practical for small farmers and rural families. Researchers at the National University’s Tropical Bee Research Center (CINAT) have also raised concerns about the scientific basis for the restrictions.

Of the 58 native stingless-bee species recorded in Costa Rica, researchers have documented 20 species being maintained in managed colonies. That is considerably more than the two species covered by the regulation’s simpler commercial approval process. Specialists agree that native bees need protection but have warned that more information is required before deciding how many colonies should be allowed or which species are appropriate for commercial production.

For traditional beekeepers, the rules could have financial consequences. Some families maintain several species and depend on the sale of small quantities of honey and other products to supplement their income. Others raise bees primarily to preserve traditional knowledge and maintain healthy populations of pollinators on their properties.

The National Chamber of Stingless Beekeepers has previously called for additional species to be included in the regulations, particularly the jicote gato (Melipona beecheii) and jicote barcino (Melipona costarricensis). The organization and other critics argue that overly restrictive rules could discourage beekeepers from registering their operations and push some producers into the informal market.

Another concern involves potential penalties. The lawsuit challenges provisions that refer violations to Costa Rica’s Wildlife Conservation Law, arguing that beekeepers could face legal uncertainty over activities involving insects that naturally move between managed colonies and the surrounding environment. The case now moves forward in the Constitutional Chamber, where judges will examine whether the disputed rules comply with Costa Rica’s Constitution and environmental protections.

The court has given the Attorney General’s Office and the ministries of Environment and Energy and the Presidency 15 days to respond to the legal challenge. Importantly, accepting the case does not mean the judges have ruled against the regulations. The existing requirements remain in effect while the court considers the arguments.

Beekeepers also face a registration deadline in November 2026, when the 12-month period established under the regulations is scheduled to expire. The dispute comes at a time when Costa Rica is already confronting broader concerns about the survival of native bees. Earlier this year, the Constitutional Chamber ordered authorities to enforce a nationwide ban on insecticides containing fipronil after a separate case involving damage to bee colonies in Lepanto, Puntarenas.

The complainants in that case reported losing at least 24 native bee colonies and serious damage to hundreds of additional hives. The ruling highlighted the risks that agricultural chemicals can pose to pollinators and reinforced the importance of protecting native insects that play an essential role in Costa Rica’s ecosystems.

For now, the latest legal dispute presents a difficult question for authorities: how to protect native bees without placing unnecessary burdens on the people who raise and care for them. With dozens of native species, a long tradition of small-scale beekeeping and an economy closely connected to agriculture and conservation, Costa Rica has considerable interest in finding the right balance.

The Supreme Court’s eventual ruling could help determine how the country manages its native bees for years to come, affecting not only honey producers but also the forests and farms that depend on these small but valuable pollinators.

World.title: Costa Rica’s President Invites Pope Leo XIV to Visit in 2027
World.content:
President Laura Fernández formally invited Pope Leo XIV to visit Costa Rica during a private audience at the Vatican, proposing a trip in 2027 that would make him the first pontiff to set foot in the country since John Paul II in March 1983. Fernández delivered the invitation in a letter and handed it to the pope in person at the Apostolic Palace. In it, she extended what she called a fraternal and respectful invitation on behalf of the people and government of Costa Rica, describing the country as a land where work and peace prevail.

The letter ties the proposed visit to two anniversaries Costa Rica will mark in 2027. One is the 203rd anniversary of the declaration of Our Lady of the Angels, known here as La Negrita, the patron saint. The other is the 180th anniversary of the Constitution recognizing Catholicism as the official religion of the state.

No date has been set and the letter leaves the timing to the pope, and Fernández offered to coordinate preparations for an eventual pastoral and official visit through the Vatican’s Secretariat of State and the Apostolic Nunciature in San José. The Vatican has not said whether the pope will accept.

Fernández also presented the pope with a replica of the Virgin of the Angels and coffees from several Costa Rican growing regions. It is not the first time Costa Rican coffee has reached Leo XIV. Speaking to Catholic media after the meeting, Fernández said she had invited the pope to come and greet La Negrita, and that it would be very special for Costa Rica to receive a pope again after 1983. She said the conversation lasted about 30 minutes, that she told him Costa Ricans had been praying for him, and that she felt at home.

She added that the pope appeared in good spirits and in good health following a recent medical procedure, though she said the two did not discuss his recovery directly. The Holy See Press Office said in a statement after the audience that Fernández also met with Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, and Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, secretary for relations with states and international organizations.

According to the statement, those talks highlighted good relations between the Holy See and Costa Rica and between the state and the local Church and covered social and political issues in the country and the region, particularly security and migration. Fernández said she discussed with the pope the situation of Nicaraguan migrants, the largest migrant group in Costa Rica, as well as cooperation with the United States on people going through deportation proceedings.

On security, she said her government pairs investment in education, health and support for young people with measures against organized crime, including efforts to stop inmates from directing violence from inside prisons. The audience came two weeks after Fernández toured El Salvador’s CECOT mega-prison, and as Costa Rica moves inmates into its own maximum-security facility, the CACCO.

Bishop Bartolomé Buigues of Alajuela, vice president of the Costa Rican Episcopal Conference, said closer engagement between the Church and civil authorities is of great importance. The bishops’ conference thanked the president for promoting the meeting. The Vatican stop opened Fernández’s third official trip abroad since taking office in May, following visits to El Salvador and Colombia. Her schedule in Rome also includes a meeting with Italian President Sergio Mattarella.

She then travels to Madrid for the 30th Ibero-American Summit of Heads of State and Government on Nov. 4 and 5 and is scheduled to return to Costa Rica on Nov. 6. A papal visit would carry particular weight in a country where devotion to La Negrita draws pilgrims from every province to the Basilica of Our Lady of the Angels in Cartago each August. John Paul II’s 1983 stop, part of a tour of Central America, remains the last time a pope visited the country.

World.title: 46 US Veterans Tried Ayahuasca in Costa Rica, Where Rules Remain Murky
World.content:
Forty-six American military veterans and first responders spent a week at an ayahuasca retreat in Guanacaste in September, hoping the Amazonian brew would ease trauma they carried home from combat zones and emergency scenes. Their accounts, published Wednesday by the New York Post, describe former Army Rangers and Navy SEALs weeping in ceremony tents and returning home calmer.

The stories are moving. They also land in a place where the Ministry of Health has spent nearly two years warning the public against therapeutic ayahuasca use, while the best-known center that serves it holds a ministry authorization the ministry itself tried, and failed, to cancel.

The retreat ran from Sept. 5 to 12 at Rythmia Life Advancement Center near Tamarindo, in the area of Santa Cruz, spanning the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 attacks. It was organized with The Coming Home Project, a nonprofit founded in 2021 by Navy SEAL veteran Nate Brown to combat veteran suicide, and funded largely by the Birds Eye View Project, a Texas veterans charity, according to the organizers.

The Post put the group at 46, while a September press release from the organizers said 47 took part. Days combined yoga, individual and group counseling, classes and meditation, with ayahuasca ceremonies held at night in tents. Rythmia and Coming Home reviewed each participant’s medical history, medications and mental health beforehand, the Post reported.

The need behind such efforts is stark. A 2026 Department of Veterans Affairs report counted 6,488 veteran suicides in 2024, an average of nearly 18 a day. Participants described the week as a turning point. A 44-year-old firefighter and former Army Ranger, identified only as Dave L., told the Post that the constant inner conflict he lived with had grown much quieter since he returned home. He stopped short of calling a single retreat a cure.

Jeff McNairy, Rythmia’s chief medical officer and a psychiatrist, told the paper that trauma is the condition he considers ayahuasca best suited to treat. He said roughly half the participants vomited on any given night, a reaction the center describes as a psychosomatic release of trauma.

What the coverage does not include is outcome data. No standardized symptom scores, follow-up assessments or comparison group were reported for the group. Rythmia advertises a self-reported success rate above 97% among more than 23,000 guests since 2016, a figure drawn from its own guest surveys rather than independent clinical measurement.

The broader research is promising but young. An observational study run with the nonprofit Heroic Hearts Project followed 58 veterans who attended ayahuasca or psilocybin retreats in Peru and Jamaica between 2021 and 2024. Its research director, neuroscientist Grace Blest-Hopley, has said more than 80% of those who entered with PTSD no longer met the diagnostic criteria afterward.

The study’s published averages were more modest, with PTSD symptom scores falling about 26% among the ayahuasca group. Researchers at the University of Texas are now studying how brain responses in combat veterans change after ayahuasca treatment. None of this yet amounts to the large controlled trials regulators require before approving a treatment.

The risks are well documented. About 70% of users experience acute nausea and more than half report unsettling psychological effects, according to research cited by the Post. Combined with common SSRI antidepressants, the brew can trigger serotonin syndrome, which can be fatal, and it can provoke prolonged psychosis in people with underlying psychiatric vulnerabilities.

Those medications and histories are common among veterans with PTSD, which is why screening matters as much as the ceremony itself. Costa Rica has no law written for this industry. In January 2025 the Ministry of Health issued a health warning on ayahuasca and ibogaine, urging the public not to consume or promote either for therapeutic purposes, not to join rituals that use psychoactive substances for healing, and to report anyone offering them.

The ministry said no product based on either plant holds the sanitary registration it requires. Rythmia is the exception, and an awkward one. The center promotes itself as the world’s only medically licensed ayahuasca center, with a round-the-clock medical team that McNairy said includes five doctors and 12 registered nurses.

According to a February 2025 opinion from the Attorney General’s Office (PGR), the Ministry of Health told Rythmia in July 2022 that it could keep using ayahuasca for therapeutic purposes on a temporary basis until a regulation was issued. In October 2024, Health Minister Mary Munive asked the PGR to endorse annulling that authorization.

The PGR declined and said the ministry’s request contained extremely serious errors, including a failure to identify which rules the authorization violated, and noted that no regulation governed or banned ayahuasca when the permission was granted. It is not clear whether the ministry has revisited the case since.

Elsewhere, safeguards vary widely. A study published in January in JAMA Network Open interviewed representatives of 49 publicly advertised psychedelic retreat organizations, most of them based in the United States. About seven in 10 worked with a licensed health professional or someone trained in emergency response, but only about two-thirds had such a person present at retreats even some of the time.

By one estimate, Costa Rica hosts about 80 psychedelic retreat centers, some 60 of them offering ayahuasca, making it the second most popular destination for this kind of travel after Peru.

The consequences of thin oversight have already been felt here. Lauren Levis, a 40-year-old social worker from New Mexico, died in August 2024 after taking iboga at Soul Centro, a retreat in Paquera on the Nicoya Peninsula. Her brother has said she collapsed in a shower after an all-night ceremony, and that an electrocardiogram taken before the retreat showed marked abnormalities, yet she was allowed to attend.

Judicial investigators sent their findings to prosecutors in March 2025, nearly eight months after her death. A Norwegian woman died after taking ibogaine at another facility near Liberia in 2014. The veterans’ relief may prove genuine, and researchers are working to measure how much of it lasts. For now, the safeguards around ayahuasca in Costa Rica depend largely on the operators who serve it.

Researchers who study the retreat industry advise anyone weighing one to ask for a written medical screening that covers heart conditions, psychiatric history and every medication, a medical professional on site rather than on call, a clear emergency plan with transport to the nearest hospital, and straight answers about the legal status of what is being served. Medical experts also warn that safely tapering off antidepressants can take six to 12 weeks under supervision, far longer than many retreats allow.

World.title: Mark the 2027 holiday dates on your calendar!
World.content:
Mark the 2027 holiday dates on your calendar!

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize has announced the official schedule of public and bank holidays for 2027.

The schedule was issued in Belmopan in accordance with the Holidays Act, Chapter 289 of the Laws of Belize.

The year will begin with New Year’s Day on Friday, January 1, followed by George Price Day on Friday, January 15.

National Heroes and Benefactors Day will be observed on Monday, March 8, in lieu of March 9. The Easter holiday period will include Good Friday on March 26, Holy Saturday on March 27, and Easter Monday on March 29.

Other holidays include Labour Day on Monday, May 3, observed in lieu of May 1, and Emancipation Day on Monday, August 2, in lieu of August 1.

St. George’s Caye Day will fall on Friday, September 10, followed by Independence Day on Tuesday, September 21.

Indigenous People’s Resistance Day will be observed on Monday, October 11, in lieu of October 12, while Garifuna Settlement Day will be celebrated on Friday, November 19.

The final holidays of 2027 will be Christmas Day on Saturday, December 25, and Boxing Day on Monday, December 27.

Belizeans are encouraged to take note of the dates when planning travel, family activities, and business operations throughout the year.

World.title: Belize represented at regional meeting on drug trafficking and organized crime
World.content:
Belize represented at regional meeting on drug trafficking and organized crime

By Zoila Palma: Miguel Guerra, Member of Parliament for Cayo West, represented the National Assembly of Belize at the 17th Meeting of the Inter-Parliamentary Commission on Citizen Security and Administration of Justice (CISCAJ), held on Thursday, October 29, 2026, in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic.

The meeting was convened by the Forum of Presidents of Legislative Powers (FOPREL) and brought together parliamentarians from member legislatures, along with strategic partners from the Organization of American States (OAS). Discussions focused on strengthening regional cooperation to address emerging threats linked to synthetic drugs, new psychoactive substances, and transnational organized crime.

Participants received presentations on the regional threat posed by synthetic drugs, a proposed Special Framework Law on Synthetic Drugs and New Psychoactive Substances, and a Parliamentary Follow-up Guide on Drugs in Latin America.

These presentations were followed by an inter-parliamentary debate on the challenges facing countries across the region and the need for a coordinated legislative response.

The meeting concluded with the approval of a resolution calling for stronger parliamentary action against synthetic drugs and transnational organized crime, alongside the Special Framework Law on Synthetic Drugs and New Psychoactive Substances.

World.title: Three reportedly dead in Coastal Plain Highway shooting; Lloyd Leslie Jr. identified among victims
World.content:
Three reportedly dead in Coastal Plain Highway shooting; Lloyd Leslie Jr. identified among victims

By Breaking Belize News Staff: At least three people are reportedly dead following a shooting incident along the Coastal Plain Highway on Friday morning, October 30, with one of the victims identified as Lloyd Leslie Jr.

According to preliminary reports, the incident occurred between Miles 21 and 22 of the highway, where a vehicle carrying several occupants reportedly ended up overturned off the roadway after being fired upon.

Initial information circulating this morning suggested that the vehicle may have come under gunfire before crashing. However, authorities have not confirmed whether shots were fired or what caused the incident.

Early reports indicated that as many as six people may have been travelling in the vehicle, although the number of occupants and the full extent of the casualties remain unconfirmed.

7 News Belize has since reported that relatives of Lloyd Leslie Jr. confirmed his death. The identities of the other reported victims have not yet been established.

Police have reportedly blocked access to the Coastal Plain Highway at its northern entrance near La Democracia while investigators process the scene and attempt to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy.

Authorities have reportedly advised motorists that the highway will remain closed until later this afternoon as investigations continue.

Breaking Belize News will provide further updates as additional information becomes available.

World.title: Multiple people killed in shooting on Coastal Road
World.content:
Multiple people killed in shooting on Coastal Road

By Zoila Palma: Police are investigating a triple murder that occurred this morning on the Coastal Road.

According to reports, 3 persons traveling in a red SUV were shot and killed.

Authorities have blocked off that part of the highway and are processing the scene.

World.title: Government of Belize seeks to improve project delivery and address Sargassum challenges
World.content:
Government of Belize seeks to improve project delivery and address Sargassum challenges

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize has concluded a three-day Joint Country Portfolio Performance Review with the World Bank Group, the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), and the Caribbean Development Bank (CDB), aimed at strengthening coordination and improving the implementation of development projects across the country.

The review, held from October 26 to 28, 2026, was led by Minister of Economic Transformation Dr. Osmond Martinez and brought together the Financial Secretary, chief executive officers of key ministries, project executing units, and representatives of the three development partners.

Discussions focused on reviewing ongoing projects, addressing implementation challenges, strengthening institutional capacity, and improving coordination among the agencies involved.

One major area of discussion was Belize’s response to sargassum.

The development partners agreed to continue working with the Government to explore restructuring existing investments to support targeted short-term interventions, while identifying opportunities for new investments. Longer-term efforts will focus on helping Belize better map, prioritize, and plan interventions for a more coordinated response.

The World Bank also commended the Government on its Cabinet-approved policy to improve procedures for investment loans under the Public Sector Investment Program.

The policy is expected to help accelerate project readiness, strengthen accountability, and improve implementation.

The review concluded with discussions on reducing duplication, building project delivery capacity, and broadening market participation, as the Government and its partners seek to ensure development investments deliver meaningful results for Belizeans.

World.title: Belizeans less confident about their money and the economy, SIB reports
World.content:
Belizeans less confident about their money and the economy, SIB reports

By Zoila Palma: Consumer confidence in Belize declined sharply in September 2026, reaching its lowest level in almost two and a half years, as households became more pessimistic about the economy, their financial situations, and making major purchases.
